Final Cardinals-Broncos Injury Report Revealed
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Denver Broncos have revealed their final Week 7 injury report.
The Cardinals have ruled out all of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Andrew Wingard (knee), Walter Nolen III (ankle) and Jon Gaines (knee) ahead of Sunday's clash at State Farm Stadium.
That marks four starters Arizona is already down entering the weekend, with more potentially on the way.
Budda Baker (groin/illness), Carson Beck (back), Max Melton (knee) and Darius Robinson (back) are officially listed as questionable.
In Denver, three players in Tyler Badie (thumb), Jonah Eliss (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) are out while Jonah Coleman (ankle) and Pat Surtain II (ankle) are questionable for the Broncos.
Both teams are able to make up to two standard practice squad elevations on Saturday, which could tip who is probable to play or not play depending on which positions are activated. Official game inactives are due on Sunday at 11:35 AM while kickoff is at 1:05 PM in the desert.
The Cardinals are desperately looking to play spoiler once again, though some massive injuries in the likes of Nolen and Love will make things tough. With Gaines out, Arizona will start Hayden Conner at right guard against a Broncos defense that has already generated 60 pressures this season.
Arizona is confident Baker is trending in the right direction while Robinson and Melton are still up in the air.
With four established players out and possibly more on the way, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur knows there's a tall task ahead with a staunch Denver defense.
"They’re very smart. They’re very well coached. I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league," he said to reporters earlier this week.
"They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it.
"They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. Yes, it’s the last two weeks, but it’s really been all year, and it’s been for a few years now. We have our hands full with this group, for sure.”
Arizona is 2-4 on the season while the Broncos are 4-2.

title: Larry Fitzgerald Shares Emotional Message to Cardinals Fans Ahead of Ring of Honor Ceremony
full_text:
It's Larry Fitzgerald's weekend in the desert, and the Arizona Cardinals' legend couldn't be more thankful for the Red Sea as he prepares to enter the team's Ring of Honor.
“Just how much I appreciate them. What it meant to be able to don that Cardinals helmet, the memories that we've been able to share out there in Glendale. I still remember 2006 like it was yesterday," Fitzgerald told reporters this weekend when asked about Arizona fans.
"We had that preseason opener with the stadium patch against the Steelers. Just the electricity driving up to the stadium, first time pulling in the A lot and seeing all the people up on top of the stands cheering and just the energy that I received all those times coming into that place and the love that I receive still to this day going around in the community. I just want to be able to reiterate how much that has meant to me and my family and something that I'll never forget.”
Fitzgerald, after being inducted into the NFL Hall of Fame earlier this year, will go into the Cardinals' Ring of Honor as the team plays host to the Denver Broncos in Week 7.
Reflecting in a press conference with reporters, Fitzgerald said he doesn't take seeing the flurry of No. 11 jerseys lightly.
"I felt like the responsibility was a lot more when I was playing," Fitzgerald continued on being asked about emerging as an Arizona sports icon.
"I'm washed now and the kids are like, 'Hey, you're Larry Fitzgerald.' I say, 'Yeah, yeah.' They're like, 'My dad used to really like you. My dad used to really like you.' So it's kind of moved on, but I always remember driving to the stadium and (I'd be) looking out in the stands and looking out into the people walking around and I'm like, 'Man, there's a lot 11 jerseys there.' I'm saying (to myself) most of those kids I know didn't have the money to buy them and being a parent now, I'm not going to buy my kid a jersey of a player that I don't respect if they don't play hard or they're not active in their community.
"There's a criteria that we all would have as a parent to be OK with our son wearing or our daughter wearing their jersey, so that responsibility was never lost on me. I still think to a certain degree that I have it, but it's not like I'm in the spotlight like (TE) Trey (McBride) is or how (S) Budda (Baker) is or 'J Love' (RB Jeremiyah Love) is. They're in the fight every single day, so I think the onus is a little bit higher with them.”

title: Jeremiyah Love, Walter Nolen III Get Final Injury Call For Cardinals-Broncos
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are going to be down some serious star power against the Denver Broncos.
Head coach Mike LaFleur has ruled out Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Walter Nolen III (ankle) among a few others for Week 7, which includes Andrew Wingard (knee) and Jon Gaines (knee).
"All right, just to get this through. So Jeremiyah, Walt, and Dewey will all be out for Sunday, and then unfortunately, Jon Gaines had a practice injury yesterday, so he'll be out as well," LaFleur said.
The Cardinals' coach also confirmed Carson Beck and Darius Robinson's injuries weren't serious. Budda Baker is also being monitored, but the team feels good about him according to LaFleur.
The #AZCardinals are ruling out RB Jeremiyah Love, S Andrew Wingard, OL Jon Gaines and DL Walter Nolen III for Week 7’s battle against the Denver Broncos. Carson Beck dealing with back spasms. Not long term. No conversations to put Love on IR. Feels good about Budda Baker.
Arizona isn't expected to place Love or Nolen on injured reserve. Love will miss his second consecutive game while Nolen will be out for the first time in 2026.
This will massively hamper the Cardinals' chances to pull off another upset, this time coming against the Broncos — who are playing some of the toughest defense in the league.
"I don't care what scheme you run on defense, as long as you have conviction in it, which they do. There's clarity with the players, which they do. You have good players that matches the scheme that they're trying to run, which they do. Like they're all on the same page," LaFleur said of Denver's defense.
"Cover two, cover three, quarters, I mean, everyone has everything. It's how you're coaching it and how you're mixing and matching it, and what you know VJ [Vance Joseph] is thinking that he thinks is going to be best vs. us. We're going to get a little bit of everything. I'm assuming. I mean, that's usually what ends up happening.
"And then there's specific areas where you're anticipating maybe a little bit more of this than that, based on who we have compared to maybe based on some other teams. You never really know exactly what you're going to see. You just go off of what you saw on tape, some of your past experiences. But as we know, this defense has been playing really well for a few years, and it's going to be a challenge not only because of the scheme, but because of the players that are actually running the scheme."
The Cardinals will release their final practice reports for today, though Arizona clearly will be down some massive names.

title: Why Larry Fitzgerald Chose Now For Cardinals Ring of Honor Moment
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals move into this weekend with one player in mind: Larry Fitzgerald.
The Hall of Fame receiver is set to be inducted into the Cardinals' Ring of Honor in Arizona's Week 7 home battle against the Denver Broncos, a long awaited weekend that's sure to have State Farm Stadium packed with loyal fans who witnessed one of the best careers in Arizona sports history.
Fitzgerald, speaking with reporters this week, says the moment was actually supposed to happen years ago.
“Fortunately, I have a great relationship with (Owner) Michael (Bidwill) and the family, so this has been something we've talked about since the time I left. Actually, about three years ago, we decided on a date, and I had something family-wise come up shortly after we had agreed on it," he said.
"And Michael was like, 'hey, if it feels right.' We've always been in constant communication and that's one of the best things about being in the same place for such a long time. You build really strong relationships. As I said, he's like an uncle to me. We felt like this was the right time and we thought it was cool to be able to do it in October, which is Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
"The Cardinals have been great about early detection and really being proactive in the community amongst so many other things. We just felt like it was the right time. (Senior Vice President, Fan Engagement and Operations) Lisa Manning was very important in getting us across the finish line as well.”
Fitzgerald's mother passed due to breast cancer back in 2003, which has since led the perennial All-Star receiver to be heavily involved in raising awareness through his foundation alongside millions donated to the cause.
Week 7 fit Fitzgerald's calendar for a handful of reasons, which includes his son Devin — who plays football at Notre Dame. The Fighting Irish have a bye week this weekend.
"I mean, life is full. Chasing the kids around. Devin has the bye week. One of the reasons I picked this week is because Notre Dame is on the bye. (To) be able to have him here and to be able to be with Apollo and Milo, to be able to do it together, that's something that was really important," Fitzgerald continued. "Business is going well. Life is good. I feel like I've built a nice off ramp for myself."

title: Walter Nolen, Jeremiyah Love and More Cardinals Stars Miss Practice
full_text:
TEMPE — Things are not looking good for the Arizona Cardinals in the health department.
The likes of Walter Nolen III, Jeremiyah Love and Budda Baker were the biggest names absent from the Cardinals' Thursday practice. Arizona plays host to the Denver Broncos in Week 7.
Nolen (ankle), Love (ankle) and Baker (groin/illness) all have not practiced for two consecutive days now in the build-up to Sunday. Also not spotted at practice today was Andrew Wingard (knee) and Max Melton (knee) — Wingard was a DNP yesterday while Melton was limited on Wednesday.
Earlier today, CBS Sports reported that Love is not expected to play, which would mark a second consecutive game missed for the third overall pick. His current ankle injury has been managed the last few weeks and is different from the one that saw him miss the end of preseason play.
It's looking as if the Cardinals will again rely on Bam Knight, Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull against a stout Broncos defense.
Nolen's absence would be massive in the trenches, as the second-year defensive lineman was starting to come into his own, playing a big part in helping Arizona control the line of scrimmage and get after the quarterback.
In terms of ceiling and potential, Nolen's is by far the highest out of anybody along the Cardinals' defensive line. Missing him against a struggling Broncos offense would be huge.
Baker's absence would leave an obvious hole in the team's secondary in terms of both talent and game-planning. After a rough start, Baker's quickly turned the corner and has pieced together a strong overall 2026 campaign.
"There's just certain things where if you can try to get him to the point of attack on each play, like you got to do it, just because he makes those plays," Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis told reporters on Baker.
"He puts people in negatives. He creates negative plays, that's a thing week to week is like where can we get Budda around the ball without being obvious?"
The Cardinals, sitting at 2-4, are hoping to string together consecutive wins for the first time all season when Denver comes to State Farm Stadium.
The official practice report will drop later today, but from a health perspective, things do not look good for Arizona.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur will meet with reporters on Friday morning, where he'll likely verify who is in and out for the weekend.

title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update for Cardinals-Broncos is Disappointing
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals aren't expected to have running back Jeremiyah Love available for their Week 7 tilt against the Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
Love is dealing with an ankle injury and missed last week's matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. He didn't practice on Wednesday and now isn't probable to play against Denver:
The current expectation is that the #Cardinals will be without standout rookie running back Jeremiyah Love this week against the #Broncos , sources tell @CBSSports . Love (ankle) missed last week’s game vs. the Rams. Now expected to be out this week too. pic.twitter.com/2rmINyQrKC
“Yes, he’s feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying. (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%," LaFleur said of Love this week.
The Cardinals are likely to lean on Bam Knight and Tyler Allgeier once again. The duo helped revamp Arizona's rushing attack last week. It was particularly Knight who tallied 80 yards on the ground with a 31-yard splash play to ignite the Cardinals' offense.
“Not shocking. He’s a stud. He’s a tough dude. He’s a tough tackle. I’ve seen it in a green jersey over in New York and then got to see it obviously yesterday. He ran hard," LaFleur said of Knight when speaking with reporters on Monday.
"I thought the guys did great job. I thought everyone was connected. We have a lot to clean up in the run game. Obviously, we hit some of those ‘G series’ like you’re talking about right there, but we have a lot to clean up with our downhill direct runs, but they still were getting dirty two (and) three-yard runs when it wasn’t necessarily executed.”
Love, the third overall pick in this past draft, has been incredibly exciting when healthy and on the field. However, he's been dealing with multiple ankle injuries since the preseason, which has limited his role in Arizona's offense and impact to begin his rookie campaign.

title: Cardinals Linked to 3 Different QBs in Latest NFL Mock Drafts
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-4 to begin the first six weeks of the season — which is on the lower end of a top ten pick and not quite bad enough for a top five spot.
The Cardinals are heavily believed to be eying a quarterback if they will indeed pick that high, even with third-round pick Carson Beck currently on the roster. Arizona is expected to play Beck this season before exploring options in 2027.
As it stands, three recent mock drafts all had the Cardinals plucking quarterbacks from the draft order:
Gilberto Manzano : "I think Carr might be the fourth-best quarterback in this year’s class because he doesn’t stand out physically with average size (6'2", 215 pounds) and arm strength. But scouts consider him the safest QB option because of how well he reads defenses. Coach Mike LaFleur just spent three seasons working with Rams coach Sean McVay, who values accuracy and high-level decision making before and after the snap.
"Carr, who has completed 66.8% of his passes for 1,639 yards, 16 touchdowns and only one interception, could hit the ground running and run LaFleur’s scheme efficiently."
Field Yates : "The Cardinals made enough of an investment in Carson Beck this April (65th overall) to suggest he could be the long-term starter, but I'm not sold on that being the case. Enter the dynamic Chambliss, who makes up for below-average size (6-foot, 205 pounds) with playmaking, clutch production, experience and craftiness.
"No quarterback in this class has played better in big games than Chambliss, who averaged 307 passing yards and accounted for six touchdowns in three College Football Playoff games last season. He has led Ole Miss to three wins over AP Top 25 teams in 2026."
Josh Edwards: "Saturday was hardly Austin Simmons' best day of the season, but he is a big quarterback with a strong arm. He operates in the pocket well and has thrown with great touch and anticipation. Thinking back to last season, it was a tale of two seasons for Ty Simpson , who was taken No. 13 overall by the Rams. The first half of the year was excellent, but the second half of the season was very much impacted by injury. All it takes is one team to believe in the talent, but Simpson's stock was on the ropes."

title: Cardinals Claim Panthers OL Off Waivers
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have claimed former Carolina Panthers offensive tackle Albert Reese IV, the team officially announced.
More on Reese from the team's official press release:
"Reese (6-7, 325) entered the NFL with Carolina in May as an undrafted rookie free agent from Mississippi State and was inactive for each of the Panthers first five games this season. A native of Edmonton, Alberta, Reese played 49 games (22 starts) at tackle over five seasons (2021-25) at Mississippi State. He started all nine games played in 2025 and started all 12 games in 2024 and won the Kent Hull Trophy as the best offensive lineman in Mississippi."
Reese was just waived earlier this week. Panthers OL Taylor Morton returned from injury, which prompted the move.
The Cardinals are currently down two starting offensive linemen due to injury while illness is spreading through the team, which has impacted new backup tackle Jedrick Wills according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
Arizona plays the Denver Broncos this week.
The Cardinals believe they got their rushing attack sorted last week after Bam Knight rushed for 80 yards, a much needed sign of life after Arizona's unit upfront struggled. To pair, the Cardinals' line didn't allow a single sack on Jacoby Brissett in Week 6.
"I do think in some aspects our run game has grown from a variation standpoint in terms of what we’re doing schematically and then how those guys are executing, but there are still aspects of our run game we need to improve," LaFleur told reporters today.
"I think the operation’s the one that is the biggest. There's no yards that go with operation in terms of what you guys can see, but we know that when we’re operating at the level that we’re capable of it does lead to yards, which leads to points, which leads to obviously the result that we’re all hunting up, so I'd say those two aspects."

title: Falcons Face Wounded 49ers Team Missing Key Weapons
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons (2-4) take on the San Francisco 49ers (6-0) this week at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Neither team has had a bye this season, and the injuries are starting to pile up.
The Falcons had 11 players listed as questionable on Friday's injury report , and they already ruled out linebacker Divine Deablo and nickel Billy Bowman Jr.
The 49ers are coming off a short week after their win over the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football, and they'll be without key offensive weapons against the Falcons .
San Francisco ruled out a pair of starting wide receivers in long-time Falcons nemesis Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel.
Evans leads the team with 420 receiving yards. Samuel is third on the team with 206 yards, and he's added 78 rushing yards on just nine carries.
Evans spent 12 years with the NFC South rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and he's had more than his share of success against the Falcons. In 21 games, he has 1,652 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns. He's only had more yards against the Carolina Panthers (1,760), but he's faced the Panthers 23 times. His per-game average against the Falcons is higher at 78.7 vs. 76.5.
He may be 33 years old, but he still went for six catches for 132 yards against the Falcons in December. It was the second-best game of his career against the Falcons, with his top game coming way back in 2016 when he had 150 yards and two touchdowns in a Buccaneers loss in Tampa.
With the Falcons having injuries at linebacker and nickel, missing Samuel comes as maybe even a bigger break. While he's listed as a wide receiver, he's built like a running back. He specializes in catching short passes and turning them into longer gains. He puts a lot of stress on the linebackers and nickelbacks of defenses.
The 49ers also list wide receiver Christian Kirk as questionable. With Brock Purdy playing the way he is, the 49ers still have Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, who leads the team with five touchdown receptions. The running back and tight end are still players who will stress the linebackers and nickelbacks of the Falcons.
Brandin Cooks is next on the depth chart behind Evans, but the 49ers may rely on more two-tight end sets on Sunday.
On the other side of the ball, starting safety Marques Sigle has been ruled out. He's only played in four of the team's six games, and he's still the fifth-leading tackler. The 49ers will rely even more heavily on All-World linebacker Fred Warner to try to contain Falcons' running back Bijan Robinson.
The game kicks off at Mercedes-Benz Stadium at 1:00 p.m. EST and will be televised on FOX.

title: Roddy White Stresses What Falcons Need from Michael Penix Jr. to Be Great
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has played like a franchise quarterback for large portions of this season. There's just one problem -- Penix hasn't been on the field enough.
That's what former Falcons wide receiver Roddy White argued when he discussed the status of the organization, especially, the team's quarterback position.
Penix is in his third season with the Falcons. Yet, he's started just 16 games. Penix missed 10 contests in 2025 and the beginning of this season because of a knee injury.
"As far as where our franchise is right now, we do need him to be available each and every week," said White while speaking to SI on Falcons at the the Chase for Business’ Make Your Move Summit in Atlanta this week. "It's been tough to deal with when he's not in there because the game plan, and the team, changes so much.
"Everyone in that locker room trusts and believes in him, and he gives us the best opportunity to win. We love it when he's out there, but he has to be out there to help us win and get some of these W's in these close games that we've been playing up to this point."
Penix's injury past was a storyline for the quarterback before he came to Atlanta. The signal-caller went through multiple knee and shoulder injuries during his extensive college career.
Then, during his first full year as an NFL starter, Penix partially tore his left ACL. The injury sidelined him until Week 3 of this season.
He's started every game since then. So on one hand, the Penix critics about his injury past should be more silent. But in Week 5 against the Baltimore Ravens, Penix exited late in the fourth quarter with a rib injury. Penix missed overtime, which ended in a loss for Atlanta.
"Those are the times that you need your quarterback to come through and make plays for you so you can win those," added White.
The former Falcons wideout used Drake London as an example for how different the Falcons offense is with and without Penix.
When Penix has started this season, London, who White called one of the best receivers in the league, has averaged 40 receiving yards per game. When Penix starts, London is posting 117.5 receiving yards per contest.
White spoke with media while partnering with Chase Bank to help entrepreneurs in the Southeast this past week. At the summit from Oct. 20-22, small-business owners from the Atlanta area and the surrounding states gathered to network and learn from Chase Bank the best practices for beginning a small business.
The former Falcons receiver is a small business owner himself. He owns a construction company that focuses on building single-family houses, small developments and commercial real estate. The company primarily works in Atlanta but also sometimes in North and South Carolina.
"A lot of us just out here communicating, doing business with each other,  learning from each other, helping each other along the way.," said White at the summit. "Chase helps us navigate through the business space, as far as what directions to go in, what people you need to talk to for banking situations and how you can build your business on a week to week, month to month, year to year basis.
"This is an opportunity to also come in and learn from each other and also just communicate within the structure of a business and have fun with each other and learn from each other."
More than 1,000 small-business owners gathered at the summit. All types of different industries were represented.
White started his business after 11 seasons with the Falcons from 2005-15. The receiver registered six consecutive 1,100-yard campaigns from 2007-12. He also earned four straight trips to the Pro Bowl from 2008-11 and made first-team All-Pro in 2010.
White remains the all-time Falcons leader in receiving touchdowns. White is also second on the team's receptions and receiving yards list behind only Julio Jones.

title: Falcons' Lengthy Injury Report Raises Questions Before 49ers Game
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons will enter Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers with a lot of questions surrounding their roster availability, as four players have been ruled out and 10 others are listed as questionable.
Running back Brian Robinson Jr., linebacker Divine Deablo, defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. and offensive tackle Michael Jerrell will miss Sunday's contest.
The extensive injury report could force Atlanta to make adjustments on both sides of the ball as it prepares for a challenging matchup.
Robinson's absence was one of the more notable developments on Atlanta's final injury report. The running back was limited during Wednesday's practice before missing Thursday and Friday, ultimately being ruled out for Sunday's game.
With Robinson unavailable, the Falcons will need additional contributions from their remaining running backs. Stefanski confirmed that Khalil Herbert, who is currently on the practice squad, will serve as the backup.
Atlanta will likely elevate Herbert from the practice squad for the 49ers matchup. Robinson's absence could also affect how the Falcons distribute carries and handle passing downs against San Francisco's defense.
Deablo's absence could create another challenge for Atlanta's defense, particularly with rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels also dealing with an injury.
Daniels offered an encouraging update on his condition , saying he "feels good." His availability remains important as the Falcons determine their linebacker rotation and who will handle defensive communication duties.
If Daniels is active, he could be a candidate to wear the green dot which he has done in games this season. Harold Perkins Jr. and Josh Woods are other potential options if Daniels cannot play.
Whoever assumes that responsibility will need to help keep Atlanta organized against a San Francisco offense that uses motion and varied personnel groupings to create favorable matchups.
The Falcons also received a positive update regarding cornerback A.J. Terrell, who is working his way back from a groin injury.
Stefanski said he thought Terrell "looks better," suggesting the cornerback has made progress during the week. Terrell's potential return would provide a boost to a secondary that will be without Bowman and could have other defensive backs unavailable.
Terrell's status is especially important against San Francisco, given the uncertainty surrounding Atlanta's cornerback depth.
Several other players remain questionable, including defensive linemen Samson Ebukam and Za'Darius Smith, defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. and defensive backs C.J. Henderson and Avieon Terrell. Their availability could influence Atlanta's defensive rotations and personnel packages.
Stefanski noted that San Francisco is dealing with similar week to week challenges, making preparation and roster flexibility important components of Sunday's matchup.
The Falcons must now wait for the final availability decisions before determining their game day personnel. Robinson's absence is confirmed, while Terrell's potential return and Daniels' status remain important storylines to monitor.
Atlanta will look to overcome those personnel challenges when it hosts San Francisco on Sunday, with the outcome potentially hinting on how effectively its available players handle expanded responsibilities.

title: Kyle Pitts Sr. Showing Why Atlanta Falcons Must Get Him More Involved
full_text:
Kyle Pitts Sr.’s volatile usage in the Atlanta Falcons offense has been a recurring topic since the franchise invested the 2021 fourth overall NFL Draft pick in the tight end out of Florida.
“We want to get him the ball,” Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said of the 6-foot-6, 250-pound target. “He’s one of our best players on the team.”
Through six games, Pitts has 15 catches for 169 yards and three touchdowns. According to Pro Football Focus , he is also second in the NFL in yards after catch per reception, averaging 7.5
“I think he’s at his best when he has the ball in his hands in open space,” Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees discussed Pitts. “Kyle’s shown that throughout his entire career, he’s certainly shown that over the last few weeks. It’s our job to put him in a position to have those plays.”
He had his best game of the season as Atlanta turned to him when its offense was spiraling in its 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears .
“For us to reach out full potential, he’s got to be a big part of that,” Rees said.
The Falcons’ potent rushing attack, led by Bijan Robinson , was neutralized, and the pass game wasn’t picking up much traction either.
Trailing 31-7, the Falcons attempted to make a fourth-quarter comeback.
The unit began finding a rhythm. Pitts was at the forefront, finishing with a team-high five receptions and two touchdowns on a 60-yard output.
“Just going out there and trying to play as fast as I can, and be an asset to this offense any way I can,” Pitts told reporters after the game. “And being there for Mike and the rest of this offense.
During the offseason, Atlanta made the 26-year-old Pitts the third-highest-paid NFL tight end , inking a three-year, $54 million extension with $36 million guaranteed .
However, his performance hasn’t matched his play at times. But it’s not all Pitts’ fault.
Through the first three weeks of the season, the opening two of those being quarterbacked by the now-cut Cooper Rush , Pitts had just three targets.
Since Week 4, Pitts’ opportunities have increased. He has 13 receptions on 16 targets.
And Penix wants to remind people that Atlanta’s pass attack isn’t a one-trick pony, “ Drake London’s somewhere down there somewhere” type of attack.
“Whenever KP is open, I’m not just looking past him,” Penix said. “So that whole narrative is crazy, especially with him being the person I’ve spent the most time with since I’ve been here. So for people to say I don’t think about Kyle, I only think about Drake, it’s like this is somebody I was with every day in the offseason.”
The Falcons (2-4) next host the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers (6-0) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium this Sunday. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. on FOX.
Atlanta looks for a statement that would end a two-game skid and keep them in striking distance of the NFC South divisional race.

title: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert
full_text:
Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster.
The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta.
San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons.
If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener.
Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie.
Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization.
The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September.
Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure.
The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad .
Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay.
For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender.
Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two.
Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen.

title: Falcons OC Tommy Rees Takes Blame for Offense's Slow Starts
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees is taking responsibility for the offense’s slow starts as the team prepares to face the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
The Falcons have struggled to find an offensive rhythm over their last two games, putting themselves in difficult situations and making it harder to maintain their offensive identity. Rees acknowledged that the early struggles have become a significant concern and emphasized that improving the offense starts with him.
“Last week we did not have great success early down. It’s such a key because you keep the team on balance,” Rees said. “It opens up so much more of the call sheet.”
Atlanta’s recent performances highlight the problem.
Against the Baltimore Ravens, the Falcons managed just three points in the first quarter before taking a 14-9 lead into halftime. Atlanta ultimately fell in overtime after struggling to sustain its offensive production. The following week against the Chicago Bears , the Falcons fell behind 14- 0 before finding the end zone. Atlanta eventually trailed 31-7 before scoring twice in the fourth quarter, but still lost 31-23.
The slow starts have forced Atlanta to play from behind, creating challenges for an offense that wants to establish its running game and maintain balance.
“Us starting slow, us having drives that fell out early in the game, early in a drive - that’s on me. It’s not on them. I got to put them in the right position to have success,” Rees said.
To get back on the right track, Rees wants to emphasize the fundamentals that have driven Atlanta's offensive success. That simply includes establishing Bijan Robinson early and creating opportunities for quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to operate within a balanced attack.
“There’s always calls you want back,” Rees said. “We know our identity. We know what we’ve been good at, and we’ve played good offensive football. It starts with the run game.”
Instead, the coaching staff must find ways to keep its best players involved regardless of the game situation.
“You can’t abandon your identity,” Rees said. “You’ve got to find other ways to keep your best players involved. You got to find ways to highlight what you do well.”
That approach will be tested against San Francisco, which Rees described as aggressive.
“They play great team football. Play great team defense,” Rees said. “They rally to the football. They populate the ball, then bog you down in space.”
For Atlanta, the priority is clear. The Falcons must execute better on early downs, establish the run, and avoid digging themselves into another early deficit.
Rees knows those improvements begin with his own decisions. Against the 49ers, he will have an opportunity to show that accountability can lead to a faster start and a more consistent offensive performance.

title: Falcons Release DB as A.J. Terrell's Return Gets Closer
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have released cornerback Malcolm DeWalt IV, potentially creating an opportunity for the team to adjust its secondary ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers.
DeWalt entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent following the 2026 NFL Draft. Although he did not arrive with the same recognition as some of his fellow rookies, the 24-year-old quickly caught Atlanta’s attention with his athleticism, length and potential to develop into a dependable defensive back.
Standing 6’2 and weighing 190 pounds, DeWalt possesses the physical tools teams look for in an outside cornerback. His collegiate career included stops at Snow College, Butte College and Akron, where he continued developing his coverage skills before getting his opportunity at the professional level.
DeWalt made the most of that opportunity during the offseason. He impressed during rookie minicamp and carried that momentum into training camp and the preseason, earning a spot on Atlanta’s initial 53-man roster.
However, DeWalt did not record any defensive statistics during the 2026 regular season. His release could mean another roster change for a Falcons team
The timing of DeWalt’s release is particularly noteworthy because Atlanta is working toward getting its top cornerback back on the field.
The Falcons designated A.J. Terrell to return from injured reserve on Wednesday, opening a 21-day window for the veteran to practice and potentially return to game action. Terrell has missed the previous four games with a groin injury suffered against the Carolina Panthers in Week 2.
His potential return against San Francisco would provide a significant boost to a secondary that has dealt with injuries at cornerback. C.J. Henderson has also been sidelined, forcing Atlanta to rely on younger options, including Avieon Terrell.
Although the Falcons have not confirmed that DeWalt’s release is directly connected to A.J. Terrell’s possible return, the timing makes it a reasonable possibility as the team evaluates its roster needs.
Atlanta could also bring DeWalt back to its practice squad if he clears waivers. That would allow the organization to continue developing a young cornerback who showed promise throughout the offseason without immediately occupying a spot on the active roster.
For DeWalt, the release does not necessarily mean his time with Atlanta is over. For the Falcons, the move could provide additional flexibility as they prepare for San Francisco and work to strengthen their secondary for the remainder of the season.

title: Brock Purdy Has a Skill That Could Give Falcons Fits
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – One week after struggling against Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears' passing attack, the Atlanta Falcons face another difficult test Sunday against Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers.
Kyle Shanahan is widely regarded as one of the NFL's great offensive minds, and he deserves a lot of praise, but his quarterback does, too. Brock Purdy has been outstanding this season, throwing for 1,460 yards and 14 touchdowns to just two interceptions. Of the quarterbacks who have played six games this season, none have a better completion percentage (69.6%), passer rating (118.1), or EPA per dropback (+0.30).
Purdy thrives on quick processing, accuracy, and consistently making the right decision within Shanahan's offense.
That might not generate the same national buzz as the highlight-reel plays of some of the league's other star quarterbacks, but the results are hard to argue with. The Falcons know where San Francisco's offense starts: with its quarterback.
"He's a very, very special quarterback," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. "I haven't studied the rest of the league – and I'm watching a lot of his tape right now, but it's hard to imagine someone who is playing the position better than he is right now."
Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson can overwhelm defenses with their physical gifts, while Patrick Mahomes can turn broken plays into something extraordinary. Purdy has the traits that a Shanahan offense values most.
"He's an elite processor. You see how quickly he gets through his progressions," Stefanski explained. "He has elite accuracy. And I think he's an elite scrambler. I think he's the best or one of the best off-schedule quarterbacks playing right now.
"You watch him – he's a smart scrambler. He's looking to pass. And then when he runs, he can score from 50 yards out, as he's done. So just very, very smart. Hard to get on the ground. This is a great player."
After being picked apart by Caleb Williams and the Bears , Atlanta's secondary faces another major test against Purdy.
The potential return of veteran cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson would provide a welcome boost. Still, the Falcons will need more than healthier personnel to slow an offense built on quick decisions, accurate throws, and the ability to punish defenses when coverage breaks down.
If the Falcons’ secondary returns to health and the front seven can consistently pressure Purdy’s quick release, they can slow this potent offense. If Sunday looks anything like last week against Chicago, with coverage breakdowns and a clean pocket, Shanahan will make them pay for every mistake. Purdy doesn’t need many.

title: Jahan Dotson Making His Case for Bigger Role in Falcons Offense
full_text:
Jahan Dotson is quietly emerging as a reliable weapon in the Atlanta Falcons ' passing game, and his recent production suggests he could be in line for a bigger role as the season progresses.
Dotson delivered one of his most productive performances of the season Sunday, catching three passes for a team-high 87 yards and a touchdown. The 87-yard performance marked the fourth-highest receiving total of his five-year career, highlighting the big-play ability he has brought to Atlanta's offense.
More importantly, Sunday's performance was not an isolated showing. Dotson has recorded at least 50 receiving yards in each of the last three weeks, making him one of just seven NFL players to reach that mark in every game during that stretch through the early afternoon slate of Week 6.
His recent consistency is particularly encouraging considering his relatively modest target volume. According to Next Gen Stats , Dotson owns a 14.2% target share, the third-highest mark among Falcons receivers, while his 34.6% air yards share ranks second on the team and among the top 20 players in the NFL.
Those numbers show Dotson is making the most of his opportunities while serving as an important downfield option for Atlanta. Although he has not received the same volume of targets as some of the team's other playmakers, his ability to generate yardage has helped him establish a place in the passing game.
Following the Falcons' game against Pittsburgh, Dotson said he spoke with former Atlanta quarterback Matt Ryan. Dotson also explained that his approach remains centered on doing his job.
"For me, it's about getting open and being available to the quarterback. Whether I'm getting the ball or not," Dotson said.
That mentality has allowed Dotson to remain productive without needing a high volume of targets. His recent performances have also showcased the confidence he has in his ability to make difficult catches.
His back shoulder touchdown reception on Sunday was a prime example.
Jahan Dotson WHAT A CATCH CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Bl2VvmwJmQ
"I have always had this in his bag," Dotson said, referring to the back shoulder catch. He also recalled the challenge of proving that ability on the field. "He had to go out and show them," Dotson said.
While the touchdown added to his recent scoring production, Dotson made it clear that he values consistent yardage just as much as finding the end zone.
"I'm a big yards guy. Touchdowns are cool. But I like yards," Dotson said.
For Atlanta, that approach could be particularly valuable as the offense looks for more consistent production from its supporting receivers.
Dotson still has to sustain his production to earn a more prominent role, but his recent numbers make a strong case for continued involvement. If he maintains his current trajectory, the Falcons could have another dependable receiving option capable of taking pressure off their top targets.

title: Top Four Reasons The Bengals Could Beat The Ravens Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens used to be one of the best home teams in the NFL.
Sunday will be a difficult test for rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who is once again juggling unusual personnel situations and tricky injury situations including starting quarterback Lamar Jackson, who is questionable with an ankle injury and made progress this week but perhaps not enough to play. The Bengals are fresh off a bye and in considerably better health. Jackson has owned them with an 11-2 record while averaging 29 points per game, but the Bengals offense has also had some legendary days at Baltimore’s expense and Minter’s defense was quite shaky in critical areas through the first third of the season.
These are the top four reasons the Bengals could win Sunday and push the Ravens down in the AFC North standings:
Even if Jackson plays, he has barely practiced for three weeks since suffering the injury, he has never worked much at all with new center Cam Jurgens at all (more on that in a minute) and his legs have been a huge part of his success against Cincy. Jackson has 837 rushing yards against them; most of any QB against any NFL team, but how much of that will be in the cards even if Jackson does suit up?
Rookie play caller Declan Doyle, coming off his worst performance as an offensive coordinator, has been hesitant to lean into designed runs and RPOs and Jackson’s legs have not been as much of a weapon since 2024, honestly. The Bengals also fortified their defensive line in a major way, they are holding opposing passers to the same rating Baltimore’s vaunted secondary is (87.0) and it certainly looks like this will be a situation where Jackson will have to feel out his ankle though the game.
That’s enough to sway the margins with two teams this well matched.
“I don't feel like I have to be 100%,” Jackson said on Friday about being able to play. “If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But (if) I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all.”
The Bengals have arguably the deepest and most impactful rotation of defensive tackles in the NFL right now and it goes way beyond just offseason-acquisition Dexter Lawrence . They are leading the NFL in sacks and pressures from that position and Jurgens has only had really two full workdays on the job in practice and that was somewhat split between two QBS.
Jurgens has not played center with any consistency in quite some time, moving to guard with the Eagles, he was playing poorly for Philadelphia and may have been on the cusp of being benched before the trade, he barely knows the offense and his teammates and he just came out of concussion protocol. If that seems like a lot, that’s because it is.
This will be the Ravens fifth offensive line combination in seven weeks and there is little interior cohesion and it’s been a problem all season. Not sure Jurgens fixes it right away against Sexy Dexy and this bunch and Lawrence knows him well from his time with the Giants battling Jurgens in the NFC East.
The Ravens are a joke in the fourth quarter, and they continue to set records for choking away double-digits leads and have blown three already this season and lost two of those games. With 16 losses in games where they lead by 10 or more since 2019, and having just done it again last week in Cleveland, this might be the Bengals catching them in a vulnerable moment.
None of the Ravens’ corners has been any good in the second half of games and top receivers have gutted them to the point it might need to be addressed before the trade deadline and its left hybrid safety Kyle Hamilton exacerbated by it all. Minter has tried to explain it away at times (I know a corner I would be trying to trade away ) but their late-game mental breakdowns are real and this team lacks the clutch gene and Joe Burrow has it and it might come down to the final possession. (Oh, and Bengals receiver Ja’Marr Chase has done things to the Ravens no WR has done to any other team in league history).
Former Bengal Trey Hendrickson may need to take this game over in a revenge spot; Baltimore is bottom seven in the NFL in fourth-quarter pressure rate and sack rate, while the Bengals are number one and it’s not even close with a 50% pressure rate and sublime 18.5% sack rate in the final quarter.
Baltimore’s choking is most acute at home. The Ravens recently had a five-game losing streak at home and they snapped it Week 4 against the Titans, but again failed to score in the second half of that game after Jackson went down and allowed Tennessee to hang around.
Kicker Tyer Loop hasn’t been great anywhere but has really struggled at home since the preseason and now he has competition back in the building. The Ravens seem incapable of putting forth a pure, focused four-quarter game at home and that might be what it takes to beat a talented Bengals squad.
Burrow is just 2-4 at Baltimore, so the Ravens do have that going for them, but he won at M&T Bank Stadium last year and two of those losses came when mastermind Mike Macdonald was running the Baltimore defense.

title: Ravens Final Week 7 Injury Report Reveals Major Change for Lamar Jackson
full_text:
After taking the practice field for the first time since suffering what he revealed was a high ankle sprain during his Friday media availability, Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was one of five players given a designation on the team's final injury report .
Fortunately for them, he joined defensive tackle Broderick Washington in being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday in a massively important Week 7 AFC North showdown.
Game status vs. Bengals pic.twitter.com/bJIL9hngwi
"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson said. "If it feels better tomorrow, we'll know tomorrow. So I can't call it. I just have a grace period until Sunday."
While seeing the two-time league MVP on the practice field all week was a welcome sight, it was still on a limited basis. However, head coach Jesse Minter shared that Jackson "was able to get a pretty good amount of work in" Friday's practice session.
"Between Lamar and our staff and us [coaches], it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective and things like that it can be," Minter said. "He's had a good couple days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours.
Minter had already ruled out veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins with a knee injury that will keep him sidelined for multiple games, and he also ruled out fourth-year outside linebacker Tavius Robinson with what he revealed was a season-ending pectoral injury. This leaves the Ravens without one of their three starting safeties and their sack leader through the first six weeks with 3.5 .
The only other player given a final designation was third-year cornerback T.J. Tampa, who is listed as doubtful to play with a knee injury, as remains on injured reserve but returned to practice for the first time this week in a limited capacity.
The team's media podium might as well have been a ballroom floor with all the dancing around the question of whether Jackson or primary backup Tyler Huntley would be starting against the Bengals this week.
Usually, only the head coach and starting quarterback step to the podium to address the media on the Friday before upcoming games, which had been Huntley the previous two weeks and Jackson the four weeks before.
This time around, the Ravens had both quarterbacks speak after practice, and neither confirmed or denied who would and wouldn't start on Sunday, although Huntley expressed that he'd be ready to make his third straight start and 19th of his career if called upon.
"I just got to be ready to play Sunday if that's the case," Huntley said. Once we get to Sunday, we'll see."
The Ravens have posted 116 points, 14 touchdowns, 967 passing yards and 1,464 total yards in the 14 quarters with Jackson under center, and barely managed a third of those figures in the 10 quarters without him with 40 points, four touchdowns, 429 passing yards and 742 total yards.
While having the best dual-threat quarterback of all time back in the lineup would be a major boost not only for overall morale but also for the production and efficiency of the offense, Jackson doesn't want to be selfish by rushing back on the field if he can't be his usual dynamic and elusive self.
"I'm just trying to move how I move," Jackson said. "If I can't do that, I can't help my team. I can't put my team in a situation like that. I feel like I'm doing a disservice then."
The Bengals coaches were likely going to prepare to face either quarterback anyway. By having Jackson listed as questionable, which essentially equates to probable, and having him speak to the media in surprising depth about the nature and severity of his injury, they're giving their rivals a worst-case scenario for them to seriously consider coming to fruition on Saturday. Jackson as an 11-3 career record against the Bengals as a starter and was playing at an MVP level prior to suffering his injury.
"I don't feel like I have to be 100%.," Jackson said. "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But I'm restricted. Like, I can't do what I do. I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, [there's] no positives in that. That's not helping my team at all. I feel like I'm being selfish because it's about me at that point, you know, getting out there and be hurt. That's dumb."

title: Ravens Head Coach Explains Lamar Jackson's Status For Week 7
full_text:
Ravens head coach Jesse Minter did not make an announcements about quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status for Sunday’s critical game against the Bengals, but left the door open that he could return from an ankle injury.
Minter would not commit to how Jackson’s status would be reflected on the final injury report – questionable would seem to be the most likely designation – and said the next 48 hours will play a role in whether back-up Snoop Huntley makes his third straight start of if Jackson is able to start the game with Baltimore trying to avoid consecutive losses in the AFC North.
“He was able to get in the work he needed to get in to potentially have a shot to play,” Minter said of Jackson’s three straight days of limited work in practice but not full participation. Minter also revealed that emerging edge talent Tavius Robinson was lost for the season with a pectoral injury and veteran safety Jaylinn Hawkins will not play Sunday as he deals with an injury.
The Ravens continue to put clips of Jackson at practice on their social media; make of that what you will. Huntley and Jackson both met with the media Friday and Jackson revealed that he is dealing with a high-ankle sprain, which generally carry a longer recovery time. He was wearing a wrap on the ankle as he spoke for the first time since suffering the injury, calling it "very, very painful."
"I'm headed on the right direction, but I can't call it right now," Jackson said of his status.
Jackson was unable to take the practice field at all the last two weeks and made definite strides this week. Minter had referred to Jackson’s status as “day to day” for weeks but also ruled him out on the past two Fridays. This meeting with the media was quite different. Minter reiterated that the decision will be made in consultation with the doctors and the quarterback himself; Jackson is in the final guaranteed year of his contract and has more leverage over this franchise than any player in the league arguably has over any franchise.
“We’ll see how it goes in the next 48 hours,” Minter said, adding as to the timetable of a final determination on his playing status could “go as long as it needs to take.”
Minter was hesitant to speak at length on what Jackson was and was knot able to do during the three sessions he took part in, though video of the portions open to the media appeared to indicate him being less encumbered on Thursday than he had been on Wednesday. Minter said Jackson put in “a pretty good amount of work” on Friday.
Jackson has not played since the first half of Week 4’s victory over the Titans. He was in MVP form at the time but was caught from behind stepping up in the pocket and trying to scramble and has yet to take the field in a game since then. Huntley said he is operating as if he could be called on again Sunday.
“You just prepare to play and when it comes down to Sunday we’ll see,” Huntley said.
The Bengals are coming off a bye and have revamped their defensive front , and will provide a strong challenge. Newly acquired center Cam Jurgens will be making his debut with Baltimore after missing two games in the concussion protocol.
Baltimore's secondary was already struggling - again blowing 10 point leads and with one of the worst fourth-quarter defenses in the NFL- prior to Hawkins being ruled out. Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase has already set NFL records against the Ravens and Minter had better be ready to make some changes to his cornerback usage, especially if his defense will have to operate with a limited back-up QB.

title: Trenton Simpson Details Key To Breakout Campaign With Ravens
full_text:
In the modern NFL, a position with one of the steepest learning curves for players making the transition from college to the professional level is at off-ball linebacker.
Given the complexities and illusions thereof that offenses look to portray and display on a down-to-down basis with pre-snap motions and an emphasis on targeting the middle of the field in the passing game, becoming just a serviceable inside linebacker, let alone a good-to-above-average one, is harder than ever and takes time.
More often than not, it may take multiple seasons and some tough growing pains and learning lessons for a full maturation to take place and for a talented player at the position to begin realizing their full potential.
That was the career arc for Baltimore Ravens 2020 first-rounder Patrick Queen, who broke out in a big way in his fourth season, earning Pro Bowl and Second Team All Pro honors in 2023 before he departed for greener pastures in free agency the following offseason.
Three years later, his successor appears to be following in his footsteps. Through the first third of the final year of his rookie contract, 2023 third-rounder Trenton Simpson has had quite an impressive start to his breakout campaign .
Through six games, he is one of only two NFL defenders who have recorded 40-plus tackles, five-plus tackles for loss and an interception this season. The only other player to have reached such a notable feat is his teammate, three-time All Pro Kyle Hamilton.
Only two NFL defenders have each recorded 40+ tackles, 5+ TFL and an INT this season. Both play for the @Ravens : Kyle Hamilton and Trenton Simpson. pic.twitter.com/rGcFayw0iW
After opening each of the last two seasons at the starting WILL spot next to four-time Pro Bowl veteran Roquan Smith , only to get benched and replaced in the lineup, Simpson pointed to the different approach he took to his contract year as the primary reason for his breakout and why the game is finally starting to slow down for him.
"I come in every morning at 6 o'clock, [and] I meet with my linebacker coach," Simpson said. "[Also], my mentality [and] the way I'm playing is just no fear, one play at a time, [give] everything I've got [and] focus on my one key. When the ball is snapped, if I see something, trust it, go and just play like a Raven, hit anything that moves."
While most of the Ravens coaching staff was overhauled when former head coach John Harbaugh was fired after a massively disappointing 2025 season, one of the few holdovers that first-year head coach Jesse Minter retained was inside linebackers coach Tyler Santucci. This meant that Simpson would have the same position coach in back-to-back seasons for the first time in his career, which is clearly paying major dividends given all his success.
"Coming in early allows [me] to get extra two hours on film, taking care of my body [and] getting an extra lift a week," Simpson said. "I'd say [I'm focusing on] nutrition, getting massages now [and] becoming a real pro.
"All the linebackers come in early, but I think that's allowed all of us to play well together. It allows us to all see the things on the same page. Everybody's playing at a high level in that room. I think it's really working."
In addition to Santucci playing a major role, Simpson also credits the incredible example that Smith sets day in and day out as another invaluable asset in his continued development and maturation as a player.
"He showed me the way," Simpson said. "He's been an All-Pro player [and] he's one of the best at it. [I've been] seeing what he's done over these last four years and [I'm] trying to translate it to my game because I've noticed playing beside him [that] he's so ahead before the ball even snaps.
"I think this year that's what coming in and watching more film has allowed me to do. If I see a formation, it's like, 'It's only going to be one or two things.' Then, once you see it, you just go."
Given Simpson's age, having just turned 25 this past summer, and the upward trajectory that he is currently on, he's a prime candidate for an in-season early contract extension . In the past, as recently as last year with nose tackle Travis Jones, the Ravens have had no problem locking in young rising stars in the midst of or heading toward breakouts.
Of the three remaining members of the team's 2023 NFL Draft class playing in the final year of their rookie deals, both Simpson and fourth-round edge rusher Tavius Robinson have shown that they're worthy of being extended. However, Simpson is more likely to agree to an early deal, since Robinson leads the team in sacks and plays a premium position that teams across the league would pay much more for if he reaches, or even comes close to, double-digit sacks this year.
Simpson has expressed that he wants to remain with the Ravens for the long haul on numerous occasions, including most recently on an episode of 'The Lounge' podcast earlier this week.
"I want to send a message to this organization like, y'all drafted me four years ago, and I want to prove to y'all that I want to be here and be a Raven for the rest of my career," Simpson said. "I know going out to practice every day and playing with my hair on fire in games, that'll make that happen."
Since Minter's variation of the Ravens scheme has helped unlock his full potential, Simpson might be compelled to want to stick around that much more at a reasonable price, if it means he can keep playing alongside Smith, whose play and impact were negatively affected following Queen's departure. By not letting this homegrown ascending talent walk, they could very well wind up having the best off-ball linebacker tandem once again.

title: The Ravens Must Explore These 3 Options To Fix Their Cornerback Problem
full_text:
The Ravens’ secondary is a primary concern.
Rookie head coach Jesse Minter can try to downplay it at times, and talk around it, but the fact that he is flooding the field with more defensive backs than anyone in the AFC  (in dime coverage 33% of the time, nearly twice as much as anyone in his conference) with not much to show for it has to be grating on him. Hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton, playing more linebacker now, has been the voice of reason, calling out this group for not playing to its standard, and this better get cleaned up quickly.
The Ravens get Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow off a bye on Sunday then it’s Josh Allen off a bye in Buffalo and Trevor Lawrence, Bryce Young and CJ Stroud are all in good form and looming. The schedule is about to get very real, and the Ravens need to get more out of their cornerbacks in particular. And Minter knows it.
“I think every week we're chasing certain things,” Minter said on Wednesday. “Really, after the Dallas game, I didn't think we – as much as their weapons were what they were – I really didn't think we played the run that well and played blocks and played really physically. I thought going into that next game we really improved in that area. Then it was obviously third down, and we're chasing improvement in that area.
“So, I think there's a lot of things that the guys are getting more in tune with each other, with how we play, physicality, being able to stop the run and the different coverages that we try to play. But there's always a million things that we're chasing, and it's no different this week. But I do see – I've told the defense now for a few weeks in a row, you see improvement. We're not anywhere where we want to be, but I see us getting better. And to Kyle's point, let's just keep chasing improvement every single day."
Minter needs to consider these measures to try to fix his secondary and especially to cull more impact from his corners , which has been a specialty of his throughout his career. This should be the progression:
Ravens GM Eric DeCosta has been whispering about his good this kid is for years and bragging to the local media – barely covertly, I guess – about how other teams covet him and want him in trade . Well, your team’s corners are allowing a bottom-10 passer rating and have combined for a handful of pass breakups and no picks despite being thrown on more in the fourth quarter than anyone else.
So now that Tampa is coming back from his latest injury setback, let’s get him on the field and give him a real runway. Not just a handful of dime snaps, but real stuff. Like starting outside corner stuff, because you need to fix your slot in the worst way possible , and Marlon Humphrey needs to try to earn his $19M there.
Young corners Keyon Martin and Chandler Rivers are allowing a passer rating of 119 in the slot and overall the numbers in the slot are brutal: 117.7 passer rating (27th) and 510 yards (27th). These elite QBs will shred them there and that’s where Humphrey needs to be (and if that doesn’t work just keep reading).
Minter doesn’t want to play veteran Chidobe Awuzie and hasn’t ever seemed to favor him, and it’s hard to see that changing with Tampa working back to the lineup. I like corner Amani Oruwariye and he has the long levers and body type that worked so well for Minter running his zone stuff with the Chargers.
He’s played in the league and played okay at times and has a skillset that would seem to lend itself to this scheme. This dude is 6-foot-2, 200 pounds. Probably worthy of a look-see if this team keeps blowing leads and getting torched by competent wide receivers. The Ravens also haven’t been tested by tight ends really yet but the propensity for that is increasing as soon as Sunday .
One could argue despite all the money and resources and former first-round picks at this position it is both the most underachieving and/or the biggest position of need on the roster. Yoi have to give to get and moving out Humphrey’s salary to create wiggle room to add wouldn’t be crazy.
The Ravens have the least cap space in the NFL, with limited options to restructure to add in a meaningful way, and addition by subtraction could be in order. The Chargers are a miserable 0-6, Minter knows their defensive backs incredibly well, and the Ravens and Chargers made a trade a year ago in which Minter turned benched first-round pick Odafe Oweh into a stud in LA.
Maybe he could do it again on Baltimore’s side this year, but it might require moving salary to create space, and specifically create space at corner.  I wouldn’t discount the idea and as longtime NFL personnel guy Pat Kirwan pointed out to me before the season the Ravens should be able to run a cheaper secondary with the scheme the star and not carrying bloated $20M contracts for allegedly top man-coverage guys who don’t pick the ball off.
