title: Panthers Fantasy Predictions: Where I Disagree With the Experts in Week 7
full_text:
It wasn't that long ago that starting multiple Panthers in fantasy football would've felt like a pretty big gamble. Five games into the season, that's starting to change.
Bryce Young is averaging 309.8 passing yards per game, Chuba Hubbard has rushed for 242 yards over the last two weeks and Jalen Coker came back against Philadelphia and immediately saw 13 targets. Tetairoa McMillan still finished with 86 receiving yards of his own, so Coker's return didn't exactly slow him down.
That's what makes Sunday's game against Tampa Bay interesting from a fantasy standpoint. Carolina suddenly has several guys you can feel pretty good about putting in your lineup.
I took a look at what the fantasy experts are projecting for some of Carolina's top players and compared those numbers with what I think we'll actually see Sunday. I'm pretty close on a couple of them, but there are a few spots where I'm going higher.
FantasyPros projection: 245.5 passing yards, 1.7 TDs, 0.7 INTs, 18.5 fantasy points
My projection: 275 passing yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 10 rushing yards
My fantasy projection: 18 points
FantasyPros and I end up in almost the exact same place on fantasy points. It's the passing yards where I have a hard time agreeing with them.
Young hasn't thrown for fewer than 281 yards in a game this season and is averaging 309.8 through five starts. I'm not saying he's going to throw for 300 every Sunday, but I'm also not ready to knock him all the way down into the 240s when we haven't seen anything close to that yet.
He completed only 20 of 39 passes against Philadelphia, and there were stretches where the offense couldn't get much going. Still, I thought Young played better against the Eagles than that completion percentage suggested , and he finished with 281 yards and two touchdowns.
Coker being back also gives me another reason to go higher on the yardage. He and McMillan combined for 22 targets and 183 yards against Philadelphia, and if Tampa Bay makes things difficult for Hubbard on the ground, Young may have to throw it quite a bit again. I'll take 275 yards and two touchdowns.
Expert projection: Around 6 catches for 73 yards
My projection: 6 catches, 85 yards, 1 TD
My fantasy projection: 14.5 standard | 20.5 PPR
Coker might be my favorite Panthers fantasy play this week. He hadn't played since Week 2, came back against Philadelphia and Young threw his way 13 times. He caught six of them for 97 yards, including a 32-yard catch on third-and-9 that helped keep Carolina's 94-yard touchdown drive alive.
That's why I'm willing to go a little higher than the experts. Carolina didn't spend much time easing Coker back into things, and Young clearly had no problem going right back to him.
The touchdown is where I'm taking a chance. He didn't get one against Philadelphia, but if the targets are anywhere close to what we saw last week, I like his chances of getting one Sunday. Six catches for 85 yards isn't that far from what the experts are expecting, but the touchdown would turn it into a pretty big fantasy day.
Expert projection: Around 6 catches for 72 yards and a TD
My projection: 7 catches, 90 yards
My fantasy projection: 9 standard | 16 PPR
I was curious to see what Coker's return would do to McMillan's numbers. McMillan had become Young's clear No. 1 receiver while Coker was out, so it made sense to wonder if some of those targets would disappear.
At least against Philadelphia, they didn't. McMillan still saw nine targets and caught six passes for 86 yards, while Coker had 13 targets and 97 yards. There was plenty to go around for both of them.
That's why I'm going a little higher on McMillan's yardage. He already has 471 yards through five games, so putting him around 90 against Tampa Bay doesn't feel like much of a stretch.
Where I'm going the other way is the touchdown. The expert projection gives him one and mine doesn't, which is a pretty big difference in a standard league. In PPR, I feel better about McMillan because I think the catches will be there, and if he does get into the end zone, I'll gladly be too low.
Expert projection: Around 14-15 PPR points
My projection: 19 carries, 78 yards; 3 catches, 22 yards
My fantasy projection: 10 standard | 13 PPR
If I were only looking at what Hubbard has done the last two weeks, I'd probably put another 100-yard rushing game next to his name and move on. He ran for 122 yards against New Orleans and followed it with 120 against Philadelphia, where Carolina gave him 28 carries.
Tampa Bay is what makes me back off a little. It's a tougher matchup on the ground, and I think there's a good chance Carolina has more success getting the ball to Young, Coker and McMillan than trying to run Hubbard into a tough front all afternoon.
That doesn't mean Hubbard won't get his touches. Carolina has shown it'll stick with him, and his work in the passing game gives him a little more value in PPR. I'm putting him right around 100 total yards and leaving off the touchdown, which puts me a little below the expert projections.
Of course, if Carolina gets down around the goal line and Hubbard punches one in, that changes things in a hurry.
If I'm picking one based strictly on fantasy value this week, give me Coker. Young might be the safer play, McMillan has been the more consistent receiver and Hubbard has spent the last two weeks running through people, but those 13 targets in Coker's first game back are hard for me to ignore.
What I really liked was that McMillan still got nine targets of his own. Maybe instead of Coker taking opportunities away from McMillan, we're starting to see what Young can do when he finally has both of them on the field.
That's probably the bigger fantasy story with this offense. Young is averaging more than 300 yards passing, Carolina just had two receivers go over 85 yards in the same game and Hubbard has back-to-back 100-yard rushing games.
Panthers players aren't just desperation fantasy starts anymore. I'm going a little higher than the experts on Coker and McMillan this week, and we'll see Sunday if they make me look smart.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Rejuvenated Panthers' RB Chuba Hubbard Has Recaptured His 2024 Form
full_text:
He was a fourth-round pick in 2021 from Oklahoma State University. Running back Chuba Hubbard was the 126th overall pick in that draft by the Carolina Panthers. In three of his first four NFL seasons, he was the team’s top ground gainer.
That fourth year saw him total career highs in attempts (250), rushing yards (1,195), receptions (43), yards from scrimmage (1,366), and total touchdowns (11), despite missing the final two games of the season. Furthermore, the team inked him to a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension in the midst of what would be his best season to date.
Then came 2025, and Panthers’ general manager Dan Morgan wanted to add a little experienced depth to the backfield. Carolina inked running back Rico Dowdle, a 1,079-yard rusher with the Dallas Cowboys in 2024, to a one-year deal. Hubbard would start the team’s first six games but a calf injury opened the door for Dowdle, who finished the season with 1,076 on the ground and six scores.
Once healthy, Hubbard became a bigger factor later in the season. In the 34-31 playoff loss to the Los Angeles Rams, he totaled 13 carries for 46 yards and a pair of touchdowns.
This offseason, Dowdle took the free-agent highway to Pittsburgh. The Panthers still had oft-injured Jonathon Brooks and 2025 fourth-round pick Trevor Etienne, while Morgan added AJ Dillon in free agency. And they still had Hubbard, who has really come on strong in the team’s last two outings.
Panthers RB Chubba Hubbard Week 6 🏈 28 CAR 🏈 120 YDS 🏈 1 TD Panthers defeat the Eagles 25-14 pic.twitter.com/laajx6putG
The 27-year-old pro has started all five contests this season, and his carries have increased on a game-by-game basis. He began 2026 with 10 carries for 49 yards and one TD in the Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
His breakout game this season came on Sunday night against the Detroit Lions, totaling 20 attempts for 122 yards and two touchdowns in a 32-26 win. The Panthers returned to the field last Sunday and Hubbard racked up 28 carries for 120 yards and one score in the 24-15 victory at Philadelphia.
Per @NextGenStats : Chuba Hubbard was hit behind the line of scrimmage on 17 of his carries but gained 56 yards on those runs. Bully. pic.twitter.com/C1qEGQaHgd
The six-year pro suddenly ranks 10th in the NFL with 426 rushing yards. Meanwhile, Hubbard leads Carolina in total yards from scrimmage (511) and total touchdowns (6). And it’s also worth a mention that the 6’1”, 210-pound performer now ranks fourth in Panthers’ history in rushing yards (4,112) behind only Jonathan Stewart (7,318), DeAngelo Williams (6,846), and Cam Newton (5,036).
Head coach Dave Canales's and play-caller Brad Idzik’s offense is looking very balanced these days, and Hubbard’s bounce back season is becoming a huge factor as 2026 unfolds.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: A Win Isn't Enough: 4 Things Panthers Need to Show Against Buccaneers
full_text:
Obviously, the first thing I want to see Sunday is a Panthers win. Carolina is 3-2, has won three of its last four and has a chance to move to 4-2 against Tampa Bay.
But we're past the point where that's the only thing I'm watching.
The Panthers have looked like a different team over the last month, and now I want to see if some of this stuff is going to stick. Was the run defense the last two weeks for real? Can the offense keep rolling now that Jalen Coker is back? And please, can we get through a game without 149 yards in penalties?
Here are four things I'll be watching Sunday besides the final score.
I'm not ready to say it is, but I'm definitely more interested in this conversation than I was a couple of weeks ago.
Carolina held Philadelphia to 35 rushing yards Sunday and has now held back-to-back opponents under 50 yards on the ground. That's a pretty big turnaround for a defense that is still allowing 5.12 yards per carry on the season.
Now let's see them do it again.
Bucky Irving is exactly the kind of back who can tell us whether we're looking at real improvement or just a couple of good weeks. He ran for 165 yards against Dallas earlier this season and has already gone over 100 yards twice against Carolina in his career.
I'm not asking the Panthers to hold him to 35 yards. Keep him from controlling the game, don't start giving up five or six yards every time Tampa Bay hands him the ball and make the Buccaneers beat you some other way. Do that again Sunday and I'll feel a whole lot better about where this run defense is headed.
I don't need to see Bryce Young throw for 300 yards every week. I do want Carolina to keep trusting the version of Young we've watched through the first five games.
He's averaging 309.8 passing yards per game and threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns against Philadelphia. The completion percentage wasn't pretty, but I thought Young played better against the Eagles than his 20-of-39 line suggested .
We also finally got Coker and Tetairoa McMillan on the field together, and I want to see more of that. Coker had 97 yards in his return, McMillan had 86 and suddenly Young has a couple of guys on the outside who can make things happen.
Tampa Bay is good against the run, so there may be stretches Sunday where Young has to carry the offense. Fine by me. If it's working, don't get cute.
Thirteen penalties for 149 yards. I still don't know how Carolina won that game.
The Panthers had eight penalties for 105 yards in the first half alone against Philadelphia. They had returns wiped out, kept putting themselves in bad situations and spent a good chunk of the afternoon making things much harder than they needed to be.
I wrote after the game that Carolina finally won the kind of game it usually finds a way to lose , and that's one of the reasons I came away encouraged. But let's not make winning that way a habit.
There are going to be penalties Sunday, and I'm not expecting perfection. Just don't make me watch another game where I'm checking for a flag every time somebody makes a big play.
Tampa Bay is 1-5. Carolina is 3-2, has won three of its last four and gets this game at home. That doesn't guarantee anything, especially against a division opponent, but I think we're past the point where we should be looking at a game like this and wondering if the Panthers are good enough to win it.
The Buccaneers have been competitive despite their record, and I'm certainly not treating this like some automatic win. Baker Mayfield practiced in full Wednesday and Thursday as he works his way back from a thumb injury, so Tampa Bay could have him back under center Sunday. Even if rookie Jalon Daniels gets another start, this is still a division game against a team that has given Carolina plenty of problems over the years.
If we're going to talk about the Panthers as a possible playoff team and a contender in the NFC South, games like this come with that conversation. They don't have to beat Tampa Bay by three touchdowns, and I'm not expecting them to play perfect football. Just take care of the ball, stop beating yourselves and don't spend the afternoon giving a 1-5 team chance after chance to stay in the game.
We've spent enough years watching the Panthers play down to teams they should beat. Carolina has spent the last month giving us reasons to believe this team might actually be different, and Sunday is another chance to show it.
Go play like the better team.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: NFL Analyst Makes Bold Dave Canales Claim Panthers Fans Have Waited Years to Hear
full_text:
For most of Dave Canales' time in Carolina, the conversation has been about what the Panthers might eventually become. There have been good stretches, some bad ones and plenty of weeks where we were left wondering whether this thing was actually headed in the right direction.
We're finally getting an answer.
NFL.com's Nick Shook has the Panthers at No. 13 in his latest power rankings, but what he said about Canales and the Panthers stood out more to me than the ranking itself. Shook called Carolina more consistent than it has ever been under Canales and said the Panthers look like a playoff team. He also said he's very optimistic about Carolina's chances of winning the NFC South.
That's not something we've heard much around here lately, but I'm starting to understand why he's saying it.
Carolina is 3-2 and has won three of its last four games. Bryce Young is playing the best football of his career, Chuba Hubbard just ran for 120 yards in Philadelphia, and the Panthers finally have Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan healthy and on the field together.
The defense is doing its part, too. Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards in Sunday's 25-14 win and has now held back-to-back opponents under 50 rushing yards. There are still things that need to be cleaned up, but we're seeing this team play well in more than one area at the same time.
That hasn't always been the case under Canales. There have been games when the offense looked good and the defense couldn't get a stop, or the defense kept Carolina in it while the offense couldn't do much with the opportunity. We're seeing a more complete team now.
I'm not saying Canales suddenly has everything figured out. I gave him a B for the win in Philadelphia , and I still think that's about right. Carolina committed 13 penalties for a franchise-record 149 yards, and letting the clock run out at the end of the first half with three timeouts is still a decision I don't understand.
But there's a difference between questioning some of the decisions Canales makes on Sundays and questioning whether the Panthers are actually getting better under him. I'm having a much harder time questioning the second one.
The Panthers have given us good stretches before, only to turn around and look like a completely different team the next week. That's probably why I'm still a little hesitant to go as far as Shook and call Carolina a playoff team after five games.
Sunday in Philadelphia moved me a little closer, though. The Panthers made a mess of things and still found a way to win , which is something we haven't seen nearly enough around here. They overcame 149 penalty yards, got the running game going when they needed it and finished the game instead of giving Philadelphia another chance to steal it.
Tampa Bay comes to Charlotte on Sunday with first place in the NFC South on the line. If Carolina wins again and moves to 4-2, we're probably going to have to look at this team a little differently.
That's why I think Shook's comments are worth paying attention to. Calling Carolina consistent and talking about the Panthers as a playoff team would've sounded pretty wild not that long ago.
It doesn't sound nearly as wild anymore.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: 3 Bold Predictions for Panthers' Important Matchup with Buccaneers
full_text:
Coming off an impressive road win against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6, the Carolina Panthers are back at home, at Bank of America Stadium, welcoming the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Tampa Bay's season is already on life support, 1-5 to start, with little to no room for error. Injuries have also plagued the Buccaneers, as starting QB Baker Mayfield has been out with a thumb injury.
However, Mayfield is trending towards returning against Carolina, as the Panthers' defense deals with injuries all over the field.
With Mayfield back and the Buccaneers coming into Charlotte in last place in the NFC South , they're going to play desperate. Carolina won't have it easy regardless of what Tampa Bay's record is coming in.
Here are three bold predictions for Buccaneers at Panthers on Sunday.
Will Lee III has been up and down since taking on an elevated role, with both Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn out due to injury. Last week, with the Devonta Smith assignment, Lee had some really good reps, not allowing Smith to make a catch, but he also got mossed on a 19-yard touchdown.
Against the Cleveland Browns in Week 3, Lee should've had a pick six, but couldn't secure the ball. There's clearly talent in Carolina's fourth-round rookie; it just has to show more consistently.
Playing against Mayfield, who hasn't played since Week 3, Lee will make multiple big plays in this game. Mayfield wasn't balling out before the injury either, so it's not absurd to say turnovers are still on the board even with his return.
Bryce Young isn't a Lamar Jackson or Josh Allen threat with his legs, but he can be effective in scramble situations. That scenario could very well play out here. While Tampa Bay's defensive line is very good against the run, the pass rush has been awful.
That said, the Buccaneers haven't allowed a single rushing touchdown by a QB this season. That changes on Sunday. In the red zone, Young can find room to scramble to the outside and dive toward the pylon for a touchdown.
While Tampa Bay has lost all but one game this season, it has turned multiple games into ugly rock fights. Even with Carolina's offense being as good as it has been, the Panthers have already had an ugly offensive game against the Browns, so theres evidence that the offense can be limited.
Both teams will turn the ball over. The Buccaneers' run defense is great, and Carolina's is improving from the embarrassing Week 1 showing. It's also just a division game; these games can get weird. Carolina should be able to limit Tampa's pass game, even with Mayfield back.
While it may be a frustrating game to watch, Carolina should still have all the tools to come out with a victory.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Panthers Crack the NFL's Top 10 — And It's Getting Harder to Call It Crazy
full_text:
The Panthers are 3-2, have won three of their last four and just left Philadelphia with a 25-14 win. Apparently, that's enough for at least one national writer to put Carolina among the 10 best teams in football.
USA TODAY's Nate Davis has the Panthers at No. 10 in his latest NFL power rankings. Davis focused on what Bryce Young has done through five games , and it's easy to see why.
Young is averaging 309.8 passing yards per game, which leads the NFL, and he's coming off another solid performance against the Eagles. He finished with 281 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in a game Carolina controlled for most of the afternoon.
So is No. 10 too high? I think it probably is, at least for now. But I don't think it's nearly as ridiculous as it would've sounded when the season started.
The Panthers have played five games and won three of them. They've also won three of their last four, and I'm starting to think this might be more than just a good stretch.
A lot of that starts with Young. He has thrown for 1,549 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games, while Carolina's 146 points are the most the franchise has ever scored through the first five games of a season.
The encouraging part is that it hasn't just been Young carrying everything. Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards Sunday, Jalen Coker returned with 97 receiving yards and Tetairoa McMillan added 86.
We've been waiting to see what this offense would look like once Coker and McMillan were on the field together. Sunday gave us our first real look , and I liked what I saw.
The defense did its part, too. Philadelphia finished with only 222 total yards and 35 on the ground, and the Panthers have now held an opponent under 50 rushing yards in back-to-back games.
Put all of that together and I don't have much trouble saying Carolina is a good football team right now. Putting the Panthers among the 10 best teams in the league is where I'm not quite there yet.
I'm not going to ignore who Philadelphia was missing Sunday. Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley didn't play, and the Eagles were also without their top three running backs. If we're going to use that win as the reason for moving Carolina this high, that has to be part of the conversation.
The 13 penalties for 149 yards bother me, too. Carolina had eight for 105 yards in the first half alone, and against a healthier offense, that probably gets you beat.
At the same time, I'm not going to knock the Panthers for winning a game they were supposed to win. We've watched this team do the opposite plenty of times.
That's why Sunday's win felt a little different . Carolina made enough mistakes to give Philadelphia chances to hang around, but instead of finding a way to give the game away, the Panthers finished it.
If I were doing my own power rankings today, I'd probably have Carolina around 12 or 13. That feels about right to me. The Panthers have shown enough that putting them in the top half of the league shouldn't be controversial anymore, but I need another win or two before I'm putting them in the top 10.
Tampa Bay comes to Charlotte on Sunday with first place in the NFC South on the line. If Carolina beats the Buccaneers and moves to 4-2, I'll have a much harder time arguing with Davis next week.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. title: 1 Realistic Trade Deadline Move the Panthers Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are, with the trade deadline inching closer, in a great position. They are so far the class of the NFC South, and they have some holes on the roster that present an opportunity for addition.
Last year, the Panthers didn't let success change their plans, but this year might be different. They are defending a title now, and they face a difficult schedule. With other NFC South teams struggling, it's the perfect time to make a move to go for it.
They're not going to complete a blockbuster because it's not necessary nor is it Dan Morgan's style. So don't expect a Saquon Barkley or Brian Thomas Jr. sort of move. But there is one simple, moderately cheap move the Panthers have to make as soon as possible.
The Panthers currently need cornerback help. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson won't be back for at least a few more weeks. Carolina has survived thus far, but they can't keep trotting Akayleb Evans and Will Lee III, who is improving, out there.
Yes, Horn and Jackson will be back eventually. But over the next six weeks, the Panthers face some tough passing offenses. Is Dan Morgan willing to risk facing Lamar Jackson, Jordan Love, and Tyler Shough with backups?
The Panthers' defense was at its best when it was flexible with inside and outside cornerbacks, so even when Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson return, the Panthers need depth. What if one of their injuries flares up?
So, the Panthers should trade for Alontae Taylor. He's primarily a slot corner, but the Panthers can, like the Tennessee Titans have, move him around. With him and Horn, they can switch in and out of the slot for the best matchups. It would give Ejiro Evero a ton of flexibility.
As ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted, there is a cost involved. He's on a three-year deal for $58 million. That's not cheap. The Panthers don't exactly have the salary cap to bring that on without some major concessions.
"Perhaps a new team could rework that money on a new deal while asking Tennessee to front some of the bill in exchange for a quality pick," Fowler wrote.
While it's not in Morgan's style to send over quality picks in deals, the Panthers could find a common ground for Taylor, who was benched by the Titans last time out. If ever a player was in need of a change of scenery, it's him.
And the Panthers are a drastic change of scenery from the Titans. So, from a player-fit perspective, it works really well. The Panthers have draft capital to work with, and they need the help. Imagine being able to send Taylor, Horn, Jackson, and Lee out there at various points for various looks.
It's a defensive coordinator's dream. Make it happen, Panthers.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: The Panthers Have a Serious Conundrum Up Front
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are just five games into their 2026 season, and this certainly looks like a different team on both sides of the ball than a year ago. The offense is humming and looks balanced with quarterback Bryce Young playing the best football of his young career, and running back Chuba Hubbard regaining his standout form from 2024.
Defensively, the team has overcome a very rough start on opening week against the Bears and has settled in nicely. The club is still missing the cornerback tandem of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson and is getting contributions from its younger players.
Still, one aspect of Dave Canales’s club that has been dealing with adversity dating all the way back to January is the offensive line. You will recall that starting left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon early in last season’s playoff lost to the Rams.
That forced Panthers general manager, Dan Morgan to make some big decisions. He plucked starting left tackle Rasheed Walker from the Green Bay Packers via a one year contract. He then used the 19th overall selection in April’s draft to select University of Georgia standout Monroe Freeling.
Then came June when mainstay right tackle Taylor Moton was diagnosed with blood clots in his lung. That put Walker at left tackle and Freeling on the right side to start the season. Last Sunday, Freeling was dealing with a knee injury suffered against the Lions in Week 4 and was inactive at Philadelphia last Sunday. Enter the 10-year pro, who took the field for the first time in 2026.
Pro Football Focus’ Gordon McGuinness came out with his updated offensive line rankings this week. Despite a 25-14 road win over the Birds, the Panthers’ front slipped from one spot from 25th to 26th. McGuinness took some time to mention the big change for Carolina up front.
“Right tackle Taylor Moton returned to the lineup for the first time this season, securing a 63.5 PFF pass-blocking grade and permitting a pair of pressures from 46 pass-blocking snaps in the win over the Philadelphia Eagles…”
Now comes a Sunday showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A season ago, Canales’s team unseated the Bucs as NFC South champions. It’s been a struggle for Todd Bowles’s club early in 2026 as the team is off to a 1-5 start. However, veteran signal-caller Baker Mayfield could make his return after missinng the last three games with a thumb issue.
Back to the Panthers. Freeling remains on the mend, but spoke this week about what he’s learned from a pro who’s made 130 starts (including playoffs) in 10 seasons.
#Panthers tackle Monroe Freeling is focused on getting better at his craft and getting healthy. But he’s learned a lot from Taylor Moton. A fun story about a rookie learning from a vet here: pic.twitter.com/gsMESjZKZH
If Moton remains healthy, it’s hard to fathom that Freeling will be back at right tackle anytime soon. And that may not be such a bad thing.
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Panthers Could Face a Tough Trade Decision With One Surprising Starter
full_text:
The Panthers are 3-2, so most of the talk around the trade deadline has been about who Dan Morgan could bring to Carolina. After the last few years, it's a nice change to actually be talking about adding players instead of wondering who might be headed out.
I recently looked at five realistic trade targets Carolina could pursue before the deadline , but that doesn't mean Morgan won't listen if somebody calls about one of his guys.
Bobby Brown III is a name I wouldn't have thought much about a few weeks ago. He's playing, he's been good up front and Carolina isn't exactly in a position where it needs to start getting rid of defensive linemen. Still, I can see why another team would call.
That's the difference between Brown and some of the more obvious names Carolina could move. If you're trading somebody who barely plays, you're probably not getting much in return.
Brown has generated seven pressures this season and has been a solid part of Carolina's defensive line. He's also under contract through 2027 after signing a three-year, $21 million deal with the Panthers.
An October look at Carolina's possible trade chips even pointed to Brown as the player who might bring back the best return. That doesn't mean Morgan is shopping him, because there's been no indication that's happening. But I could see a team looking for help up front calling Carolina and asking what it would take.
The Panthers have some options around him, too. They used a second-round pick on Lee Hunter, traded a 2028 sixth-round pick for TeRah Edwards before the season and now have Tershawn Wharton back.
That doesn't suddenly make Brown expendable. We've already seen enough injuries this season to know how quickly depth can disappear, and Morgan made it pretty clear before the season that having enough bodies up front mattered to him.
There's also the money. Brown is under contract for next season, but his cap number climbs to around $9.8 million in 2027. Carolina doesn't have to do anything about that now, but it's at least something to think about if another team comes calling with a good offer.
This is where I'd have a hard time actually pulling the trigger. The Panthers aren't 1-4 and looking toward next season. They're 3-2 and have a real chance to play meaningful football over the next couple of months.
We just watched Carolina find a way to win the kind of game it usually loses in Philadelphia. Trading a starting defensive lineman who's helping you win doesn't make much sense unless you're getting something worthwhile back.
Carolina has spent too much time trying to build depth up front to turn around and give some of it away for a late pick. If somebody calls and offers a sixth-rounder, I'm keeping Brown. I'd rather have him for the rest of this season, especially with Carolina right in the middle of the division race.
But if a team trying to make a run gets desperate for defensive-line help and offers Morgan something he wasn't expecting, I'd listen. Maybe that offer never comes, and that's fine. Brown is still a player who can help Carolina right now.
That's really what makes his name interesting around the deadline. He's not somebody Carolina needs to trade, and I don't think the Panthers should be calling around trying to move him. He's good enough, though, that another team might be the one making the call.
If that happens, I'd hear them out.
It just better be a pretty good offer.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Panthers Should Be Willing to Pay Proposed Trade Cost for Eagles Defender
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline just 19 days away and after a 3-2 start to the season, the Carolina Panthers could be buyers. No, a deadline deal won't be some blockbuster move for one of the league's biggest stars, but adding an instant starter who may need a fresh start is always on the table.
Carolina has a decent cushion at the top of the NFC South and already has a road division win against the Atlanta Falcons. There's clear belief in the building that another playoff push is imminent, so theres no reason Carolina can't buy into this season even more than they did in the offseason.
As for what area needs to be addressed, it's certainly not the offense, which currently ranks second in the NFL in yards per game. Bryce Young leads the NFL in passing yards per game , being the only QB to post over 300 per game.
That leaves the defense, which has been solid since the Week 1 disaster against the Chicago Bears, but with one clear area of vulnerability: cornerback . With Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn both out for an extended time, the Panthers could trade for a Super Bowl champion.
Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox dropped his trade block board entering Week 7 of the NFL season. On that list of potential trade candidates, Eagles CB Riq Woolen appeared as a possible trade piece, given where the Eagles stand right now.
Coming off a home loss to the Panthers, the Eagles are 2-4 and just one game ahead of last place in the NFC East. Philadelphia will be without its starting QB, Jalen Hurts, for the rest of the season as he deals with blood clots.
Along with Hurts' season being cut short, the entire offense has dealt with adversity. The offensive line is a complete shell of what it used to be, riddled with injuries and an in-season retirement from Lane Johnson.
Star RB Saquon Barkley has missed two games due to a hamstring injury, but is trending towards returning. The season just isn't at all what the Eagles planned for, and with long-term questions surrounding the QB, the Eagles could be sellers and load up on as much draft compensation as possible.
Woolen, fresh off the Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl 60 victory, signed a one-year deal with the Eagles in free agency. Being on an expiring contract, and not being outstanding thus far in Philly, won't command too steep of a price.
In Knox's analysis of Woolen's trade value, he landed on a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick. Carolina doesn't own a fifth-round pick in 2027, but they do own two fourth-round picks.
The Panthers can send Philadelphia the Vikings' fourth-round pick, which was acquired in a trade that sent Adam Thielen back to Minnesota.
This gives Philadelphia another draft pick in a season when they might be more focused on the draft than on winning games, and Carolina a bona fide starter at secondary next to Will Lee III.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Caleb Williams, Kyler Gordon, Colston Loveland Troll Dave Portnoy After Bears Beat Patriots
full_text:
There are few bigger trolls on the internet than Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy, so it was funny to see him get a taste of his own medicine from Caleb Williams, Colston Loveland and Kyler Gordon.
Portnoy had a lot to say about Williams after he went down with a hamstring injury in Week 2 before it was later discovered that the Bears quarterback had a more serious issue than initially thought.
Rest assured, Williams saw Portnoy mocking him, so he took the opportunity to troll Portnoy after the Bears beat his favorite team , the New England Patriots, in Week 7.
On Instagram, Williams reposted a social media post of Portnoy's that included a photo of a handful of Barstool analysts picking the Bears to beat the Patriots. Portnoy had also included several eye emojis.
"On to the next," Williams wrote in the caption of the post.
FETISH ALERT 🚨     See you in Feb @CALEBcsw pic.twitter.com/lRIzAFfT9n
It's pretty comical that Portnoy would accuse Williams of having a fetish considering he takes every chance he gets to knock Williams, but I digress
Of course, this isn't the first time Portnoy and Williams have had a back-and-forth.
As we mentioned, Portnoy mocked Williams after his hamstring injury, as did the rest of the internet , and Williams later fired back at him with a repost on social media that basically accused Portnoy of being soft.
Portnoy then knocked Williams for not divulging more about his injury when Williams first addressed the media during the week the Bears quarterback returned to the field.
Bears players weren't done there.
Gordon and Loveland did a pizza review after the game, which was a clear troll of Portnoy and the countless pizza reviews he has done over the years.
It was pretty well done, except they forgot the score.
Bears players Kyler Gordon and Colston Loveland dropped a pizza review after last night’s win We cannot confirm or deny if they were trolling any Patriots fans that do pizza reviews pic.twitter.com/6Og9saWd8Q
The Bears have struggled mightily to beat the Patriots over the years, and that was the case for a lot of teams during the Tom Brady era.
Before their win on Thursday night, the Bears had lost six of their last seven against New England, with the last win coming in 2022.
However, with that win and the one in Week 7, the Bears are starting to flip the script and have now won two of three.
Barring a meeting in the Super Bowl, this will be the last time these two teams square off until at least 2028, as New England is not on Chicago's schedule next season .
In 2028, the Bears are slated to face one AFC East opponent, but who that is will depend upon where the Bears finish in the division.

title: Bears' Power Couple Rushes in to Take Credit for Late-Game Poor Decisions
full_text:
It's endearing, even heart warming.
The Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams relationship gets tighter by the day, and a good example is what happened at the end of Thursday night's 30-24 Bears win over the New England Patriots.
It seems, the coach is falling on the grenade for the quarterback, who in turn has been doing it for his coach at times. It's truly a selfless approach they're working toward, but maybe it's better if it's not necessary.
Johnson seemed to do this on Friday when he had his day-after press conference. The subject was the way Williams took a 10-yard sack on third-and-5 from the Patriots' 30-yard line with 1:39 left to play and the Bears up only 27-21.
The play left the ball back where Cairo Santos would need to make a team-record and career-long 58-yard field goal to lock away the victory, rather than the 48-yarder he would have had if they just downed the ball at the line of scrimmage.
What was Caleb Williams thinking here?? You can NOT take a sack in this situation. An insanely dumb and costly mistake 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/igHC0vFttZ
After the game, Williams came up with an explanation that was anything but suitable.
“I didn't know how far it was," Williams said. "I know I took the sack. We're going to go back and look at that.
"I thought I could take the sack in that situation, keep the clock going, or maybe make them use their last timeout. But in that situation, we'll go back and look at it. I'll learn from it if we get in that situation again."
He did everything except say the sun got in his eyes.
Ben Johnson made 3 bad calls that could cost them the game: 1. Accepted the defensive penalty: bad clock management. 2. Let Caleb take a sack which almost took them out of FG range. 3. Opted to take a chance on a very long FG. Imagine if the FG was missed. https://t.co/hA6OgsKNxH
Asked about it on Friday, Johnson stood up for his QB and fell on that grenade.
"I didn’t do a good enough job communicating to him in that situation," Johnson said. "I have to do a better job letting him know that it’s more important. The yards are more important for us in that spot than the clock running or burning timeouts on the opposition or anything of that nature. So 100% on me."
It's hard to believe Williams wouldn't know this.
The timeout situation Williams spoke of was going to occur no matter what happened, unless there was an incomplete pass. And that's what made Johnson's play call terrible, anyway.
The primary goal then is to force the Patriots to call that timeout and make it a shorter field goal. It should have meant keeping the ball on the ground and letting the clock run. Just getting a short gain even without the first down could have made it a 43-yard or 44-yard field goal, and that's an easy ask for most kickers except maybe former Bears kicker Cody Parkey.
Here’s a look at that all-important sack on third down. Absolutely brutal situational work from Caleb Williams. Cannnnnnnot take a sack here. pic.twitter.com/mFexZJVqRG
They keep it on the ground and they also make New England use its last timeout. Even if the kick fails from the 38-yard line, the Patriots still needed to go 62 yards in about 90 seconds without a timeout. It's not impossible, but definitely unlikely unless the Bears defense treats a play like they did at the end of the first half with that 48-yard dump-off throw to back Rhamondre Stevenson breaking for a TD.
There's enough blame for both here. The fact they were even considering a pass is on Johnson. Taking the sack is on Williams. So both are at fault.
Johnson is always going to be a daring coach. It's what the Bears fans love about him and what gave him a reputation around the league. But a daring play in that instance is about the worst thing they could do. A 5-yard pass isn't impossible but is no guarantee.
The Bears are doing well on third-and-5 situations, at 57.1% (8 of 14). Still, it's not a guarantee and an incompletion stops the clock. If the field goal misses, then New England is at its 38 fully armed with a timeout. Everyone saw before halftime how quickly New England could strike against poor tackling on Rhamondre Stevenson's TD.
RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️ 📺 Prime Video pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW
As for Williams, he needs to be smarter than a 10-yard sack. Even if he does take the sack, going backwards 10 yards isn't helping his kicker. It doesn't take AI or a chart or analytics to know this.
He took a similar sack against the Lions in Detroit in 2024 while Johnson was Detroit's offensive coordinator. The clock wasn't stopped and time elapsed on an incompletion. The circumstances were a bit different but the end result of the sack was the same. They couldn't take the sack.
Both Johnson and Williams deserve blame for nearly botching the game-clinching situation. Johnson needs to be less of a gambler in that spot and Williams smarter. Put it this way: There's more brains available to be shared by both.
Falling on the grenade for each other might be cute but it's better when there's no explosion set to occur, and in this instance both had the chance to prevent it.
"You're watching the game and you go, 'Are either one of these teams capable of going to the Super Bowl?'" — DP recaps the Bears' win over the Patriots on TNF. pic.twitter.com/NUkYAS5L2d

title: Did Cole Kmet Play Final Game for Bears? Contract Decision Looms After Season-Ending Injury
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were dealt a devastating blow on Thursday night after tight end Cole Kmet went down with a knee injury.
Kmet suffered the injury in the fourth quarter of the game against the New England Patriots, and the cart had to be brought out, which was the first sign it was something significant.
Unfortunately, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that on Friday afternoon, revealing that Kmet has a season-ending knee injury. We're still waiting on the specifics of the issue, though.
"Bears TE Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season with a knee injury," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond relayed.
"He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s going to be sorely missed. He’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life. He’s a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. It does. I hate it for him," Johnson said.
There's a lot of time between now and next offseason, but it's very possible we might not see Kmet play another game with the Bears, which is the only team he has ever known in the NFL.
The former Bears second-round pick has one more year left on his current contract, but it also carries a cap hit of $15.4 million, which the Bears likely aren't going to be keen on keeping on the books, especially after drafting Colston Loveland and Sam Roush in consecutive years.
Kmet's 2027 cap hit went up after the team restructured his deal back in April, so it wasn't always that high.
There is a clear out in the deal, with the Bears being able to cut Kmet for a dead-money charge of $5.4 million and a savings of $10 million, according to Over The Cap .
One possible scenario is the Bears tight end accepts a re-work of his deal and takes a pay cut. We'd say that's more possible now that Kmet will be coming back from a significant injury, which figures to soften his market considerably if he hits free agency.
But a major factor in Kmet wanting to stay will be his role. Chicago might want to give Roush a push to a bigger role than the TE3 job he had before Kmet's injury, in which case Kmet would have to take a lesser role.
But, then again, the Bears run 12 and 13 personnel quite a bit, so there is ample room for Kmet to still see a lot of action, even if Roush's workload increases next season.
At this point, Kmet's chances of staying with the Bears are probably slightly better than 50/50.
The good news for him is that the injury occurred fairly early in the season, so Kmet has a good chance to be ready to roll by the time next season starts.

title: Why Bears May Not Need a Trade with Cole Kmet Going on Season-Ending IR
full_text:
Replacing injured tight end Cole Kmet is difficult for the Bears from a physical and emotional standpoint.
Kmet is being placed on season-ending injured reserve with his knee injury suffered Thursday, according to Ben Johnson in his Friday press conference.
They've often referred to Kmet as the heart of the team because he has been with the team the longest, plus he is a Chicago area native.
"He's Chicago. He's been here his whole life," Johnson said. "It stinks."
Someone must fill in and it would seem the Bears are unlikely to be looking to trade for a tight end, unless they can find one with all-purpose skills who is available for a late draft pick.
They do have Stephen Carlson available on the practice squad to move up and assist Colston Loveland and Sam Roush. They also have Qadir Ismail. Carlson would be an obvious choice for promotion and as an experienced NFL player who has been with the team for four years there would be no need for him to learn the offense.
"We've been very pleased with the improvement he's made over the first seven weeks," Johnson said of Roush.  "There's a high likelihood that his rep count is going to go up."
The 29-year-old former Browns tight end has been with the Bears, on the practice squad mostly, since May of 2023, but has never been targeted with a pass in the regular season. He has been in three Bears games, two last year and one in 2023. However, he played 25 games with seven starts and caught six passes for 62 yards with Cleveland in 2019 and 2020 after coming out of Princeton as an undrafted free agent.
Rookie Sam Roush had a rough day. Two drops and missed block on field goal. Too early to write him off yet. Posted a video that forgot about the earlier drop. Added here. pic.twitter.com/aMotjJ94S7
He's had 16 catches for 156 yards over the last four preseasons, so they know he has that ability to handle this end. The blocking might not be what they got from Kmet or either of the other two tight ends. Kmet had been enjoying a strong blocking season with Pro Football Focus grading him 14th among 124 tight ends in the league as a run blocker. Colston Loveland, who was strong as a rookie, hasn't been far behind Kmet as a run blocker in 28th of the 124.
Perhaps the suprising part of this for Bears fans who had been condemning Roush after his missed block on field goal unit may have cost them the Vikings game is the fact he is graded 21st out of 124 as a run blocker by PFF. So he's having an outstanding start as a blocker despite fan and media criticism. Much of the credit for getting these players working within the scheme must go to Jim Dray, their tight ends coach.
Ismail is more a receiving tight end who is 6-6, 232 pounds and almost the size of a wide receiver more than a tight end.
There is another option available on the practice squad injured list. Undrafted Iowa rookie Hayden Large is on the practice squad injured list after suffering what was called a core injury in training camp.
Whether he's healed from his is uncertain, but players on the practice squad injured list have been available for return to the practice squad or 53-man roster since 2022. They have the same rules as any other player. There would be a 21-day window to reinstate him. However, his injury status now isn't certain. Large made the practice squad mainly because of his blocking.
#Bears QB Tyson Bagent scrambles and makes a nice throw to TE Stephen Carlson. But after review, Carlson was out of bounds. pic.twitter.com/A7mGIXdslC
"There's a lot of solutions out there to make sure that we can still run the ball, pass-protect, and our route running I think we're still going to be OK," Johnson said. "I'm not discounting the impact of a guy like Cole has. Like I've said before, he's one of the glue guys with a huge amount of dependability from the coaching staff, from his teammates. We knew what we were going to get from that player every time he took the field and he was consistently one of the highest graded players on our offense week-in and week-out.
"He will be missed, no question about it. But in terms of what we do, it's not going to change a whole lot."
Johnson said this is an option for them but also mentioned the other practice squad tight ends as possibilities.
They also have tight end Nikola Kalinic on the practice squad injury list but he had a knee injury. Also, without making a trade they could claim James Mitchell from the Dallas practice squad. He made 13 catches, including a touchdown, for Detroit in three seasons under Johnson.
Carlson had shown promise in Cleveland but a knee injury had halted his career. Now, perhaps a knee injury is opening the way for him to contribute.
Still, with tight end being a position where injuries often occur because of the physicality and athleticism involved, and with some of their players at the position owning pasts involving injuries, they need to be looking on the waiver wire or even trade market to add more depth.
Whatever they do, Johnson again stressed they are not changing their offense without Kmet.
"We trained all of our tight ends to be able to do all of the jobs and so I don't really see us changing who we are or what we do as a result of that," Johnson said.
What a way to get your first catch of the season! Incredible TD grab from Stephen Carlson! (via @Browns ) pic.twitter.com/9fNdcu0xhD

title: Caleb Williams is Top 5, Shade for Josh Allen & More National Reactions to Bears QB's Ascension
full_text:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is becoming an elite player at the position right before our very eyes.
Through four contests, (he missed two due to a hamstring injury ), Williams looks like he is taking that next step in his third season, something we saw more evidence of on Thursday night against the New England Patriots .
Williams went on the national stage and looked phenomenal . He completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two scores, and he could've had more if not for a few dropped passes by his tight end, Colston Loveland. Williams didn't turn the ball over, either.
The former No. 1 overall pick has been sensational in three of the four games he has played, with the only exception being the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, which was played in terrible weather conditions.
At this rate, it looks like Mother Nature is the only thing that can slow Williams down.
ESPN analyst and former NFL defensive back Donte Whitner is ready to proclaim Williams a top-five quarterback, something he said on "Get Up!" on Friday.
"Last week, I made a statement that said that there were a lot of questions around Caleb Williams," he began. "Every question was answered for me last night. He threw for 308 passing yards, two touchdowns versus an elite New England Patriots defense."
"Caleb Williams is a top-five quarterback in the NFL today. And I'm going to tell you why," Whitner added. "Arm strength, elite. Ability to escape the pocket with speed, elite. The creativity is elite, but his No. 1 attribute is his elite football instincts. Caleb Williams has a sixth sense. He can sense the pressure without even seeing it. You can't coach that."
Inject all of that straight into our veins.
Even former NFL quarterback and fellow ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky had to admit he was wrong for saying the Bears should've drafted Jayden Daniels over Williams in 2024.
"I can sit here and tell everybody, I was probably the first person that was... I would take Jayden Daniels over Caleb Williams," Orlovsky said.
"This is not a slight on Jayden Daniels at all," he added. "Jayden Daniels, still a massive fan, I think he's going to be great as well. I was wrong on that thought (that Daniels is better than Williams)."
Orlovsky also called Williams "flawless" and said "you can not find better quarterback tape" than the Bears quarterbacks.
Kudos to Orlovsky, even though he tried to take a victory lap after the 2024 season when Daniels looked like the better quarterback. What a difference a few seasons can make.
Colin Cowherd got on FS1 on Friday and proclaimed Williams as the "most talented quarterback" in the NFL and compared him to Josh Allen, with one exception.
"Everybody is afraid to say it, I'm not. I think Caleb is the most talented quarterback in this league," Cowherd said .
"It’s like watching Josh Allen without the interceptions,” he added.
ESPN's Stephen A. Smith got in on the love train for Williams, saying he believes the Bears quarterback is going to lead the team to the Super Bowl in the next few years.
“I think that [Caleb Williams] is going to lead Chicago to a Super Bowl championship within the next two years," Stephen A. said .
We can go on and on, but you get the idea.
It's very clear the national media is giving Williams his flowers, and deservedly so.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Bears' Kyler Gordon Sets Lofty Sack Goal For 2026 Season
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came away with an impressive 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night.
The game featured elite performances by both quarterbacks, as Caleb Williams and Drake Maye combined for 629 passing yards and five TDs (although the latter did throw an ugly interception in the end zone). The Bears pressured Maye consistently, but he regularly evaded the extra rushers and found an open receiver.
The Bears did, however, bring him down for two sacks. One of them came via cornerback Kyler Gordon, who already has four over his first 48 snaps . He's proven to be the perfect weapon for Dennis Allen's hyper-aggressive scheme.
Aside from the sack, Gordon also pressured Maye on a few other plays in last night's contest. At first glance, he can often be mistaken for a defensive end (albeit a light one) blistering off the edge.
Apparently, he also wants to put up an edge rusher stat line this season.
Unsurprisingly, reporters from the Bears' beat swarmed Gordon in the postgame locker room. They asked him about his sack goal for the season. After some initial hesitancy, he didn't shy away from voicing his atmospheric objective.
"You want me to say that out loud? My goal is ten [sacks], but we're going to see" Gordon said. "DE numbers."
Defensive end numbers is right. No defensive back has ever finished a season with double-digit sacks. Seahawks safety Jamal Adams set the record with 9.5 sacks in the 2020 NFL season.
Despite missing the first four games, Gordon is already well on his way to making history for the cornerback position. Only 12 defensive backs have eclipsed six sacks in a season. Notably, all but two of them were safeties.
Every great defense needs a player that opposing offenses have to gameplan around. Over the first month of the season, the Bears didn't really have that . They've found it over the past two contests, though. Gordon is Chicago's defensive X-factor.
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen probably isn't surprised to see Gordon take the opportunity and run with it . The cover man was the only player Allen mentioned by name in his introductory press conference. At that time, he called Gordon an "outstanding nickel player" and said he had a vision for how to deploy him.
Now that he's finally healthy, we're seeing that promise come to fruition. It'll be up to Gordon to show how far he can take it.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Mike Vrabel Bluntly Explains How the Bears Beat His Patriots
full_text:
The Chicago Bears held on to defeat the New England Patriots 30-24 on Thursday Night Football. That final score doesn't necessarily paint the best picture for Chicago given how the game was progressing, but New England is the one that has to reconcile with the result.
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel recognized that the Bears are a strong opponent, but also conceded that his team didn't cover the basics, like tackling and situational execution in the red zone on both sides of the ball.
"It's a thin margin when you play good teams. We did some good things. But again, didn't do enough. We didn't get enough stops in the red zone and we didn't convert our red zone opportunity the one time," Vrabel said postgame .
Chicago linebacker D'Marco Jackson intercepted New England quarterback Drake Maye during the Patriots' failed red zone attempt. Maye scored on a seven-yard touchdown run during New England's only other red zone trip.
Unfortunately, Jackson was seen in a walking boot after the game.
Vrabel has plenty to worry about with his own team. Overall, though, there's probably more optimism to be had for the Patriots.
New England's defense was tested against an elite offense led by Caleb Williams (308 passing yards, two touchdown passes) and D'Andre Swift (78 rushing yards, one touchdown run). Still, the Bears' 405 total yards of offense is comparable to Chicago's 388.3 yards per game average through its first six games. Ben Johnson's offense was typically great, but not far ahead where it had been all season.
Vrabel should be overjoyed by how good his quarterback looked. By that same token, Ben Johnson should be less than enthused about Dennis Allen's defense's showing.
The Bears gave up two chunk plays in the two touchdown passes from Maye to Eli Raridon for 30 yards and Rhamondre Stevenson for 48 yards right before the half. Stevenson's touchdown was a checkdown that became an explosive touchdown run because of Jaylon Johnson's poor route to the ball and cornerback Kyler Gordon and safety Dillon Thieneman running into each other.
Coverage was a massive problem for Chicago all game. Enough to keep the coaching staff up at night, since it's now a trend.
It hasn't been long since this secondary was gashed up.
Two weeks ago, Green Bay Packers Jordan Love had 367 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and a 137.5 passer rating. Love completed 6-of-7 pass attempts over 20 yards for 258 yards during the 31-7 massacre at Lambeau Field .
Kyler Gordon's return has been a saving grace in the slot, but it's one step forward, two steps back with Malik Muhammad getting injured on the outside during Thursday Night Football.
Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson have been sore spots. You wonder if reinforcements is needed at the cornerback spot before the trade deadline passes.
Safety Cam Lewis didn't impress either, with serious struggles in blitz packages.
While the pass rush is banged up, the weakness is in the secondary. That's what'll undo any championship season in the Windy City this fall and winter.
Andrew Hughes is a freelance journalist based in Austin, Texas, who has bylines across ON SI and The Sporting News. His work has been featured in The Miami Herald, Bleacher Report, and Yahoo Sports. Andrew graduated from Brooklyn College with a degree in journalism in 2017 and has been a sports fan since 1993.

title: Chicago Bears Report Card for Week 7 Win: Stamp Them Contenders
full_text:
This one was all about trust.
Ben Johnson trusted kicker Cairo Santos to try a 58-yard field goal and risk the field position in the fourth quarter to get a nine-point lead, even after a miss off the right upright from 53 yards.
Caleb Williams trusted receivers Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland after a few misplays earlier in the game on big throws, and the results were first down conversions when the Bears needed them on huge third and fourth downs.
Johnson trusted Williams enough to keep throwing and to gamble on fourth downs when the running game was hit or miss on the night. He also trusted Joe Thuney to carry the ball, for some reason. But you get the idea.
"So, we believe in each other," Williams said. "Whenever anything happens, Cairo misses, cool. I’ve got your back, the defense has got your back. When maybe we don't score or put us in that situation, Cairo has our back."
This is genuinely one of the greatest throws I’ve ever seen dude Flat out ridiculous ball placement. Stupid arm arrogance lmaooooo. I can’t believe this is the QB for the Chicago Bears. Sick catch from Rome too https://t.co/LXmkqYFep8
Williams pointed at his throws over the middle to Odunze to convert two third-and-longs.
“I was decisive about going to Rome, believing in him, trusting in him," Williams said.
It worked for the Bears to the tune of a 30-24 victory over a Super Bowl team on a night reserved to honor the memory of the late Mike Ditka. One of Ditka's favorite phrases was "big-time football," when they beat another contender in the regular season.  Thursday night's win was exactly that.
Now they can take this 5-2 record that includes wins over Carolina, Philadelphia and New England, and go face the other team from the last Super Bowl, the Lombardi Trophy-winning Seahawks.
There's been no public memorial for Mike Ditka. So Chicago turned Soldier Field into one. Every fan got a fake mustache. The stadium clocks read 89:00 all afternoon. The opponent? The Patriots, the team his '85 Bears beat 46-10 in Super Bowl XX. Iron Mike would've loved it.…
It's a strange record when they are 0-2 in their own division and 5-0 outside of it, but this is where they are.
Here are the grades for this trustworthy contender.
The commitment was there even if the results came up short. They went against a very stout front and averaged only 3.9 per rush, but D'Andre Swift came up with tough yards and 22 carries was a heavy workload for him without injured Kyle Monangai. They probably could have leaned a bit more to Roschon Johnson but perhaps that trust wasn't so thorough after his fumble last week. Still, the line did enough and Swift was very tough at the goal line with a TD run in the first quarter and later on a pair of big runs for first downs.
D’Andre Swift gets in for the games first Touchdown #DaBears pic.twitter.com/VrsZdZ1D5j
This was one of the few times in Bears history when their quarterback stood in against another big-time passer in what amounted to a shootout and they came away a winner in the end. Maybe beating Jordan Love in the playoffs was another recent one, but Maye has definitely been one of the best young QBs in the league for two seasons and actually had a better passer rating in the game than Williams, 117.8-116.7. He also was better at yards per attempt, although both had wildly high numbers (Maye 10.3 and Williams 9.3). The better receiver group, led by Luther Burden's four catches and 130 yards, and they made a difference. It probably didn't help Maye that Romeo Doubs was out, injured. Ultimately, one pass decided it. Maye threw the interception in the first half in the end zone to D'Marco Jackson. Williams did not turn it over.
The Luther Burden III Breakout is HERE!! 🚀 Sorry, haters!! pic.twitter.com/OPkwh5SEyn
It's been rare since Dennis Allen became coach that the Bears so thoroughly contained a rushing game. This was one capable of turning out big yards with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson, but the backs were held to 13 carries for 44 yards even with middle linebacker T.J. Edwards out with a hamstring injury. Edwards and Devin Bush were outstanding against the run while the line forced the scrimmage line back into the backfield.
The big pick wasn't all the Bears did right in the secondary. Even with Malik Muhammad exiting due to a toe injury, they managed to prevent most big plays. The Patriots had only two plays 20 yards or longer, one of which was the disaster to end the first half when they let Stevenson take a shorter pass 48 yards as Jaylon Johnson whiffed for the second time on a TD play. By contrast, the Bears had eight pass plays 20 yards or longer. As poorly as Johnson tackled, you didn't see his man in coverage making receptions all over the field. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson fought off an injury and played an outstanding game, as well. A.J. Brown had only three catches and Patriots wide receivers made only seven receptions for the game. Part of the reason the wide receivers weren't used was the Bears' pass rush. The Patriots had to go to tighter formations with a tight end or two retained for pass protection when it was evident early how the blitz, especially by Kyler Gordon, was beating their offensive line and getting to Maye.
There’s one DB for the Chicago Bears who refuses to tackle… I mean, absolutely refuses to!
The missed Cairo Santos 53-yard field goal might have been their only blemish, but tying the team record at 58 yards made up for it. The kickoff team and punt team again controlled field position, while Zavion Thomas and the kick return team answered Maye's 6-yard TD scramble by breaking a kick return 47 yards to Patriots territory.
Dennis Allen continues to bottle up teams leaning heavily on backups. Not having Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo up front for the second straight game proved no problem as they allowed backs only 3.5 yards per carry and got 1 1/2 of their two sacks from defensive backs. It would have been three if Dillon Thieneman hadn't bounced off Maye on another attempt like he was stone. Ben Johnson's silly play call on a run by guard Joe Thuney should be put in the circular file, but he had a strong night with play calling overall and made good on both of his fourth-down gambles, while going 3-for-4 in the red zone for TDs.
#Bears K Cairo Santos was with Mike Vrabel on the #Titans in 2019, when he went 4-for-9 on FGs and Tennessee released him. “I think the last FG Cairo missed was when he kicked for the Titans. We always joke about it.” Santos hit a career-long 58-yard FG to beat Vrabel tonight. https://t.co/szsk9E892z pic.twitter.com/h9l5T6T5M4
After this it's apparent — if it wasn't already — that the Bears must be considered in the Super Bowl picture. Beat Seattle and you can plant yourself among the favorites. Eventually it might help to actually win a game within their own division, though.

title: Chicago Bears Best Available Options at TE Following Cole Kmet's Injury
full_text:
It sounds like the Chicago Bears will be without one of their locker room leaders and key offensive pieces for the rest of the season.
Tight end Cole Kmet went down with a knee injury in the team's 30-24 win over the New England Patriots on Thursday night, and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said this morning that the outlook for the star TE doesn't look good.
There's no sugarcoating it; Kmet being sidelined for the rest of the season would be a massive blow to Chicago's offense. He's played 62% of the snaps for Chicago's offense thus far. An extended absence could thrust third-round pick Sam Roush (who's seen 22% of the action in 13 personnel) into the lineup more often.
However, with Roush struggling mightily to begin his rookie season, the team could also look to free agency to fill the void. Who would be their best options if they go that route?
Albert Okwuegbunam was once considered a promising tight end with the Broncos, who selected the field-stretching TE in the fourth round of the 2020 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old has rare speed for the position, evidenced by a 4.49-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Scouting Combine.
Okwuegbunam has bounced around the Colts and Raiders practice squads over the past two seasons (he also played in one game for Las Vegas last season) and is currently a free agent. He is now five years removed from his best season (330 yards, 2 TDs), but would at least provide some potential juice in the receiving game if they wanted to prioritize that on the open market.
Will Dissly was once considered a solid starter. His three-year, $24 million deal ranked 15th at the position in 2022. He's never been a threat to beat defenses over the top, but he is a well-rounded player who is equally effective in the receiving game as he is as a run blocker.
To his credit, the 30-year-old is two years removed from his best season as a receiver, as he caught 50 passes for 481 yards with the Chargers in 2024. Los Angeles released him in March, and he's been on the market ever since. While he wouldn't be a flashy addition by any means (he never has been), he'd definitely be their best option to replace what Kmet brought in the blocking department.
Jaheim Bell would be the Bears' best option if they wanted to cash in on some untapped potential. The Patriots selected him in the seventh round of the 2024 NFL Draft, and he's still only 25. Some thought New England landed a potential diamond in the rough, as Bell had one of the better performances among TEs at the NFL Scouting Combine (he ran a 4.61-second 40-yard dash to go along with a 35" vertical and 10'4" broad jump).
Unfortunately, that athleticism hasn't translated to the field, as he has only two catches for 20 yards in his career. Bell has bounced back and forth (two stints each way) between the Eagles and Steelers practice squads over the past two seasons. While he's not a good candidate to replicate what Kmet brings to the running game, he'd at least provide some upside in the receiving game if they can tap into his athleticism.
Jordan Akins is by far the most accomplished player on this list. While he might not have enjoyed the same level of hype as Dissly did earlier in his career, he's been a solid backup for a long time. The 34-year-old has three seasons with at least 400 receiving yards under his belt. He's also two years removed from a 390-yard campaign with the Browns.
Most recently, Akins spent the 2025 campaign on the Jaguars practice squad. The only downside to Akins would be his age, as he's arguably the most well-rounded candidate on this list. While he's a few tiers below Kmet in every area, he'd be a solid pickup if he were willing to run it back one more time.
