He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Week 7 Stock Report: Williams Among Those Rising, Johnson Leads the Falling
full_text:
The Chicago Bears kept rolling right along on Thursday night, securing their fifth win of the season over the New England Patriots.
After the victory over New England , the Bears sit at 5-2 and in second place in the NFC North, which is the highest they can finish after this week.
A loss by the Green Bay Packers on Sunday to the Detroit Lions will keep Chicago in that spot going into Week 8, otherwise Chicago will fall to third place.
Now, the Bears will have a long break to rest up ahead of the Week 8 game against the Seattle Seahawks on "Monday Night Football."
But before we turn the page to next week, here's a look back at Week 7 and the Bears players who saw their stocks rise or fall.
Williams just looks like a different quarterback this season and we mean that in the best way possible.
It's very clear the former No. 1 overall pick has a better command of the offense, better decision-making and much more poise in the pocket. Williams is also showing improved accuracy, which was a major point of emphasis this offseason.
Before the season, the Bears were hoping Williams would give them the green light to be confident in signing him to a massive contract extension next year. So far, he has done just that as he continues to ascend to elite status following his outstanding showing in Week 7.
Johnson had a pair of instances of putrid effort on tackles.
One of them came on a Drake Maye scramble, and the other was on the end-of-half touchdown pass to Rhamondre Stevenson.
Johnson actually held up well in coverage, allowing just one catch on two targets for 14 yards, but that performance is an outlier rather than the norm this season.
The veteran cornerback remains on the fast track to get cut in 2027.
There is no longer any doubt about who the Bears' No. 1 wideout is. Burden entered the game with the most receiving yards on the team and he left with an even bigger lead.
While Burden didn't do much in the second half, his first-half contribution was more than enough and sparked the Bears' offense.
In all, Burden finished with four catches for 130 yards and a score and had long gains of 58 and 24, with the latter coming on his touchdown grab on a screen pass that displayed his electric speed.
As Rome Odunze continues to fail to answer the bell in what is a crucial season for him, Burden is taking that next step.
The Bears planned on relying heavily on van den Berg after the trade of Gervon Dexter, but it appears that faith was misplaced.
The rookie sixth-round pick was a ghost once again on Thursday night, as he didn't record a single stat and played a season-low five snaps.
It was another reminder that the Bears need to make some kind of addition to the interior of the defensive line , which has been as disappointment overall this season.
Pushed into a bigger role once again with T.J. Edwards out due to injury, Jackson was all over the place against the Pats, with the veteran linebacker tallying six tackles and three run stops, according to Pro Football Focus .
Jackson also made what was one of the game's biggest plays when he picked off Drake Maye in the end zone in the second quarter.
After seeing his stellar play on Thursday night, there's no doubt that the Bears have an elite linebackers room with Jackson, Edwards and Devin Bush.
Johnson was heavily involved in the offense in Week 6 and had a good game, his fourth-quarter fumble not withstanding.
However, Johnson was barely involved in Week 7. He saw just 10 snaps after playing 27 and 31 in each of the last two games, and he had just two carries for 13 yards and wasn't targeted in the passing game.
Johnson's lack of a role was especially surprising because Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor just said earlier in the week that Chicago was looking to avoid putting too much on D'Andre Swift's plate in order to keep him fresh for the whole season, yet Swift saw a whopping 26 touches, including 22 carries.
We don't think it was head coach Ben Johnson punishing Johnson for his fumble last week, as the veteran back saw important totes down the stretch after that, so this was likely just the Bears taking advantage of the extra rest Swift will have before Week 8.
Loveland continues to pick up steam after a lackluster start to the season. His seven catches for 69 yards were both season-highs for him, and he found the end zone for a second straight game.
In his last four games, Loveland has posted 57 receiving yards or more, and he has topped 60 in each of the last two games while also scoring in each contest.
It hasn't been all perfect, though, as Loveland dropped a few passes or else he could have had much more. Even still, the Bears will deal with those as long as Loveland is producing.
We're old enough to remember when Raymond was the team's leading receiver after the first three games.
However, a lot has changed since then, as Raymond didn't post a single catch on two targets on Thursday night and he hasn't topped 18 yards in any of the last four games.
To be quite frank, we always figured Raymond was going to revert to the No. 3 wide receiver he was supposed to be after a hot start, so this isn't surprising in the least.
Thomas' impact in the return game was felt once again.
Thomas totaled 92 yards on three kickoff returns, but he really shined with his 47-yard return in the second quarter that set Chicago up for a field goal nine plays later.
Now, over his last three games, Thomas has returns of 61 and 47 yards, and he's averaging a healthy 25.7 yards per kick return.
Thomas did have a bad holding penalty on offense, and he still isn't making much of a contribution in that area overall, but we never really expected him to in his first season, anyway.
Gordon was an absolute menace for a second straight week.
He tallied another sack, bringing him up to four on the season, which is the second-most on the team, and he added five tackles, including two for loss, and a team-high five run stops. Gordon was only targeted once in coverage and didn't give up a completion.
The Bears were hoping Gordon could provide a jolt to the defense upon his return, and he has done that and then some over two games.
Santos missed a 50-plus-yard attempt for a second straight game, but he quickly erased that with a clutch field goal near the end of regulation.
Johnson made the gutsy call to give Santos a 58-yard try, even though a miss would have set the Patriots up near midfield with a chance to win the game. It was extra risky because Santos had never made a kick from that far.
However, Santos delivered in a pressure-packed situation, which gives confidence he can be relied upon in the kinds of scenarios the Bears might find themselves in a lot this season.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Ravens Defender Hopes to Avoid Ja'Marr Chase as Bengals Star Reveals Key to Beating Baltimore
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase has left a permanent scar on the Ravens' secondary throughout his career, and one of Baltimore's starting corners, Marlon Humphrey , is already dreading the challenge ahead.
Humphrey gave an honest answer about facing Chase.
“It would be cool if I didn’t match up with him so much,” Humphrey said. "He's obviously one of the best in the game, Tee is right up there with him in the top ten I think of this league."
Over Chase's career, he has caught 61 passes for 1,036 yards and seven touchdowns against the Ravens. Humphrey has been on the field for most of those performances. This could force Ravens coach Kevin Minter to pit third-year corner Nate Wiggins against Chase more often.
Wiggins has certainly improved since entering the league, but neither player has been able to stop Chase.
Another possible matchup against Chase, instead of Humphrey, is former teammate Chidobe Awuzie. He has had success covering Chase in the past largely due to their familiarity with each other. Awuzie has not played much for the Ravens this season so far with 82 total snaps.
During his weekly press conference, Chase said the key to beating the Ravens' secondary is winning downfield catches. He added that while the Ravens' defense is solid, it faces a bigger challenge against the Bengals' offense .
"Winning downfield catches, that's the key," Chase said. "They're a well-rounded defense at the end of the day, but they gotta play us."
Chase has consistently torched the Ravens, and he has had success against a Jesse Minter defense before. In 2024, Chase had seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers and Minter's defense.
While the Bengals must build momentum in the run game against Baltimore, Chase should remain the focal point of the Bengals' offensive game plan on Sunday. One area they can dial up more looks for Chase should come from lining him up outside more than they have so far this season.
"They're not going to give up anything easy," Burrow said. "And we have guys that can make contested plays on the outside, and we can make plays outside the pocket, outside the structure. These guys make everything so hard.
"And if you don't make contested plays, you're going to have a long day because they're going to stop the run and they're going to make you throw it deep. They're going to play everything down from shallow to deep. And if you don't make those contested plays down the field, it's going to be a long day."

title: Ja’Marr Chase Owns the Ravens as Bengals Hold Several Key Advantages
full_text:
The 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals travel to Baltimore to take on the 4-2 Ravens in their first daytime clash in B’More since 2021.
The biggest story leading into the game is the health of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. The former MVP missed the last two games including a loss to the Cleveland Browns last weekend.
This rivalry has already been robbed too many times when it comes to these two quarterbacks facing off, so let's hope Jackson plays.
I don't want to hear any excuses afterwards.
The real star in this AFC North rivalry has been Ja'Marr Chase. His average of 120 yards per game vs Baltimore is the most receiving yards per game by any player vs a single opponent in NFL history.
I never thought we'd have ANOTHER “Ravens Killer” after A.J. Green left, but of course Chase found a way to surpass Green.
Per Next Gen Stats, Chase and Marlon Humphrey have matched up on 83 snaps since he entered the league. Nobody has covered Chase more since 2021 and he's seen 21 targets, catching 14 balls for 318 yards against Humphrey.
For the non-mathematicians, that's 15.1 yards per reception for Chase, the most that any receiver averages against ANY defender during that span.
It sounds like Humphrey would like to cover Chase a little less in this one and he's been lining up almost exclusively on the boundary this season (95.7% of snaps) where he has allowed 69% of the passes targeted in his direction to be caught.
Joe Burrow is tasked with feeding his receivers in an effort to outduel Jackson on Sunday.
Burrow is still getting the ball out as quickly as anyone. This season, he's releasing the ball under 2.5 seconds on a league-high 57.1% of his throws.
That doesn't mean he's throwing short. Burrow has thrown downfield on 18.5% of his quick-throws and has completed 15 of 20 of these passes for 265 yards and 5 touchdowns.
Baltimore's defense has allowed an 81.8% completion percentage on quick-throws that go downfield this season.
And we're not just talking about deep passes. The Bengals and Joe Burrow are peppering the intermediate area (10-19 yards) with precision. Burrow is completing a league-high 73.2% of his passes and has averaged 12.0 yards per attempt, the third-most. The Bengals average a league-leading +0.95 EPA per pass into the intermediate part of the field.
The Ravens defense has allowed 69.8% of passes into the intermediate area to be completed, the second-highest rate in the NFL and those passes have gone for the third-most 617 yards. Their +0.62 EPA allowed per throw into the intermediate area ranks 24th in the league.
Baltimore is a heavy 2-high defense with 81.9% of all of their defensive plays featuring two safeties in deep coverage. That's the second-highest rate in the league and the Bengals have averaged +0.27 EPA per play against that coverage, third-best in the NFL.
If the Bengals offense can keep pace, it'll be up to the Cincinnati defense to answer the call and make a few plays like they did in that Thanksgiving Day win in Baltimore last season.
It starts with slowing down Derrick Henry and he might just be slowing down on his own already.
The guy is a machine, no doubt, but eventually time comes for us all.
Henry is averaging 2.4 yards AFTER contact per carry this season. His lowest average since 2018.
He's also being stopped for zero or negative yardage on 54% of his carries this season. That's his highest rate since 2018.
Henry has run outside zone on 44.2% of his runs this season. That's 57 carries for 302 yards and four touchdowns.
The Bengals have the highest Run Stuff Rate on outside runs in the league at 34.5%.
I bet that run stuff rate surprised you, too.
The biggest weapon for Baltimore's offense is receiver Zay Flowers. He's dicing up defenses from the slot this season and leading the league in separation as they keep finding creative ways to get Flowers open.
Last season, DJ Turner shadowed Flowers and did a great job.
Turner matched up with Flowers 21 times across two games last season and allowed one catch for 14 yards on four targets.
Baltimore has had some issues on their offensive line and traded for Cam Jurgens from the Eagles. He's healthy now after recovering from a concussion and should assume the starting center job for the Ravens.
I'm sure they're happy to get some stability inside, but Jurgens hasn't been good this season. Out of 85 interior offensive linemen, Cam Jurgens ranks 85th in PFF’s Pass blocking grade and that's largely because his 95.4% Pass Block Efficiency also ranks 85th and his 13.0 grade in True Pass Sets is 10 points lower than the 84th ranked interior offensive lineman.
Sounds like Dexter Lawrence gets another game to leave his mark and make the Bengals decision to trade for him look even better.
Speaking of offseason decisions, can we take a second to appreciate the decision the Bengals made when they had to replace Trey Hendrickson and landed Boye Mafe as the guy to do the job?
To this point, Mafe has been EVERYTHING the Bengals could've hoped for and it's just the cherry on top that he's outperforming Trey Hendrickson in every statistical category.
Now seems like a good time for this comparison pic.twitter.com/3EoZWIci7T
Trey Hendrickson says he forgives the Bengals and that this game isn't about him.

title: Lamar Jackson's Game Status Gets Clearer Ahead of Matchup With Bengals
full_text:
The Bengals and Ravens have finalized game statuses for Sunday's action in the AFC North. Cincinnati is healthy, with veteran safety Kyle Dugger set to return after suffering a quad injury last month.
On the other hand, the Ravens are hoping to have Lamar Jackson on the field for the first time since Week 4. He has been limited all week with an ankle injury and is questionable entering the game.
"Right now I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said on Friday. "We'll see. Hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction."
Jackson suffered the injury on October 4. He sounded unsure about playing on Sunday against the Bengals.
“Just trying to move how I move,” he said. “If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team.”
“Lamar [Jackson] was actually able to get a little bit of limited work in today in preparation. So, that’s where that’s at. Again, it’s a day-by-day thing, but he was able to get a little bit of work in and be involved in the preparation," Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said about Jackson on Wednesday before commenting on Jackson's workload. "[I am] not really [going] to get into the specifics of anything with that. I know this, when it’s ready for [Lamar Jackson] to be able to play, from both sides, and we feel like that’s the best thing to do; that’s what we’ll do.”
Cincinnati had a rare early bye week in 2026, but it helped them get much healthier over the past 10 days, and now they can attack the most important game of the season so far from the strongest health position possible.
It's basically a coin-flip game, with Cincinnati projected to win 54% of the time on ESPN's Matchup Predictor. Whoever can create a timely turnover or two will have a big advantage.
"It's critical," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the turnover battle on Wednesday. "Just winning the turnovers in general in a division game like this. I can think of many times we played the Ravens, and you feel like you leave the game with like three possessions, and so if you lose or gain one, that's always critical. Now the game's going to end up being an 18-possession game, of course, because I say that. But just any time it's like that, it turns out to be a big part of the game."
The action kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Bengals Have an Easy Trade Deadline Decision to Make, But They're Not Alone
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are putting in the final preparations as they gear up for a massive showdown with the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
The outcome of the game on Sunday between the AFC North foes will change the trajectory of both teams. In a division that has shown to be one of the toughest in the NFL, wins are at a premium.
Cincinnati has the talent to claim the division, but what if they could get even better? There's one move the Bengals should make at the trade deadline, however, it seems the longer they wait, the higher the price could get.
There has been a lot of chatter about Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor being moved before the November 10th trade deadline.
Taylor is one of the top running backs in the NFL, and adding him to an explosive offense like the Bengals' would make the unit virtually unstoppable.
Bengals running back Chase Brown has not had an ideal start to the 2026 season, and this is a team that can't afford to wait much longer for its run game to produce more.
With $8.5 million in cap space , the Bengals could potentially make the move for Taylor. However, they may not be the only team interested in adding the former All-Pro running back.
Another team that could potentially be in the market for a running back is the New York Giants. Things aren't going well for fan favorite, Cam Skattebo, who only has 294 rushing yards on the season. While he may be having a disappointing season, Skattebo could be one piece of a potential trade to the Colts.
Then there's the Minnesota Vikings. Not sure anyone had the Vikings at 5-0, leading the NFC North at this point in the season.
It's no surprise that defensive coordinator Brian Flores has his unit on top of their game, but the Vikings' run game could use a jolt.
The Vikings are 19th in rushing yards this season. Adding Taylor could catapult the unit, making Minnesota the most feared team in the NFL.
If this really is an all-in season for the Bengals, then making a move for Taylor makes a lot of sense. It's the kind of move that shows the rest of the league that the Bengals are not playing around.
The Bengals are going to be a pass heavy offense given the playmakers they have. With Taylor, planning for the Bengals will be a nightmare for opposing coaching staffs. This should be an easy decision for the front office.

title: Relive Ja'Marr Chase's Unforgettable Touchdown vs. Ravens as Bengals Rivalry Renews in Week 7
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' Week 7 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens is seismic. Cincinnati will be looking to avoid a 0-2 start in AFC North play while also keeping pace with the rest of the division, who are all 4-2 heading into the week.
There's also some so-called "bad blood" that might be brought up for this one. Ravens defensive end Trey Hendrickson spent four seasons with the Bengals before deciding to join one of the team's biggest rivals prior to this season. It may not be on the team's mind, but the fan base is hoping to see the Bengals' offensive line shut down Hendrickson.
Even without the Hendrickson storyline, this game is always a big deal. There is a lot of history between the two franchises, and recently, Jeremy Rauch of Fox19 shared an epic breakdown of a touchdown Ja'Marr Chase scored against the Ravens back in 2021, by Bengals receiving coach Troy Walters.
The 2021 season was a memorable season for the Bengals. It was the year that the team made it all the way to the big game.
On their way there, they had a massive early season matchup with the Ravens that ended with a 41-17 win. In the win, Chase pulled off one of the greatest plays of his career when he put the Ravens' defense in a blender to fly down the field for an 82 yard touchdown reception.
Three Ravens whiffed in an attempt to tackle Chase on the play.
"I remember it because it was third down. It was a tight game," said Walters. Baltimore had our number. After that play, the rest was history in terms of that game.
Not that the fans aren't respecting Chase's greatness, but the Bengals wide receiver has had so many epic plays that it's hard to keep up with his highlight reel career.
Just two weeks ago, Chase pulled off an unbelievable one-handed touchdown snag in the team's 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins.
The Ravens were no match for the Bengals back in 2021. However, will that be the same story this season?
A win over the Ravens puts the Bengals at 4-2, which is similar to the situation they were in back in 2021. After their first meeting with the Ravens back then, the Bengals moved to 5-2. There are a lot of similarities lining up from that game. Maybe Chase can add another highlight to his future ring of honor video package.

Lawrence and that unit are preparing for how Lamar Jackson (ankle) is going to play, and they know they'll have to deal with Derrick Henry. The beast of a running back has ripped Cincinnati apart in his career.

We got to build a wall and keep him behind it.”
Lawrence has transformed this run defense in a very positive way.
The veteran has an 82.5 Pro Football Focus grade on 226 snaps and has helped Cincinnati lead the league in run-stuff rate so far (23.93%). Something's gotta give between these two monsters on opposite sides of the ball.

"Just play a complete game, as complete as we can play," Lawrence said about the goal on Sunday. "We know it's not gonna be perfect, but some of the mistakes that we've had that can be there. They can be eliminated."

title: 'Just Gonna Dead It' - Ja'Marr Chase Reveals Future of  'People's Elbow' Celebration After Fine Flip
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase spoke to the media for the first time in a few weeks on Thursday. The superstar receiver has a massive game on deck this weekend against Baltimore, and even though he won his celebration fine appeal against the NFL, don't expect the "people's elbow" to make a return near the Chesapeake Bay.
Chase is letting a sleeping dog rest and not touching those celebration moves anymore despite the league siding with his reasoning for bringing it out in the first place.
"If we could do the celly, we would bring it back, but I don't think they're gonna let us," Chase said. "You know what I'm saying? So it's too many opinions on the celebration, so they're probably just gonna dead it. But I'm just happy that I got a chance to get the opportunity to win my money back."
The NFL fined Tee Higgins four times and Chase twice from doing the celebration in September's game against Houston. The two players were fined $89,556 total for the arm signage.
That's behind Chase; now he's focused on igniting what's been a pretty light season in terms of receiving yards so far (289 yards through five games).
"Started off pretty slow, first game. Haven't had a 100-yard game yet. I think that's a really big key on why I'm so low," Chase noted. "But I'm getting good opportunities. Defense is changing looks, and there hasn't been too many downfield passes for me to make the 100 yards, but they're still using me a good way."
Chase hasn't played under the Baltimore sun since 2021, when he was late for a team activity that week, but still balled out with eight catches for 201 yards and a touchdown.
"I got fined for damn near missing a whole meeting that week that year," Chase said. "So I actually had to play good. I came late to a morning practice, and yeah, I think it was a Friday or Saturday I came late and then after the game, after we won, they (the coaches) was like, 'If you doing stuff like that, you come late every time.' So that's a good little part."
Chase has tightened up the time allocation much better in the ensuing half decade. He takes on the Baltimore secondary Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: 'In Here Reading Books' - Ja'Marr Chase Details Quick Concussion Recovery
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase is back behind the podcast microphone this week after a break due to his concussion and the Bengals bye week.
Cincinnati's best player broke down how the whole concussion process played out in the most detailed comments yet about the injury .
Chase suffered more of a "whiplash" concussion because of how he got twisted on the play against Jacksonville.
Although he's not holding any ill will towards the Jaguars.
"I thought I was really fine. But after seeing the video, I felt like it was more like a whiplash concussion from just my neck being hit side to side," Chase noted. "I don't think it was anything too crazy from a player. No dirty play. I just think it was maybe a reaction of him trying to grab me or something like that. I can't say he was trying to play dirty at the end of the day; after I really got up and stuff, that's when I found out.
"When you get a concussion, you don't know until they tell you, 'Let's go talk to you.' Then they pull you in a tent, and they ask you a couple questions. Depends on how many questions you get right."
It was Chase's first concussion of his NFL (and possibly) playing career, so he had a chance to return the next week against Miami, and did just that.
He had to be off his phone all week and stay away from screens to let his brain recover in time for the Miami bout.
Chase stuck to paper books for entertainment the old-fashioned way. He did a lot of reading in the past few weeks, including books like The Superior Man, and The 48 Laws of Power.
"I didn't really sit in the dark room. I tried to stay in like a routine to make sure I was okay at the end of the day," Chase said. "But I didn't really wear shades that much. I wore shades on the regular when we had walk-throughs ... I wasn't on my phone. I couldn't play video games. I was in here reading books just to keep my mind off stuff."
Ja'Marr Chase Book Club could be a fun segment on the podcast moving forward.

title: Bengals Top Fit For Potential Secondary Trade Option Ahead of 2026 Deadline
full_text:
Trade deadline season is upon us, and Cincinnati could push in some assets to the middle of the table to improve their 2026 roster. One way to really round out the defensive secondary depth could be to go after Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.
The 30-year-old has one more full season left on his current contract extension. He's struggled with a 52.4 Pro Football Focus grade last season and a 55.1 mark this season, but he graded out at 64 or higher in every season before that dating to 2017.
Cincinnati's already dealt with multiple injuries in the safety room, and more options couldn't hurt.
CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani sees Baker as a strong trade fit for the Bengals . The safety has 42 tackles, a career-high 3.5 sacks, one interception, and four pass breakups this season.
"Budda Baker has been a star for the Arizona Cardinals ever since he was selected No. 36 overall in the 2017 NFL Draft out of Washington," Dajani wrote . "He made the Pro Bowl as a rookie — the first of what have turned into eight Pro Bowl appearances. Not many players have made 1,000 tackles before age 30. Just Bobby Wagner, Roquan Smith, Luke Kuechly, Lavonte David, Ray Lewis, Fred Warner, and ... Budda Baker.
"Baker is still a stud, as evidenced by the Cardinals' upset win over the Rams on Sunday. He recorded six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defensed. He stopped at least one touchdown from being scored, and he was effective in blitzing the quarterback and stopping the running backs. Someone come get him."
Given his age (30) and expensive contract, Baker might be had for a Day 3 draft pick in 2027.
There are no firm reports that Baker is on the trade block, but Arizona hasn't even gotten the quarterback of the future in place yet to start contending at some point this decade. Baker may be long past his prime by the time they do, but the Bengals have a superstar quarterback he can help win right now.
The money may make this really hard in reality. According to Spotrac, Baker has a $9.79 million cap hit the rest of this season and a $20.9 million cap hit in 2027. Paying big money to him and Bryan Cook may not be palatable for Cincinnati . They'd likely have to release someone in the process of this trade just to stay under the 2026 salary cap.

title: Is Shedeur Sanders in Cleveland in 2027? Exploring His Path Forward With Browns
full_text:
When the 2025 campaign concluded, it seemed that the Cleveland Browns had found their long-term starter.
While he had a lot of work to do to become a reliable starting quarterback in the NFL, then-rookie Shedeur Sanders showed enough to warrant real consideration to be the leader of the Browns moving forward.
However, the moment the front office moved on from head coach Kevin Stefanski and opened a new chapter in the franchise's storied history, that sentiment came crashing down.
After battling for the starting job all offseason, Sanders lost the race to controversial quarterback Deshaun Watson, who has begun the 2026 season off nicely. He has experienced plenty of bumps in the road along the way, but has the Browns atop the AFC North standings with a 4-2 record through six weeks.
While it is obviously great to see the Browns playing competitive football, Watson's success puts the Browns in a difficult situation moving forward.
Watson's currently in the final year of his deal, and with how controversial and rocky his tenure in Cleveland has been since he was traded just a few years back, it seems unlikely that the two sides would work out a return deal.
That means that Sanders could end up becoming the starter yet again.
But is he ready for that? And is the front office even thinking about such a decision?
When the Browns named Watson the starter, both the front office and Monken confirmed it was primarily an experience-based decision.
The 31-year-old has been in the league since 2017, throwing for 19,078 yards and 130 touchdowns along the way. He hasn't played the best since joining the Browns back in 2022, but still commands an offense well and can recognize different tendencies.
Sanders, on the other hand, is still quite raw. He put together a rookie campaign that saw 1,400 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The numbers may not show it, but he got himself into trouble quite a few times, throwing the ball into odd situations or scrambling into traffic both into and outside of the pocket. To put it simply, he looked like a first-year signal caller.
From the organization's perspective, starting Watson may have been just the safer option for a team looking to give Monken a chance to succeed in his first year as a head coach. Instead of working out the kinks in Sanders' game on game day, they can do so on the practice field and behind closed doors.
With the Browns being 4-2, it seems like the decision has paid off so far.
However, the bigger question is whether that short-term success aligns with Cleveland's long-term plans.
Keeping Watson ahead of him on the depth chart gives Sanders time to learn, but with the path ahead so murky, things could just continue to get even more complicated, especially if Watson leaves in the offseason.
It seems like a relatively odd question to ask, especially considering the 24-year-old has a lot to prove.
But the last thing the Browns want to do is frustrate or put wrinkles in the timeline of yet another quarterback. It is something they have done time and time again, routinely resetting the quarterback development process in Cleveland.
For a young quarterback trying to establish himself in the NFL, though, the situation he is in is a difficult balancing act. Sitting behind a veteran can provide him with valuable experience, but after getting time to develop on the field in 2025, he now has to do it off it in 2026.
There is no reason to assume Sanders is unhappy with his current situation , but if the Browns keep Watson around in 2027 or make a move for another quarterback to take his place, his long-term outlook in Cleveland will begin to look grim.
Sooner rather than later, the Browns will have to determine whether or not the future revolves around him.
Could the Browns make a move in the 2027 NFL Draft to select a top quarterback? Maybe, but it doesn't seem likely at this point.
The team has gone from quarterback to quarterback over the last few campaigns, and even drafted two back in 2025: Sanders and Dillon Gabriel, and one in 2026: Taylen Green. Drafting yet another would continue to crowd the quarterback room, making it even more difficult for a coaching staff to develop one of them properly.
Instead, it seems far more likely that the Browns, who have two picks in the first round of the upcoming draft, will select pieces to fit alongside one of the quarterbacks they currently have.
No matter what the Browns end up doing with Sanders moving forward, the 2026 campaign will certainly be looked back on with plenty of confusion.
If Cleveland really does believe Sanders is the future, why not start him from Week 1 onward? If they don't think he has what it takes to be a starter in the league, at least not yet, why didn't they just say that?
For now, questions will continue to be asked. And only the guys at the top really know what plan is in motion for 2027.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out.
Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville.
Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver.
The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”.
When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover.
The defense cannot allow easy throws for Cam Ward, as he has struggled in his second year , and not giving him momentum will be key. On the other hand, if Denzel Ward has to miss any game this season, Sunday’s game may be the one to do it against a struggling offense.
Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers.
However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game.
The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week.
He is a physical veteran that helps shut down the offense’s running game by playing near the tackle box, but Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has stepped in and is improving every game he is on the field.
The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since.
The offense relies on his speed to be a change of pace and utilize the screen game in lieu of a traditional running play.
Quinshon Judkins will play against the Titans after missing last week. The offense could finally have the top-two running backs in the backfield that they envisioned when the season started. The Titans have big Jeffery Simmons at defensive tackle and he feasted against the Browns’ offense last season.
The addition of the two running backs can help lift the offense.
The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games.
He still leads the team with four sacks and the second-year defensive tackle has made major strides this season in anchoring the aggressive line.
Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game.
The Titans’ Tony Pollard has had a solid season running the football, and the line will need to keep him down and make Cameron Ward beat them with his arm.
Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line.
If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2.

title: How the Browns Could Change the Game with this Position-Altering Trade
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are 4-2 to begin the 2026 NFL regular season.
Through the first six weeks, there have been plenty of positives for the Browns to be excited about, especially with the defensive side of the ball. But with the positives come some negatives, with many of them unfortunately being on the offensive end.
Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson has been somewhat all over the place, the rushing attack has been absent and the tight end room has become incredibly thin.
In order to capitalize on the momentum they have established, landing a few key pieces at the trade deadline could be the perfect way to round out the roster and fill a few holes.
One player who has stood out as of late is tight end Sam LaPorta of the Detroit Lions, who seems to be frustrated with his current situation. On a recent episode of Pardon My Take, LaPorta shared his frustration with not receiving a contract extension from the Lions.
"You know, like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, you know, I break my fucking back for the team," he said, "and then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love ... And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good.
"I'll go get paid somewhere else."
Sam LaPorta on not receiving an extension from the Lions, via @PardonMyTake : "You know, like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, you know, I break my fucking back for the team and then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling and maybe they're just not showing the… pic.twitter.com/MocZjCmq1f
The last part of LaPorta's quote is eye-opening because the 25-year-old is on the last year of a four-year contract worth nearly $10 million . As one of the league's best tight ends, he is rightfully hoping to see Detroit dish him out some cash to lock him down on a long-term deal.
But that simply hasn't happened yet.
On Thursday, Oct. 22, members of the Lions were open to the media for roughly 45 minutes, but LaPorta did not show up.
Lions TE Sam LaPorta was a "no show" during the 45-minute player media access yesterday, per @freep (h/t @officialctpod ) pic.twitter.com/q4ubT8p0nz
If this situation continues, the Browns should pick up the phone and give the Lions a call.
Very rarely does a franchise have the opportunity to have two of the league's best tight ends on the same roster. And oftentimes, it is hard for a front office to justify paying two players a good chunk of money at that position.
However, the Browns are notorious for running multi-tight end sets.
Under Kevin Stefanski, the team featured a 12 personnel scheme, highlighting two tight ends, two wideouts and a running back. Under Todd Monken, that scheme is maintained, with him also utilizing three-tight-end groupings from time to time.
He also enjoys hitting the deep shot or explosive play if it is open, something LaPorta has thrived with.
He has recorded a long of 38 yards or more in each of the last four seasons, all while averaging a whopping 11.4 yards per reception. Across the last four campaigns, he has totaled 2,420 yards and 23 touchdowns.
According to Free Press, Lions tight end Sam LaPorta HID from media, forcing teammates to answer questions about  what he said. Many Lions declined to answer pic.twitter.com/ZZetKqDdTb
Bringing LaPorta to Cleveland would give the Browns a one-two punch that no one else in the league could match up against.
With the rest of the tight end room featuring Blake Whiteheart, Carsen Ryan, Joe Royer, Jack Stoll and Brendan Bates, landing a go-to option like LaPorta would take less pressure off the depth and instead put it back on those who can handle it.
Fannin Jr. x LaPorta would set the stage for offenses to start investing more in a well-rounded, dynamic offense. Not only would the Browns have two of the best tight ends in the league, but they would also be pairing them with two up-and-coming stars outside the hashes in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
A move like this wouldn't just make the Browns an even better team, but it would change how teams think about the position moving forward.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Where the Cleveland Browns Need Help the Most Ahead of the  NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the NFL trade deadline inches closer and closer, all 32 teams are getting ready to make one final push in improving their rosters in order to successfully navigate the second half of the season.
The AFC North-leading Cleveland Browns are no exception and as a matter of fact, they could become one of the teams to watch closely as they might end up investing in the same position group that was at the forefront of their free agency acquisitions over the spring.
As it turns out, the Cleveland Browns offensive line, while showing some improvement in regards to last years’ unmitigated disaster, is still struggling to gel after replacing all five starters for the 2026 season.
While the Browns’ two rookies on the O-Line -- left tackle Spencer Fano and Austin Barber at the right guard -- have been playing decently and Elgton Jekins is among the best pass blocking centers in the league when healthy , the unit has been struggling mightily in the ground game.
Pro Football Reference has the Browns tied for the fourth worst average yards per rushing attempt before the first contact at just 2.0, and having no ground game has really handicapped Cleveland’s offense, including the play-action phase.
Back in early March, the Browns finalized a trade for Tytus Howard with the Texans, giving up a fifth round pick, and subsequently extending his deal for three years and $63 million to play right tackle. So far, Howard leads the league in false start penalties (5) and is just one flag away from co-leading the league in that department, regardless of position or infraction.
A few days after the Howard deal, the Browns agreed to sign free agent Zion Johnson from the Chargers for three years and $49.5 million to plug in at left guard, which is future Hall of Famer Joel Bitonio’s former spot. While he has shown some improvement over the weeks in pass protection, he’s still struggling to get some push on running plays through the middle.
Likewise, Jenkins was signed as a free agent through a two-year $24 million deal. And Teven Jenkins was re-signed to the tune of one year and $5 million, hoping he could retain the right guard job before a back injury in the summer opened the door for Barber to take the spot, one he will not relinquish in the near future -- unless he changes position. More on that, below.
As a unit, ESPN Analytics has the Browns ranked 27th in pass block win rate and 24th in run block win rate after six games . And according to PFF’s grades, every single one of these three veterans is ranked much higher in pass protection than run blocking, with Elgton Jenkins’ discrepancy being truly noteworthy.
Something needs to change in the trenches for the Browns offense.
The most intriguing name could be Quenton Nelson, a future Hall of Famer who’s on the last year of his current deal. At 30 years-old, he’s not quite what he used to be, but he’s plenty good enough to anchor an offensive line.
With the Colts recently dismissing general manager Chris Ballard, this team is likely looking at a rebuild, and accumulating draft capital should be a priority. Nelson likely won’t fetch much due to his age and a 10 million cap hit for 2026, but Cleveland could fit that number under its cap if interested. Nelson could then take the left side, move Johnson to the right, and have Barber kick out to right tackle, which should be his position for the future anyway.
A much more affordable option would be the Eagles’ Landon Dickerson, after Philly saw Superstar right tackle Lane Johnson retire and then sent starting center Cam Jurgens away via trade. Dickerson has been hurt, but he’s still a better left guard than Johnson, and like Elgton Jenkins, has plenty of experience at center. Perhaps he could take over in the middle and send Jenkins to left guard, or take left guard and move the rest of the pieces as described above.
Finally, the Bucs’ Ben Bredeson is another interior lineman who could be available before the deadline. Like in Dickerson’s case, he’s a left guard with some flexibility to play center. And, he has no more guaranteed money left on his current deal, so that could help grease the skids towards a projected deal.
Of course, Cleveland has some internal options too. Dawand Jones could be tried at right tackle or right guard, kicking Barber out to tackle. KT Leveston showed some promise at guard, too, during the preseason after a very rough 2025 playing tackle.
The point is that this unit needs to get better, quickly. They need to overcome a lack of explosiveness from the backfield in the ground game, and a quarterback who loves to hold on to the ball really long, leading to sacks. This unit is better than last years’ patchwork line, but by no means should the Browns consider themselves done in the trenches.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Why the Browns Should Be Active at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Before the 2026 NFL Season began, nobody thought the Cleveland Browns would be 4-2 after the first six weeks.
However, given the start they have had, the Browns should definitely be interested in becoming buyers at the trade deadline to fill some holes in the roster.
Here's why the Browns should make some calls and what they should be looking out for.
If there is a year to take advantage of the road map to the playoffs, it is this season.
Not only do the Browns have the easiest strength of schedule , but they also get an entire month without having to travel.
For the rest of the season, the Browns will face opponents such as the 1-5 Tennessee Titans, 2-4 New Orleans Saints, 2-4 Houston Texans, and 2-4 Atlanta Falcons.
From weeks 10-14, Cleveland gets to play one home game, go on a bye week, and come out of it playing the next three at home as well.
If there's a year where the schedule is in your favor, it is this one. That said, a couple of trades in order to help secure more wins would be a good move for the organization.
Since trading for him back in 2022, Deshaun Watson has either not been healthy, not played well, or at times both.
This season, it feels like the stars are aligning and the Browns are actually getting the play they want out of the guy they traded for.
Once again, a couple of trades for some offensive pieces may set the Browns and Deshaun Watson up for further success going down the stretch of the year.
So we know the Browns should try to call up some other teams to talk about trades, but who should they go after, and what should they give up?
At the moment, Cleveland desperately needs help with their offensive line. Additionally, some secondary depth could be useful with the recent injury to Grant Delpit.
In the 2027 NFL Draft, the Browns currently have 11 picks available to use. Out of those, they have two first-rounders, 3 fourth rounds, and numerous late-round picks that may get used if the right trade is there.
Historically, Browns General Manager Andrew Berry has done a fantastic job of buying low on players with high upside. We saw him do it twice in the wide receiver room with Amari Cooper and Jerry Jeudy.
Maybe there is a couple of offensive lineman who aren't playing well with their current team and simply need a change of scenery? One of those late-round picks could get sent in return for a guy like that.
Now, if the Browns really want to make a splash, they could go after a guy like Sam LaPorta from Detroit, who has had some poor contract negotiations with the Lions in the past few weeks.
If there's going to be a year to make some moves, it's 2026.
With the wins the Browns have managed to pull off so far, combined with the favorable schedule, the road to the playoffs is much easier than in years past.
Don't be surprised if you see the Browns sending picks away for some players here in a few weeks, before the trade deadline.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Why the Browns Will Not Trade for Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
It has been no secret that despite the Cleveland Browns’ 4-2 record, they have struggled to run the football. The Browns rank 24th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, and  are only that high due to Deshaun Watson’s 32 yard average. Indianapolis Colts’ Jonathan Taylor could be available via trade before the November 10 deadline.
Taylor is averaging four yards per carry this season and he is sixth in the NFL with 492 yards. He would be a major upgrade to the running back room as Quinshon Judkins and Reheim Sanders are injured. The running backs that got carries last week for the Browns were not even on the team at the start of the season.
With the Browns making a playoff push, trading for Taylor should be a no brainer. However, the Browns may want to back off and shift their focus elsewhere. The Colts will be asking for a first or second-round pick plus a late pick swap for Taylor. The Browns have two first-round picks in the draft, and they should hold on to both of them.
The talent is in place on the roster around the quarterback. They should keep their picks and hope to package them to move up and pick a quarterback that they like. At the moment, they are winning too much to be able to use their own pick on a quarterback and the Los Angeles Rams will probably turn their season around, so that pick may be too low.
Valuable running backs can be had anywhere in the draft. The Browns have plenty of middle round-picks to find one and that guy would then be on a rookie contract. Watson’s contract is finally starting to dwindle, but it will still get in the way of adding good players. They have put themselves in a position where they have to draft players on rookie contracts to contribute.
Quinshon Judkins showed promise in his rookie season, but he has not looked the same this season. He is adjusting to rushing from the shotgun position and with experience, he will get better. The backup at the beginning season was Dylan Sampson, but he got injured early in the first game of the season. He is expected to be back and the Browns should wait and find out what they have in a fully healthy position group.
Taylor cannot bring his offensive line with him to Cleveland , which would help as the Browns’ unit has failed to make any lanes for the running backs. Cleveland’s offensive line has only played six games together with a new head coach, offensive coordinator, and line coach. The rushing attack is not a finished product and there is still plenty of time for improvement without having to drain the resources by trading for Taylor.
If the Browns wish to add to the room then they have other options. Saquon Barkley may be on the trading block from the Philadelphia Eagles, and the price tag would be less for him. The compensation would still be a valuable pick and he has struggled with injuries as he only has 36 carries this season.
While the 4-2 start has been surprising, the roster is still very young and Watson has not been good for any length of time in a game. A deep playoff run is unlikely for this season and running backs’ health is iffy from year to year. The Browns are better off staying put or adding a running back that will split carries. The potential for Cleveland’s running backs has not been touched, and the offense will benefit when the group is full and healthy.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Browns’ Latest Injury Update Raises Concerns Ahead of Titans Matchup
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are missing several notable players from practice ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Tennessee Titans . Camryn Justice of News 5 reported on six total players expected to be out for Wednesday practice:
#Browns players not expected to practice today due to injury: Kalia Davis (quad) Grant Delpit (concussion, shoulder) Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) Elgton Jenkins (knee) Teven Jenkins (back) Carson Schwesinger (ankle)
Grant Delpit is one of the Browns' key defensive players and was injured after being accidentally struck by teammate Derek Barnett during a tackle attempt on Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Delpit is listed as having a shoulder injury as well as a concussion.
Grant Delpit Took A Hard Hit To The Head As He Was Going In For The Tackle. This Definitely Does Not Look Good. Hope He’s All Good. Scary Moment. 😬 pic.twitter.com/u3VMCaBu40
Delpit is the most uncertain name on the Browns' injury report, as he sustained the concussion during Sunday's matchup against Baltimore. The NFL's concussion protocol can be difficult to navigate, and his absence from Wednesday's practice raises questions about his availability this Sunday.
Delpit would be a big miss for the Browns, with one interception, one sack, and 25 combined tackles this year. Luckily for the Browns, they added depth at safety in the draft, and rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to emerge in recent weeks, with 24 tackles and just two receptions allowed this season. The Browns have some insurance at the position while Delpit works toward a return.
Carson Schwesinger has been a defensive star for the Browns this season. Unfortunately, Schwesinger has been dealing with an ankle injury in recent weeks. The injury kept him out of practice most of last week ahead of the Ravens matchup, and he was limited in Friday's final practice.
With Schwesinger missing Wednesday's practice, the Browns appear to be taking a similar approach this week. However, if his performance against the Ravens is any indication, Schwesinger should be available against the Titans.
Elgton Jenkins has anchored the Browns' offensive line at center this season and has been a bright spot for the position group. Jenkins was listed with a knee injury ahead of Wednesday's practice after playing every offensive snap against the Ravens in Week 6.
While his absence is worth monitoring, Jenkins' ability to play through last week's matchup is encouraging. For now, the Browns will hope the injury remains a practice concern rather than one that affects his availability on Sunday.
The Browns' injury report remains long, but it shows some encouraging signs compared to last week's report ahead of the Ravens matchup. Mason Graham and Quinshon Judkins, who both missed the Ravens game, returned to practice, with signs pointing to both potentially returning to action against the Titans.
#Browns DT Mason Graham continued practicing today as he aims to return this week from the MCL sprain and ankle sprain he sustained in Week 4. pic.twitter.com/fSpap4sJZ2
While Delpit's status is concerning, the team has some depth at safety to help offset a potential absence. Meanwhile, Schwesinger and Jenkins have shown they can play through injuries, giving Cleveland reason to be optimistic heading into Sunday's matchup.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: How Many More Wins Can We Expect from the Browns after Week 6?
full_text:
So far in 2026, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people. Quite frankly, even Browns fans themselves thought they were in for another 3-4-win season that sets them up for yet another high draft pick in 2027.
However, head coach Todd Monken has turned the team around in just his first season. Through six weeks, they have been winners four times already.
At this pace, the Browns can make the playoffs. But how far can the Browns really go? Let's take a look at the remainder of the season for Cleveland by breaking it down into three segments.
Starting with the Titans matchup, the Browns are set for three straight road games.
Realistically, the Browns need to try and win two out of three games here. Of course, it would be nice to win all three, winning in Pittsburgh has not been historically easy for the Browns.
As for the Titans and Saints matchups, these are two games the Browns need to make sure they win. Credit to New Orleans and Tennessee, but going into each matchup, the Browns are the better team.
Let's say the Browns hypothetically win two out of three. That would put their record at 6-3 before heading into the best part of their schedule.
After New Orleans, the Browns are set up for success being at home for five straight weeks.
Starting off against the Texans, this is a tough game. CJ Stroud is playing some of his best football and their defense is a top unit in the league. However, this is still weeks away, and you never know what will change by then.
After Week 10, the Browns got lucky with a later bye week this season. Coming out of it, you get the Raiders, Bengals, and Falcons.
Against Las Vegas, the Browns should be able to shut down the Raider offense and put some points on the board against their defense. While it may be close, this is one the Browns need to win.
Your first place 4-2 #Browns ' upcoming schedule: Week 7 @ Titans (1-5) Week 8 @ Steelers (4-2) Week 9 @ Saints (2-4) Week 10 vs. Texans (2-4) Week 11 BYE Week 12 vs. Raiders (3-3) #DawgPound
Following that game, the Bengals come to town for the first battle of Ohio in 2026. If they beat the Raiders, maybe some momentum can carry over to what will be a crucial divisional matchup.
Then, the game with the biggest storyline. The Atlanta Falcons, led by former Browns head coach Kevin Stefanski, come to play in Week 14. Simply put, the Browns MUST win this one.
Going back to our hypotheticals, let's say the Browns go 2-2 in this stretch. 8-5 would most likely put them somewhere in contention for a wildcard spot, making the final four weeks the biggest yet.
Hopefully, the Browns learned what needs to change to win in MetLife Stadium. That's where they will play for the second time this season when they travel to take on the New York Giants.
Let's say the Browns can get a huge win in Week 15 against the Giants. That leads them straight into their second Ravens matchup the following week.
Something that is pretty clear with the AFC North is that home games give each team an incredible boost. The Browns will most likely struggle in both late divisional games against the Ravens and Bengals.
If the Browns drop one in Baltimore, they then play their final home game against the Colts. Who knows what the season will look like by then, but there could be a serious chance that with a win against Indianapolis, Week 18 in Cincinatti is a potential game for the division title.
Regardless of division, let's say the Browns once again go 2-2 dropping both AFC North matchups. Our hypothetical record is now 10-7, which may be enough to sneak into the playoffs.
Overall, the road to making the postseason for the first time since 2023 is not horrible on paper.
The important thing for Cleveland is to keep their focus on one game at a time, and keep stacking up wins.
For the NFL's second-youngest team, learning how to win going forward is what matters the most.

title: Browns Reveal Promising Update on Mason Graham Following Lower-Body Injury
full_text:
Even without Mason Graham, the Cleveland Browns' defense is elite.
And whenever he does ultimately return, there's a chance that the Browns get even better.
Fortunately, on Wednesday, Oct. 21, the Browns announced that Graham is getting healthier by the day. He is currently recovering from an ankle and knee injury he suffered in the Browns' Thursday Night Football clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
According to head coach Todd Monken, Graham wanted to play last weekend in the Browns' Week 6 clash with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, he ultimately wasn't able to suit up.
He did share, though, that in the Browns' Sunday meeting with the Tennessee Titans , he should be ready to go.
"I think so. He wanted to go [vs. Baltimore]. He played for Jesse [Minter] at Michigan," Monken said. "He loves football. I think he's thankful and I am thankful it wasn't worse. Pretty good chance we will have him this week."
Browns coach Todd Monken said DT Mason Graham wanted to play last Sunday against the Ravens and his former coach at Michigan, Jesse Minter. "I think there's a pretty good chance we'll have him this week."
And it is obvious that the 23-year-old loves the game.
He made an incredible jump from his rookie campaign, becoming a much more impactful defender.
In his rookie season, he was named to the All-Rookie team by the Pro Football Writers of America , even though he only recorded 0.5 sacks, 49 tackles, seven for a loss and four quarterback hits.
This year, across the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, he was one of the most dominant rushers in the league before injury. He totaled 15 combined tackles, seven of which were solo, and four sacks . His presence in the backfield led to 33 yards lost for opposing quarterbacks when he was credited with the sack.
That type of pressure and ability to back an offense up is incredibly important.
But even when he has been kept off the field, the Browns have had players step up to fill his void.
Maliek Collins is up to 3.5 sacks and five tackles for a loss this season, while Isaiah McGuire sits not far behind at 3.0 sacks and five tackles for a loss. Alongside Collins and McGuire, Adin Huntington, Sam Kamara and Mike Hall Jr. have put in the work, each totaling a sack or more as well.
In Sunday's win, the Browns' run defense had a 97th percentile EPA/rush allowed performance and a 98th percentile designed rushing success rate allowed performance. Their total Defense Impact Metric, according to Pro Football Focus, has them ranked within the Top 5 in the league.
They also rank first in tackles for a loss, fewest rushing touchdowns allowed and second in total sacks.
When Graham returns, that unit will be even better, with those who have filled his spot being warmed up now.
There are just a few more days for Graham to get cleared for this weekend, and even if he just plays on limited snaps, it will be a nice bump for the defense to try and lead the Browns to a 5-2 record.
The Browns and Titans will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville this Sunday.

title: Cowboys’ Easy Remaining Schedule Could Fuel Much-Needed Turnaround
full_text:
A 2-4 start for the Dallas Cowboys has dampened the mood surrounding the team following an offseason full of hype.
The Cowboys entered the year as one of the more impressive offenses and their moves on defense, including the hiring of first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker , made them one of the teams to watch in the NFC. They were also considered a legitimate contender for the NFC East title.
Despite the slow start, however, Jerry Jones remains optimistic. The owner and general manager is still supportive of head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who is suddenly feeling the heat , and said he's willing to make moves at the trade deadline to salvage the season.
Some might wonder if it's wise to spend future assets on more players this season, given the fact that the struggles in Dallas seem to be with coaching more so than with the personnel. That said, it's easy to see why Jones isn't ready to punt on this season when you look at the remaining schedule.
The Cowboys, who will visit the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7, have the third easiest remaining schedule. Only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Jacksonville Jaguars have a softer slate of games than Dallas for the remainder of the year.
Remaining Strength of Schedule 1. MIN --- hardest --- 2. ATL 3. MIA ... 30. DAL 31. TB 32. JAX --- easiest ---- pic.twitter.com/3ZNbIcafwe
As we all know, this doesn't guarantee anything for the Cowboys. They already had one wildly disappointing game in which they were favored this season, losing at home to Tampa Bay in Week 5. The Bucs were not only 0-4 at the time, but they were starting undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels.
That said, the games coming up are winnable and the Cowboys happen to play in a historically bad NFC East . The talent on their team, coupled with this schedule means they should be able to pull off the division title. If not, it could spell the end for Coach Schotty.

title: Cowboys Matched With Titans For Potential Trade to Add to Injury-Plagued Position
full_text:
One analyst believes the Dallas Cowboys and Tennessee Titans are potential trade partners.
The idea comes from The Athletic's Daniel Popper , who tabbed 50 players he believes could be on the trade block ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.
One of those players was Titans linebacker Cody Barton, who Popper sees as a fit with the Cowboys.
"Barton is in the second year of a three-year deal he signed with the Titans in 2025. He does not have any guaranteed money after this year, and the Titans would take on only a $1.72 million dead-money charge in 2027 if they traded him before the deadline," he said. "Barton is not a fast linebacker from sideline to sideline. But he is an instinctive coverage player."
With the Titans in the midst of yet another disappointing season as they continue to try and rebuild, Tennessee could sell off anything that isn't nailed down.
Barton might be one of those guys. He's 30 years old and doesn't figure to have much of a future in Nashville. He will also be on the final year of his contract in 2027 and Tennessee could end up cutting him, so trading him now makes even more sense.
If the Cowboys can keep the trio of DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters and Jaishawn Barham healthy, they should be in good shape.
However, that has proven difficult over six games, as Overshown has missed five due to injury and Winters is now hurt with an Achilles issue and is expected to sit out at least one game.
If injuries continue to be an issue at the position, the Cowboys could very well explore a minor trade for a linebacker, which is what dealing for Barton would amount to.
Barton doesn't do anything at an elite level, but he's still a solid, starting-caliber linebacker who would be an adequate addition should the Cowboys have a need.
According to Pro Football Focus , Barton has respectable grades of 62.6 overall, 60.0 in run defense, 56.4 in tackling, 66.9 in the pass-rush and 61.7 in coverage.
When it comes to compensation, Barton will be cheap. He'll likely fetch no better than a fifth-round pick for Tennessee.
Linebacker certainly isn't at the top of the list of needs Dallas has with a little over two weeks left until the trade deadline, but as we know, things can change quickly in the NFL, and that's especially true at the linebacker position in Dallas, which has had a terrible run of bad luck when it comes to injuries.

title: Cowboys Legend Troy Aikman Opens Door to Potential Dallas Return
full_text:
There's been a lot going on with Troy Aikman as of late as the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback's contract with ESPN is up after the year . Aikman sounds as though he might be ready for something different after spending the past 25 years as a broadcaster.
One common theory is that Aikman is itching for a front office role, and he got a taste of that this year as he spent time as a consultant with the Miami Dolphins .
If he were to move into such a role, it feels like a natural fit for him to join the Cowboys, a team he led to three Super Bowls during his playing career. It's tough to see Jerry and Stephen Jones welcoming Aikman, since they like to do everything themselves, but Aikman sounds as though he would be open to the idea.
While speaking with Mike Fisher , Aikman discussed his feelings about a reunion. He admitted there might not be an opportunity, but said he would take a look at that option if Jerry Jones was open to a conversation.
"I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don't know if there ever would be an opportunity," Aikman said . "But if Jerry came to me and felt in his heart that I could lend some services that would help make them better, I'd have a hard time not taking a good look at that."
Earlier this week, Jones was asked about Aikman's future beyond broadcasting and said there's no area (other than returning to the field) where Aikman wouldn't succeed .
"No, I think when I say no, Troy is very capable. And he's so really relatively speaking, he's in his youth, as careers go. And he's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area short of getting back out on the field. I don't know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into," Jones said.
While it would be a welcome change for fans, we shouldn't get our hopes up. The Jones family has made themselves front and center for every decision. They do lean heavily on vice president of player personnel Will McClay, but McClay is often working in the background. That wouldn't be the case with Aikman, who could command plenty of attention, which is something the Jones family might not be willing to welcome.

title: Former NFL Star Rips 'Puppet' Brian Schottenheimer for Criticizing George Pickens
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer did something out of the norm this week when he criticized wide receiver George Pickens amid concerns about his effort.
Schottenheimer's criticism was centered around Pickens' run-blocking, which he feels can be better.
It was unusual for the Cowboys coach to take that approach, as Schottenheimer normally defends Pickens when he's taking heat.
"He needs to understand that he impacts us in the running game as well," Schotty said of Pickens, per WFAA's Ed Werder. "You know, he's got to do the same thing in the run game — picking up safeties and blocking corners — just like Javonte does, picking up blitzes so he can catch balls. That's part of the team-first mindset, and GP does understand that. And you know when he's going, they're going to play soft inside. When he's not going, the safety gets pretty good runs at our backs, and that's going to improve.”
Former NFL star wide receiver Chad Ochocinco ripped the Cowboys coach, calling him a puppet and accusing him of deflecting from his own and his team's overall failures.
"And you know why he did that? Trying to take the pressure off his a** because he understood using Pickens name, it would stick," Ochocinco said on the Night Cap podcast.
"Let's address the real problems. Your god**** defense. It ain't got nothing to do with (Pickens) at all," he added. "You can't stop the run, you can't stop the pass. Why you talking about what George Pickens is doing on offense when your Achilles heel, what you need to do is worry about your defense. You need to be calling them out."
Johnson went on to call Schottenheimer a "puppet" and said he's just trying to "get the heat off your back" by criticizing Pickens. He also believes Schottenheimer is going to get fired if he loses three more games.
There's a few things that are hard to argue with here, and one of them is the "puppet" label on Schottenheimer, which we agree with.
He might be calling the plays, but that's about all of the shots that Schottenheimer is calling. He's in that job specifically because he doesn't care about Jerry Jones being as heavily involved as he is, which has proven to be a recipe for failure for three decades now.
While Ocho is also right about the defense being the bigger issue for the Cowboys, his co-hosts, Shannon Sharpe and Joe Johnson, were quick to point out that the offense has been an issue lately , also, which is certainly true given the 29 points the team has scored in the past two games.
That's another problem that falls on Schottenheimer's shoulders as the play-caller. He just has not been good, which leaves Dallas with two inadequate play-callers when we include defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
Nobody is going to sit here and say that Pickens doesn't deserve some criticism for effort issues, and especially in run-blocking, but so do a lot of guys on the Cowboys, as DeMarcus Ware and Ben DiNucci have pointed out recently .
Not to mention, Pickens is hardly the biggest issue the Cowboys have and there are much bigger problems Schottenheimer needs to be calling out publicly, like his defense, so example.
To his credit, Pickens took the diplomatic road in his response to Schottenheimer's criticism .
“I feel like, like I said, as a team, I feel like run, pass, a lot of stuff, you know what I mean? One week, it was you guys were saying defense, one week you’re saying this," Pickens said to reporters.
"I feel like if you narrow the comments down, you’re talking about the team. So most definitely, I feel like as a team, just keep improving," he added.
And Pickens is right. There is no one-man solution to the Cowboys' issues, at least when it comes to the players.
It's going to take a total team effort to save this sinking ship.

title: Former Cowboys Star Trevon Diggs Released From Seahawks Practice Squad
full_text:
Trevon Diggs was once known as a premier cornerback in the NFL. A second-round pick for the Dallas Cowboys in 2020 out of Alabama, Diggs led the league with 11 interceptions during his second season in the league.
He continued to develop as an overall cornerback, and was rewarded with a five-year, $97 million extension in 2023. Unfortunately, he was never able to live up to that contract and was released last season.
Diggs was claimed by the Green Bay Packers, but was released in January. This season, he was signed to the Seattle Seahawks practice squad in August and was elevated to the active roster for three games, but played in just 21 total snaps . On Friday, he was released, making it the third time since December 2025.
Diggs played just two games after signing his extension with Dallas before suffering a torn ACL in practice. He was able to return to the field in 2024, but played just 11 games with continued knee problems .
There were concerns from the front office on how Diggs rehabbed, as the former Pro Bowler elected to work away from the team. That led to the Cowboys slashing $500,000 from his salary due to a clause in his contract.
Diggs played in just eight games that season with the Cowboys, and was released following a Christmas Day win over the Washington Commanders. Diggs, who had family in the area, asked to stay in D.C. after the game, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer declined, saying he needed to travel back with the team. Diggs stayed behind anyway, and was let go.
Diggs might not have been in Seattle long, but he made a lasting impression, albeit not for the right reasons.
While playing against the San Francisco 49ers, Diggs decided to trash talke Mike Evans, who had a hilarious response. Evans, who had 113 yards and a touchdown on seven receptions looked back at Diggs and then turned him around to read the name on his jersey.
Mike Evans and Trevon Diggs talking after the play 👀 (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/6pI64V6qBW
It's tough to see Diggs getting too many opportunities now that he's been unable to find a role with two franchises after being let go by the Cowboys.
