title: Cowboys' Christian Parker is All Business and No Feelings for Homecoming vs. Eagles
full_text:
When the Dallas Cowboys take on the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, it will be Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker's first game back in his old stomping grounds.
Prior to taking the Cowboys' defensive coordinator job , Parker was the Eagles' passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach, working under Philly's defensive coordinator, Vic Fangio.
Before that, Parker also worked under Fangio in 2021, when Fangio was the Denver Broncos' head coach and Parker was Denver's defensive backs coach.
When asked about going back to his old home at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday night, Parker made it clear he's all business and it's just another divisional matchup for him.
"It's just another division game," Parker stated , per Patrik Walker of DallasCowboys.com. "It's another divisional opponent and another task for us as a team."
There's a lot riding on this game for Parker and the Cowboys, and not just because it's an NFC East matchup.
Dallas' defense has been one of the worst in the NFL through six games. The Cowboys rank 30th in total yards allowed per game, 23rd in passing yards, 32nd in rushing yards and 25th in points.
As a result, Parker, who has looked overmatched in his first season as a defensive play-caller, is already on the hot seat , at least when it comes to Cowboys fans and analysts. Things have been so bad that Dallas even brought in veteran defensive coach Mike Pettine as a consultant to help Parker out.
Despite all of the struggles, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones and others continue to express confidence in Parker .
As bad as the Cowboys have been, the Eagles might be in a worse spot after it was revealed Jalen Hurts would miss the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs.
With the Eagles in dire straits and the Cowboys sitting at 2-4, they cannot lose this game, but that remains a very real possibility given what we've witnessed from Dallas this season.
Parker worked under the Eagles' defensive coordinator for three seasons (one in Denver, two in Philly) before taking the job in Dallas.
Fangio was asked during the week if he has been in touch with his former assistant lately. Fangio said the two have not spoken around the first or second game of the regular season.
“No. We talked right before training camp started, had a text exchange either after the first or second game, but that's been the extent of it. Makes it a little different being in the same division," he said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic .
Upon taking the job, it was obvious to point out that Parker's defense might look a lot like Fangio's because he worked under the high-profile defensive coach for a few seasons.
However, Parker made it clear he wanted the Cowboys' defense to have its own identity .
"This is our defense. I don't want it to be called the Eagles defense or Vic (Fangio's) defense. This is going to be ours. We've been real intentional about going about that process from the language that we use, the work flow that we have and everything else. It's been real fun," Parker said back in May.
While Parker's defense has looked a lot like Fangio's, the results have not been good at all and, at this rate, he might not be around for another season if things don't turn around the rest of the way.

title: Cowboys Legend's Troubling Assessment of Dallas' Defense Points to Culture Problem
full_text:
There are a laundry list of issues on the Dallas Cowboys' defense in 2026, so it's impossible to point to just one thing and say that's the cause of their struggles.
The two biggest issues are players simply underperforming, and the coaching, as defensive coordinator Christian Parker simply doesn't have any answers for everything that plagues the unit.
But Cowboys legend DeMarcus Ware thinks the issues on defense are deeper than just those two things.
He also believes Cowboys defenders don't have the right attitude, especially in the trenches, and he questions the team's effort, ego, heart and pride.
"“When I played and there were problems, the first thing we did was how do we control the trenches?" Ware said on 96.7 The Ticket. "That comes down to mentality. That’s something that’s free. It’s the effort and attitude of the team. That’s something that can be changed, that’s not a quantitative thing. It’s a heart thing, a pride thing, an ego thing these guys have to sort of turn up. Yes, a lot of people are saying their season is over, but in the locker room there has to be a mentality shift to say we still got it.”
Ware also admitted that if the Cowboys lose to the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, the season is likely over.
“If the Dallas Cowboys can win this game, it’s going to be that momentum builder. If they lose this game, and you go to 2-5, to be honest with you, the season is probably over … the season can be over if you lose this football game. Because you’re going to lose your morale and your confidence is gone," Ware said . “It’s a must-win football game.”
We completely agree with Ware. Even in a terrible NFC East , it feels like Dallas' season is already on life support, so a loss could be the death blow.
Ware is the second former Cowboys player to question the team's effort .
Former Dallas quarterback Ben DiNucci did the same, except he focused on the offensive side of the ball.
"You can’t turn on the Cowboys tape from last night and tell me guys on that offense are giving 100%," DiNucci said . "Lazy, no attention to details, no creativity with play calls."
Yes, a lack of effort is certainly on the players, but an issue like that starts with the culture of the team, and the first person to blame for a lackluster culture is the head coach.
So, this is on the shoulders of Brian Schottenheimer mostly, but also on Parker, who clearly isn't doing a good enough job motivating his players on defense.
That could be a result of several things, but the biggest issue may be that Cowboys players simply don't have any faith in the staff, and we wouldn't blame them one bit if that's the case.
Schottenheimer and Parker have been terrible with play-calling and there is no sign they're capable of improving.
And until they do that, there is no hope for the Cowboys to turn things around.

title: Cowboys Get Much-Needed Secondary Reinforcements With Safety Return
full_text:
P.J. Locke was signed by the Dallas Cowboys this offseason and was seen as a potential free agency steal. While Locke has never been known as an elite defender, he's a versatile player who can line up at either safety position and has played in the slot.
More importantly, he had experience working with defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Locke was on the Denver Broncos where Parker spent two seasons as his defensive backs coach. That experience was on display during training camp as Locke was continually on the same page as Parker.
Unfortunately, Locke was only able to play in two games so far this season after suffering a torn plantar fascia in Week 2 against the Washington Commanders. That injury forced the Cowboys to send Locke to the IR , although he was designated to return. Now as they prepare for Week 7, Locke is nearing a return and had his 21-day practice window opened on Friday .
By opening his window, the Cowboys will be able to get Locke back on the practice field but he won't count against the 53-man roster. They will have 21 days to decide if they want to move him to the active roster, or send him to the season-ending IR. It seems unlikely Locke will play against the Eagles on Monday Night Football, but it's still encouraging to see some of their defensive players return to practice.
Locke isn't the only player returning to the Dallas defense. They already expect starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown to be on the field for the first time since Week 1 after suffering a hamstring injury.
In addition to the good news for Overshown, Dallas saw some major progress from Cobie Durant. The veteran cornerback returned to practice for the first time since suffering an injury in Week 2, after being on the wrong end of some friendly-fire .
Durant was one of the few defensive backs playing well and his return could be a major boost, especially now that the Cowboys added Joey Porter Jr., who has been lights out since arriving.
In addition to these updates, the Cowboys also opened the 21-day practice window for outside linebacker Marist Liufau , who suffered a fractured forearm during the preseason finale. He has yet to play in the regular season in his new role, making him a question mark on the base defense. That said, Liufau is a stud on special teams and could give that unit a shot in the arm.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Reveals Future of Play-Calling Duties Amid Cowboys Struggles
full_text:
Two consecutive losses have the Dallas Cowboys entering Week 7 with a record of 2-4 and plenty of questions to answer. Many of those questions are focused on their defensive performance, which has been an issue for head coach Brian Schottenheimer since taking the job last season.
Following their latest defeats, Schottenheimer finds himself answering some unfamiliar questions as well. His offense, which was one of the best in the league last year, has looked inept during losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers.
That had Coach Schotty being asked about some potentially drastic changes. He was on 105.3 The Fan and was asked if he has considered giving up play-calling duties. Schottenheimer said he would fix the issues and plans to evaluate everything. That said, he was quick to shut down that idea, emphatically answering, “ No, absolutely not .”
Schottenheimer has had some brilliant moments calling plays, but the past two weeks have been tough to watch. That includes the Cowboys abandoning the run during their Week 6 loss to the Packers, something that Schottenheimer defended by saying they were attacking through the air due to the defensive formation .
Schottenheimer expressed confidence in their offense as well. While admitting they haven't played well during their past two games, he says they're still the same team from a year ago. He also said he is " an elite play-caller ."
“I have incredible confidence in our offense. We have not played well the last two weeks, we have addressed a lot of the reasons why. We haven’t changed who we are. We are still a good explosive offense with weapons. We can hurt you a lot of different ways. I certainly haven’t lost the ability to call plays. I’m an elite play-caller in this league, and it can change around quickly.”
Dallas is paying a lot for their offense, with Dak Prescott under contract for $60 million per season, CeeDee Lamb averaging $34 million, and George Pickens at $27.3 million on the franchise tag . Beyond that, players such as Tyler Smith, Javonte Williams, and Jake Ferguson all have signed extension recently.
Talent on offense is clearly not the issue in Dallas, which is why it's fair to ask Schottenheimer the tough questions. It's also fair for him to say he wants to hold onto those duties, especially given the success he had in 2025. Now, it's on the head coach to make good on his "elite" claim and put together a strong outing against the Eagles on Monday Night Football.

title: Cowboys & Jets Paired as Logical Trade Partners With Dallas' Need For Pass-Rush Juice
full_text:
We're only six games into the 2026 campaign and it already feels like the Dallas Cowboys' season is on life support.
Not only has the defense been terrible despite a massive overhaul , but the offense has struggled badly the last few weeks, also, and that only makes the outlook for Dallas more bleak.
There is little hope for a turnaround, especially given the fact that head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker appear to be completely in over their heads .
But we don't anticipate owner Jerry Jones going down without a fight. As a result, we anticipate Dallas making a move at the trade deadline as a last-ditch effort to try and save the season.
Daniel Popper of The Athletic has listed his 50 trade candidates going into the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10 and among them is New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald, who Popper believes could be a good fit for the Cowboys.
"The Jets have depth at edge rusher, and rookie David Bailey is emerging, though free-agent addition Joseph Ossai is now dealing with an ankle injury," Popper wrote.
"McDonald is a twitchy rusher with some diversity in his attack, including an inside spin move," he added.
Citing McDonald as a potential trade candidate makes sense for multiple reasons.
Popper pointed to the additions the Jets made at edge rusher this past offseason, with the team adding Joseph Ossai, David Bailey and Kingsley Enagbare, which has led to less snaps for the 2023 first-round pick. The Jets clearly have sufficient depth that will enable them to unload McDonald.
McDonald isn't attached to the current regime, either and only has one more year left on his contract after 2026. The Jets could also use more draft capital as they continue to go through their rebuild and McDonald could fetch a nice return from teams needing edge rusher help.
Given the sorry state of affairs in the Cowboys' edge rushers room, any player at the position with production would be welcomed.
Over six games, the Cowboys have gotten just 2.5 sack out of their edge rushers, which is well below expectations.
McDonald has two sacks in just 47% of snaps this season, which is nearly more than what the Cowboys' entire edge rushers room has combined.
McDonald has also shown he's capable of more. Over 32 games the past two years, McDonald has tallied 18.5 sacks, including a career-high 10.5 in 2024. He posted eight in 2025 despite his missing two games due to injury.
We would love to see the Cowboys add an elite edge rusher at the deadline because that's the kind of talent infusion this pathetic defense and pass-rush needs .
However, we know how difficult it is to acquire those guys and chances are there won't be one available. Knowing that, Dallas must settle for the next tier and McDonald qualifies as being included in that group.
If he can be had, Jones and the Cowboys should pull the trigger on a trade for McDonald, who can help them the rest of this season and next, at least.

title: Broncos Trade Deadline: 5 Realistic Targets to Move the Needle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos still have three games to go between now and the November 10 NFL trade deadline .
The Broncos have some apparent needs, including running back and offensive line, but the next three weeks could reshape the conversation. If the return of rookie running back Jonah Coleman sparks the Broncos' ground game and J.K. Dobbins snaps out of his funk, the team could be more than content to stand pat at the deadline.
This team did face a ridiculous initial six-game schedule, which could explain why the Broncos' offensive line has looked so lackluster, especially as run blockers. With the schedule easing up for the foreseeable future, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the starting five rubber-band back into the top-five status it had entering the 2026 season.
Some would point to tight end as a need, and while I certainly wouldn't disagree, it doesn't feel like the Broncos see it that way. Even if they did, Bo Nix's middle-of-the-field avoidance in the passing game would make the pursuit of a pass-catching tight end pointless, though the Broncos could still use an upgrade at the Y.
Looking around the league, there are five realistic trade options the Broncos could consider. This is an already well-built veteran roster, so any trade acquisition would have to represent a clear upgrade over what Denver already has at that position.
Let's break down these five players.
The Indianapolis Colts could be poised to hold a fire sale at the trade deadline, having just fired GM Chris Ballard amid the team's disappointing 2-4 start. For now, the Colts are retaining head coach Shane Steichen, but if he survives into next season, this team's next GM could be looking to orchestrate a reboot, which will require draft assets.
Indy's best personnel resources could be put on the trade block. Taylor is certainly one of them.
Although his yards-per-carry average is currently at a career low (4.0), Taylor already has 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. He just signed a two-year, $44 million deal before the season started, so the Broncos would have to ensure they could fit his contract under the salary cap.
If Taylor was suddenly traded to Denver, Sean Payton would have to consider putting Bo Nix under center more often, at least on first and second down, instead of in the shotgun. Taylor needs that head of steam that the under-center offense can offer a ball-carrier.
Taylor is one of the NFL's best and most prolific running backs, and while it wouldn't be cheap to acquire him, I doubt it would cost the Broncos anywhere near as much as the San Francisco 49ers once gave to the Carolina Panthers for Christian McCaffrey. Taylor will turn 28 in January and he has a  lot of mileage on his three-time Pro Bowl tires.
Imagine for a moment — if you will — a Broncos offensive line that features Nelson at left guard and Quinn Meinerz at right guard. That would be one heck of a way to spark a run game. Nelson is playing on an expiring contract, which makes him an even more realistic trade candidate for the Colts.
That also helps make Nelson realistic for the Broncos, but the team would have to rethink it's long-term strategy at left guard. Current starter, Ben Powers, is expected to depart in free agency next year, and the Broncos drafted Kage Casey in the fourth round this past spring with an eye on being the future at left guard.
Casey had a really good summer, but he's been a healthy scratch thus far. Would Denver want to give up draft capital and sign a proven All-Pro like Nelson to a lucrative multi-year contract rather than follow through on its plan to develop Casey?
That's the rub, but when it comes to this offensive line's failure to launch, Powers is the least to blame of Denver's trio of culprits. Center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey have been far more problematic, both as run and pass blockers.
As for Nelson, giving up a second-round pick would likely get the job done, but if the market heats up for his services, it wouldn't be a shock to see the Colts ask for more. He's going to be 31 next year, but he's coming off his eighth straight Pro Bowl nod and was a second-team All-Pro last season (for the third time in his career). He's also a three-time first-team All-Pro.
Irving has one more year left on his contract, but the Bucs are headed in the wrong direction. He's rushed for 452 yards and two touchdowns this season, averaging a healthy 4.7 yards per carry.
Irving was Nix's teammate at Oregon for two years, and they entered the NFL draft together in 2024. Nix went to Denver in Round 1 while Irving landed in Tampa in Round 4. They made a lot of hay together in Oregon, so I'd imagine they could hit the ground running as pros.
Irving is only 24, and while he rushed for 1,122 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, injuries caused him to finish with half that production in Year 2. He's appeared in every game this season for Tampa, though.
Depending on Tampa's desparation, I would start with a third-round pick for Irving's services. If the Bucs wanted a second-rounder, it might be a bridge too far, given that Denver could find a good running back in the draft next spring. But that wouldn't help them in the present.
While we're talking potential fire sales, Vea has to be in the conversation of realistic targets. He asked for a trade this past summer, but instead of dealing him, the Bucs gave him a one-year, $30 million extension.
The Broncos' defensive line has been okay this season, but when it comes to stopping the run, they've struggled. Only one team has been worse against the run, and one of Denver's biggest issues is the lack of mass up front.
The 6-foot-4, 347-pound Vea would be an immediate solution. The problem? He's about to turn 32 in February, so any team interested in his services would have to be confident that he has plenty left in the tank.
If a third-round pick would get it done, I'd be on the phone right now with the Bucs. At least to check on the possibility.
Barkley has been banged up this year, but the Eagles could be poised to sell off some of their top assets, being in a similar situation as the Colts, minus the firing of their general manager. Barkley turns 30 in February, so any team acquiring him would have to verify his health and feel confident in his long-term viability.
Barkley is under contract for two more years, which could be advantageous for the Broncos. That would give them the chance to make use of his talents now, and give them time to determine whether he's worth re-signing beyond 2028 when his contract expires.
When Barkley is healthy and in the zone, there's no better running back in the NFL. But it would probably take a second-round pick plus perhaps a 2028 Day 3 selection to pry him off Philly's hands.

title: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Coleman & Hufanga
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are coming off a "mini-bye" — three extra days of rest and preparation between their Week 6 Thursday night game and Sunday's road trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals . Denver's actual bye isn't until Week 10.
Given the gauntlet of opponents the Broncos faced to get to 4-2, they earned those three days. The question is whether that chance to breathe gave Sean Payton enough time to tweak the Broncos' offense, dig Bo Nix out of his slump, and get the run game firing on all cylinders.
This matchup with the Cardinals could answer that question and more, given that they rank bottom 10 in net yards and points allowed. It's a road game, and the Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Los Angeles Rams, but if Nix and Payton's offense can't get right against the NFL's second-worst scoring defense, it will only deepen doubts that the Broncos will ever turn the ship around this season.
On Friday, the Broncos and Cardinals dropped their final Week 7 injury reports. Let's break them down.
The Broncos are starting to get healthier. That may be a relative term, given that three players have been ruled out, but it's more about the caliber of players returning.
Surtain is questionable after returning to practice on Wednesday . He was limited all three days this week, so if he's fully healthy, he'll play. If not, the Broncos will be wise and wait until Week 8 to insert him back into the lineup.
Coleman is also listed as questionable, but only because Sean Payton wants Arizona to wonder for as long as possible whether the Broncos will actually activate their rookie running back. The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from injured reserve earlier this week.
It's great to see Moss back to full participation. And Waddle has been fully cleared, though he was limited the first two days of the week.
Badie, Elliss, and Hufanga are out this week. It wouldn't be a surprise to see Badie and Elliss placed on IR to make room for Coleman and the return of veteran rush linebacker Jonathon Cooper, who's expected to come back from the commissioner's exempt list this week.
Friday's #DENvsAZ injury report: 📰 » https://t.co/mxd0ceioJ8 pic.twitter.com/yYI47WTUFp
Broncos fans won't get to see Love in action. Instead, it'll be Tyler Allgeier pounding the rock.
We'll be closely monitoring Baker's status on gameday. He did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, and was limited on Friday, but it'll be a surprise if he doesn't suit up.
The Cardinals are pretty banged up on both sides of the ball, but Seumalo, Duvernay, and Sweat are fully cleared to play.

title: Davis Webb Hints at What Jonah Coleman's Return Could Mean for Broncos
full_text:
The Denver Bronco's rushing offense ranks 26th in the NFL, averaging a paltry 84.2 yard per game. Granted, the Broncos have faced some top-tier defensive fronts in each of their six games thus far, but their rushing production has been nowhere near good enough.
With the schedule opening up now, there's a chance that the combined efforts of J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, which, again, have been lackluster thus far, could suddenly kick into high gear. But Dobbins doesn't seem to have the same burst he did last year, and the Broncos are reluctant to lean on Harvey much as a between-the-tackles runner.
Thankfully, Jonah Coleman is about to rejoin the Broncos' backfield, and his return from injured reserve could be the spark this run game needs to get up off the mat. The rookie hit injured reserve with an ankle injury after his Week 2 debut at Mile High — a victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars that Coleman helped seal with a touchdown and some tough running to close out the game.
The Broncos started Coleman's clock to return from IR this week, and he's been a full participant in practice each day. On Friday, offensive coordinator Davis Webb talked about Coleman's return and what the rookie brings to the table.
"First of all, he's very smart. He's handled the playbook very quickly from day one, rookie minicamp on," Webb said.
We've heard a lot about Coleman's football IQ and makeup since the Broncos drafted him in the fourth round. Head coach Sean Payton often says , "You don't feel a rookie," when asked about Coleman.
This carry at the end of the Jaguars game showcases Coleman's football smarts and presence of mind, avoiding the sideline to keep the clock ticking.
Jonah Coleman with a heads up play to stay in bounds and go down after picking up the first. pic.twitter.com/b3rjBgmChq
He's only touched the ball in one game as a pro, but Coleman was impressive in that Week 2 game , and we know he was playing hurt late when he busted off a pair of 12-yard runs to move the chains, kill the clock, and ice the victory for Denver.
"Every time he's gotten an opportunity, whether that be in a regular-season game, obviously the Jacksonville Jaguars game sticks out, the Atlanta Falcons game in the preseason sticks out," Webb said of Coleman. "So we're excited to get him back into the fold. I think the last couple weeks, our whole running back room is kind of slowly going up, turning in the right direction."
I believe Webb that the Broncos' ground game is trending upward, if for no other reason than Coleman's return. There are other signs of life, including Dobbins's running in the first half last week against the Seattle Seahawks and his late-game performance the week prior against the Los Angeles Chargers.
As in all things offense for the Broncos, though, the consistency just hasn't been there. We would be remiss to pin this run game's hopes solely on the return of a still-untested rookie, but including Coleman in the mix with Dobbins, sprinkled here and there with the odd Harvey carry, is the most substantial reason for hope this rushing offense has had in weeks.
When the Broncos officially activate Coleman, they'll have to make a corresponding roster cut. It's looking like that player could be fellow running back Tyler Badie, who suffered a thumb injury early in Week 6's game and never returned.
Badie has not practiced all week, and if the Broncos expect him to miss more than one or two games, they might opt to just bite the bullet and put him on IR. That would open up a spot for Coleman, and give Badie plenty of time to heal up. Either that, or the Broncos will have to cut a player at another position.
The rookie Jonah Coleman gives the Broncos a fourth quarter lead 🐴 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/wpnL52qLn8
The Broncos will travel to take on the Arizona Cardinals this week, whose rushing defense ranks 20th in the NFL. Arizona is allowing 120.8 yards per game on the ground, giving the Broncos a great opportunity to establish the run and keep the chains moving .
When it comes to things Payton likes to say, let's also not forget his comment about the quarterback position being the hardest to play without a running game. The Broncos had three extra days of preparation over their "mini-bye," and for the first time this season, they're not playing a battle-tested, playoff-caliber front seven.
The Broncos believe they have the horses in the running back room to field a competitive run game. We haven't seen much of one yet, but that initial six-game gauntlet of opponents was brutal and unprecedented in modern Broncos canon.
“We think it’s a deep room and a talented room," Payton said on Wednesday of the running backs. "So all those things are a positive.”
This is the week for a Bo Nix breakout . And that starts with a productive run game on the road at State Farm Stadium.

title: Bo Nix Breakout? Mile High Roundtable Picks Broncos vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are coming off a "mini-bye," looking to send a message this week that this offense shouldn't be written off.
Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert.
At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks.
That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals.
How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores.
Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert.
Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.”
Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Still, it will be nice to provide the fan base some hope.
Pick : Broncos 20, Cardinals16
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-2 : It's easy to think the Broncos will have their way with the Cardinals. But the Cardinals have shown they can challenge other teams , so it will be important for the Broncos' offense to come out strong. If the Broncos can do that and build a comfortable lead, the defense should be able to finish it from there, even with the Cardinals putting up a fight.
Pick : Broncos 23, Cardinals 16
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 3-3 : 10 days between games feels like forever, but reality is the Broncos have really hit their stride after their Thursday night game in each of the past two seasons. This won't be a dominant display, but it will be the first time this season both the Broncos' offense and defense play good complementary football, and Nix finds consistent success. Nix throws for a couple of touchdowns and rushes for another, giving fans some hope that he's close to being back.
Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 13
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 3-3 : If there was any opportunity to try to get the offense on track, it's this week against Arizona. Denver got the mini-bye, and Arizona's defense has allowed the most points in the league this season. Criticism of Nix is getting more intense by the minute, so it would be great to see him try to push the ball down the field and take chances against one of the worst defenses the league has to offer. I think he's gonna do it this week.
Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 17
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 2-4 : The Broncos are coming off a mini-bye, which frankly has come at a good time for a sputtering offense. Another week with Payton calling the plays again should be beneficial for Nix, but ultimately, the Broncos will have to play well to beat a tricky and plucky Cardinals team. The defense keys the win with a few takeaways off Jacoby Brissett, while the offense — just about — does enough to show some signs of life.
Pick : Broncos 24, Cardinals 14
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 2-4 : The Cardinals aren't pushovers and shouldn't be overlooked, but against their defense, the Broncos can get things jump-started. The Cardinals allow the second-highest explosive pass rate, which, despite ranking 18th in generating explosive offensive passing plays, is something the Broncos struggle with, as their 4.6% rate is 3% higher than Arizona's at 32nd. The Broncos' defense should be able to carry it enough to allow the offense to work things out, and this is the best opportunity for Nix and company to do that, similarly to the Dallas Cowboys game a season ago. The Broncos show progress in Arizona, and while they don't fix everything in a week, they do walk out with the win.
Pick : Broncos 18, Cardinals 10
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 2-4 : Nix and the Broncos have a chance to put up some major points against the Cardinals and their weak defense. The Cardinals have one of the worst defenses against the pass, teeing up Nix and the Broncos' receivers to breathe life into what has been a disappointing offensive start to the season. Defensively, if the Broncos can limit Trey McBride's impact, this should be their easiest win this season.

title: 5 Overlooked Broncos Who Could Swing the Cardinals Game
full_text:
Many are writing off the Arizona Cardinals as the Denver Broncos prepare to face them this Sunday, but they're a feisty team that shouldn't be overlooked.
The Cardinals' struggle areas mirror the Broncos', especially on defense and in the passing game. Today, we're looking at a handful of Broncos flying under the radar going into the desert.
The Broncos will want to get these players involved to improve the likelihood of walking out with a win .
Look, everyone is frustrated with the checkdowns and the designed throws to running backs, but the Cardinals struggle to run down the ball out of the backfield, especially in space. They're one of the worst teams at handling it, but Arizona's opponents have yet to fully exploit those issues.
Denver has a great matchup against the Cardinals' linebackers, and Harvey should be heavily used as both a receiver and a rusher.
The Cardinals are even worse at covering tight ends because of their linebacker issues. Evan Engram could be used here, but he would be more likely to draw Budda Baker (if he plays). Adam Trautman has struggled on a weekly basis, while Adkins has looked like a capable starter.
Denver should use some three-tight-end sets and get favorable passing matchups with Adkins against Arizona's linebackers.
The Cardinals' offensive line has struggled to block interior defensive linemen and edge defenders like Jones. While the Cardinals haven’t allowed a lot of pressure ( 12th-fewest pressures , with the seventh-ranked pass-blocking efficiency), they're weak against these types of defenders.
Jones has really come on over the last two weeks, so ride the hot hand to help generate some pressure and put the heat on Jacoby Brissett.
With Talanoa Hufanga and Patrick Surtain II out vs. the Seahawks, Rapp got called up off the practice squad and played 65 of 85 defensive snaps. There is a good chance Denver does that again against the Cardinals.
It would give Rapp the tough task of helping to cover Cardinals tight end Trey McBride and their quietly good receiver corps. Rapp played well against the Seahawks, and if the Broncos turn to him again, they'll need another strong performance.
With a few weeks to go until the NFL trade deadline (November 10), Mims is trending in the wrong direction. He isn't being used as a kick returner often; his play as a punt returner has been mediocre at best, and his effort on offense has been terrible.
As things stand, Mims is playing his way to be traded, and it's on him to flip the script. Maybe he makes something happen in this game; he certainly needs a big day.

title: Broncos Week 7 Injury Report: Who’s Trending For the Field—or IR
full_text:
The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup.
On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday.
Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals.
Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up.
Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year.
“He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday.
Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go.
Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report .
Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited.
Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side.
“They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback.
"I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.”

title: Broncos' Biggest Trade Deadline Need Has Become Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' running back room has failed to perform through six weeks of the 2026 season.
The Broncos are 4-2, but they've gotten little help from their run game. There have been flashes, like Jonah Coleman's rookie debut in Week 2 and the first half of Week 6's win over the Seattle Seahawks, but as a consistent foundation, the Broncos don't have much to build on.
Meanwhile, Bo Nix has been mired in a slump , especially over the past three games. He's won 28 games as a pro, but you could easily count on one hand the number of times he's had a 100-yard rusher.
As Sean Payton has said, quarterback is the hardest position to play in the NFL sans a run game. With the NFL trade deadline approaching on November 10, the Broncos' biggest need is staring them in the face.
Now, there's a chance the worm could turn for this running back ahead of November 10. The Broncos have three games between now and then, and aside from the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8, the defensive competition on the docket pales in comparison to what this offense has faced in the first six weeks.
That's worth remembering: the caliber of defenses the Broncos have gone against to start this season. Not as an excuse, but it's a fact that Denver played the second-toughest schedule through six games based on opposing defenses. It was one slugfest after another.
This is one reason the buzz among the players and coaches at Dove Valley centers on Nix and the offense being poised to finally break out and maybe even go on a run. It's possible, but if the Broncos don't get the answers they're looking for within the next three games, they've got to look hard at possible trades.
Without a viable rushing attack, the Broncos may be able to survive the regular season and make the playoffs, but if they don't win the No. 1 seed and they have to play on the road, the lack of a ground game will catch up with them.
J.K. Dobbins is on pace for a career-low season, averaging 3.3 yards per carry. RJ Harvey has burst and is tough to tackle, but the Broncos seem reluctant to lean on him as a down-to-down rusher.
Coleman is set to return from injured reserve this week, and he's the Broncos' best hope at their run game finally breaking out — beyond a sudden Dobbins resurgence. The rookie runs with good vision and has a blend of power, burst, and contact balance that makes him effective. But Coleman is young and inexperienced.
Dobbins has pointed to the Broncos' schedule as the biggest explanation for the run game's failure to launch, and there's some truth to that. But he doesn't look like the same runner we saw for 10 games last season; he's indecisive and lacking burst.
With only three games between now and the trade deadline, the Broncos need to find out quickly how much Coleman's return can actually help them. Dobbins has been trending toward 20 carries per game of late, but the Broncos would be wise to split a good chunk of those off for Coleman.
There are some potentially great options out there for the Broncos. The Indianapolis Colts are open to parting with Jonathan Taylor , and it's possible the Philadelphia Eagles could listen to offers for Saquon Barkley, given the buzz that they could be poised to kick off a roster reboot.
I'm not sure a back like Tennessee's Tony Pollard would offer a true upgrade over Dobbins worth trading for. And while it would be awesome to see Kyren Williams in the Orange and Blue, the Los Angeles Rams aren't likely to be sellers ahead of the deadline, unless they're unable to snap their two-game losing streak and things only get worse before November 10.
Tampa Bay's Bucky Irving could be interesting, too, as the Bucs seem destined for a losing season and a new coaching regime. The Broncos have options and future draft capital to play with.
Some people would argue that offensive line is a bigger weakness, and I don't disagree that the unit has been disappointing thus far, but if the Broncos went out and acquired left guard Quenton Nelson, as great as he is, he's not going to suddenly spark the offense in the same way that true top-tier running back would.
So, if the Broncos are of a buyer's mindset ahead of the deadline, it's all about the running back market. However, and this is a big caveat, the Broncos have three games left to see whether guys like Dobbins and Harvey can be more productive and how Coleman can help elevate things with his return from IR.

title: Broncos vs. Cardinals: 3 Keys to Avoiding an Arizona Letdown
full_text:
On one hand, Denver Broncos fans can feel good about the team's 4-2 overall record and the defense's performance over the past couple of weeks, particularly with the injuries that have impacted the secondary.
On the other hand, Broncos fans can't be blamed for being worried about the offense, which has yet to put together four quarters of quality play. While it's true the Broncos have faced some good opponents to start the season, they've only surpassed 300 yards of total offense in one game thus far.
One might think facing a 2-4 team is a way to get things right. However, the Arizona Cardinals are not a team to take lightly , as evidenced by their Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Rams.
How do the Broncos come out on top in the desert? Let's examine three keys to the Broncos improving to 5-2 rather than winding up in the same position the Rams were in last week.
The Cardinals deserve a lot of credit for finding a way to beat the Rams, despite not scoring a touchdown. But six drives that end in field goals (18 points) are enough when your opponent scores on just three of 10 drives for 16 total points.
"Three of 10 drives for 16 points" could easily describe the Broncos' offense in more than one game this season. But that brings us to a big reason the Cardinals didn't need a touchdown to beat the Rams: they controlled the ball for most of the game.
Against the Rams, the Cardinals won the time of possession, controlling the ball for 34:52 of the game, while L.A. controlled the ball for 25:08. The Cardinals might not have been great on offense, but they did enough to move the chains, keep the Rams' offense on the sideline, and find ways to score.
Time of possession was also key to the Cardinals' season-opening win against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Cardinals controlled the ball for 37:31 while the Chargers controlled it for 22:29.
And time of possession was a key reason the Cardinals stayed in the game when they played the San Francisco 49ers, despite a 36-30 loss. The Cardinals had the ball for 38:44 while the 49ers had it for 21:16. The Cardinals trailed by 11 at halftime (17-6), then outscored the 49ers 24-19 in the second half.
But against the Seattle Seahawks and New York Giants, the Cardinals lost the time-of-possession battle. The Cardinals won that battle against the Detroit Lions, but the difference was less than 30 seconds.
That Rams game is a good example of why a team must be able to move the chains to have success against the Cardinals. And while the 49ers' offense can be explosive, the Broncos have yet to show that trait this season.
Thus, it will be important for the Broncos to show they can control the time of possession and get more points off drives. Doing so will take pressure off the defense.
It will be particularly important for the Broncos to have a good day on offense for two reasons. First, the Cardinals don't have a lot of defensive standouts, with safety Budda Baker as their best player — and he happens to lead the team in sacks with 3.5. The Broncos have to capitalize against a defense that lacks playmakers.
Second, there's no guarantee that the Broncos' offense will always have great field position, even with the defense playing better. That brings us to this point.
This might seem like an obvious point, but against the Cardinals, it carries a lot of importance. That is because the Cardinals have done a good job of taking care of the football over six games.
The Cardinals have just six turnovers in their first six games. The only game in which they had multiple turnovers was against the Giants — the Cardinals had three, but so did New York.
Additionally, the Cardinals have lost the turnover battle just once, that coming against the Lions — and it was Arizona with one while Detroit had none.
Otherwise, the Cardinals have tied with their opponent in turnovers, one to one, against the Rams, 49ers, and Seahawks, while winning the turnover battle against the Chargers, who had two while the Arizona had none.
Because the Cardinals have done a good job limiting turnovers, the Broncos can't depend on the defense to create takeaways, even though that defense has forced six turnovers in the past two weeks. The Broncos' offense has more reason to play well, and taking care of the football is a big step toward having a good day.
The Broncos' offense, to its credit, did not have a single turnover against the Seahawks and has just six in the first six games. But expecting the Broncos' defense to force three turnovers as it did in each of the last two games may be asking a bit much. Bo Nix and the offense need to do their part and do it well.
As for the Cardinals' offense, they don't have a lot of true standouts. Jacoby Brissett is the bridge quarterback to whoever the Cardinals ultimately decide will be the young signal-caller to build around, whether that's Carson Beck or somebody they draft in 2027.
Running back Jeremiyah Love hasn't lived up to expectations thus far, as he's averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, while free-agent signing Tyler Allgeier is averaging 3.0 yards per carry. The Cardinals traded  wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans, leaving them with Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne as their top pass catchers.
But the Cardinals do have one elite playmaker: McBride.
McBride not only leads the Cardinals in receptions with 49, but that number ties him with Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba for the most catches in the NFL through six games. The Cardinals tight end has averaged 7.4 yards per reception and has scored three touchdowns.
Trey McBride somehow makes the grab for the TD 😳 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/GwP9zr7VDe
Broncos fans are all too familiar with the defense's struggles to take opposing tight ends out of the game, particularly those who rank among the best in the NFL. But the Broncos likely won't be able to shut McBride down, even if they have everyone on defense healthy.
That being said, the Broncos do need to find a way to limit McBride's impact. It's possible that linebacker Justin Strnad could get a lot of work here, but who knows what wrinkle Vance Joseph might add to the defense, even if Talanoa Hufanga misses this game and the Broncos might limit Patrick Surtain II's snaps as he returns from an ankle injury, if he plays.
If the Broncos can limit McBride's impact — and if the offense can play well early and build a lead — the pass rush should be able to capitalize.
Brissett has taken 12 sacks in six games, so the Broncos stand a good chance of notching another multi-sack game. But while the Broncos' pass rush is likely to have a good day, the defensive backfield must limit McBride's impact and gains.
On paper, the Broncos are the better team, but what's on paper doesn't always translate to the field. The Cardinals are a well-coached team and have shown they can challenge top-tier opponents in the NFL, especially when they win the time-of-possession battle and limit turnovers.
But because the Cardinals don't have a top defense, the Broncos' offense needs to show it can sustain more drives. If Nix is going to find the game that gets him out of his slump, this is the one.
This game will also require veterans like wide receivers Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle and running back J.K. Dobbins to prove they can make an impact. Getting a healthy Jonah Coleman back should help with the running game.
The defense should do its part, though it may come more in the sack department than in turnovers, which the Cardinals have avoided in most of their games. The main concern is limiting McBride's impact.
If the Broncos' offense can control the time of possession, finish drives, and take care of the football, they should win this one. But if the Broncos have another outing where they score on just three drives for 17 or fewer points, it could come back to haunt them.

title: Courtland Sutton's Bold Prediction Puts Bo Nix Critics on Notice
full_text:
Since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks, the noise surrounding Bo Nix has reached a fever pitch.
Whether it's at the local or national level, the Nix pile-on has reached epic proportions . Since returning from his ankle injury, he hasn't looked the same, but his last three games, in particular, have people around the NFL genuinely concerned. That includes many Broncos fans.
Outside the building, the noise has been deafening. Inside, it's a different story, according to Pro Bowl wide receiver Courtland Sutton, who took to the podium on Wednesday ahead of the Broncos' Week 7 road game against the Arizona Cardinals.
"Man, there's a sign that's in the building, and I may word it wrong, but I think it's like 'one of the things that can keep a team from being successful is outside noise,'" Sutton said on Wednesday. "For us, the most important thing is this team—everyone that's inside this building. We all know because we're here every day."
Sutton believes that people are entitled to their opinions. And folks are certainly exercising their freedom of speech when it comes to Nix and the Broncos' offense.
Even the nature of the questions Sutton fielded on Wednesday belied the reality of the Broncos sitting at 4-2. You could see that he was a little mystified by the lack of focus on that fact and how the Broncos weathered their initial six-game gauntlet.
"I mean, I'm sure y'all have heard it, and it's not to be taken lightly from the questions you're asking me, but we are 4-2 in this situation," Sutton said.
So, yes. Let's keep things in perspective. The Broncos are 4-2. Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 regular-season starts.
Denver's record has done little to assuage the growing concern over Nix's play, mainly because it contrasts so sharply with the caliber of quarterbacking he showed in his first two years in the league. That's the outside perspective, though; inside the building, Sutton and his teammates see the same all-in preparation and work that Nix has always put in.
"There's not one person, if you ask anybody that's in that building that comes and watches us practice, there's not one person that can say that Bo Nix doesn't come out to practice and give us everything that he has to help us be successful, whether it's in the film room preparing, understanding the game plan, and coming out to practice," Sutton said. "People can say what they want to say. We know that he's putting his all into being the best version of himself so that we can have success."
And that success has been there. That's one of the reasons Sean Payton immediately shot down a question on Monday about whether he's considered benching Nix.
"To answer your question, no," Payton said .
Like Payton and the Broncos' shot-callers, Sutton remains fully of the belief that the worm is going to turn for Nix, and he'll be off and running like the player we saw last year who led this team to a 14-3 finish and the AFC West crown.
"Like I said earlier, at some point the tide's going to turn," Sutton said. "Everyone's entitled to their opinion, and good for them. But we know that he's working his butt off for us to be able to have success, and at some point the tide's going to turn, and everyone's going to be, 'Oh man, Bo Nix is the best. Bo Nix this, Bo Nix that.' And it's like, 'No, keep that same energy.'"
Sutton and his teammates look forward to that moment with relish. He's not panicking, despite being on pace for a career-low season, and we know Nix isn't either.
Nix has maintained his cool throughout this process, even as questions about his health have intensified over the past three weeks. On Wednesday, he may have seemed a bit exasperated to answer the same question about his ankle for the 100th time, but that's the closest I've seen him come to showing any kind of frustration.
"I've told y'all several times I'm all the way back," Nix said toward the end of his presser.
Nix did acknowledge the mental aspect of recovering from a serious injury, but he was adamant, once again, that his ankle is fully healed. However, that doesn't mean that his psyche has caught up quite yet; that much is clear.
The Broncos genuinely believe in Nix — that includes the coaches and the players. He faced a brutal opening schedule — the toughest in the NFL — but things are about to open up.
The Broncos' remaining schedule is the fourth-easiest in the NFL. There are a few toughies along the way, like the Kansas City Chiefs at home in Week 8 and the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 12.
Week 9's road game against the Carolina Panthers could end up being a tougher matchup than it appeared to be when the schedule first dropped back in May. But compared to the weekly onslaught Denver faced to open the season, it's a piece of cake.
The resistance training Nix and the Broncos underwent over the first six weeks has built up some serious strength, both physical and mental. This team's callus is thick, and that's bad news for the opponents remaining on the schedule.
Nix talked Wednesday about his goal to be peaking at the right time — December, January, and February — which is another reason he and the Broncos aren't freaking out like the media and fans are. The Broncos understand how hard it is to win in this league, and they appreciate each one, regardless of the style points.
Despite his foibles in recovering from his ankle, Nix has led the Broncos to a 4-2 start. That can't get lost amid the Nix pile-on.
He's always been more of a finisher. If what Sutton said is any indication, the best of Nix is yet to come.

title: Broncos Can’t Afford to Lose These 2 Matchups vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The schedule might be opening up a bit, but the 4-2 Denver Broncos can't afford to ease off the gas.
Though the schedule is easier, the Broncos have some feisty teams left on the docket, including the 2-4 Arizona Cardinals this week. This isn't a 'gimme' game by any means.
As always, the key matchups will dictate the outcome of this game. If the Broncos want to walk out with a win, they'll have to come out on top in these two matchups.
Nix has played poorly, especially in the past three weeks, and it goes beyond the tough defenses and the type of coverage he's faced. The physical aspect of his ankle isn't the issue, as both Nix and Sean Payton have stated multiple times.
However, Nix did acknowledge on Wednesday that the mental aspect of his ankle recovery has played some role in his early-season performance. When you watch the tape, there is a clear issue with the mental part of the game, so what he said makes sense.
Nix appears to be extra cautious about taking hits. He hasn't been as tough as a runner as he was in years past, and the mental aspect is also showing up in his tendency to bail on clean pockets early.
Nix leads the NFL in clean-pocket bail rate and ranks in the top five in shortest time before leaving the pocket. He's not standing tall and delivering the ball.
Then there's the lack of confidence when attacking vertically, something Nix has talked about at the podium, too. There's a fear of attacking vertically due, perhaps, to some early interceptions, but the Cardinals game is a prime opportunity to work on getting over it.
The Cardinals' defense ranks 31st in explosive pass play rate allowed this season.
Queen's Under Pressure should be the walk-on song for Jacoby Brissett. He's not the most pressured quarterback — ranking eighth-lowest in dropbacks under pressure — but he is one of the worst when pressure does get there.
Brissett averages 3.7 yards per attempt under pressure (third-lowest), and his three interceptions tie for the most. He's not really inclined to take off and scramble, either.
Johnson is part of why Brissett has faced so little pressure. Johnson ranks in the top 10 among tackles in almost every major pass-protection metric.
He has developed into a franchise left tackle and is having the best season of his career by far. However, Johnson hasn't exactly faced the toughest schedule in terms of opposing pass rushers, and none have presented quite the threat that Bonitto does.
In terms of turning pressures into sacks, Bonitto is off to his fastest start as a pro. He ranks 18th in total pressures by edge rushers, but he's also in the top 10 in pass-rush win rate. But when you filter for true pass sets, he drops to 14th.
Bonitto, however, has built up a head of steam over the last couple of weeks, and with the emergence of Que Robinson and the return of Jonathon Cooper , it could put more pressure on the Cardinals' other blockers. Bonitto could be even tougher to contain moving forward.

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 8
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions begin divisional play, taking on the Green Bay Packers after getting a week off to heal up, most notably with safety Brian Branch.
However, in recent days, the Lions have not seen Branch as one of their homegrown players taking center stage and being the main storyline. Instead, a contract dispute, or lack of urgency towards a deal, with tight end Sam LaPorta has owned the news cycle.
The tight end position , which was thought to be a set position upon a presumed re-signing, now sits in flux. With Saturday’s slate of college football coming up, extra attention was paid to the tight end spot.
Here are five players the Lions should look at during Saturday’s slate.
Johnson is a player the Lions might not be able to afford missing out on after Kenyon Sadiq flew off the board this spring. Sadiq, a freakishly athletic tight end from Oregon, has Johnson following in his footsteps.
Johnson has great size for a tight end, at 6-foot-5, 257 pounds. He has yet to post a drop this year while also being a star run and pass blocker. Separation and versatility are also strong calling cards, and the few times he cannot create separation, it is no problem with his ability to pull the ball down in traffic.
Last season, there was less looks at the tight end tape for Oregon’s Sadiq considering Motown’s situation. This year, Johnson might find himself as a Detroit draft darling. His Ducks take on Illinois at 3 p.m. EST.
Reynolds, a junior, has the option to return to the Hokies after the year is done. However, as his play stands currently, with over 400 receiving yards at the midpoint of the season, it is very probable the Massachusetts native goes pro.
While he has a drop on the season, he can read zones well to plant. He has less athleticism, size, and versatility than Johnson, but makes plays and is an instant upgrade on the Lions’ tight end room sans Sam LaPorta.
The Hokies travel to Clemson and Death Valley at 7 p.m. EST.
Roberts is a player that has dragged himself into the draft conversation. In what has been a down year for Michigan State football , the defensive tackle has put together a strong campaign.
That campaign came to a head last Saturday against Northwestern, with the Washington native recording eight tackles, three tackles for loss and two sacks, all of which were career-best marks.
Roberts has burst off the line that has seen him go unblocked in each of the last two games, and excels in forklifting players to create havoc. He is a run-stuffer with some pass-rush potential being tapped his senior year.
The Spartans take on UCLA in the Rose Bowl at 3:30 p.m. EST.
West is a tweener defensive lineman, taking some reps on the inside as well as the outside. In 158 pass rush snaps, West has 11 pressures and taken part of a trio of sacks.
His run-stop ability will keep teams watching the tape, with his rate ranking among the top quadrant of the class alongside his pass rush ability. West followed head coach Bob Chesney to the Bruins from James Madison, and has seen a dip in production that could be expected.
West has similarities with Eric O’Neill, another former JMU transfer that made the Lions roster out of camp after an underwhelming season with Rutgers.
The Bruins, as mentioned above, host the Spartans at 3:30 p.m. EST.
The Group of Six spot belongs to Finley, who elected to remain a Bulldog despite offers to improve his competition this season. He is a blocking heavy tight end with soft hands, ranking just outside the top quarter of tight ends in receiving grade on PFF.
Finley joins Temple’s Peter Clarke as the top Group of Six tight ends highlighted. However, Finley has a pass upgrade, although his drop rate is not among the lowest currently.
The Bulldog’s four touchdowns have doubled his combined scores in the last two seasons as a senior.
The Bulldogs take on Old Dominion at 5 p.m. EST.

title: Behind Enemy Lines: Can Lions Slow Down Packers Passing Attack?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking to come out of the bye week with a win in Week 7.
On Sunday, the Lions will host the divisional rival Green Bay Packers, which have won three consecutive games.
Reporter Bill Huber covers the Packers for Packers OnSI . He recently answered five questions from Lions OnSI to preview Sunday's divisional affair.
Bill Huber: Josh Jacobs is going to play, I was told on Thursday. I suppose Friday’s practice might not go well, but this is different than a player coming off a significant injury who needs some ramp-up to get ready for the games. Jacobs has been around the team throughout his six-game stay on the exempt list and he’s been able to go through workouts with the training staff. So, physically and mentally, he should be ready to go.
There will be some rust, obviously, after being out since the end of training camp. But, shoot, a rusty Jacobs should still be a shot in the arm for a running game that’s not just the worst in the league but on pace to be the worst in the NFL.
The Packers don’t need a great running game to score points. They just need to stay out of second-and-10. The blocking hasn’t been good enough, to be sure, but Jacobs’ vision and strength will be an asset in grinding out hard yards
Huber : It's the biggest statistical matchup on the field. Green Bay’s passing game has been excellent and Detroit’s pass defense is on pace to at least threaten the NFL record for most passing yards allowed per game.
Christian Watson was drafted as a size-speed threat but has blossomed into an all-around receiver. Until being somewhat limited by the Cowboys last week, he was on pace for 1,600 receiving yards and 20 touchdowns. That’s unprecedented in NFL history. Meanwhile, Matthew Golden has been a breakout star after a quiet rookie season. He averaged 25.8 yards per game last year but is averaging 83.5 yards this season.
Together, they’re on pace for close to 3,000 yards.
Two things stand out for this game. First, the Packers have to establish the run to maximize their play-action game. Jordan Love was 1-of-7 in play-action last week because the Cowboys weren’t buying what the Packers were selling. Two, Love has had 19 passes dropped. That’s the most in the league and more than all the NFC North quarterbacks combined.
Huber : They’ve got to get the offensive line and running game squared away. The pass protection has been leaky for most of the season, with Jordan Love paying the price. The second thing is finding a running game. They’re averaging less than 60 rushing yards per game and 3.0 rushing yards per attempt.
They are playing an unsustainable brand of football. You can’t put your quarterback in harm’s way without him getting knocked out of the game, and you can’t play winning football without the ability to run the football to run out the clock or control the game in one of those classic cold-weather games.
Defensively, they’ve just got to survive until Micah Parsons returns. So far, so good, but the pass rush hasn’t been good enough unless it’s been schemed up by coordinator Jonathan Gannon.
Huber : Offensively, it’s the tackles. Left tackle Rasheed Walker left in free agency and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2. In their place, Jordan Morgan has been OK at left tackle and Anthony Belton has been in survival mode at times at right tackle.
Aidan Hutchinson has to be licking his chops about the potential of a big day fueled by the fans and coming against two young tackles.
Defensively, nobody considers Javon Bullard a premier player in the slot. A second-round pick in 2024, he has zero career interceptions or forced fumbles. He’s an excellent player, though. His six passes defensed are more than he had his first two seasons combined. He’ll face a huge matchup against Amon-Ra St. Brown. This matchup will be worth the price of admission.
Huber : As we barrel through the Upper Peninsula to visit family while I’m at the game, I’m leaning toward Detroit.
The Lions, as usual, are really good. Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs – you know the names. They have elite players all over the offense. It’s odd to see them toward the bottom of the league in some key categories on offense. They’re scoring 32 points per game with the upside to get close to 40.
The Packers should score a lot of points, too, but it strikes me that they’ll have to play a nearly perfect game while the Lions have some margin for error. The ability of the Lions’ front to get after Love will make the difference in getting the key stop or two needed to win.

title: Detroit Lions Had Former Vikings Nose Tackle Visit For Tryout
full_text:
The Detroit Lions welcomed former Minnesota Vikings nose tackle Taki Taimani to the teams Allen Park Performance Center for a visit on Friday, according to the NFL's official transaction wire.
After playing collegiately at Oregon and Washington, the 6-foot-1, 325-pound defender went undrafted in 2024.
He was subsequently signed by the Minnesota Vikings. He was able to secure a spot on their 53-man roster coming out of his first training camp.
In 2025, he was not able to make the team, but was brought back on the practice squad.
Prior to the official roster cuts this season, Taimani was waived with an injury designation and reverted to injured reserve list the following day.
Earlier this week, the front office signed safety Myles Bryant to the practice squad . Defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina was also added recently to the practice squad.
According to a league scouting report , Taimani is a "A two-gapping wide-body capable of standing firm when manning his gaps, Taimani has some pop and anchor to battle along the interior but is a non-factor as a rusher. He has shown the ability to play at a variety of weights, but he’s lacking initial snap quickness and rarely captures lateral positioning or the neutral zone off the snap. Taimani might not have the traits or versatility to be drafted, but players with power who can challenge run games will always have a chance to make a roster."
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard still has the tough task of managing a defense that could use some more help in the secondary.
Getting Brian Branch to assist the back end will certainly be a benefit, but the Packers game will be his first game action in 10 months.
Sheppard was asked this week if he team can replicate the success the defense had against the Cardinals.
“I mean each week is different to be honest, as you know. I'm not telling you nothing you don't know. And week-to-week, you try to do what's best for the defense and for the team's success week-to-week. And every week's different," said Sheppard. "Every week's going to call for certain things to change. Every week's going to call for different guys needed to step up depending on where the ball is focused on and so on and so forth. So, I don't want to say we're going to replicate anything. What I want to say is I definitely want to build on a lot of the positives that came from that game. And I just want to credit the players, man.
"That's the thing that gets lost in all that. People start to, 'Oh, what did you change? What did you do?' The players went out and executed and played at a high level and played at a high level like they expect to do every week. It just showed up in Arizona on a more consistent basis than it had the previous four weeks.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 Week 7 Friday Injury Report: Two Questionable
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official Week 7 injury designation report, ahead of their Week 7 contest against the Green Bay Packers.
According to the team, safety Brian Branch and offensive lineman Cade Mays were both ruled questionable.
Veteran Rock Ya-Sin, who was limited at practice on both Wednesday and Thursday, was a full participant on Friday and should be cleared to play against a division rival at Ford Field.
Ya-Sin does not have any injury designation this week and has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury that kept him out of action for the past few weeks.
Head coach Dan Campbell indicated they have a decent idea at this point of how much the team is going to play Branch and Mays in their first appearance of the the 2026 NFL season.
Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing was asked this week how the offense could settle in earlier and start a little faster, including the offensive line.
Additional NFL Insider Analysis: Odds Detroit Lions Defeat Green Bay Packers in Week 7
While Detroit's offense has been among the top scoring units in the NFL, there have been issues with three-and-outs, penalties and scoring early in games.
"Yeah, I think again, it's emphasized, it's stressed," said Petzing. "And at the end of the day, sometimes it's play calls. Sometimes it's execution. It's always a combination of both. And honestly, and I've said it here before, anytime we don't score, I'm a little irked whether it's the first drive of the game or the last drive of the game. "So again, it's doing your job. It's calling the right plays. It's staying in the moment and doing it as hard and as fast as you can. I think that's got to be the focus.”

title: Sam LaPorta Addresses Lions Distraction: I Want Security
full_text:
Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta spoke to local reporters briefly at the teams Allen Park Performance Center, after his recent comments during a podcast interview caused quite the stir among the fanbase.
"I feel bad if there was any sort of distraction to the team or teammates or to the coaches," said LaPorta. "I think there may have been a little bit of a misconception with, I guess, like my intentions are, 'I want to play for this team. I give everything I have.' My teammates do as well. They all love me, respect me and support me and they want to see me be happy and compensated."
LaPorta acknowledged he allowed the business side of the game to make him emotional, given he wants to be paid similar to other tight ends who are performing at a high level and to provide additional security for his growing family.
In the coming months, LaPorta and his wife are expecting their first child.
"I guess I would not expect anyone else to really care even care, but emotionally for me and my family, it is an emotional thing for us," said LaPorta. "We want to have stability. We are excited in the coming months, we're going to have our first kid, me and my wife. We are going to welcome our baby girl into the world in Metro Detroit. We want to be here with the Lions.
"I'm getting emotional about it. In the grand scheme of things, it is really a business. You have to respect what the front office is doing," LaPorta commented further. "They are the ones calling the shots. They are the ones that brought me in. It's my first team. They have been nothing but supportive of me and my career."
Dan Campbell indicated the 25-year-old has remained locked in, despite the issues surrounding his contract.
“We’re two days from Green Bay, you know, but that’s what it is -- it’s on the outside world as a distraction. In this building, it’s not,” Campbell explained. “This kid is locked in. He’s been locked in all year. He was locked in when he came in on Tuesday. He was locked in Wednesday, Thursday. He’s locked in today.”
Despite playing on the last year of his deal, LaPorta has performed consistently and has been a significant factor in the Lions offense playing at an elite level.
“We picked the guys we picked for a reason. We know their character and we know what they’re about deep down. Listen, Sam’s a stud. He’s going to help us win games. He’s an unselfish teammate. He’s an unselfish player," said Campbell. "You can never take anything personal when you start talking about business. That’s why business and football, they don’t belong with each other. But it’s the world we’re in. It makes the world go round for all for all of us.”

title: Lions Are Facing Packers Team That Will Not Have Key Linebacker
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will not have to worry about one of the Green Bay Packers defensive captains in a Week 7 contest at Ford Field.
On Friday, reports indicated that Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will be ruled out for Sunday's game after a collision in practice resulted in an injury. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur stated that the veteran defender took a knee to the shin, and while it's not expected to result in an injured reserve stint, Franklin will be out against the Lions.
This game is a pivotal showdown between two teams angling for a leg up behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North. Green Bay enters the game at 4-2, while the Lions are 3-2 coming off of a Week 6 bye.
The Packers have already taken a hit defensively at the linebacker position, as Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season after suffering a torn Achilles in Week 4 against Tampa Bay.
As a result, the Packers are expected to start Ty'Ron Hopper and Isaiah McDuffie at linebacker this week against Detroit. The linebacking corps for Green Bay was a huge part of slowing Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs in the two meetings last year, both of which were won by the Packers.
Hopper has started two of his 39 career appearances, both of which came last year for Green Bay. McDuffie, meanwhile, has filled in for Cooper since his injury and will be making his 33rd start over the last three seasons for the Packers.
Now, the Lions will have the opportunity to expose an inexperienced linebacking corps that includes a backup thrust into action due to Franklin's injury happening late in the week.
Franklin has been a very impactful player for Green Bay's defense through the first six games of the season. He has recorded 41 combined tackles including 18 solos, along with two tackles for loss and a forced fumble.
He is in his first season with the Packers after beginning his career with the Indianapolis Colts. A seventh-round pick of the Colts in the 2018 Draft, Franklin played the first eight years of his career in Indianapolis before being dealt to Green Bay this offseason.
