title: Dan Campbell Loses His Cool Talking About Sam LaPorta
full_text:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell was not too pleased with having to answer several questions about Sam LaPorta.
Several of the questions were obviously going to be about LaPorta's controversial comments expressed on the "Pardon My Take" podcast earlier this week.
The former NFL tight end expressed that LaPorta has still been locked in this week and that he does not feel that the comments are a distraction inside the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
But clearly, the Lions head man would much rather be fielding questions about the Packers then about a star tight end not being happy with his NFL contract.
"It's all good, man. You can never take anything personal when you start talking about business," Campbell expressed, before a reporter tried to ask one more question about LaPorta. "That is why business and football, they do not belong with each other. But, it is the world we are in. It makes the world go around, for all of us."
Before walking off angrily to end the media session, Campbell expressed, "I am not answering anything. I mean, I have answered this I don't know how many times. So, I said I did not want this to be a distraction. And now, it is becoming one, since you keep asking these things. That's why."
It is clear that players and the coaching staff are never going to throw LaPorta under the bus , especially regarding a contract dispute.
"I don’t want to overstep my boundaries. But I know Sam’s a hell of a player, and the front office does a hell of a job, so I think it will work itself out," Jack Campbell told 97.1 The Ticket this week. :But it’s not, like, lingering in the locker room or anything. Everyone knows, it’s a business. Brad does such a good job. So now it’s up to him to figure out how they can. But nowadays I feel like you can do so much stuff with the cap.
"I’m not a business guy or know much about the cap and all that, but I feel like you can figure out how to restructure things and move this and that and make it not count against the cap as much ... But they do have some unique decisions to make, because I’m like, we’re gonna have to figure what to do with BB (Brian Branch), too."

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup With Packers
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a chance to get right back in the middle of the NFC North title race.
In Week 7, the Lions host the Green Bay Packers to begin a stretch of back-to-back divisional games against the top two squads in the standings. This could be a season-defining stretch, as falling could be tough to recover from given how strong the division is.
Here are 10 thoughts on the Lions’ Week 7 matchup with the Packers.
Last season, the Green Bay Packers made a point of emphasis to slow down Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. He was held to 50 yards on 19 total touches in the first meeting last year, then 86 yards on 20 touches in their Thanksgiving rematch. With an even bigger workload this year, Gibbs will need to be more productive if the Lions are going to notch a win in Sunday’s meeting.
Green Bay’s defense is under new leadership with first-year coordinator Jonathon Gannon, so the plan could look different from their perspective. However, it’s no secret how impactful Gibbs is to Detroit’s offense, and so there will be eyes on him all afternoon.
Sunday’s game marks the start of a huge two-game divisional stretch for the Lions. After not playing a divisional opponent through their first five games, they will play the top two teams in the division back-to-back with the Packers and then Vikings coming to town.
With the Packers at 4-2 and the Vikings still unbeaten, taking at least one of the two games is pivotal for the Lions to keep pace in the NFC North. If the Lions are unable to do so, then it would appear the most likely path to the postseason would be through the Wild Card.
On the same token, it’s also worth noting that the Lions will play all three divisional opponents in a four-game stretch to end the year. All three of those games will be on the road, though, and taking advantage of their opportunities at home will be of utmost importance.
Barring any unfortunate developments between now and Sunday, the Lions are going to get two big members of their team back in center Cade Mays and safety Brian Branch. It will be both player’s first appearance of the season, and Mays’ first regular season game as a Lion after signing with the team in free agency.
On Wednesday, head coach Dan Campbell said the plan will be for Mays to start at center and not rotate in Juice Scruggs. For Scruggs, who has been one of the top-performing centers up to this point in the league, that could mean a move to left guard though Christian Mahogany has also been playing well.
Branch, meanwhile, is recovering from a torn Achilles and could have a big impact on the defense in his return. Time will tell what his workload will be, and it’s unfair to immediately expect him to be the level of player he was pre-injury, but his presence alone could go a long way toward stabilizing some of the secondary issues Detroit has had this season.
The Packers will get a big return of their own on Sunday, as running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be active for the first time this season. Jacobs had been on the Commissioner’s Exempt List following an offseason incident, but has been cleared to play and is expected to against Detroit.
Green Bay currently ranks last in the league in rushing yards per game, and Jacobs could provide them a boost in that area. Additionally, the Packers have the third-lowest amount of rushing attempts up to this point, so Jacobs’ presence could change their offensive approach as a whole.
With Sunday being his first appearance of the season, it will be intriguing to see just how much of a workload he’s given. Regardless, the Lions’ run defense will be tested by an offense that, on paper, hasn’t done much in the rushing department.
Packers wide receiver Christian Watson has emerged as a legitimate downfield threat, and has caused the Lions some problems in the past. In seven career games against Detroit, Watson has notched four games with at least 80 receiving yards including 194 yards on 17 receptions in two games last year.
Through six games, Watson ranks fifth in receiving yards with 538 and second in receiving touchdowns with six. He is averaging 18.6 yards per reception, and as a result can be expected to test a struggling Lions secondary down the field.
Not to be outdone, Packers’ second-year wideout Matthew Golden is also enjoying a fine start to the season. He’s right behind Watson in receiving yards with 501, and has three touchdowns to his name.
If the Lions are to jump past the Packers in the division, which they would do with a win, the effort starts and ends with good cornerback play and shutting down Jordan Love’s top two passing options. If they can’t, it will lead to the game becoming a shootout and put pressure on Detroit’s offense.
Though the Lions have struggled and rank at the bottom of the league against the pass, their pass-rush has been a huge point of success up to this point in the season. They currently lead the league in sacks, with D.J. Wonnum pacing the team with five.
Aidan Hutchinson has managed four sacks despite his gravity attracting plenty of attention from opposing offensive lines. Additionally, Alim McNeill has provided pop from the interior offensive line with 3.5. With all the threats Green Bay has on the outside, having this pass-rush presence could go a long way against a Packers offensive line that has struggled at points this season.
Last year, the Lions were swept by the Packers for the first time under Campbell. Even in the first year of his tenure, when the team finished 3-13-1, they were able to manage a victory against their rival at home. Now, Campbell’s team has a renewed fire to return the favor after last year’s struggles.
The Lions are also looking to snap a sort of ominous skid that has developed. After going a stretch over two seasons without losing back-to-back games, the Lions haven’t won back-to-back games since last September, when they won four consecutive games after losing to the Packers in the season opener.
Sunday’s game against Green Bay is their latest opportunity to snap that drought, and could be huge for them generating momentum throughout the rest of their season.
The Lions have the ability to make the Packers one-dimensional offensively with their struggles running the ball. While they give up some big plays through the air, the pass-rush is the great neutralizer as Aidan Hutchinson and D.J. Wonnum both get home for sacks.
Offensively, the Lions can help themselves out by controlling time of possession and finishing possessions with touchdowns as opposed to field goals. Jared Goff goes another game without a turnover, and the Lions pour it on late as the defense gets multiple key stops.
The Lions come out of the bye flat, and Green Bay takes advantage with an early scoring strike from Love to Watson. The defense gets in position to make stops, but can’t get off the field on third-down as Tucker Kraft is a force in the middle of the field.
Detroit should be able to score on Green Bay’s defense, but the Packers will sell out to stop Gibbs. If he can’t get going, the Lions will become one-dimensional and predictable, which will force them into having to put together a mistake-free late rally in a close loss.
Against an offensive line that has sputtered, the Lions will keep the Packers under 250 yards passing. Pass-rush will be the key, as the personnel the Lions have in the defensive backfield has struggled. However, Branch’s return will provide a boost, and the pass-rush limits the damage Love can do by getting to him quickly.
The best way for the Lions to avoid getting picked apart is to get after the quarterback, and Hutchinson and Wonnum have the ability to do that. Ultimately, the impact of the pass-rush will be the difference in the game.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Lions OC Drew Petzing on 'Megamind' Nickname: I Do Have a Big Forehead
full_text:
Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing did not seem all too comfortable with discovering what supporters were calling him on social media.
Speaking with local reporters prior to practice on Thursday afternoon, Petzing was asked if had been told yet that he was being called "Megamind" online.
“I don't know if I want to know that," Petzing said with a sense of trepidation.
When he discovered what his nickname was, he replied, “I do have a big forehead, so I guess that would be my reaction.”
In his first five games leading the Lions' offense, the returns have been overwhelmingly positive. Detroit's passing and rushing attack are in the top 5 and the offensive line is the top PFF-graded unit to start the season.
Part of the reason head coach Dan Campbell has to feel more comfortable , despite the 3-2 record, is the play of the offensive line and the emergency of running back Jahmyr Gibbs.
Despite the offense scoring more points, the unit is still looking to start games faster and improve on third-down.
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: 3 Players Impacted Most By Return of Safety Brian Branch
For Petzing, the last couple of weeks has seen him match up against coaches and teams that are familiar with his scheme.
Against the Panthers, his brother is on the Carolina coaching staff. Detroit last played Arizona, where Petzing spent three seasons as their offensive coordinator.
This week, the Lions face the Packers, who hired Jonathan Gannon to be their defensive coordinator . Recall, Gannon was the Cardinals head coach during Petzing's recent stint with the NFC West squad.
“Yeah, it is helpful and it was helpful last week too. And I don't know if there's much that isn't on tape that he's relaying to us, but there is some, I'm sure," said Jared Goff. "They both know each other pretty well and know each other's tendencies and it was the same last week and they got us on stuff, we got them on stuff, and it'll probably be the same this week and hopefully come out on top.”
Goff later added, "What they did in Arizona was not the same thing they did in Philly. And then what they're doing in Green Bay is not the same thing they did in Arizona or Philly. There are elements of all of it as there are on a lot of teams in the NFL, but some of it there are some things, but again, not much that you can't see on tape that he'd be able to relay. Again, I'm sure there's tendencies that he knows and vice versa. So, we'll see how that plays out .”

title: Grading Trade Proposal With Chargers That Upgrades Lions' Defense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions could end up being one of the most active teams leading up to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline .
After losing out on the Joey Porter Jr. sweepstakes, they're still likely in the market for an upgrade at cornerback.
Subsequently, the Lions could be a viable landing spot for cornerback Donte Jackson, who is presently a member of the 0-6 L.A. Chargers. NFL writer Bill Barnwell believes such could be the case.
Jackson has not had a highly proficient season in coverage up to this point, with just two passes defensed and zero interceptions to his name. And for his efforts, he's earned a lowly Pro Football Focus coverage grade of 54.7, just the 70th-best coverage mark among 102 qualified cornerbacks.
However, he's fared much better against the run, earning a PFF run-defense grade of 77.5 (the 13th-best mark among all qualified corners).
It's also important to note that Jackson was highly productive in coverage a season ago, securing four interceptions and allowing a passer rating of just 56.3 on 399 coverage snaps. Plus, he earned a 75.0 PFF grade for his performance against the pass, which ranked as the 16th-best mark out of 114 qualified CBs.
In his latest article for ESPN.com, Barnwell proposed a trade between Dan Campbell's and Jim Harbaugh's squads that would net Detroit Jackson and EDGE Khalil Mack in exchange for a pair of mid-round draft picks (2027 fourth-and-sixth-round picks).
There is certainly logic behind such a swap for both teams. The Chargers are clearly already out of the playoff race, and the Lions could use help at each of the aforementioned positions. It will be interesting to see, however, if the usual stingy Brad Holmes decides to part with multiple draft picks for two rental players.
In addition to both Jackson and Mack being free agents at season's end, they are both due a sizable amount of money the rest of the season. Jackson is set to be paid $4 million over the remainder of the season, while Mack is owed $5.3 million. It'd be a hefty tab for Holmes & Co. to pick up; consequently, the deal would be significantly more feasible if the Chargers decided to cover a portion of Jackson's and Mack's salaries the rest of the way in 2026.
Jackson would supply Detroit with a solid cover corner to pair with incumbent No. 1 CB D.J. Reed. Meanwhile, Mack, with 116 career sacks to his name, would be a godsend for the Lions’ pass-rushing department. He'd provide the organization with a proficient pass-rusher to complement Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson's production.
As Barnwell writes, “The Lions have the league's second-best offense in terms of points scored per drive, but the defense needs help. And here Detroit adds two experienced starters on that side of the ball, giving the team a better shot at competing in what's going to be a dogfight in the NFC North.”
This mock trade would significantly upgrade defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit going into the second half of the 2026 campaign. And it would greatly increase Detroit's chances of capturing the NFC North crown and making a deep playoff run.
As a result, I'm willing to give this trade proposal a “B+” grade.

title: Packers WR Matthew Golden Is NFL’s Breakout Star (Drops Be Damned)
full_text:
DETROIT – When the Green Bay Packers opted to let Romeo Doubs go in free agency and trade Dontayvion Wicks, it was with the goal of giving Matthew Golden more opportunities.
That faith has been rewarded.
Golden enters Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions ranked sixth in the NFL with 501 receiving yards. He’s 16th with 30 catches, fifth with a 16.7-yard average and tied for 13th with three touchdowns.
According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, Golden has increased his receiving output from 25.8 yards per game last season to 83.5 yards per game this season. That’s an increase of 57.7 yards per game and the largest season-to-season improvement since Josh Gordon was plus-67.3 in 2013.
Golden’s been really good, to state the obvious. He’d be great if not for his league-high seven drops.
“There was a lot of plays left out there,” Golden said after dropping two touchdowns against Dallas. “Those are plays that you want back, especially just knowing the type of game – Sunday night, how important it was for us to come out with this win. For me, I’m not going to be too down about it because I know 10 times out of 10, I’m going to make those plays. That’s just going to come with it. I’m not going to get too down about it.”
As last year’s first-round pick, Golden caught 29 passes for 361 yards and zero touchdowns in 14 games as a rookie. He’s surpassed all those numbers in just six games.
He’s on pace to finish with 1,420 yards, which would rank seventh in franchise history. Only Davante Adams in 2021 and Jordy Nelson in 2014 reached 1,500 yards. Having eclipsed 100 yards in back-to-back games and three of the last four, who knows what lofty numbers he could reach.
Last week, he became the first Packers player with 100-plus receiving yards in back-to-back games since Adams in 2021. He also became the first Packers player with 90-plus receiving yards four times in the first six games of a season since Greg Jennings in 2008.
While he’s obviously left plenty of yards on the field with the drops, he’s also been deprived of a lot of yards through the interference penalties he’s drawn. In fact, he’s drawn more interference penalties for more yards than any player in the league.
Defensive Pass Interferences Drawn pic.twitter.com/n24nddzGe0
Entering Week 7, Golden was tied for third in the league with nine catches of 20-plus yards.
Lions coach Dan Campbell, whose pass defense is the worst in the NFL, knows he’ll have his hands full.
“I did a lot of homework on him,” Campbell said of last year’s predraft process. “We like Golden. He was really good ball skills, man, can track it, pluck it, and then the speed – speed, explosiveness – really showed up and he's really taken a step up.
“He's really improved his game even from a year ago. He's taken that second-year jump and he's just really throughout the year he's grown. Every game he's gotten better and better, and you can tell there is a lot of trust between the quarterback and him and (Christian) Watson for that matter, but he's upped his game. He's playing at a high level.”
Golden has been the big-play threat everyone imagined after his blazing 40-yard time at the 2025 Scouting Combine. According to PFF, 54 receivers have been targeted at least 25 times headed into Sunday’s game. Golden is just 52nd in catch rate but 13th in yards per route and fifth in average distance of target because of the big-play production.
Of the 55 receivers who have been targeted 20-plus yards downfield at least five times, Golden is fourth in catches (five) and yards (194). Two drops have prevented him from putting up even bigger numbers.
The drops are perplexing from a player who showed impeccable hands during training camp. It’s why nobody is reaching for the panic button .
“I’m not concerned (about the drops), " offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said, “just because I know the type of player that he is. It’s just one of those things that you can’t lose trust in yourself. You got here for a reason. You are the player who you are for a reason.
“We all trust him. Jordan trusts him. I know he’s going to make those plays. The ball’s going to keep coming his way, so yeah, it’s just one of those things. You just got to work through it, trust yourself and keep your confidence.”
Jordan Love hasn’t lost any trust in Golden. Just before halftime on Sunday, Golden dropped what should have been a 23-yard touchdown. On the next play, Love extended the play and hit Golden for 21 yards to set up a touchdown.
“It means a lot,” Golden said after the game. “Just being able to be in that position, obviously, he trusts me enough to continue to keep going to me. I feel like this all started back in training camp, OTAs, when we continued to put the work in each and every day and just continued to build chemistry. And obviously it showed tonight that the chemistry is there.
“I feel like we still have a lot left out there. I’m excited for what’s in store.”

title: Ten Most Important Packers for Pivotal Game Against Lions Features Backup
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers have won three games in a row after knocking off the Dallas Cowboys a week ago. They’re 4-2. That’s the good news.
The bad news is they could be in last place in the NFC North with a loss on Sunday against the Detroit Lions.
Most pundits expected the NFC North to be a dogfight this year, and that is certainly emerging. The Vikings are 5-0 and look primed to be 6-0 with a date on Sunday against the lowly Colts. The Bears have shaken off all the regression theories that followed them and are 5-2 after beating New England on Thursday.
That means the loser of Sunday’s game will sit in the basement of the NFC North.
How can they stay hot rather than falling into the cellar? Here are the top 10 players to lead them to a pivotal victory.
Anthony Belton has held up well in his audition to be the team’s starting right tackle for the rest of this season and perhaps beyond following Zach Bako-Bewele’s season-ending knee injury.
This week, Belton will square off against perhaps the top rusher he will face this season.
The Lions are not a good defense once the ball goes in the air. They are ranked dead last in passing yards allowed per game.
Before the ball goes in the air? That’s different. Led by Aidan Hutchinson, who has four sacks on the season, the Lions lead the league even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Hutchinson’s snaps are split almost evenly between the left side and the right side, so Belton should see plenty of him.
If Jordan Love has time to throw, there are plenty of holes in Detroit’s secondary to exploit. A quarterback has never completed a pass on his back. Keeping Hutchinson out of Love’s lap will be a good way to ensure Love is able to find his targets down the field.
This portion of the story could just as easily go to Matt LaFleur, Luke Butkus and Adam Stenavich.
It was probably too much to expect Kevin Zeitler to be ready to play against Tampa Bay or Chicago with a full workload. Zeitler had not done football activities since January and was not on a roster for offseason practices and training camp.
Kevin Zeitler, who spent the 2024 season with the Lions, is ready when the Packers need him. https://t.co/SmVnxMkO88
When Zeitler showed up in Green Bay, the Packers were desperate but did not feel good putting him on the field with a limited amount of practice time.
A ramp-up period that resembled training camp for Zeitler made some sense.
That time is up. Zeitler has been in Green Bay for almost a month. He said he’s ready to play.
“Hey, it’s just part of it,” Zeitler said this week . “It’s a big shoutout to Glove doing a great job out there as well as the group who’s been out there and kind of getting into a groove.
“Right now, the only thing that matters is winning and right now they’re getting the job done. It’s a blessing. It obviously gives me time to keep learning the offense, keep getting back in the swing of things and I’ll be ready when I’m called upon, whenever that is.”
If he’s ready, then it’s time to call upon him. Travis Glover has performed admirably, but he’s not the player Kevin Zeitler is. If the goal is to put the best five players on the field, Zeitler is one of them.
With Alim McNeil coming to town, it’s time to make the call.
“Next man up” is a popular saying in any locker room, but now it’s truly time for the next man up at linebacker.
Zaire Franklin is going to miss Sunday’s game with a shin injury sustained at practice.
Who is next? Ty’Ron Hopper. The former third-round pick has largely been a bench warmer during his time in Green Bay. Now, there will be nowhere to hide for Hopper as he’s pressed into action.
Hopper has had some nice moments when called upon. He had an interception in last year’s wild-card loss to Chicago and another Chicago a couple weeks ago. He’s made the most of his opportunities.
“He’s maximized them. He’s taken advantage of them,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “He’s done a great job, and I think we saw, his progression has been pretty cool to watch, just how he’s developed over the years, especially I think we kind of got a good sense early on in training camp that he’s on his way, so this will be a great opportunity for him to get even more reps.”
His assignment this week? He’ll be tasked with stopping all-world running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. There’s no time for Hopper to find his bearings. He needs to be ready immediately.
Is a shootout in order in Detroit? That feels like the type of game this is going to play out to be. If that is the case, every play and every point is going to be precious.
Last week, Matthew Golden could have had the best game of his career. He caught one touchdown pass and went over 100 yards receiving. He could have had three touchdowns and flirted with 200 yards if he simply held onto the ball. Golden’s two drops are almost shocking, though not something the Packers are worried about at the moment.
“That’s just one of those things, the one thing is you’ve just got to trust yourself,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “Things like this happen. There’s been other guys – (Dontayvion) Wicks a couple years ago sticks out where he had the case of some drops – but the one thing is you’ve got to work hard, keep working on the JUGS, keep catching ball and just trust your hands and trust yourself, and he’ll keep making those spectacular plays.”
Of course, if Golden is on this list, Christian Watson needs to be, as well. A lot of the same points for Golden apply to Watson. He dropped a touchdown last week but, like Golden, has been excellent in the early going this season.
Watson has a lot of good memories at Ford Field. He caught a bomb to open the game against Detroit on Thanksgiving in 2023. He finished that day with 94 receiving yards on five catches, including one touchdown. Last year on Thanksgiving, Watson had four catches for 80 yards and a 51-yard touchdown. He plays well on turf, and he plays even faster than he already is.
In a week in which points should be expected with these two offenses, someone on defense is going to have to make a big play to turn the tide in their team’s favor. The Lions will likely rely on Aidan Hutchinson and Alim McNeil to hit Jordan Love to make their plays.
The Packers have a host of candidates who could be their big playmaker, but that man since Edgerrin Cooper left the lineup on defense has been Evan Williams.
Last week, Williams was part of a brilliant sequencing by Jonathan Gannon to fool Dak Prescott into thinking he was blitzing. Instead, Williams dropped into coverage and stepped in front of Prescott’s intended receiver for an interception to snuff out a potential scoring drive for the Cowboys.
This week, the challenge is stiffer. The Lions have more talent on offense, including a quarterback who has not thrown an interception this season. The chess match against Jared Goff will come down to Green Bay’s ability to disguise coverage.
“I think it’s fun. I definitely think it’s challenging, but it’s fun, man, when you’re able to beat people with disguise,” safety Xavier McKinney said. “It’s not as easy as you would think. It’s hard to really stress yourself out but then also know you got to be in a certain place in a certain spot.
“I really credit the coaches for this, helping us out with the disguise game. Obviously, we work it out there on the field. We talk to each other all the time like, ‘How you want to do this? What we want to show here?’ But I think as far as them presenting it to us from the jump when they first got here, it was something that we had to constantly work on. To see where it’s gotten up until now and to see where it could possibly get to at the end of this thing, I think it’s going to keep getting better each and every week.”
If it gets better this week, perhaps Williams will be the recipient of Goff’s first interception of the season.

title: Packers-Lions Final Injury Report: Zaire Franklin Out; Backups Thrown Into Fire
full_text:
DETROIT – There’s never a good time to play without your starting linebackers.
That’s especially true for the Green Bay Packers, who will play without premier starter Edgerrin Cooper and defensive captain Zaire Franklin for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions. It’s not exactly ideal considering the Lions are second in the NFL in scoring, fourth in total offense and have a premier running back with Jahmyr Gibbs.
Cooper, of course, is on injured reserve with a torn Achilles. Franklin suffered an injured shin at practice on Thursday and is out on the Packers’ final injury report.
“Unfortunate deal,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice. “That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing.”
Franklin was the only player ruled out by LaFleur on the injury report.
Left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, defensive tackle Jordon Riley and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste are questionable.
Quarterback Jordan Love (back) and cornerback Brandon Cisse (stinger) are among those off the final injury report.
Melton missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned on Friday. Riley remains on injured reserve but just completed his second week of practice. Banks hasn’t played since his one and only game against the Jets in Week 2. St-Juste was inactive last week.
“Big, stout physical D-lineman. Exactly what we need,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Riley before practice.
As expected , unning back Josh Jacobs appears ready to make his debut after being removed from the exempt list this week. The NFL gave him a one-week roster exemption, so he will have to be activated by 3 p.m. Saturday, which is the same deadline for any other roster moves, such as activating Riley or practice-squad elevations.
“Yeah, I believe so,” LaFleur said of Jacobs being ready. “But we’ll get through it and see how he’s feeling and the confidence he has in himself, which I think is pretty strong. But those conversations will take place after practice.”
The Packers will be going with their backups at linebacker against the explosive Lions offense. Isaiah McDuffie started for Cooper the last two games, though he mostly split the reps with third-year player Ty'Ron Hopper. Now, they’ll both be in the starting lineup.
McDuffie is a known commodity. He has started 40 games in his career, including eight games in 2023, all 17 in 2024 and 12 in 2025. He topped 90 tackles each of the last two seasons.
Hopper is the unknown. A third-round pick in 2024, he’s barely played for most of his career. He hadn’t played more than 18 snaps in a game until logging all 67 snaps in last year’s finale at Minnesota. This year, he played six snaps the first four games but 39 vs. Chicago two weeks ago and 33 vs. Dallas last week.
He produced two tackles and one interception against the Bears and five tackles and one breakup against the Cowboys.
“He’s maximized them. He’s taken advantage of them,” LaFleur said. “He’s done a great job, and I think we saw, his progression has been pretty cool to watch, just how he’s developed over the years.
“Especially I think we got a good sense early on in training camp that he’s on his way, so this will be a great opportunity for him to get even more reps.”
Franklin is a captain on defense. He presumably will be replaced in green-dot duty by McDuffie, who is a captain on special teams.
“Man, I’ve always had a lot of respect for Duff,” Franklin said of McDuffie after the Dallas game. “I always seen him make a lot of plays on defense from afar, but he’s a consummate professional. He’s ready. He plays any spot, he does anything the team asks him for and he’s a captain for a reason.
“He’s a heartbeat of this team and we feed off of each other, man. I feel like we got very similar careers and similar mentalities and I love playing with Duff. That’s a great man right there.”
The trickle-down effect will impact the special teams.
Star safety Brian Branch said he’s “ready to roll” as he makes his debut following last season’s torn Achilles. Officially, he is questionable.
“I’m really excited, to be honest,” he told reporters in Detroit. “Play the game that you love that you've been missing out for so long. To come back like this is a blessing to be able to play this game. I'm just going to execute [the game plan] and, if I execute, it's going to be a hell of a game.”
Branch had 109 tackles and four interceptions in 16 games in 2024. Last season, he had 75 tackles, zero interceptions and a career-high 2.5 sacks in 12 games before the injury. In 43 games, he has seven interceptions, 38 passes defensed and 20 tackles for losses.

title: It’s One Game, But Check Out Impact Packers-Lions Will Make on Playoff Race
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Everyone likes to say division games count for two. It’s true.
If the Green Bay Packers beat the Detroit Lions on Sunday at Ford Field, they will be 5-2 and the Lions will be 3-3. That’s a game-and-a-half gap in the NFC North standings, with Green Bay in second place and Detroit in last place.
If the Lions beat the Packers, Detroit will be 4-2 and Green Bay will be 4-3. That would be a half-game edge for Detroit while Green Bay would be in last place in the division.
That reality is shown in the latest playoff simulators.
According to The Athletic’s simulator , the Packers have a 53 percent chance of reaching the playoffs, with a 3 percent chance as the No. 1 seed, an 11 percent chance of winning the NFC North and a 42 percent chance of earning a wild card.
A win by the Packers would push their playoff chances up to 70 percent, including 5 percent as the No. 1 seed and 19 percent as the division champion. A loss by the Packers would shrink their playoff chances to 42 percent, with a 1 percent chance of earning the No. 1 seed and a 5 percent chance of winning the NFC North.
Yes, one game would mean a 28-point difference in playoff probability, which is fairly typical of all the simulators.
At NFL.com , the Packers have a 54 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. That would soar to 69 percent with a win over Detroit but would fall to 45 percent with a loss. That’s a 24-point difference.
Similarly, Detroit has a 70 percent playoff probability. That would move to 78 percent with a win but 56 percent with a loss.
At Playoff Status , the Packers have a 61 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs, with an 11 percent chance as the division champion and a 3 percent chance as the No. 1 seed.
With a win, those would improve to a 71 percent chance of reaching the playoffs, with a 15 percent chance as the division champions and a 4 percent chance as the No. 1 seed. With a loss, their playoff hopes would fall to 55 percent, including only a 7 percent chance of winning the North. So, that’s only a modest 16 point difference.
At ESPN, the Packers enter the game with a 56 percent playoff probability. With a win, that would improve to 72 percent. With a loss, that would fall to 44 percent. That’s a 28-point difference.
At Stick to the Model , the Packers enter Sunday with a 49 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs. With a win, the Packers would have a 68 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs; with a loss, that would fall to 40 percent. That’s also a 28-point difference.
“You got to stay focused on what’s right in front of you, and that’s taking the right approach each and every day, which those guys have done an unbelievable job with,” coach Matt LaFleur said this week.
“The mentality is always to go 1-0. You can’t worry about your record. You can’t worry about anything else outside of what’s right in front of you. We know we have an NFC rival that is a really good football team and we got to play our best in order to go on the road and get a win.”
That’s true. Led by their elite offense, the Lions are one of the best teams in the NFL. They are three-point favorites over the Packers, who have the seventh-shortest NFC playoff odds at FanDuel Sportsbook – so right on the fringe of making the seven-team field.
“Yeah, we talk about it I feel like every year, just how important these division matchup games are, how much they mean,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I feel like since I’ve been the starter, the division’s been winning a lot of games and it’s been a very tight competition throughout the whole course of the division, through the whole season.
“It’s one of those things where you’ve got to take advantage, you’ve got to win these matchups when they present themselves. Obviously, the goal for us is to win the division and all that’s still out there in front of us. You’ve got to handle business against these teams and everybody in the division is very good.”
Of course, playoff projections are just that. They’re projections. There’s no level of artificial intelligence capable of accurately predicting how 53 players are going to perform on any given Sunday.
The Packers will have to play their best game of the season to beat Detroit. They’ll have to play well again to beat Carolina. And New England. And Minnesota. And the Rams. And the rest of the teams that will stand between them and January football.
“It’s a good environment over there,” Love said of Ford Field. “They definitely got a loud crowd and it’s a tough place to play, but we’ve had the right mindset in the past. These NFC North games, you got to go out there and win, and we’ve done some good things. I think it just comes down to us going out there and winning the matchups.”

title: Packers Friday Update From Practice: Another Major Blow Before Playing Lions
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers’ deepest position group had been linebacker.
With rising star Edgerrin Cooper on injured reserve following a torn Achilles, fellow starter and defensive captain Zaire Franklin will miss Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions with an injured shin.
“Unfortunately, Zaire, there was a little collision, he got kneed in the shin, so he’s going to be out this game,” coach Matt LaFleur said before Friday’s practice when asked about Franklin being limited participation at Thursday’s practice.
LaFleur said he doesn’t think it’s broken, but:
“We’re kind of working through it right now. I don’t think it’s going to be anything too long term but, yeah, just unfortunate deal. That happens when you play football, especially the way our guys have been practicing. But I think we’ve got a lot of confidence in McDuffie and Hopper and Nick Niemann, if need be, to go in there and do a great job for us.”
Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper, who had been splitting the snaps in Cooper’s absence, will be the starters against the Lions.
The defense was just hitting its stride. During its three-game winning streak – with Cooper missing two of the games – Green Bay hadn’t allowed more than 14 points.
“Man, I think it’s just a credit to who we can be,” Franklin said after the 23-13 win over Dallas. “Obviously, we got a lot of things to continue to clean up and get better at, but I feel like we as a defense on the rise. I think every week we continue to get better and better, taking the ball away, stopping the run, limiting explosive plays.
“That’s recipes to being great, so we got some stuff to clean up, but I think the ceiling is extremely high.”
Franklin had 10 tackles in the blowout loss to Atlanta, eight in the win at Tampa Bay and nine in the blowout home win over Chicago. In last week’s win, he had only three tackles but a quarterback hit that seemed to set the tone.
There’s a reason why Franklin was voted a team captain beyond wearing the green dot and relaying the signals.
“He’s a very serious person, so you better be on top of it. Not just players. Coaches,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said last week. “When he has questions, you better have answers or he will expose you, so it’s good. It’s a challenge.
“When we put up something, he’s going to ask the why and I believe in those guys knowing the why. But he definitely asks some questions that, we get out of the meeting room, we’re like, is that right? Is that what we really want to do? But it’s good. He’s a serious person. He’s all about ball. He’s like that on the field and in the meeting room.”
McDuffie, whose 40 career starts include 29 the past two seasons, provides a wealth of experience and solid production. Hopper is a bit more of a wild card, with some intriguing glimpses in limited playing time.
A third-round pick in 2024, he played 18 snaps on defense as a rookie and 126 in 2025, when he made his first two NFL starts. He has 12 tackles this season while playing 78 snaps on defense. He intercepted a pass against the Bears in the playoffs last year and another against the Bears a couple weeks ago.
Asked if consistency was the next step, Gannon said: “Yeah, I think that’s every player. Consistency of doing what you’re coached to do with the way that you want to do it with technique, fundamentals, playmaking. But I thought he played well.”
One reason why the Packers had McDuffie and Hopper sharing Cooper’s workload is because it allowed both players to remain vital cogs on Cam Achord’s special teams. That probably won’t be the case now. In fact, both players might be off special teams altogether or playing limited snaps, so not only will the defense be weaker but so will the special teams.
Niemann and Kristian Welch, who were full-time players on most of the units, will have to raise their game to another level.
The only linebacker on the practice squad is Jack Dingle. He is an elite size-speed prospect who understands that special teams will be his ticket to success.
“That’s the No. 1 thing,” he said at the Bengals’ local pro day in April . “Get on a team and start learning special teams right away. That’s very important to these coaches. I’ve talked to a lot of current NFL players and they say, ‘Learn that kick-step on punt man. If you make the punt team, you’ll make the team.’”
Last week, the Packers elevated edge player Arron Mosby from the practice squad. His calling card has been special teams so he could play on Sunday, whether it’s as a promotion to the 53-man roster or another elevation.
Franklin was the only player who did not practice for the Packers. The only player who didn’t practice on Thursday was receiver Bo Melton (back), but he was back on the field.
As we reported on Thursday , the expectation is running back Josh Jacobs will play against the Lions.
“Yeah, I believe so,” LaFleur said. “But again, we’ll get through it and see how he’s feeling and the confidence he has in himself, which I think is pretty strong. But those conversations will take place after practice.”
The teams will reveal their final injury reports after Friday’s practices. For now, here are the reports from Thursday. Remember, the Lions are coming off their bye so are mostly healthy.
Packers Thursday Injury Report
Did not participate: WR Bo Melton (back).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), CB Brandon Cisse (hip), LB Zaire Franklin (shin), Matthew Golden (shoulder), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), edge Lukas Van Ness (illness), WR Christian Watson (ankle), WR Savion Williams (ankle).
Full participation: QB Jordan Love (back).
Riley has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows.
Lions Thursday Injury Report
Limited participation: CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring).
Full participation: S Brian Branch (Achilles), C Cade Mays (wrist).
Branch has been designated to return from injured reserve and is within his 21-day practice windows.

title: Wait Continues as Packers G Kevin Zeitler Gets Ready to Face Former Team
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Something unexpected happened after the Green Bay Packers signed Kevin Zeitler to fill the gaping hole at right guard.
So, there’s a chance Zeitler will spend his fourth consecutive game on the bench when the Packers play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
The acclimation is going “great,” Zeitler said after practice on Thursday.
“I think everyone here’s been amazing,” Zeitler said. “It’s been really cool to be a part of this organization. I love watching the way the guys work. The O-line group is an incredible grouping of guys, from vets to young guys. I am so pumped to be here.”
Zeitler was inactive for his first week with the team. The last two weeks, he’s played 11 snaps of field-goal/extra-point protection but none on offense.
It’s been an odd turn of events for Zeitler. In his first 14 seasons, he started 213 of 214 appearances. From 2015 with Cincinnati through 2025 with Tennessee, Zeitler played in and started all but seven games.
Yes, Zeitler wants to play. But the ultimate goal is being accomplished.
“Hey, it’s just part of it,” Zeitler said. “It’s a big shoutout to Glove doing a great job out there as well as the group who’s been out there and kind of getting into a groove. Right now, the only thing that matters is winning and right now they’re getting the job done. It’s a blessing. It obviously gives me time to keep learning the offense, keep getting back in the swing of things and I’ll be ready when I’m called upon, whenever that is. It is what it is.”
Will he be called upon this week at Detroit? At the start of Thursday’s practice, when the line works on cadence with Jordan Love, Glover was the right guard. During individual drills, Glover got the first rep while Zeitler grabbed a dummy. Zeitler, though, did get some reps alongside center Sean Rhyan or right tackle Anthony Belton during combo drills.
It could all be subterfuge, but it seems like Glover is in line to make his fourth consecutive start vs. the rival Lions.
Really, it’s not a shock that it’s worked out this way. The Packers have won three consecutive games with their new offensive line. Glover hasn’t been great but the line has played better since he took over at right guard and veteran Laken Tomlinson was signed to play left guard.
Before the Packers signed Tomlinson, he spent three weeks on the Cowboys’ practice squad, so he was ready to go physically. Zeitler wasn’t with a team during training camp or the first three weeks of the season, making this stretch the equivalent of training camp.
“The key is finding your way to making it a training camp,” he said. “Right now, obviously, when you’re in-season, reps are at a premium for the guys that are out there. For me, it’s about finding ways to get mental reps, standing behind them, it’s tons of extra film on my own, making flashcards and trying to ingrain the whole system into my system as fast as I can. You just find ways to get it done.”
The coaches are happy with his progress. If needed, there would be no hesitation to put him in the lineup.
“Yeah, I think he looked better last week,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday, one day before this practice week started. “Obviously, he dressed for the game so we were prepared to put him in if we needed him. So, I think every week we’re just going to keep evaluating what’s going on there.
“I think for our O-line’s sake, we’ve played better the last few weeks. So again, just like last week, we’re not going to change just to change, but we want to put the best five guys out there that we think gives us the best chance to win. We’re just going to keep evaluating it as the week goes on.”
The Packers are the 36-year-old’s seventh team. The fifth of those teams was the Lions, for whom he started all 14 games in 2024.
He’s got a lot of respect for their coach, Dan Campbell, who has led the Lions’ revival after decades of mostly losing teams.
“It’s amazing,” Zeitler said. “Just the ultimate leader of men and sets the attitude of the room. Everyone who’s there, you buy in. No matter how you are as a person, you’re all about it. Great leader of men. …
“The way he leads, the way he is, he’s the type of guy everyone wants to be around, wants to be a part of, play well for. He does great things over there.”
While it’s understandable why Green Bay’s coaches might not want to upset the apple cart after three consecutive wins, the running game remains the worst in the league and quarterback Jordan Love has taken too many hits.
With Sunday’s game being in raucous Ford Field, this will be a good litmus test for what the coaches are thinking in terms of their commitment to Glover. If the line is struggling handling the Lions, who lead the league in sacks, and the noise, maybe this will be the week to see what Zeitler can add.
“Right now, the team is doing some really good things and I’m very happy for them,” he said. “We need to win. That is the No. 1 thing in this league. Winning is what matters. I’ll take the time and, whenever I’m called upon, I’ll be ready.”

title: Packers CB Brandon Cisse Updates Health, Rookie Progress
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse is a bit like those old Timex watch commercials that he’s far too young to remember.
He’s taken a licking and kept on ticking.
Cisse missed the final 8 minutes of Sunday night’s win over the Dallas Cowboys due to a stinger but will be in the starting lineup, as usual, for Sunday’s game against the rival Detroit Lions.
“It’s just numb,” Cisse said on Thursday when asked to describe the sensation. “You’ve got to wait for the arm feeling to come back (and) you can’t really feel your fingers. It’s just kind of like your shoulder and everything goes numb for a second.”
After being limited participation for a second consecutive day with neck and shoulder injuries, Cisse proclaimed himself “all good.”
“I’m rehabbing and doing good,” he said.
Cisse has started all six games but dropped out of three of them with cramps or injuries. He’s been on the injury report for neck, shoulder and hip injuries. He even was limited for a couple days before the Atlanta game after having a wisdom tooth removed. He’d obviously rather have played every snap in every game this season, but his ability to answer the call has been impressive.
He knows his importance to the team as a starting cornerback for a defense that ranks first in interceptions, third in opponent passer rating, second in passing yards allowed per attempt and sixth in passing yards allowed per game.
“Just trying to be out there as much as possible,” Cisse said. “I know the impact that I bring to the table when I’m out there and the kind of player that I can become. That comes with experience. You want to see as much as you can and be out there as much as possible and help change games and help my teammates.
“Anytime I get a chance to be out there and play through something, I’m going to be out there.”
That’s obviously of great importance for the game against the high-powered Lions. Quarterback Jared Goff is second in the league in passer rating and hasn’t thrown an interception. Amon-Ra St. Brown is one of the league’s best receivers. Jameson Williams is a big-play threat. Isaac TeSlaa is a quality No. 3 receiver.
“Obviously a big challenge,” Cisse said. “They’ve got a very good core of guys. Obviously, they’ve done a really good job with their receiver room there. They’ve got four guys who can really play and, obviously, the tight end’s a really big challenge, as well. And the running back is one of the best in the league, if not the best in the league.
“And, obviously, the quarterback’s an elite quarterback. Got to make sure you’ve got your eyes in the right place and make sure we’re all ready to go.”
A similar scouting report could have been provided before last week’s game against Dallas. The Packers dominated against the Cowboys’ powerhouse group led by quarterback Dak Prescott and receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Dallas didn’t go over 200 passing yards until the fourth quarter and didn’t reach double-digits points until late in the game.
Is there confidence to be gained from a strong performance against a strong offense?
“Every week’s a new week,” he said. “It’s all about proving yourself, so every week, I try to go out there and be the best version of myself and let go of the last game and build off of it, take the good and the bad, and get the bad things corrected this week and try to go have a dominant outing this weekend.”
According to Pro Football Focus, 87 cornerbacks have played at least 100 coverage snaps entering Week 7. Cisse is tied for 32nd with a 60 percent completion rate allowed and ranks 21st with 14.2 snaps per reception allowed. He grabbed his first career interception last week against Dallas.
He’s allowed more than two catches in only two games. One was the blowout loss to Atlanta, when Drake London had a huge game against the secondary. The second was against Dallas, when he allowed 4-of-9 passing for only 46 yards.
Asked if he’s happy with his progress, Cisse shared the same sentiment from multiple interviews during training camp.
“No, not yet,” he said. “Got to keep getting better each week, keep building and see where it goes.”
Cisse is one of 13 rookie cornerbacks to have played at least 50 coverage snaps. He is second in snaps per reception and snaps per target.
“It’s definitely a hard adjustment at times, but that’s what they brought me here to do and that’s the kind of player that I know I can become,” he said. “I’m excited to keep accepting the challenge and continue to grow.”

title: Packers-Lions Thursday Injury Report: Three Huge Updates for Green Bay
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love progressed to full participation at practice on Thursday. Barring an unforeseen setback, he is locked in for Sunday’s game against the Detroit Lions.
There were two additions to the injury report, and they are big ones. Starting linebacker and team captain Zaire Franklin (shin) and starting edge defender and leading pass rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness) were limited participation.
Franklin is second on the team with 41 tackles. He had games of 10, nine and eight before only three last week against Dallas, though he did have a big quarterback hit early in the game. Van Ness leads the team with 3.5 sacks and nine quarterback hits. As the team’s best pass rusher, the defense will need him to make life uncomfortable for Lions quarterback Jared Goff.
The Packers, who are coming off a Sunday night game, have 12 players on their injury report. The Lions, who are coming off their bye, have only three.
However, only one Green Bay player didn’t practice, receiver Bo Melton (back). Fellow receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle) were limited participation. There’s no reason for concern, though. Watson and Golden will play, coach Matt LaFleur said before practice, and Williams made his season debut last week following an ankle injury that kept him out for five games.
Defensive tackle Jordon Riley is in his second game back from a torn Achilles.
“I think he’s shown a ton of progress,” LaFleur said before practice. “It was good to get him out there last week and get his feet wet a little bit. If he continues to show that progress, then we’ll see where we’re at and he’d be ready to go.”
Riley completed his fifth practice and has been limited in all five.
“It’s really like riding a bike, man,” he said after practice. “So each day, you going to get better. Each day, you going to remember things that you learned in the past, stuff like that. Day 1 stuff. I’m in a better spot than I ever thought I was going to be as far as technical standpoint. Each day, I learned something with my game and each day I’ve been coached up to fix it the next day. So, we doing a good job with that.”
True or false: Josh Jacobs will save the Packers' run game. ⬇️ https://t.co/JseydlPrHE
Center Sean Rhyan has played all 389 snaps this season but there was a brief scare when he was slow to get up after Love’s interception.
“They came to me,” Rhyan said. “I was like, what the f*** do I need to get checked for?”
He had to go through concussion testing, cleared it between series, and was right back on the field.
“They were saying that I got up slow or something,” he said. “When you got [Anthony Belton’s] big body falling on you, sometimes it’s like, ‘Ah, let me just feel myself real quick.’”
As the center of the line, Rhyan will have a big role in helping the offense navigate the noise at Ford Field.
“Just got to listen a little harder, I guess,” he said. “We played there a lot, we kind of know what to expect – real hostile, real loud, kind of dark, on turf. Just keep on going, you know? But at the end of the game, we’re still playing 11 on 11. So, we’re going to go over there and do our thing.”
The update is there is no update. The Lions’ injury report is unchanged from Wednesday, with every player practicing and only one player – cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) – limited participation against while safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participation.
All three players are starters. Branch is set to make his season debut following last year’s Achilles injury and Mays is poised to make his season debut, as well, after starting 12 games for the Panthers last year.
Branch will not be on a rep count, defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard told reporters earlier in the week.
“Whenever you could gain a player like BB and his caliber back, it’s outstanding. You know what I mean? I’m not big on giving you projections and, ‘Oh, he’s going to do this, he’s going to do that.’ It’s just beautiful to have BB back. There are multiple things, obviously, that player can do to help us, and we’ll find the spots that we feel is right and he feels right for him as we progress here.”

title: Packers Thursday Update From Practice: Latest on Josh Jacobs, Jordan Love
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Josh Jacobs and Jordan Love practiced on Thursday, and the expectation is they will be on the field for Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions.
Love was listed as limited participation on Wednesday’s injury report with a sore back.
“He was pretty beat up” from the Dallas game, coach Matt LaFleur said before Thursday’s practice. “He took some shots. Saw him in there with the chiropractor postgame, so I knew something was up.”
Love on Wednesday said he had “no” concerns about his availability for the game.
“We talk about it all the time: You want to, obviously, limit me taking hits in the pocket,” Love said.
Meanwhile, for the first time since the end of training camp, star running back Josh Jacobs was participating in a real practice. The team held a jog-through practice on Wednesday; Thursday was the real deal in full pads.
“We’ve been getting him ramped up,” LaFleur said. “He’s been in the building (and) we’ve been doing things with him in terms of our strength staff, our athletic training staff. Certainly, you can’t simulate football until you get out there so I think these next two days are going to be great work for him as we ramp him up.”
Josh Jacobs in slow-mo today at Packers practice. pic.twitter.com/9Ezw8UmxhC
LaFleur said there will be “a lot of conversation and a little bit of the eyeball test” before determining whether Jacobs will play against the Lions. However, Jacobs is in good shape, he knows the offense and he stayed around the team during his six-week stay on the exempt list.
For those reasons, the expectation is Jacobs will be on the field against the Lions in a battle of two-loss teams that could have significant playoff ramifications.
“Last couple months, it’s been weird, man,” he told reporters on Wednesday . “Honestly, it’s been weird. I’ve still been around the guys. Obviously, I couldn’t practice, still could go to meetings, so I’ve been around. So, it’s been weird, like just watching and knowing that you feel good and your body is probably the best that I’ve been since I’ve been here, it’s just weird. Like that’s the only way I could really explain it.”
The Packers have by far the worst rushing attack in the NFL. Jacobs, obviously, would help fix the problem.
True or false: Josh Jacobs will save the Packers' run game. ⬇️ https://t.co/JseydlPrHE
The only player who didn’t practice for the Packers was receiver Bo Melton (back).
Receivers Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder) were limited on Wednesday, but LaFleur had no concerns about their availability for the game.
Cornerback Brandon Cisse, who missed the end of last week’s game against Dallas with a stinger, was limited on Wednesday and practicing again on Thursday.
Defensive tackle Jordon Riley, who was designated for return from injured reserve last week following last year’s torn Achilles, was limited participation on Wednesday and on the field on Thursday. He might be activated this week, which would help Green Bay’s depleted defensive line.
“I think he’s shown a ton of progress,” LaFleur said. “It was good to get him out there last week and get his feet wet a little bit. If he continues to show that progress, then we’ll see where we’re at and he’d be ready to go.”
The Packers will be behind from a preparation standpoint. While LaFleur turned Wednesday into a mental day, the Lions are healthy while coming off their bye.
“I think it’s more about getting our guys’ bodies in the right position,” he said. “I think every team around the league has had an ample number of reps. Certainly reps are at a premium, there’s no substitute for them. But, at the same, you need your guys feeling good when they go out there on the grass.”
Because they’re coming off their bye, the Lions had only three players on Wednesday’s injury report. One of them is star safety Brian Branch, who will be making his season debut following last year’s torn Achilles.
“Well, you get a tremendous football player,” LaFleur said. “I think he’s one of the best safeties in the league. There’s a lot of things he can do that others can’t, and they’re comfortable playing him man to man on wide receivers like we’ve seen in the past, and he adds an element of just physicality, toughness. Just a great player.”
The teams will release fresh injury reports after their Thursday practices. For now, here are the reports from Wednesday. The Packers, who played on Sunday night, have 10 players listed. The Lions, who had their bye, have only three.

title: True or False: Josh Jacobs Will Save Packers’ Historically Feeble Run Game
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – In Week 3, the Green Bay Packers were crushed by the Atlanta Falcons. Part of their problem that night was their offensive line was overwhelmed by the Falcons’ attacking defensive front.
At the time, it felt like the Packers would be just fine if they could get even mediocre play from their offensive line. Changes were made and, sure enough, the Packers will take a three-game winning streak into Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions.
The Packers are 4-2 but are being held back by an impossibly bad offensive running game. Even a mediocre running game would make a huge difference for Green Bay’s offense.
Enter Josh Jacobs, who is one of the better running backs in the NFL. He can’t single-handedly rescue what’s trending toward being the worst running game in NFL history but, as coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “He’s certainly not going to hurt it.”
Will Josh Jacobs single-handedly save the running game?
The starting point for any offense is, obviously, the starting point of any series, and that’s first down.
Green Bay’s first-down running game is averaging 2.3 yards per carry. To say that’s the worst in the league is accurate. It also doesn’t do it justice. It’s a half-yard worse than No. 31 Las Vegas and a full-yard worse than No. 30 Miami. It’s 1.8 yards worse than the league median.
In 2025, Jacobs averaged 3.9 yards per first-down carry. This year, Pierre Strong leads the running backs with a 2.5-yard average.
Jacobs was stuffed – a run of 0 yards or worse – on 16 percent of his first-down carries last season. By contrast, his first-down success rate – defined as a gain of 4-plus yards – was 44.5 percent.
Compare that to this year’s run game, with 25 percent of the first-down runs resulting in stuffs and 34.2 percent being a success. In number instead of percentage, only the Dolphins have fewer successful first-down runs.
If you can’t run the ball on first down, it’s harder to throw the ball on second down. On second down overall, Jordan Love has completed 63.1 percent of his passes, averaged 7.4 yards per attempt, thrown six touchdowns and three interceptions and produced a passer rating of 94.4. He’s been sacked four times.
Digging deeper, on second-down plays requiring 8-plus yards, Love has completed 63.2 percent of his passes and averaged 9.3 yards per attempt. That’s as good as (or better) than he is overall on second down. However, he’s thrown one touchdown and two interceptions (84.5 passer rating) and taken all four sacks.
On second-and-7 or less, Love has thrown five touchdowns with just one interception (93.1 rating) and has not been sacked.
According to Sumer Sports, teams facing second-and-10 or longer this season have a 46.9 percent chance of eventually getting a first down. A gain of 3-plus yards moves that all the way to 72.5 percent. It’s not quite as extreme for Green Bay, with 50.0 percent on second-and-10 or longer and 67.4 percent on second-and-7 or shorter.
Still, it’s common sense that a first-down running play that gains a few yards is better than a first-down run that gets stopped at the line.
Obviously, Jacobs can’t turn a horrendous rushing attack into a quality rushing attack by himself. According to Sumer Sports, a whopping 81.1 percent of Green Bay’s rushing total has come after contact.
“I think it relies on everybody,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “Whether it’s scheme or blocking or running, I think everyone has to do a better job, starting with me. That’s the biggest thing. That’s a big focus for us as we’re going further into the season. Now, Josh I think will definitely help for sure. He’s an excellent player and he’ll provide some good spark for our offense, so I’m excited about that. But we just all need to do a better job.”
True, but with his toughness and vision, Jacobs will improve the first-down rushing offense – and, therefore, the offense as a whole.
According to Sports Info Solutions, MarShawn Lloyd is averaging 1.8 yards after contact per carry, Chris Brooks is averaging 1.8 yards and Pierre Strong is averaging 1.6. The only productive player has been Kaleb Johnson, who broke a couple tackles on his long run at Tampa Bay and is averaging 2.9 yards after contact. But he wound up in the doghouse after a couple fumbles and played just four snaps last week.
With the Packers, Jacobs averaged 3.1 yards after contact in 2024 and 2.9 in 2025.
“I think he’s an elite-level back,” LaFleur said this week.
More than anything, Jacobs will take what’s there and fight for a little more. Instead of trying to bounce runs around the perimeter, like Lloyd does too frequently, he’ll find the smallest of holes and turn something into something more. Last season, according to Sumer Sports, 80.6 percent of his rushing yards came after contact. Among the 52 backs with 100 carries, that ranked fifth.
Jacobs hasn’t carried the ball since last year’s playoff game. There will be some rust and he’ll need to work his way into football shape.
“Hell, yeah,” safety Xavier McKinney said when asked if Jacobs is ready. “I’ve been watching him work out and getting ready for whenever that moment was going to come. And now that it’s here, obviously, it might be some rust here and there, but a fresh-legged Josh is going to be a monster, so it’s going to be good to see.”
LaFleur wasn’t quite as bullish, saying “the eyeball test” following practices on Thursday and Friday would be the determining factor.
Will Josh Jacobs save the running game? True, if by “save” we mean improve to an acceptable level to help the offense take the next step. It worked on the offensive line with the signing of Laken Tomlinson and the insertion of Travis Glover. Certainly, adding a proven force like Jacobs will have a sizable impact, as well.

title: Why Woody Marks Could Take Over Texans' Starting RB Job in Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into Week 7 against the New York Giants facing another game without their starting running back David Montgomery.
Montgomery, who's been atop the Texans' depth chart at running back since the start of the season, has officially been ruled out for a second straight game with a groin issue .
The injury isn't expected to sideline him for much longer, but with another full week of no practice for the veteran back, he'll be out for at least one more contest.
For the Texans' run game, it does shake up the calculus a bit in the short term. Woody Marks will be the lead ball carrier in Week 7 as he was last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and veteran Dare Ogunbowale projects to be Houston's RB2 as Jawhar Jordan has just been placed on their practice squad injured reserve.
However, depending on just how well Marks performs in Week 7 without Montgomery competing for carries, there might be a runway in place for the second-year runner to claim the role as Houston's starting running back moving forward.
Throughout last week's game against the Jaguars, when Marks was tasked to be the Texans' lead ball carrier, he shined when given the opportunity––especially knowing that Jacksonville walked into Week 6 viewed as one of the best rushing defenses in the entire NFL.
Marks ran the ball 15 times for a total of 56 yards on the ground, while also hauling in two receptions for 23 yards. He looked explosive, was more efficient on the ground than he had been all season, and also made an impact in the passing game that boosts his overall stock in this offense.
And the trust that Houston has in Marks as an offensive weapon was shown clearly through his offensive snap count. Marks was on the field for 78% of the total offensive snaps, and saw a touch come his way on over a third of the plays he was out there.
So heading into this weekend, the stage will be set for Marks to have similar usage.
Without Montgomery or Jordan, Marks feels due for a confident 80% or more of the snaps. And against a rushing defense like the Giants, who host ranked bottom-five in the NFL for average yards allowed, there's a real chance that he comes out to have an even bigger performance in Week 7 than what he put out last week.
Let's say if Marks pops off for another big week against the Giants. The Texans' run game is flowing for two straight weeks, he's making plays on the ground and in the passing game, and starts to really give Houston some dynamic playmaking ability in the backfield that was severely lacking through the first five weeks.
If that happens to be the case, it's going to become real challenging for the Texans to come out of the bye week with a healthy David Montgomery and give him a higher share of the workload than Marks.
Since Montgomery's Week 1 debut where he recorded three total touchdowns on the Buffalo Bills , it's been extremely tough for the veteran running back to be an impactful playmaker for this offense.
He's averaging a career low in rushing yards per game (27.6), has the same result for his yards per carry (2.7), and might be in a running back room with a more talented runner––at least at this point in time in their careers. A breakout Week 7 performance for Marks would only strengthen that case to take away more touches from Montgomery.
So keep a close eye on how Marks performs against the Giants this coming weekend, because a strong night on his part could be just the push he needs to get a higher workload to come his way for the second half of the season.

title: Texans Injury Report vs. Giants: 3 Starters Ruled Out, Tank Dell Update
full_text:
The Houston Texans and New York Giants have officially released their third and final injury reports following Friday's practice heading into their Week 7 matchup .
And for both sides, it seems like there's due to be some key absences to take note of. In the case of the Texans specifically, there appears to be three starters that will be missing out of the action this Sunday.
Let's break everything down on the Texans' and Giants' injury report, and what it all means for gameday this weekend:
The Texans are just a bit banged up for this weekend's contest. Not only are they still dealing with some injuries that first occured in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, but they also racked up some bumps and bruises last weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
As for those who will be out for their second-straight game, that's none other than versatile defensive back Jalen Pitre, as well as veteran running back David Montgomery . Each will be out of the mix with their respective injuries––albeit minor ones––and will have their next chance to return to the lineup after the bye in Week 9.
But the Texans will also be dealing with a couple of new injuries. Starting safety Reed Blankenship will be out for this one as he's still in concussion protocol, but also suffering from a hand issue that will keep him on the sidelines as well.
Blankenship left the Texans' last game against the Jaguars in the middle of the first half due to injury, and would inevitably not return to the action. Now for Week 7, that absence within Houston's secondary will continue, and thus leave M.J. Stewart as the most likely fill-in at strong safety next to Calen Bullock.
Along with Blankenship, the Texans are also dealing with a new absence to backup offensive tackle Blake Fisher, who's suffering from a thumb injury that doesn't seem to be a serious one given that he hasn't been placed on injured reserve, though will keep him out for this Sunday against New York.
While not a starting piece of Houston's offensive front, this offense does like to roll out Fisher as a part of their jumbo packages on that side of the ball, as he's been on the field for over 60 snaps through the first five weeks.
This week, though, the Texans will have to have a different approach when it comes to those heavy personnel, whether that be by filling in a different offensive lineman to play Fisher's role, or pivoting from their jumbo packages entirely.
One piece of good news for the Texans, however, is the fact that wide receiver Tank Dell has officially been upgraded to questionable.
And while his status is technically in question for this weekend, head coach DeMeco Ryans has made it clear earlier in the week that he does expect Dell to play. So really, it'll only be a matter of time before we see his status elevated once more.
While the Texans enter this game a bit banged up, the Giants won't be without some key injuries themselves.
Two names have already been ruled out: Tremaine Edmunds and Greg Newsome, two key pieces of the Giants' defense that have started every game so far this season, yet will miss their first games of the year this weekend in Houston.
A couple of other starters for the Giants also appear to be in question leading up to gametime: that's starting right tackle Jermaine Eluemenor and safety Jevon Hollard; both of which would be a major hit to New York's plan of attack on each side of the ball if ruled out.
Kickoff between these two teams lies at 12 p.m. CT in Reliant Stadium on Sunday. By then, we'll not only have a better sense on who will and won't be playing for the Giants, but also have clear confirmation on Tank Dell's status and potential gameday elevation for the first time in over 650 days.
