title: 3 Texans Storylines I'm Watching Most in Week 7 Matchup vs. Giants
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into Week 7 against the New York Giants riding some positive momentum from their last two wins against the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars .
The vibes are feeling a whole lot better for this team compared to where they stood this time two weeks ago. Especially as the Texans head back home for their last game before the bye, paired with the implications of Tank Dell's pending Week 7 return , the energy around Reliant Stadium is going to be rocking this Sunday.
But even beyond the Texans' recent winning ways and Dell's long-awaited return, there are a select few interesting storylines that'll be worth keeping tabs on as Houston tries to head into the bye on a high note.
Let's take a look at three of the biggest Texans storylines I'll be watching for this weekend's matchup against the Giants in their effort to claim three straight wins.
With the Texans officially getting Tank Dell back into the lineup this week, Houston will now have an abundance of receivers to throw into their lineup. That includes Dell, Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Jaylin Noel, Kayshon Boutte, and Xavier Hutchinson.
It's a good problem for the Texans to have. Only a few weeks ago, Houston was desperately in need of reliable pass-catchers in their offense, and now, it almost seems as if they have more than they know what to do with.
Therefore, seeing how the Texans deploy those six wideouts will be a fascinating piece of the puzzle to watch this weekend against the Giants. How many snaps will Tank Dell get in his first game back in action? Will Marvin Harrison Jr. see increased usage , and by how much? Does Jaylin Noel get more work based on his impressive past few weeks?
Regardless of how the opportunities shake out at the position, it sets up to be a tough assignment for the Giants defense to take on, and makes the job a whole lot easier for C.J. Stroud.
The Texans' Week 6 performance against the Jaguars was successful in many ways. But one area in which Houston was lacking a bit more than usual was within their pass rush .
A total of zero sacks were seen from this defense over the course of the contest, which hasn't happened once over the course of this season and 2025. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter were both healthy, but for whatever reason––whether it be the Jaguars' protection, the slick playing surface in London, or both––the pressure just wasn't coming as strongly from Houston.
Seeing that pressure turn around for the Texans would be huge for their chances against the Giants. Not only is Houston's defense at its best when their elite edge duo is firing on all cylinders, but sending that pressure against this New York offensive line and their new starting quarterback, J.J. McCarthy, could be all that they need to get their scoring attack rattled.
The Texans are trending towards not having David Montgomery for a second straight week as he recovers from a groin injury suffered back in Week 5 . He was a DNP at practice on both Wednesday and Thursday, which doesn't bode well for his status come Sunday.
On the surface, you'd think that the Texans' run game would take a hit without Montgomery in the mix. However, it was just last week when Houston was left without their veteran running back against Jacksonville's elite run defense, and they had one of their best performances on the ground all year, led by second-year runner Woody Marks.
Could the Texans have a repeat performance against a Giants run defense, who allow the fourth-most rushing yards per game in the NFL? It's certainly possible. However, Houston will have to do it without their standout complement to Marks from last weekend in Jawhar Jordan, who was placed on the practice squad injured reserve this week.
Expect the Texans to either elevate or sign another running back to their active roster this weekend, or hope that Dare Ogunbowale could make some noise as the change-of-pace back behind Marks.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the Texans Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Houston Texans sit under three weeks away from the NFL trade deadline.
And already before and in the middle of this season, the Texans have been pretty busy on the trade market.
They've brought in Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots following the news of Jayden Higgins' season-ending ACL injury, and most recently, they've added Marvin Harrison Jr. to that same receiver room from the Arizona Cardinals.
So given that this front office has already made a couple of noteworthy moves this year as is, there's a world where the Texans stand pat at the deadline later next month. After all, this team is starting to gain some momentum after their last two wins, and if it ain't broke, maybe they don't want to fix it.
But there's also a good chance that Nick Caserio and Co. get aggressive in an effort to set this roster up in a solid position for the short- and long-term. And if that's the route that the Texans want to take at the deadline, there's one move that would make sense for Houston to make–– and it's actually not a move to bring in new talent.
Instead, the Texans should look into one move to sell off some talent; particularly in their receiver room. And two names stick out for that idea: Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte.
When looking at the Texans' current wide receiver room heading into Week 7, you'll notice that this roster has a ton of depth at the position now that Tank Dell is set to return off of injured reserve from his severe knee injury .
Now, having an abundance of depth doesn't have to be a bad thing. For a Texans offense that's seen a fair share of struggles over the past year-plus, that depth can actually be extremely valuable.
But the Texans might now be at a point where they have more depth in the receiver room than they know what to do with: Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel are all due for their respective snaps, but so are Tank Dell, Kayshon Boutte, and Xavier Hutchinson.
That's six receivers that the Texans could reasonably play on a weekly basis. Three of them are on expiring contracts heading into this offseason, and that doesn't even factor in Jayden Higgins, who is due to return in 2027 to make this position group look even stronger.
So rather than hold onto that depth at the position, and likely leave one or two players hoping for more targets on a weekly basis, why not ship off one of those weapons–– preferably on an expiring contract ––in the receiver room to claim some value for the future?
It makes too much sense for the Texans to at least consider. Without trading one of those receivers at the deadline, they're virtually guaranteed to lose one, or even multiple, on the free agent market come next offseason. Houston won't have a need to re-sign them, and those guys will want to get paid.
Therefore, it puts the expiring deals of Hutchinson and Boutte firmly on the trade radar (Tank Dell is also an expiring contract, but there's a 0% chance he's on the move any time this season). Even if for a minimal return like a day three pick, the Texans prepare better for the future and unload at a position where they have more depth than they really need.
The trade deadline sits on November 10th at 3 p.m. CT, which gives the Texans more than enough time to consider their options. But if there was one "selling" move for this front office to consider, this would be the idea to execute.

title: Texans' Week 7 Odds Point to Potential Blowout vs. Giants, J.J. McCarthy
full_text:
The Houston Texans head into their Week 7 contest against the New York Giants riding the high of logging two straight wins over their last two matchups, and now hope to extend that streak to three in their last game before the bye.
And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality.
Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better.
And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston.
According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7.
That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits.
The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7.
So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season.
Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants.
But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition?
Really, it all relies upon the defense.
Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks.
But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday.
After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it.
So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show.

title: 3 Texans Matchups to Watch Closely Against Giants in Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into Week 7 against the New York Giants with hopes of firing off their third straight win after back-to-back encouraging wins being stamped in the books.
However, for this matchup against the Giants in particular, there's going to be a handful of matchups for the Texans to keep an eye on so that they can check off that aspired third straight victory.
And even for a Giants team that might not have as much talent on paper as the Texans do, their 3-2 record, along with their current first-place standing in the NFC East tends to show that this team isn't one that should be overlooked for this wekeend whatsoever.
So with that in mind, let's break down three key matchups to keep an eye on for the Texans in their Week 7 matchup back at home against the Giants:
The biggest source of the Giants' offense is undoubtably their star wideout, Malik Nabers, who's done nothing but see his stock rise even further than it was throughout the past two weeks. Through Weeks 5 and 6, Nabers has seen 35 targets to turn those into 23 receptions, 286 yards, and a touchdown.
But this week, Nabers will be tasked with one of the most talented corners in the NFL in Derek Stingley Jr.–– someone who's come off of back-to-back All-Pro appearances in 2024 and 2025, and could be one of Nabers' toughest individual matchups of this season so far.
The Texans' secondary has been less than stellar over the past several weeks. It wasn't too long ago that this same Houston defense allowed CeeDee Lamb to have a dominant 17-reception game for 189 yards and a touchdown. But if Stingley and Co. can hold down Nabers for a limited performance, the road to victory can become a whole lot easier.
The Texans' pass rush wasn't quite as dominant as we know them to be this past weekend against the Jacksonville Jaguars . Houston combined for zero sacks throughout the contest, even while both Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter were at full strength.
For reference, there wasn't a single game in which Houston didn't log at least one sack over the course of the 2025 season, and it hadn't happened over the course of 2026 through five weeks. So that was pretty uncharted territory for this defense.
This week, the Texans will be back at home on their own turf, and might have a much better chance of gaining some traction in terms of getting pressure on the quarterback. And when Houston starts racking up sacks, the task becomes immensely more challenging for the opposing offense.
The name I'll be watching closest in Houston's efforts to build a better pass rush will be Danielle Hunter, given that he has the tougher task of lining up against Andrew Thomas on the left side of the line, and could end up being a force multiplier if Will Anderson continues on his DPOY pace.
It was too tough to single out just one player on the Texans' side of the equation here, but seeing how this defense takes on the task of facing Giants starting quarterback J.J. McCarthy will be fascinating to watch unfold.
McCarthy has had nothing short of an up-and-down first three years in the NFL. From a season-ending injury to terrible play with the Minnesota Vikings, to now being traded to and starting for the New York Giants in Week 7, there's a wide range of outcomes for just how McCarthy's day goes here against a Texans defense that many have touted as among the best in the NFL.
If the Texans' defense played like it did last weekend against the Jaguars— a game in which Trevor Lawrence threw for over 300 yards and four touchdowns— then maybe McCarthy can find his way to some steady production to keep the Giants and their scoring attack.
But if the Texans can revert back to defensive output closer to what was seen against the Tennessee Titans and Cam Ward, then this could quickly become a long day for McCarthy and this Giants offense.

title: Everything Texans WR Tank Dell Said Ahead of His Long-Awaited Return
full_text:
The Houston Texans are finally going to be getting fan-favorite wide reciever Tank Dell back in the lineup this weekend against the New York Giants.
After a long, near two-year recovery process after Dell had first suffered his devastating knee injury in December of 2024, the time has finally come for the wideout to get back on the field in Week 7, and catch some passes from C.J. Stroud as one of his top playmakers in this offense.
And ahead of Dell's long-awaited return to the field, he fielded some questions from the media a few days out from the Texans' Week 7 contest against the Giants .
Let's take a look at seven quotes from Dell leading up to him officially suiting up for this weekend's matchup.
On Wednesday, Dell was first asked about how he's feeling in the days ahead of his first time back on an NFL field in nearly two years. And overall, he's seemingly not feeling too overwhelmed. Above all, he's feeling a lot of gratitude.
"First off, I'm blessed. I want to thank God for getting me back in this position," Dell said. "I don't think I'm overwhelmed. A lot of people have been hitting me up, but I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious, of course."
"It's been two years— well, dang near two years— but I don't think I'm overwhelmed. I'm anxious to get back out there and play some football, but I'm blessed, man. That's all I can say."
The Texans won't be setting any crazy expectations for Dell this weekend , and neither will Dell himself. Of course, his competitive drive will continue to have a nose to make plays, but he's looking to live in the moment more than anything.
"Go out there and have fun, man. First game back, I'm just trying to go out there and have fun," Dell said of his expectations.
"Of course, y'all know I'm competitive, so I want to make some plays. A lot of plays. But my main thing is just to live in that moment, be where my feet are, have fun, fly around and just try to be who I am. Not try— be who I am.
Stroud is going to find Dell to make a play at some point over the course of Week 7's game against the Giants. But how does Dell envision that first catch going?
No matter how big of a play that catch ends up being, he's sure to have a pretty passionate celebration.
"I don't care if the first catch is two yards, five yards, I'm spiking the ball. I'm doing what I got to do, man," Dell said.
"It's going to feel good. I know there's a lot of questions about how I'm going to look when I get tackled. I don't care about none of that. I'm ready to get tackled. I'm going to be joyful. Y'all are going to see the passion I have after I have that first catch."
Dell has been stuck on the Texans' sidelines for over 650 days now, including throughout all of the 2025 season. And such a traumatic experience is bound to have a huge impact on anyone more than just what happens on the football field.
As to how the injury recovery process changed Dell as a person, it taught him how to truly live in the moment.
"It just made me live in the moment and be grateful for everything," Dell said of what his recovery taught him. "People say that repetitively all the time, but when you actually go through it and have to be the one who pulls yourself out of it, I feel like it makes you grateful and thankful that it could have been way worse, even though it was a crazy, traumatic incident."
"There are people out here going through things way worse than me. I got injured in a football game, but somebody else is fighting for their life for real. It's just about being grateful and thankful to be where I'm at, man, and having fun."
After Dell first went down with his knee injury against the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024, there were serious questions regarding whether or not the Texans' wideout would ever be able to play in an NFL game ever again.
Fast forward to this week, and Dell has defied those odds. But did he have any doubts himself about being able to make it through the long journey back? It certainly doesn't seem like it.
"I think I made a post a couple of days after it happened where I said, 'I'm going to be back.' In my mind, it was never a question of whether I was going to be back," Dell said. "Of course, throughout the process, you question yourself, but you have to have faith in God. I never doubted that I was going to work myself back to being able to get on the field."
"I already knew I was going to put in whatever work I had to put in. Even on the days when I woke up and didn't feel like doing anything, I still gave it my all, came in here and did everything. I was in the facility every day throughout the year and offseason. I was just making sure I put my best foot forward to come back and play football."
Compared to the last time that Dell took the field alongside the Texans' offense, today's wide receiver room in Houston is looking a whole lot different than it did then. No Stefon Diggs, no Jared Wayne, but guys like Kayshon Boutte, Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel have been brought into the mix.
And while on one hand, it puts Dell in an offense with a lot of mouths to feed, he's confident that in a deep wide receiver room like this one, getting everyone involved and making plays will allow everyone's energy to feed off one another.
"I think it's great, Dell said of the Texans' wide receiver room. "If you look back at last year, we had a lot of receivers and tight ends down in a big game. Just having more guys in the room who can go out there and make a play helps us.
"We feed off each other's energy and making plays, and I feel like we're competitive. If I see Nico make a play, in a non-selfish way, I want to go out there and make a play, too. I'm going to be happy for him, and I want to go out there and make a play. It's the same with Marvin, Kayshon, Hutch, J-Noel, everybody."
"It's exciting to have that type of room. The cream is going to rise to the top. If you're a competitor and know how you can play football, just have fun doing it. Don't be selfish or look at it as a bad thing. When there are blessings in the neighborhood, you'll get blessed, too. Just go out there, work hard and make the play when the ball comes."
Given that the Texans are going to be back at home for Dell's long-awaited return, there's no doubt that all of Reliant Stadium will be fired up the second they see their fan-favorite wideout run out of the tunnel for his first game back since 2024.
And so of course, Dell has no doubts that the environment on Sunday will be unmatched.
I feel like they're going to go crazy. I'm excited for that, too. That's what I'm saying — fill the stadium up, please," Dell said. "It's great to have that support from Houston, getting drafted by the Texans and being part of this organization. It's a beautiful organization, the same with the University of Houston. I feel like I'm a Florida boy, but, like I said before, I feel like this is home for me, too."
"It's great, and I know it's going to be a great feeling when I run out of the tunnel."

title: Texans' First Injury Report vs. Giants Features Several Concerns for Week 7
full_text:
The Houston Texans have dropped their first injury report of the week heading into their upcoming matchup against the New York Giants .
And after their first practice, there's a good chunk of players on the roster listed as either a DNP or a limited participant.
Let's break down everything to know about the Texans' Wednesday injury report:
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (knee) S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) RB David Montgomery (groin) OT Blake Fisher (thumb) OT Trent Brown (wrist) TE Dalton Schultz (calf)
WR Nico Collins (rest) LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) DE Will Anderson Jr. (rest) DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) DE Logan Hall (knee)
The Texans have been dealing with injuries to both running back David Montgomery and defensive back Jalen Pitre since their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans. Both of them missed the trip to London against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and they've both now missed their first of three practices heading into this weekend against New York. Both of them were considered week-to-week upon the announcement of their injuries a couple of weeks ago, and thus could provide a bit of optimism for their availability vs. the Giants. However, don't be surprised if either or both are due to miss another game.
As mentioned by DeMeco Ryans earlier this week, veteran safety Reed Blankenship is in concussion protocol , and therefore didn't practice with the team on Wednesday. It also seems as if he's dealing with a hand injury that's limiting him as well. So if things continue to trend in this direction for Blankenship, he could be forced out for Week 7, and instead return after the Texans' bye in Week 9. If that's the case, expect M.J. Stewart to be the next man up to start at safety next to Calen Bullock.
One noteworthy name to keep an eye on within the Texans' injury report heading deeper into the week is tight end Dalton Schultz, who seemed to suffer a calf injury in the middle of their trip to London against Jacksonville, but wound up finishing the game anyways. Given that he did finish the game out against the Jaguars, that tends to be a good sign that he'll be able to play this coming weekend. But in any event, he is forced to miss time; keep an eye on Foster Moreau, fresh off of his two-touchdown day.
Tank Dell is officially set to make his return to the NFL field this weekend. He's now logged multiple full practices over the past three weeks and will be designated for return from injured reserve for his first game in over 650 days. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about Dell's pending return earlier this weekend: "I expect Tank just to be himself, and just play the offense the right way," Ryans said. "No huge expectations for what he needs to do. We're all just going to be excited... I'm just thankful, grateful for him to have this opportunity to return." "I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there. And that's the only thing that matters."

title: Texans' DeMeco Ryans Shrugs Off Giants' Decision to Start J.J. McCarthy
full_text:
Heading into the Houston Texans' Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants , the opposition has made an eye-catching shake-up at their quarterback position.
The Giants have been rolling out Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback ever since Jaxson Dart went down with a knee injury in Week 2. However, New York head coach John Harbaugh announced Wednesday that J.J. McCarthy would start under center against Houston.
McCarthy had previously made an appearance at the end of the Giants' Week 6 game against the New Orleans Saints, in which he performed relatively well in the reps he was given: he completed 11 of 21 passes for 243 yards with a touchdown, an interception, and had two rushing attempts for 26 yards.
So now, the Giants have seen enough out of the 23-year-old quarterback from that showing to warrant another start in Week 7 on the road against Houston.
However, heading into that Week 7 duel against the Giants, it doesn't seem like Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans is too concerned about who's starting at quarterback for New York.
Ryans was asked during his Wednesday presser about his thoughts on the Giants starting J.J. McCarthy for their Week 7 matchup against Houston.
But overall, the focus remained more upon the Texans' defense being better prepared for the week ahead, no matter who the opposing quarterback is.
"For us, it really doesn't matter who plays quarterback," Ryans said of the Giants' quarterback decision. "For us, defensively, it's been about our process, and how do we do things that we do the right way, and do them well."
"So, whoever's at quarterback doesn't really dictate what we're going to do defensively. It's about us. We got to play better defensively, because it wasn't good enough in our last outing."
Of course, Ryans and the Texans won't be heading into this game without doing their due diligence scouting and studying film on McCarthy.
Knowing that he will be the guy under center could make Houston's preparation a little bit easier by having a bit more clarity on how New York's offense will look. Or, perhaps that pre-game prep can be a little more challenging without having as vast of a sample size with McCarthy as the Giants' starting quarterback.
But no matter what the Giants' quarterback looks like, that's not where Ryans head is sitting at a few days out from their Week 7 matchup. More than anything, Ryans clearly wasn't too satisfied with the output his defense showcased last week against the Jaguars –– and he wants those lapses ironed out ASAP.
In Week 6, Houston allowed Jacksonville to become the third team to score 30-plus points on them in a single game on the year. For reference, that feat only happened once over the course of the 2025 season in their Week 18 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts .
So rather than putting a ton of focus on the external factors in terms of who the Giants will have under center, Ryans is taking a different approach. He's more locked in on how he and his team can take the necessary steps forward to be the elite defense that they proved to be capable of all of last season.
Maybe this game can present a get-right opportunity for the Texans' defense and their hopes of lifting back to that elite level they stood at all of last season. But if it isn't, the conversations around exactly what's happened to this side of the ball in Houston will only continue to get louder.

title: Texans OL Emerging as Trade Candidate to Watch Before Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is a little less than three weeks away.
That means a few players around the league are due to find their way into some interesting trade rumors over the coming days––and that certainly doesn't exclude the Texans, who have already made a couple of acquisitions over the past couple of months in the case of Kayshon Boutte and Marvin Harrison Jr.
However, some of the latest buzz around the Texans seems to hint that there's one player on the roster on the verge of getting shipped out between now and the deadline: and that's none other than two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Wyatt Teller.
According to ESPN' s Dan Graziano , Teller has been seen as "potentially available" in the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline as someone who's not working out in his new situation in Houston.
"Sometimes, circumstances change or things don't work out as expected, so teams will pivot if the terms are favorable," Graziano wrote. "A couple of other 2026 free agent signings who stand out as potentially available due to their situations not working out include Texans offensive lineman Wyatt Teller and Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen."
While the return for Teller might not be too grand of a package for the Texans, seeing Teller on his way out in the next few weeks certainly wouldn't be the most shocking outcome.
Teller, who was signed earlier this offseason, was brought into Houston with the intent of being able to compete for the Texans' starting left guard spot . He was inked to a two-year, $16 million deal, with most preseason expectations settling on Teller being the favorite to eventually claim that starting spot.
However, as the season got closer and closer to kicking off, it became clear that Teller was not going to be within the interior starting offensive line unit. Instead, the Texans were bound to start rookie Keylan Rutledge at left guard , Evan Brown at center, and Ed Ingram at right guard.
Teller did get two starts for the Texans in Weeks 2 and 3 at right guard as Ingram was sidelined with a groin injury. Though once he returned, he would settle back into his regular reserve spot— a role which he hasn't exactly been in routinely throughout what's been a relatively successful pro career.
So instead of letting Teller essentially rot on the bench for the next several weeks of the regular season as an unsuccessful free agent signing, the Texans could instead look to trade him.
Houston would be able to get some type of return on their previous investment, Teller could get a fresh start elsewhere with the hope that he can find a starting spot, and both sides can walk away wiping their hands clean.
So will the move actually wind up happening for Teller? It likely depends on whether or not the Texans can get the right package in return for him.
Given that Teller's in the back-nine of his career as is, and hasn't performed well enough to be a starter on Houston's up-and-down offensive line, there are no guarantees that the front office would be able to net much of an appealing package for him, even from an offensive line-needy team.
Yet, for a day three pick or similar value? That might just be enough for this front office to have interest in pulling the trigger. Time will tell if Houston winds up receiving that, but don't be surprised if we're entering the final days of Teller's brief time as a Texan.

title: Colts Stars Respond to Trade Rumors as Deadline Approaches
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have already made one massive change this week, and with the Nov. 10 trade deadline getting closer, the speculation is not slowing down.
Since firing general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, Indianapolis has become one of the NFL's most intriguing teams to watch as the trade deadline approaches. At 2-4, names like DeForest Buckner, Jonathan Taylor and Quenton Nelson have naturally been pulled into trade conversations.
I still don't believe the Colts should tear this roster down. There are too many cornerstone players worth keeping around for whoever takes over this front office next.
But the players themselves are hearing the noise, and this week, several of the biggest names in Indianapolis addressed their futures.
Buckner is probably the easiest name to connect to trade speculation because he is 32 years old and playing on an expiring contract.
When asked directly whether he wants to remain with the Colts, though, Buckner wouldn't entertain the conversation.
“Yeah, right now I'm just focused on the Vikings,” Buckner said.
He acknowledged that he knows how the business works, but called the speculation a distraction. His focus remains preparing to help Indianapolis beat Minnesota on Sunday.
Buckner also spoke highly of Ballard, saying the two had a “great relationship” and that he has “nothing but love for him and his family.”
Like the rest of the locker room, Buckner's approach to a chaotic week has been simple: move forward and focus on the task at hand.
Taylor was much more emotional when discussing Ballard, the general manager who drafted him in 2020.
“Just lost for words,” Taylor said. “Definitely upset because at some point, it's on the team as a collective, coaches and players, in order to prove the GM right.”
Taylor said Ballard meant “a ton” to his career, pointing to their Wisconsin connection and the belief the organization showed in him coming out of the draft.
As for the possibility of being traded, Taylor wants no part of that conversation right now.
“I haven't given it any thought,” Taylor said. “That'd be crazy right now.”
He called looking ahead to what could happen a disservice to his teammates and the organization with an undefeated Minnesota team waiting Sunday.
Taylor also made it clear why he wanted to remain in Indianapolis when he signed his recent extension. He praised the way the organization treats its players and staff, calling the Colts “a special place.”
Nelson took a similar approach when asked whether Ballard's departure created questions about his own future.
“No, I have no questions,” Nelson said. “I leave that up to God.”
His focus is on getting better and being at his best this week, and Nelson called facing an undefeated Vikings team a “great opportunity” for Indianapolis to start turning things around.
But when asked if Indianapolis is somewhere he would like to continue playing long term, Nelson left little doubt.
“I love it here,” Nelson said. “Met my wife here. Really appreciate and love this organization.”
Nelson also expressed appreciation for Ballard, recalling the accountability his former general manager showed him as early as his rookie season.
For now, Buckner, Taylor and Nelson are all saying essentially the same thing: ignore the noise and prepare for Minnesota.
The trade rumors aren't going away before Nov. 10, especially after a front-office shakeup. But at least publicly, three of the Colts' biggest names are more concerned with saving this season than worrying about where they might be playing next.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Anthony Richardson May Have Just Put Final Nail in Colts Coffin
full_text:
Just when it looked like Anthony Richardson might have one last path back onto the field for the Indianapolis Colts, another problem has entered the picture.
Richardson is facing a misdemeanor charge for marijuana possession stemming from an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Indiana.
According to court records, Richardson was pulled over after police noticed an expired registration that did not match his vehicle. An officer reported smelling marijuana, and Richardson admitted he had smoked inside the car so he would not do so around his children.
Police found a small amount of marijuana and THC-infused gummies inside the vehicle. Richardson was briefly handcuffed during the search, but he was not taken into custody and was instead issued a summons.
The charge was formally filed Oct. 19, and a bench trial is scheduled for Jan. 4, 2027.
“We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information. We will have no further comment at this time,” the Colts said.
The timing could not be much worse.
Indianapolis is 2-4, Chris Ballard was fired Monday, and Daniel Jones has struggled through six starts with 1,290 passing yards, four touchdowns and six interceptions.
That had at least reopened the conversation about Richardson getting another opportunity if Jones continued to struggle. Noah Compton recently argued for Colts On SI that putting Richardson back on the field should at least be on the table as Indianapolis evaluates what is left of this season.
Richardson remained QB2 behind Jones for Sunday’s loss to Tennessee and has continued practicing with the team since the Oct. 12 stop.
Also, forty states have legalized cannabis for recreational or medical use, while Indiana remains without either a recreational or comprehensive medical marijuana program. Richardson just happens to play in one of the states where possession can still result in a criminal charge.
So no, this shouldn't suddenly change everything. But Richardson could still face consequences from the NFL.
Under the league's substance abuse policy, a first-time violation of laws involving drug possession can result in a suspension of up to four games, depending on the circumstances.
That is far from a guaranteed suspension, but it adds another layer of uncertainty to Richardson's future in Indianapolis. For a quarterback already struggling to find his way back onto the field, potentially losing more time is the last thing he needs.
The stop happened one day after Indianapolis lost 34-22 in Pittsburgh. One week later, the Colts lost at home to a previously winless Titans team, Ballard was fired the next morning, and now this becomes public four days later.
Everything surrounding this team is moving downhill fast.
If this ends up serving as the final nail in Richardson’s Colts coffin, it would be an unfortunately poetic ending to one of the most dysfunctional quarterback experiments this franchise has had.
A former No. 4 overall pick with rare physical talent, repeated injuries, a 2024 benching and a lost starting job may now have his Indianapolis tenure further complicated by something that, in most NFL markets, probably would not have become much of a story at all.
