title: Three Takeaways From Chiefs' Announcement of Josh Simmons Going on Injured Reserve
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs face their toughest test yet on Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, and making matters worse is that the club will continue to be without the services of left tackle Josh Simmons.
Last year's first-round pick hasn't played in a game all season since sustaining a back injury in August , although he did return to practice last week on a limited workload. Unfortunately, that didn't wind up parlaying into getting on the game field, as the former Ohio State standout is set to miss even more time.
Speaking to the media on Thursday, team vice president of sports medicine and performance Rick Burkholder provided a complete breakdown of the Simmons situation. The star tackle has since been placed on the injured reserve list, meaning he's out for a minimum of four additional games.
A clip of Burkholder's statement is below — let's dive into it with three key takeaways.
The #Chiefs , when they have a health situation that requires more context, send out head trainer Rick Burkholder to explain it to the media. He did that today with LT Josh Simmons. Here’s his full explanation: https://t.co/pYCEWuZHtE pic.twitter.com/FHNcMQRh5n
Burkholder opened his media availability by pinpointing when Simmons first got hurt. It's now been over two months since the sophomore tackle first reported a calf issue that turned out to be a back one.
"On August 17, Josh came to me with calf discomfort and feeling that he couldn't post on a single leg in training camp practices," Burkholder said. "This was the same leg that he had knee surgery on in 2024. He was evaluated by our physicians who, thankfully, suspected a low-back injury instead of a lower-leg or knee ailment.
"We obtained an MRI in St. Joe that confirmed that he had a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine. That disc problem was higher up than what we normally see in our offensive linemen, which complicated the case. We recommended a second opinion, as we always do with all of our injured guys and, through his agent and Josh, they selected a spine specialist in California that we have used previously and is really well-known in the NFL.
"He went there and was evaluated, and the recommendation was to do rehabilitation — not surgery — with the intent that we would do an MRI in the near future to see what that disc looked like. Josh continued to progress, and the repeat MRI a few weeks later showed that the disc improved, so no surgery was recommended and rehab would continue."
Head coach Andy Reid acknowledged the bulging disc late last month after previously being noncommittal — and even a bit mysterious — about a recovery timeline or return-to-play window. We now know what triggered Simmons' injury, how it was managed and why he didn't start the regular season on IR.
When Simmons got on the practice field last Wednesday, it was indeed in an effort to evaluate his readiness and continued ramp-up period. It also got many in Chiefs circles buzzing about the much-anticipated season debut for one of the franchise's top young players.
Given that Simmons was a limited participant from there onward and then didn't get any work in this week, something appeared to be up. Burkholder revealed that Simmons simply isn't where he needs to be progress-wise.
"Throughout this process, we've had frequent communication with the second opinion, with our doctors and Josh and his agent," Burkholder said. "Josh worked his tail off. He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to the point where he returned to practice in a limited capacity last week. However, we feel that he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps in recovery with return to competition. He's just not there yet."
Everyone then opted to take a break and come up with the best course of action for Simmons' health and eventual on-field viability.
"After discussion with Josh yesterday, we gave him some time to talk with his family and his representatives to investigate next steps as he goes through this process. That's why he was listed yesterday as both personal and with the back injury as we determined these next steps. He took the day off to get with his people."
All of this culminated with Burkholder announcing that Kansas City would be putting Simmons on IR, which the club formally did later on Thursday. As a result, Simmons is ineligible to play versus the Seahawks or in upcoming contests against the Denver Broncos, New York Jets or Atlanta Falcons. The earliest he can return is Week 11 against the Arizona Cardinals.
It wasn't solely Simmons' call. Burkholder emphasized that the IR decision was a collaborative effort that included multiple medical teams, the Chiefs' coaching staff, the front office and, of course, Burkholder and Simmons themselves.
"It was decided and agreed upon by everybody — his people, his agent, him, myself, Andy (Reid), (Brett) Veach — that he should be placed on IR to give him more time to return to full function," Burkholder said. "He'll continue with the rehab process with the goal of returning to play at the high level he achieved in the past."
The organization's hope is now that Simmons will be able to play during the stretch run of the 2026-27 campaign. Surgery still isn't the optimal route, which is a silver lining in what's otherwise still a far less than ideal set of circumstances.
"I give a lot of credit to Josh, my docs, my physicians and my staff," Burkholder added. "I just give them a ton of credit for navigating through this injury to the point where surgery is not recommended and he just needs more time to return to full function."

full_text:
Ahead of the Kansas City Chiefs' Week 7 showdown against the Seattle Seahawks , the team has a mixed bag of injury news.
On Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid indicated that wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) and right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) would not practice today, while left tackle Josh Simmons (back) is expected to participate to some extent.
Afternoon update: Despite not receiving a pre-practice designation from Reid, Simmons was not seen at practice, according to numerous reports . Later in the afternoon, Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest reported that Simmons would be listed as "DNP (back/personal)."

Rice suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders and has been sidelined since. Even with the benefit of the team's Week 5 bye, Rice was not ready to practice in the team's lead-up to Week 6.

The Chiefs also signed linebacker Aiden Fisher to the practice squad, adding the rookie seventh-round draft pick to their developmental plans. Fisher played for James Madison and Indiana before being drafted by the Houston Texans in April.

title: Chiefs vs. Seahawks: Kenneth Walker Looking to Prove Why Seattle Should’ve Paid Him
full_text:
Running back Kenneth Walker III has been nothing short of magnificent since arriving in Kansas City this offseason. Even after the Chiefs' bye week passed, he still leads the NFL in rushing yards despite having played in one fewer game than the next five guys behind him.
"K9" was perhaps the most significant acquisition that general manager Brett Veach made in the winter. It didn't come without its criticisms, though. The age-old argument about whether it's worth it or not to pay a running back big money led many to believe the injury-prone Walker would be a signing KC would soon regret. Through the first couple of months of his tenure in the red and gold, that couldn't be further from the truth. Walker looks like one of the best running backs the Chiefs franchise has ever seen and is making a legitimate case to compete for AFC Offensive Player of the Year. His impending return to his former team could provide another opportunity to show just how valuable that investment has been.
When the Chiefs travel to Seattle for this week's edition of Sunday Night Football, Walker will be making a homecoming to the team he spent his first four years with. He played a huge part in the Seahawks' 2026 Super Bowl run and took home the MVP award in the big game with a 135-yard performance on the ground.
The split between both parties was far more amicable than some departures. Walker left Seattle on decent terms after winning his first Super Bowl ring, forever cementing his place in franchise history as a result. However, he still has plenty to prove to the organization given how his contract situation unfolded this offseason.
When head coach Andy Reid was asked whether Walker would take this game a little more seriously than the others, he refuted those claims and said it'd be business as usual for the superstar tailback. That may be true from Walker's perspective, but it's hard not to wonder if facing the team that drafted him will bring out a little extra motivation.
#Chiefs HC Andy Reid on Kenneth Walker returning to Seattle Sunday evening to take on his former team #Seahawks “I don’t think he’ll have an issue with that, he’s plays aggressive, physical football anyway, that part isn’t going to change—he’s going to bring it even if he’s…
In the offseason, Walker inked a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs, but finding a new home was never something he necessarily planned on doing. The Seahawks had expressed interest in keeping him, but they couldn't meet his contract demands, sending Walker into free agency and eventually to KC. The Seahawks chose to allocate that money elsewhere and pursue a new running back in the draft by selecting Jadarian Price in the first round. It's safe to say that hasn't panned out for the reigning champions so far.
Putting aside Walker's success for a minute, Seattle's running game ranks 21st in the NFL in yards per carry and 30th in EPA per play. A slow start from the Notre Dame rookie Price and an early-season injury to Zach Charbonnet forced Seattle to turn to Emanuel Wilson. Charbonnet is actually expected to return from his lingering knee injury for his season debut this week, but there's even a story there.
Throughout his entire time with the Seahawks, there was always an ongoing joke that whenever Walker would put together a strong drive, his rhythm would be disrupted when Seattle's coaches put Charbonnet in at the goal line. Walker never got the full opportunity he deserved in Seattle, and hours after he announced he was heading to the Chiefs, the Seahawks chose to pay return specialist Rashid Shaheed more money annually instead.
Now, the Chiefs have let Walker play out to his full potential as a bell-cow back. He's on pace for 400+ touches, and for perspective, he never surpassed 255 touches from scrimmage during his time as a Seahawk.
It's almost become cliché to keep talking about Walker because of how good he's been. Seattle's run game has faltered without him, and the Chiefs have given him the freedom to establish himself as one of the league's premier backs. On Sunday, he has a chance to make a statement against the team that ultimately decided he wasn't worth the contract he deserved.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Who's in for a Big Post-Bye Stretch?
full_text:
Another week, another Kansas City Chiefs victory. Fresh off a bye to rest up but still nursing some injuries, KC hosted the Los Angeles Chargers and didn't have much trouble en route to a 22-6 victory in front of a raucous crowd at Arrowhead Stadium.
With the win came plenty of positive contributions from young players. Others, however, are raising questions of whether they've plateaued for the time being. Week 7's showdown with the Seattle Seahawks on the road should help us learn plenty about the true colors of Kansas City's youngsters.
Following Week 6, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each qualifying 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott isn't included due to him currently being on the physically unable to perform list .
This list contains plenty of usual suspects, headlined by the cornerback duo of Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane. The former had a brilliant Sunday, making multiple pass breakups and also flashing his ability as a tackler. The latter did have one terrible rep on a deep pass, although it served as one of the few low points in his debut campaign to date.
Along the defensive line, second-round edge rusher R Mason Thomas continues to win quickly. The sack numbers may not be there yet, but there's no denying his raw talent that simply must always be accounted for. First-round tackle Peter Woods is quiet in the box score for the most part but did earn the first half-sack of his career in Week 6.
Moving up a tier this week are a rookie and a sophomore. At the left tackle spot, Kansas City continues to game plan around having undrafted man Kahlil Benson in the lineup, but he shored up his play a bit coming out of the bye. He still has the occasional lapse — head coach Andy Reid alluded to one on Monday — but he's faring better than expected. Even if he isn't a clear-cut starter, he deserves props.
On the other side of the ball, defensive end Ashton Gillotte appears to be putting his plantar fascia injury behind him at least a little bit. He got a sack on Los Angeles quarterback Justin Herbert on Sunday and, per Pro Football Focus , has three pressures in consecutive games.
It brings me no joy bumping fifth-round rookie halfback Emmett Johnson down here, but his last few games haven't been very productive at all. In Weeks 4-6, he's toted the ball nine times and managed just 23 yards. That's despite combining to play 48 offensive snaps. Johnson's time should still be coming — this feels like a temporary demotion.
2025 fourth-round receiver Jalen Royals got targeted four times in the passing game with Rashee Rice ( hamstring ) out, recording a pair of receptions for 24 yards. He also played 45 snaps, marking the second game in a row his share has increased. Elsewhere as far as pass catchers are concerned, Jake Briningstool's elevation stems solely from workload (his snaps have increased by two in Weeks 4 and 6) and rookie wideout Cyrus Allen recorded his first two NFL catches over the weekend.
UDFA defensive tackle Bryson Eason isn't a primary special-teamer (he hasn't played there at all) but he also isn't seeing the field much on defense. He's somewhere in the middle, albeit not in his own tier.
There still isn't anything to see here. Simmons is making progress as he works his way back from a bulging disc , and Reid was noncommittal about his playing status on Monday. If the 2025 first-round pick isn't back this Sunday, look for Week 8 as a potential season debut spot.
Safety Nwankpa feels like he might be on the verge of increased playing time, although it might require an injury before he's unleashed on the defensive end. Running back Brashard Smith makes sense as a candidate to take special teams opportunities from wideout Nikko Remigio, who struggled once again against Los Angeles.
Jeffrey Bassa is turning himself into a trusted core player for coordinator Dave Toub on teams. Similar to Nwankpa, though, he's buried on the depth chart on defense.
Since playing 47 special teams snaps in the first three weeks of the season, fourth-round rookie cornerback Jadon Canady hasn't been active for a game. He's got to come down a tier.
Elsewhere, the trio of quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn can be classified as organizational depth for now.

title: Chiefs On SI Mailbag: Is the Chiefs' Offensive Line Set for a Disappointment in Seattle?
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 5-0 and alone atop the AFC as the only undefeated team in the conference, but they still have plenty of questions to answer ahead of their primetime Sunday night showdown against the Seattle Seahawks this weekend.
Every week here in the Chiefs On SI mailbag , we take your questions from @chiefs_kcsn on Twitter/X and @jbbrisco.com on Bluesky , navigating the biggest unknowns the Chiefs have as the season rolls on. Let's get to it!
Does the dam eventually break on the O-line without Josh Simmons? - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
It's sure looking like Sunday night's game in Seattle will be the O-line's most difficult test yet. With left tackle Josh Simmons still appearing to be in "ramp-up" territory this week, I'm assuming that undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson will get his sixth start at left tackle, while right tackle Jaylon Moore's status is questionable after leaving the Chiefs' win over the Los Angeles Chargers due to a concussion. With the inherent unknowns of concussions and the NFL's concussion protocol, Joshua Ezeudu could be getting the start at right tackle.
According to ESPN , the Seahawks have the No. 1 pass rush win rate in the league through Week 6. That has resulted in 16 sacks and the league's highest quarterback knockdown percentage and second-highest pressure percentage , so this isn't a great time to have a banged-up line.
Still, the Chiefs' interior of Kingsley Suamataia, Creed Humphrey and Trey Smith can still be trusted, and they've managed without Simmons so far. I'd be surprised if the KC O-line was entirely overwhelmed in a game-altering way in Seattle, but I'd also be surprised if they pitched a shutout against the Seahawks.
Do all roads lead to another Chiefs vs. 49ers Super Bowl? - @toptrevor.bsky.social
It sure feels that way, doesn't it? I've been enormously impressed by how the 49ers have managed yet another injury-ravaged season, and I think their ability to stay afloat (and undefeated) despite health woes has earned them a reasonable claim to the No. 1 spot in some power rankings . However, those losses can stack up and cause more significant damage later in the year, so I fear for the Niners' long-term health.
While the Chiefs still have flaws, just like every other team in the NFL, I'm hugely excited by the possibility of them regaining Simmons and potentially ending the year healthier than they started it.
KCSN’s NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 6 📊 These rankings reflect the average of our hosts’ votes — who’s too high and who’s too low? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/dGx1EC3wdL
Good, bad, or both, what has surprised you the most about the Chiefs so far this season? - @MrEd315
The biggest positive surprise has to be the absolute dominance from Kenneth Walker III . I'm not surprised that he's been good—that was to be expected—but I'm amazed by how good, how consistent, and how diversely superb he's been, while totally transforming the KC offense.
The bad surprises come from the Chiefs' special teams. Many assumed that Harrison Butker's recent issues had been largely due to lingering injury issues, giving him a chance to return to his previous level after another offseason to settle back in, but he's still missing enough kicks to cause some fair concern .
Adding in issues with special teams penalties , Nikko Remigio's fumbled punt against the Chargers and the lack of a role for Brashard Smith amidst a generally underwhelming return game, the Chiefs' third phase still has a lot of work to do.
Considering the Broncos' upcoming schedule, is the AFC West still a live fight? - @oscarbobo.bsky.social
It absolutely is! The Broncos are coming off of a gross, uninspiring win over the Seahawks, but they're still 4-2 ahead of a relatively soft stretch in their upcoming schedule. If the Broncos beat the Chiefs in Denver on November 1, the divisional race will immediately be back on after KC's early lead. If the Chiefs win at Mile High Stadium in two weeks, it would make it extremely difficult for Denver to come roaring back.

title: Chiefs Stock Watch: Who Helped and Hurt Their Case in Week 6 Win vs. Chargers?
full_text:
Five games into the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs have helped themselves in a major way by already picking up three wins against divisional opponents. Sunday's Week 6 triumph over the Los Angeles Chargers wasn't the prettiest of victories, but Andy Reid's team thoroughly outplayed its rival by a multitude of measurements nonetheless.
In the 22-6 outcome in favor of the hosts, several critical players managed to make an impact on their respective side of the ball. Others struggled to execute what was asked of them, although there's still plenty of time to turn things around.
Let's dive into the good and bad from Week 6's Chiefs victory against Los Angeles and single out three players whose stock is trending up, as well as three who could use a better showing in Week 7 and beyond.
These players stood out for positive reasons over the weekend, potentially changing the trajectory of their seasons in the process.
The Chiefs' defense is performing at a very respectable level this season, and its new-look secondary is a significant reason why. A returning player from a year ago, 2025 third-round pick Nohl Williams, has starred to this point in the campaign and may have turned in his best outing yet on Sunday.
After making a big-time downhill tackle on the Chargers' opening drive, the Cal product was banged up but stayed in the game and continued to get noticed. A pair of pass breakups — one on a second-and-9 on the next possession and a third-and-goal stop in the second half — showcased his instincts and timing. Finally, Williams prevented wideout KeAndre Lambert-Smith from converting on a fourth down in the final frame.
The sophomore stopper is disruptive, tough and thorough in the defensive backfield, which is precisely what Kansas City needs.
What a turnaround it's been over the last month for one Xavier Worthy. Through three outings, he'd averaged five targets a game but managed only 6.3 yards per reception and looked more and more like an afterthought in the offense. In his last two weeks of play, he's gone for seven targets each time and racked up 143 yards in the process, good for 13 yards per catch. Sunday was his most complete showing to date.
Worthy had a 33-yarder wiped out by an illegal block by tight end Travis Kelce right out of the gate, then followed it up with a gain of 15 on the very next play. He notched 70 yards on five receptions in the first half alone and made a nice diving snag in the second half. With the KC wideout room severely banged up at the moment , Worthy's ability to step up and rise to the occasion is a pleasant surprise for the Chiefs as the season approaches its midpoint.
Speaking of players who made the most of their opportunities in Week 6, Noah Gray matched the receiving output of Kelce by mustering 53 yards in the home win. Gray hauled in each of the three targets thrown his way and displayed some rare post-catch chops on a 31-yard rumble to boot. Kelce's ankle injury limited his effectiveness and availability a bit, so Gray being the one to help insulate the pass catchers was a nice development.
There's only room for three here, but defensive end George Karlaftis deserves considerable praise for his recent play. He's undoubtedly turning into quite the productive player for Kansas City and has been a driving force in multiple victories.
This group of three didn't live up to the hype in Week 6. It isn't necessarily time to panic, but it's certainly time to be on watch.
Back to the aforementioned receiver injuries. Given that Tyquan Thornton is on injured reserve due to a dislocated ankle and Rashee Rice needed (at least) another week to rehab a hamstring issue , this was a massive chance for a lesser-discussed wideout like Nikko Remigio to take a role and run with it on Sunday. He did nothing of the sort on the offensive end, receiving all of two offensive snaps. He also had a special teams fumble.
Coordinator Dave Toub has preached patience with his group getting out to a slow start, but mistakes persist in multiple areas of special teams. Remigio, whose role seems defined, isn't doing anything to justify being a long-term solution as a returner.
It's now been several years in a row of Harrison Butker not matching the leaguewide perception of him being one of the best in the business. It's this writer's take that those days are clearly over now , even if the team won't admit it, especially given another missed extra point and some waning effectiveness on long-range boots.
Butker's trump card is his ability to make pressure-packed kicks, which is one heck of a positive to bring to the table, but everything else is questionable right now. Week 6 only underscored that.
Had he not gotten ejected for throwing a punch, defensive back Chris Roland-Wallace wouldn't have even been considered for a spot here. He made multiple solid plays elsewhere, including a big tackle for loss and a tipped interception that got nullified by a penalty. At the end of the day, though, you simply can't put your team in a compromising position like that.

title: Adam Gase Lurking as Mike McDaniel's Chargers Offense Stalls
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers could eventually have a difficult decision to make on offense, and they might not have to look very far to find another option.
The Chargers did not bring Mike McDaniel in just to watch the offense struggle to find its footing. There was an expectation that his offensive background would help bring out the best in Justin Herbert and give this team another dimension. The vision looked very different than what was expected, and in a wrong way.
If the problems continue, it is fair to wonder whether a change in leadership could eventually become part of the conversation.
NFL Network analyst Steve Wyche reported that passing game coordinator Adam Gase would take the role as offensive coordinator if they part ways with McDaniel.
Gase is an interesting candidate because he has experienced both sides of the NFL coaching business. He has been part of an offense that looked nearly unstoppable, but he has also gone through some difficult stretches that left plenty of questions about his ability to lead a team.
His strongest stretch came with the Denver Broncos, where he served as offensive coordinator during the 2013 and 2014 seasons. The 2013 team was one of the most productive offenses the league has ever seen, putting up 606 points during the regular season. This included a stellar season for Peyton Manning and a Super Bowl. Of course, Gase’s career did not maintain that same trajectory. His time as head coach of the Miami Dolphins produced mixed results, and his two seasons with the New York Jets was a dumpster fire.
The Chargers also have to consider what is actually causing their offensive issues. Changing the person calling plays does not automatically fix everything. The offensive line, player execution, personnel decisions and the ability to establish consistency all play a role in how an offense performs. Any potential coaching change would need to address the problems on the field rather than simply give the team a different name to put in charge. For now, McDaniel should have the opportunity to get the offense back on track. But the NFL is a results-driven business, and patience can run out quickly when a team believes it has the talent to compete at a much higher level.
Will Adam Gase solve all the problems, probably not. However sometimes a change is needed, and we will never really know until it actually happens.

title: The One Massive Shakeup to the Chargers Starting Lineup that Signals an Actual Change
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are hoping to find some answers, retool and get some of their talent back following their bye week here in week seven. The 0-6 Chargers have been horrible on the offensive side of the ball and are ranked dead last in the NFL in EPA per play on offense and are the third-worst scoring offense in the NFL,
Injuries have ravaged Los Angeles and for the second year in a row, the football gods have punished the Chargers offensive line. The Chargers resorted to starting four rookies on their offensive line against division opponents in weeks five and six.
The Chargers were expected to have a much more efficient rushing attack with the hiring of Mike McDaniel as their new offensive coordinator. A switch to a wide zone rushing attack was expected under McDaniel but with some mixture of gap and zone rushing concepts.
The 2026 Chargers have been anything but efficient in the run game. Their current EPA per rush is -0.18, good enough for 28th in the NFL. EPA or expected points added, is an analytics metric used to measure the average expected points added on rushing attempts. Positive EPA indicates rushing the ball increases the chance of scoring points and negative decreases the chance.
Los Angeles' plans to run the ball may have been killed off when starting center Tyler Biadasz went down in training camp with a season ending knee injury. The way defenses attack wide zone rushing schemes is by wrecking the guards horizontal movement by penetrating the B-gap.
Right guard Cole Strange and rookie center Jake Slaughter are both smaller and faster NFL offensive linemen. Neither have the power to generate vertical push on their own and struggle to sustain blocks against NFL interior defensive linemen. This is why wide zone blocking and the quick passing game are the concepts best suited for their skillsets, if they were both playing guard.
Having Slaughter and Strange next to each other has created an obvious weak point on the offensive line. The data shows that when breaking down the Chargers rush EPA by gap, the A and B-gaps to the right are by far the least efficient option to run the ball.
I know it's not a shocker, but the Chargers run game by EPA by gap is by far worst in the A gap and B gap to the right side. Interesting that despite a rotation of bodies at left guard, runs to the left A and B gaps are the most successful but off the left tackle is awful. pic.twitter.com/c9S5gZQNs2
The lack of success in the run game is tied to the interior offensive line. Had Tyler Biadasz stayed healthy, Cole Strange may have generated a completely different data set at the right guard position. Jake Slaughter's weaknesses were well known entering the NFL. If the Chargers front office chose to ignore them or planned to have a similar skill set to Strange at left guard we may never know. But now, putting them next to each other has limited the chance of success for Strange and the Chargers offense.
Most of the other Shanahan offensive system disciples such as Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan have incorporated much more gap-rushing concepts into their offenses in recent years where Mike McDaniel has not. The San Francisco 49ers, through the first six weeks of the season, are running significantly more gap or inside zone rushing plays. 67 percent of San Francisco's runs have been between the tackles. The Chargers, by comparison, have run only 48 percent inside .
McDaniel has focused on speed and spreading the defense to create conflicts for defenders. Without the personnel to adequately run that style of offense, he should be considering copying more of what McVay and Shanahan have implemented. Despite the return of several starting offensive lineman to practice, a significant shift would likely require a bigger and stronger right guard.
Both Branson Taylor and Kayode Awosika are now available. If both enter the lineup, ideally with rookie Travis Burke holding down the left tackle spot, Awosika would line up between he and Slaughter to provide some experience on the left side of the line and send Taylor to right guard next to Joe Alt.
If the Chargers emerge from the bye week with a new starting right guard, it will signal that shift is coming. That is not Cole Strange's fault, but having Slaughter and Strange together has not be working in the current offense and Slaughter has to continue being the starting center.
The biggest benefit in  shift like this would be for Justin Herbert and the play action passing game. The Chargers play action game is getting Herbert pressured at a near 60 percent rate. If they can get the ball moving downhill, more traditional play action dropbacks should open up and open up the intermediate part of the middle of the field.
Mike McDaniel and the offensive staff, with whatever changes they are implementing over the bye week have to try something different without installing a new offense. The motion trickery and Allen Iverson-level of ball handling behind the line of scrimmage required of Herbert has created too many errors. Will the Chargers pivot or simply hope getting healthy bodies back will make a difference?

title: Mel Kiper, Others Rightfully ‘Mocking’ Chargers With Jeremiah Smith No. 1 Overall
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are a punching bag right now, on and off the field.
On it, they’re an 0-6 club on a bye week that looks like it could be 0-9 in just a few weeks. They’ve gone from Super Bowl potential to circling a tank-bowl against Miami in Week 16 as for the No. 1 pick in next year’s draft as the highlight of the season.
Off it, they’re getting justifiably slammed from all angles for looking like the worst team in football and burning another year of Justin Herbert’s prime. Herbert isn’t without blame , but the whole thing feels on brand for the Chargers.
With fans in mock draft mode already, seeing the Chargers pick first overall, though, comes with a heavy dose of criticism.
It’s all about Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith.
It’s also all about bashing the Chargers.
Field Yates at ESPN had the Chargers making such a pick in his latest mock draft while writing that “a pathetic season so far for the Chargers can be traced to several factors, one of which is that the team has no difference-makers among its pass catchers.”
Fair enough. The Chargers are, for some reason, still entertaining Quentin Johnston’s drop issues. They’re dealing with Ladd McConkey injury issues yet again. They’re not using first-round running back Omarion Hampton well. Supposed breakout tight end Oronde Gadsden is an afterthought. It goes on and on.
Then there’s Mel Kiper Jr. , who also has the Chargers taking Smith first overall. He’s taking aim at the Chargers for building terrible trenches.
“Justin Herbert’s getting criticized for what, having an offensive line that can’t block? And heavily penalized," Kiper said. “And not having their guys healthy. That’s enough to say the quarterback’s not going to be successful."
Kiper classified Herbert’s situation as "unreasonable" and “crazy,” too, which sort of sums up the 2026 Chargers really well.
The catch? Smith is a really great prospect who will boost the Chargers. But until the overarching issues Kiper mentions get fixed, it might not matter. That means Joe Hortiz and those in charge of building the roster, plus those guilty in the consistent, annual injury woes, need to fix their issues or get replaced.

title: What the Chargers Can Realistically Afford at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
NFL teams have a lot to think about when the November trade deadline arrives. With there being one big question organizations need to think about. Is the opportunity to improve a roster worth the resources required to make it happen?
For the Los Angeles Chargers , the answer depends on more than identifying a talented player who could fill a need.
Any potential acquisition must fit within the team’s financial limitations, available draft capital and long-term plans.
Making a splash might generate excitement, but the best deadline move is not necessarily the biggest one. It is the move that addresses a genuine weakness without creating another problem down the road.
The Bolts currently have seven picks in the NFL draft , which is an estimated number, as potential compensation picks could appear. With a single pick in each round. They could use that as potential value. The current General Manager Joe Hortiz loves his draft picks, so losing them for a highly touted player is just not how he rolls.
Draft capital is an important consideration.
Future selections give the organization opportunities to develop young players, build depth and find affordable contributors who can remain with the team for multiple seasons. Trading those selections is not automatically a mistake, particularly when a legitimate opportunity to improve the roster presents itself.
The round in which a player was originally drafted should not determine his trade value, either. What matters is his current production, remaining contract, age, injury history and projected role. A player with a modest reputation but a useful skill set and a manageable financial commitment could ultimately be a better investment than a more recognizable veteran who requires a premium return.
The ideal target would provide a noticeable improvement without demanding an excessive combination of draft picks and financial flexibility. If the asking price becomes too steep, walking away should remain a realistic option. The distinction between a need and a luxury is especially important when draft picks and salary-cap flexibility are involved. A player like AJ Brown last season for instance, might look appealing on paper.
But surrendering valuable draft capital for a short-term improvement can become difficult to justify, if the same position could be addressed through a less expensive alternative.
Financial considerations can be just as influential as draft compensation when determining what the Bolts can afford.
A trade does not simply involve agreeing on a collection of picks and players. It also requires understanding how the incoming contract affects the team’s current cap situation and future obligations.
According to Spotrac, the Chargers have a projected free cap space of $102 million, which is around the same amount they had last year. Two notable players looking for extensions are edge Tuli Tuipulotu and linebacker Daiyan Henley. Henley is playing the final year of his rookie contract and will possibly seek a bigger contract via good performances. The biggest situation though is Tuipulotu, who is also playing on his rookie contract. According to Spotrac, his extension could include 4 years with a projected $75 million.
The remaining salary for the season is only part of the equation. Guaranteed money, roster bonuses, future salary commitments and the possibility of an extension can all influence whether a particular acquisition makes sense. The Chargers must evaluate the full financial picture rather than focusing exclusively on a player’s immediate cap charge.
Contract structure can also affect the feasibility of a deal. Depending on the circumstances, the acquiring team may assume some or all of a player’s remaining obligations, while the trading team could retain certain financial responsibilities. The specific arrangement matters because two players with similar on-field value can carry very different costs. That does not mean the Chargers should avoid spending resources altogether. If a player addresses a significant weakness and the financial commitment is manageable, the potential benefits could outweigh the cost. The challenge is determining whether the expected improvement justifies the resources surrendered.
The Chargers do not need to win the trade deadline to improve their postseason outlook. They need to make decisions that strengthen the roster while preserving the ability to compete beyond the current season.
If an affordable upgrade becomes available, pursuing it could make sense. If the price threatens the team’s longer-term plans, patience may be the better investment.

title: One Chargers Player Who Could Surprisingly Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers are on their bye week and they are trying to find answers for their offense and get healthy after injuries have ravaged their roster. Trade rumors are a hot topic for the Chargers given their record and current roster and there are a few players more likely than others to be moved before the deadline.
The Chargers have not historically been active during the season with trades. 2025's midseason trade for Odafe Oweh was new for the franchise and also signaled a change under the direction of general manager Joe Hortiz.
The reality is, the Chargers have not been is this particular position before. Los Angeles entered the season with high expectations to be a playoff team and potential championship contenders, their roster was built and assembled with that expectation.
Since the expansion of the playoff format and the expansion to a 17-game season, trades have become more frequent than in years past but are still relatively rare. The most common positions to be moved are wide receivers and defensive linemen or edge rushers. One of the position groups in the next level of frequency is defensive backs.
The Chargers are relatively thin at cornerback but cornerbacks are always in demand. The Chargers have a decision to make next year as well with cornerbacks Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart both entering the final year of their rookie contracts. Could one of them be moved at the trade deadline for the right price?
Cam Hart and Tarheeb Still are the Chargers' two third-year cornerbacks who have been playing significant snaps, if not starting, from early on their rookie season despite both being fifth-round draft picks. Hart is more of the prototypical bigger outside boundary cornerback and Still is more versatile in alignments.
Hart has been banged up throughout his first few NFL seasons but has been a mainstay in the starting lineup in 2026. Hart has two interceptions on the year including an amazing catch in the endzone off of Patrick Mahomes in week six.
Hart could be a surprise trade target around the NFL for the specific reason. According to PFF, when the data is filtered to a minimum of 50 percent of the the defensive snaps, indicating a consistent starter, Hart is ranked ninth in the NFL in man coverage by grade.
If the Chargers get a solid offer for Hart, a former fifth-round pick with only one year left on his deal, it could be a shocking move that a contender in need of a capable man corner down the stretch of the season might make. Having two cornerbacks, whose contracts are jumping in average annual value, up for extensions next season may give the Chargers front office an added reason to at least pick up the phone when teams call about a potential trade for Hart.
Moving Hart would likely thrust Kaiir Elam onto the 53-man roster from the practice squad if the defensive coaching staff believes he is ready. It would not be easy to replace a player like Hart in the defense, but at 0-6, these are uncharted waters for the franchise.

title: One Trade Deadline Move the Chargers Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers find themselves deep in a hole that has never been overcome in the history of the NFL. With the merger starting in 1965, no team has ever gone 0-6 and made the playoffs. It is quite safe to say that, at this point, the Chargers will not be the first to do so.
With this understanding, it is important for the Bolts to look at their roster and begin rebuilding as soon as possible. The team needs to be realistic with themselves and begin to give fans some level of excitement; otherwise, the ticket sales and support for the team will continue to dwindle.
At the age of 35, Khalil Mack has earned his status as an NFL legend who deserves postseason success now that he is in the twilight of his NFL career. Mack has never won a playoff game in his career, and if he were to continue with the Chargers this season, he may never win one.
The Bolts obviously need as much ammunition as they can get to arm themselves for a successful rebuild heading into the 2027 season. Trading the veteran allows the team to get another draft pick and allows the team to respect Mack and his career, giving him an opportunity to have postseason success.
Before the team's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, Mack in regard to trade rumors: “I just got total faith in this team and this organization.… I have breath in my lungs,” According to Joaquin Ruiz , he said the latter half with a smile.
Things can change quickly, but Mack seems to be OK with another losing season. But the question is the 0-6 Chargers' OK with allowing this to happen? Are they OK with the possible loss of a draft asset because they preferred to keep a veteran with no future with the team?
If the team decides that trading Mack is the correct move, expect them to look at his current contract and look for a partnering team like the Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers and the Los Angeles Rams to all give him a call.

Estimated Trade Value: 2027 Third Round Selection + 2028 Sixth Round Selection

title: Chargers' Justin Herbert Getting Some Tua Tagovailoa-Level Heat for Struggles
full_text:
There’s plenty of blame to go around for the Los Angeles Chargers .
Joe Hortiz deserves most of it for a bad streak of roster-building that has left coaches and coordinators with a lacking roster.
That won’t stop calls for Jim Harbaugh’s job , though, nor will it take the pressure off offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel for authoring perhaps the worst stretch of Justin Herbert’s career.
But make no mistake, Herbert himself is under the microscope, too. At some point, the blame has to go his way, whether onlookers like it or not.
What some won’t like hearing, though, is NFL coaches and others making odd-seeming Brock Purdy comparisons for Herbert in the wake of his recent struggles.
Anyone with a passing familiarity of the Chargers knows how much the organization has failed him over the years.
The Chargers constantly throwing new coordinators at him, not giving him quality non-Keenan Allen weapons and the refusal to admit that interior offensive line is important and worth a premium are just some of the factors at work here.
But Herbert’s been so poor, even compared to last year, that some are questioning whether he can even run McDaniel’s scheme.
Some NFL coaches told The Athletic’s Mike Sando that McDaniel’s scheme is overly complex and it just might not be a fit.
"There are a lot of formations and motions that he's gonna present to you," one NFL coach told Sando. "I don't know if that's easy to operate for those guys or not.”
Now, things are looping back to Tua Tagovailoa comparisons and even bringing up a name like Brock Purdy.
"In Miami, when they were rolling, it was because of the explosive skill they had, and a phenomenal system," another coach told Sando. "San Francisco rolls because of Brock Purdy. I just don't know if Herbert can handle that system. That is my take, and then couple that with their line being the worst we've seen."
It’s easy to scoff at these things. But one doesn't have to look far to find chatter around the Chargers about "simplifying" things over the bye. And it was at least worth a raise of the eyebrow over the summer when McDaniel started tweaking Herbert’s footwork and stuff.
The fact the Chargers aren’t firing McDaniel or announcing any changes at all during the bye hints that they believe this is a long-term fix that will be worth it.
We’ll see if that’s true, but the last thing anyone expected was Herbert getting thrown back into Tagovailoa comparisons.

title: Chargers Scouts Get Eyes on Top Prospects at Key College Matchups
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers college scouting department has been active so far this year. The current state of the Chargers roster displays several holes some of which were predictable, others brought upon by units being decimated by injuries.
The Chargers scouts are active on the scouting trail across the country. Part of a scouts role is to build as deep of a profile and understanding of college prospects from as early on as possible. We may have limited access to games they have attended but during the week scouts are stopping at campuses to catch practice and to talk to coaches.
The process never stops and extends throughout the offseason training programs and spring practices as well. By the time a prospect declares for the draft, unless they are extremely under the radar or late bloomers, most have years of information gathered on them.
Games  and game performances are a piece of the puzzle. Scouts getting an up close look at prospects in high profile moments and getting an in-person feel for the competitive environment gives scouts invaluable context to how players rise or crumble in key moments.
Los Angeles' scouts were publicly noted at three games this past weekend, two of which were massive games for standing or rivalries. Let's dive into the three and some key prospects that the Chargers likely have their eyes on.
The biggest match of the week pitted the second ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish against the eighth ranked BYU Cougars. BYU took the victory but not without controversy on the final play in the endzone.
The Irish are stacked with NFL talent and the majority of their defense in on the NFL's radar. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is performing well this season and has climbed his was into first round consideration as he continues to play well.
Cornerback Leonard Moore is the highest-ranked player on their team and very well could be the first defender off of the board on draft night. To go along with Moore, other top prospects include linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, guard Anthonie Knapp, edge rusher Boubacar Traore are just the beginning of the long list of prospects playing for Notre Dame.
BYU has several prospects but their top prospect, running back LJ Martin, missed the game due to injury. One of BYU's other top prospects, linebacker Cade Uluave, is in his first year with the Cougars and he has been on my radar since his freshman season at Cal.
Uluave is a rangy, tough linebacker who popped on film next to current Ravens linebacker Teddye Buchanan. The Chargers were frequently in attendance at Cal's games over the past few seasons and undoubtedly have been keeping close tabs on Uluave.
The game between Florida State and Miami was a good old fashioned double overtime rivalry slugfest. The Chargers have recent history with Miami after taking edge rusher Akheem Mesidor in the first round in the most recent draft.
The Hurricanes are well stocked with NFL draft prospects including quarterback Darian Mensah, defensive tackles Ahmad Moten Sr. and Justin Scott, running back Mark Fletcher, offensive lineman Samsun Okunlola, linebacker Damon Wilson II and cornerback OJ Federique are just the start of their talented roster.
Florida State is much thinner in terms of prospects this season but 6'6 wide receiver Duce Robinson is undoubtedly on the Chargers' radar. Robinson is a enormous outside downfield threat and playmaker. He had two touchdowns and 113 yards in this game against Miami.
DUCE ROBINSON AGAIN FLORIDA STATE OMG pic.twitter.com/6J7OssUTYZ
This matchup has a handful of potential draft propects but neither team has prospect near the top of the class. The marquee player in this matchup is true freshman wide receiver Jesse Legree.
Legree will not be draft eligible until 2029 but he is firmly in the heisman running at this point as he takes the country by storm. He is currently leading the nation in both receiving yards and touchdowns through seven weeks. Going back to the conversation of how long scouts have their eyes on players, in two years, notes taken now will be compared to how Legree looks and performs as he gears up for his presumed final season of college football.

title: Which Teams Would Give Up Most Capital in a Justin Herbert Trade?
full_text:
Trading Justin Herbert is not something most Chargers fans want to think about. To be fair, this idea probably will never happen. Quarterbacks with his combination of arm strength, athletic ability and experience are difficult to find, and replacing one would be an enormous challenge.
A quarterback of his caliber would not simply attract a few phone calls, it would be much more.  However the most important part is what they would be willing to give up in return.
CBS Sports highlighted players they would like to see with a different scenery, and Herbert was one of thier picks.
Three teams stand out as the best potential buyers in that unlikely scenario, and I believe they would throw tons of capital the Chargers' way for a quarterback like Herbert.
Indianapolis might have the most interesting connection to Herbert, thanks to head coach Shane Steichen. Before becoming the Colts head coach, Steichen worked with Herbert in Los Angeles serving as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator in 2020.
That history is important. Steichen has already seen Herbert operate at the NFL level and understands what makes him such a difficult quarterback to defend. Rather than spending months evaluating whether Herbert fits his system, the Colts’ head coach would have firsthand experience to draw from.
Also their need for a quarterback in the last few weeks has been a topic of concern.
Any serious pursuit would likely require several premium draft assets, potentially including multiple first-round picks. The Colts would also need to account for Herbert’s contract while continuing to surround him with enough talent to compete.
Still, if Steichen believed Herbert could take the offense to another level, Indianapolis would have a compelling reason to explore the opportunity. The existing relationship makes this more interesting than a typical quarterback trade rumor.
Minnesota would be another team worth watching if a quarterback of Herbert’s ability suddenly entered the trade market. The Vikings have reason to think about their long-term future at the position, and landing an established quarterback could eliminate a major question for the organization.
They have a killer defense, which might be the best in the NFL. Also having elite receiver Justin Jefferson, and adding Herbert would mean championship hopes suddenly appear. Their problem is clearly finding a reliable guy under center.
If the Vikings believed their roster was ready to make a serious championship push, pursuing Herbert could become a conversation worth having. Finding a quarterback who can anchor a team for years is difficult, and opportunities like this rarely come along.
Miami could become one of the more intriguing teams in the conversation if Herbert ever became available. If the organization decided it needed a different direction at quarterback, pursuing an established talent would be an entirely different approach than starting over through the draft. A type of trade for this highly touted player would change their team around immediately.
Herbert would give the team a quarterback with the arm strength to attack every part of the field. He has shown he can make difficult throws and produce without everything around him being perfect, which would be especially valuable for a team trying to turn its offensive potential into consistent results.
There is no guarantee they would be willing or financially positioned to make that kind of move. But if Herbert unexpectedly entered the trade market, the Dolphins would have a reason to at least explore the possibility.
Brennan is sports writer focused on delivering sharp analysis, real-time reactions, and engaging storytelling focused on NFL analysis.  He is passionate about football and breaking down what matters to bring fans closer to the action.  Brennan comes from a family of Chargers fans.

title: Chargers All-Star Offensive Lineman Returns to Practice, Quieting Season-Ending Rumors
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have started the 2026 NFL season at 0-6, marking them as officially the worst team in the NFL. They have dealt with injuries, poor play from multiple units and extremely poor coaching from coaches who seemingly have never had a track record of being bad.
While it has been an odd season filled with surprises, one thing has been unsurprising: injuries piling up for players in the Powder Blue uniform. Injuries always seem to happen for the Chargers, an unfortunate certainty fans can count on year in and year out.
One of the biggest injuries suffered thus far in the 2026 NFL season has been Pro Bowl offensive tackle, former Top 5 selection, Joe Alt. Alt suffered a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 4 due to a freak helicopter-esque kick from Seahawks defender Nick Emmanwori.
The play where Joe Alt is injured by Seahawks DB Nick Emmanwori pic.twitter.com/2P0KMGTzAl
Cannot exactly say I have seen anything like that happen in an NFL game, but also I cannot say I thought the Chargers were going to be 0-6 to start this NFL season either.
Moving on, Alt has missed two games: the Chargers' losses to the Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs. Anytime you are dealing with a neck injury, it is important to prioritize safety over rushing back, allowing Alt to spend time with a specialist and get clearance to begin practicing on Oct. 18.
Alt has officially returned to practice today, Oct. 21, the Chargers' first practice since losing to the Chiefs. Along with his return, the Chargers' starting left guard, Kayode Awosika , has also returned to practice after missing time with his fibula injury. He missed a total of four games.
RT Joe Alt (neck) and LG Kayode Awosika (fibula) were participating during the portion of today’s Chargers practice open to the media.
Now that the Chargers are back with two more of their offensive linemen, the offensive line will once again be shuffled to ensure the "best 5" are out in front of Justin Herbert. With rookies Travis Burke, Logan Taylor and Alex Harkey all being starters over the last two weeks, who will be the rookies to be replaced first?
LT: Travis Burke LG: Kayode Awosika C: Jake Slaughter RG: Cole Strange RT: Joe Alt
This lineup sees Harkey and Taylor being replaced by Alt and Awosika, returning from their respective injuries. Burke continues in his role as the third tackle, continuing what has been a pretty impressive season for the fourth-round rookie.
The only step left for the Bolts is to see Rashawn Slater return from injured reserve and get this offensive line back to health. Who knows if that will be enough to turn the team around, but seeing Herbert have healthy linemen in front of him will hopefully bring more morale.

title: Rams Practice Squad Breakdown: Injuries Could Force Unexpected Players Into Action
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7, they have been hit hard by the injury bug. Wide receiver Davante Adams, along with defensive linemen Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, was placed on injured reserve this week. Additionally, wide receiver Puka Nacua’s status is uncertain as he manages a calf injury suffered in practice.
It seems as if wherever the Rams turn, another injury pops up. Every day brings another player dealing with some sort of injury. If the Rams are without Nacua and Adams on Sunday, it could force them to go to the practice squad.With injuries forcing the Rams to rely more on their depth, it seemed like a good time to take an updated look at the practice squad. As a reminder, teams are allowed to elevate a player off the practice squad three times during the regular season.
Andersen had some strong moments in the preseason , but it would be surprising to see him on the active roster unless injuries dictate it. That’s especially the case as the Rams re-signed Tanner Ingle to the practice squad after cutting him. With that said, given some of the issues on special teams, Andersen’s tackling ability could be beneficial there at some point. Andersen was one of the better special teams players for the Rams in the preseason.
Nick Andersen picks it up! 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/6UOfb3QkEU
While Austin Blaske showed some promise in the preseason, the practice squad is the best spot for him right now. The Rams will continue developing him throughout the season. At some point, he could take Justin Dedich’s role as a reliable depth player on the interior.
Given some of the inconsistencies on special teams, Jack Bouwmeester could absolutely find his way on the active roster at some point. The Rams and special teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone don’t seem sold on Evans, who might be on the hot seat. Bouwmeester is part of the International Player Pathway Program.
The Rams may like what they saw from Fourqurean during the preseason, but he’s behind Cam Lampkin on the practice squad depth chart. When the Rams needed cornerback depth last week against the Cardinals, they went to Lampkin. Still, Fourqurean is a player they’ll continue developing.
Hance is a veteran player who gives the Rams some depth at offensive tackle. The Rams like Bill Murray more, but if they got into an injury pinch, Hance would likely be one of the first players they call up.
Following the Rams placing Poona Ford on injured reserve, they signed Jalen Hunt. Hunt was an undrafted free agent originally signed by the Jacksonville Jaguars after spending seven years in college. He fits the Rams’ profile on the defensive line and will provide depth at that spot with Ford out for the season. Hunt may not see the active roster this season, but the Rams have done well developing players on the defensive line.
JALEN HUNT ALL UP IN THE BACKFIELD 💪 pic.twitter.com/9kV6j1ot6c
The Rams cut Ingle after the game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4 given some of the issues on special teams. However, they brought him back to the practice squad . Ingle hasn’t seen the active roster since, but he’s clearly someone the Rams like as they keep bringing him back. Practice Squad Elevations: 1
Heading into Week 7, Nate Landman will be out with a concussion. Kendricks is expected to get called up to the active roster for the game against the Raiders. The Rams signed Kendricks two weeks ago to provide experienced linebacker depth and another player who could contribute on special teams if needed. Kendricks will make his Rams debut on Sunday.
ERIC KENDRICKS KNOCKS IT AWAY 49ERS BALL 😳 SFvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YS7jtonSGC
Lampkin has spent the last few years developing in the Rams’ system. An argument can be made that he should’ve made the final 53-man roster at the beginning of the season, but the Rams were able to keep him on the practice squad. Lampkin was called up last week with Trent McDuffie injured. He’ll be someone the Rams keep readily available if they need help at cornerback. Practice Squad Elevations: 2
During the first few weeks of the season, the Rams elevated Elias Neal from the practice squad to contribute on special teams. Given that teams are only allowed to elevate players off of the practice squad three times, Neal hasn’t been elevated in a few weeks. It’s potentially why the Rams also signed Kendricks. Neal is someone the Rams will continue developing. Practice Squad Elevations: 2
Nelson was an in-season addition by the Rams as they signed him before last week’s game against the Cardinals. Nelson gives the Rams some depth on the edge with Myles Garrett injured. Josaiah Stewart was also managing an injury at the time. Nelson spent time with the Saints this offseason before getting cut. He has never played in a regular-season game, and that likely won’t change with the Rams.
The Rams have been developing Bill Norton over the last few seasons on the defensive line. He struggled in the preseason, but Norton is a player the Rams have kept around. However, it says a lot that they added Hunt in the wake of Ford going on injured reserve. Norton is still a developmental player at the position.
Over the past two seasons, Brennan Presley has been a standout in the preseason. However, he hasn’t made an appearance on the active roster. If the Rams are without Nacua on Sunday, Presley may get the call. The Rams may still rely on some of their more experienced players, but Presley has shown that he can make plays when he’s gotten a chance.
Ty Simpson delivers a TD strike to Brennan Presley 🔥 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/5Dc65aRqbk
It was surprising back in Week 4 when the Rams didn’t bring Dan Villari up from the practice squad. The Rams were thin at tight end with Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson out. It’s possible the Rams simply see Villari as a developmental tight end this season.
After the Rams placed Ronnie Rivers on injured reserve, there was some consideration given to bringing up Jordan Waters.. However, the Rams opted for Dean Connors instead. Waters remains a player the Rams like and will continue to develop.
Williams gives the Rams some experienced cornerback depth on the practice squad and was signed last week. Given that the Rams have used up two of Lampkin’s practice squad elevations, Williams could see the active roster at some point. He was a fourth-round pick in 2022 and spent time with the Seahawks in 2024.

title: Forget the NFC West, Can the Rams Even Make the Playoffs?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are 2-4 entering Week 7 and it can be argued that Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders is a must-win situation. A win against the Arizona Cardinals last week would have put the Rams in second place in the NFC West, right behind the San Francisco 49ers. Losing that game put them at 0-2 in the NFC West and in last place. At this point, it’s highly unlikely the Rams win the division, especially with the 49ers at 6-0.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have a four percent chance to win the NFC West. However, the playoffs are still within reach. Cue Jim Mora’s “Playoffs?! Playoffs?! You want to talk about playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game!” rant from November of 2000.
Happy 19th anniversary to the Jim Mora 'Playoffs' rant.  You shall be in our lives forever🙏 pic.twitter.com/iKk41mlvog
That’s where the Rams are at right now. It seems ridiculous to talk about the playoffs because they really need to just focus on winning a game. After losing 18-16 to the Cardinals and suffering the amount of injuries they have, the Rams simply need to focus on taking things one week at a time.
Still, that doesn’t mean that we can’t look ahead a little bit. Back in 2023, the Rams came back from a 3-6 start to make the playoffs. In 2024, they came back from a 1-4 start to make the postseason. Making the playoffs isn't completely out of the realm of possibility. The Rams just need to start stringing some wins together.
As it stands, the Rams have a 39 percent chance to make the playoffs via The Athletic . ESPN’s model has them slightly lower at 33 percent. While the Rams are playing an AFC opponent on Sunday, a win is critical to their playoff chances simply because they can’t afford many more losses.
A loss to the Raiders would put the Rams at a 27 percent chance to make the playoffs. Winning on Sunday makes it a near coin-flip at 45 percent. It’s very possible that we are looking at this game as the one that saved or ruined the Rams’ season.
To make the postseason, the Rams may need to finish 11-6 or 10-7. That means they can afford just two or three more losses over their final 11 games. They still have to play the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks twice, the San Francisco 49ers, and the Green Bay Packers. It’s likely the Rams will lose two of those games at minimum.
Looking at ESPN’s model , the biggest threats to the Rams’ playoff chances right now are the second- through fourth-place teams in the NFC North and the Seattle Seahawks. The good news is that the Rams will play the Packers after the bye week and then play the Seahawks twice in the final three weeks of the season.
Unfortunately, the timing may not work in the Rams’ favor, as the Packers have bounced back from their early-season struggles. While the Seahawks are in a rut, they may snap out of it by Week 16.
The Packers, Bears, Lions, Vikings, and Seahawks will all be teams that the Rams will be watching closely. There will likely only be one team to come out of the NFC South and NFC East divisions. However, the NFC North and NFC West could provide multiple playoff teams.
As it stands, the Rams’ most likely record is between 8-9 and 10-7. Since the NFL expanded to a 17-game format in 2021, only the Seattle Seahawks in 2024 missed the playoffs at 10-7. That’s what the Rams are looking at right now with the overall strength of the NFC. An 8-9 team has never made the playoffs as a wild card, and if the Rams were to go 9-8, they would certainly need help. They may need help at 10-7.
Realistically, the Rams are hoping they can finish ahead of the Seahawks in the NFC West and that either the Vikings collapse after starting 5-0 or the Packers lose their form again. There’s very little confidence right now that the Rams can string wins together, but the schedule has set up for it. If the Rams can win each of their next five games, that alone would increase their playoff chances to 77 percent. That would allow the Rams to lose to the Chiefs, the 49ers, and the Seahawks once and still finish 10-7. If that’s the way things play out, the Rams would have an 89 percent chance at the postseason.
They would obviously need certain things to go their way as well. Given the Rams’ poor record in the division, they would not be able to tie with the Seahawks. They would need the Seahawks to finish worse than 10-7 or take the season series and win both games in Week 16 and 18.
It seems likely with their schedules that the Bears and Lions finish with 11 wins. That leaves the Vikings and Packers as teams to monitor.
With the Vikings, they could lose four of their next five games. They play the Lions, Packers, and 49ers on the road and then also play the Bills. The Patriots on the road will be tough and the Panthers have looked good as well. It’s possible the Rams could use some help in later weeks. However, if the Vikings finish 10-7, the Rams would be seeded ahead of them.
Finally, the Rams’ game against the Packers after the bye is a must-win. If the Rams lose that game, it would be very difficult to come back from that. Assuming they win that game, it's possible the Packers could finish 10-7 and behind the Rams in the standings.
When all is said and done, we could be looking at: 1. 49ers 2. Bears 3. Panthers 4. NFC East Winner 5. Lions 6. Rams 7. Packers/Vikings
That would put the Rams in the playoffs and a trip to Carolina in the Wild Card round for a second consecutive season. Given the Rams’ current situation, they would very likely need to win three road playoff games to make the Super Bowl, but if they get healthy and find their stride, they would be a rare team with a good chance of doing that.
The Rams have come back from early-season deficits in the past. That’s certainly not the path they wanted to take this year, but it’s where they find themselves. Still, they need to show they can consistently win games. The Rams may be better than their record says they are, but they are 2-4.
🚨 NFL FRAUD METER - Week 6 🏈 The 6-0 49ers aren't frauds The 5-0 Vikings are... pic.twitter.com/f2gjARxzCJ
In 2024, it was a win against the Raiders in Week 7 that sparked a 9-3 finish. The Rams will hope a win against the Raiders in Week 7 this year does the same. The year before, the Rams lost three straight before a win against the Seahawks sparked them to a 7-1 finish.
However, the difference in both cases was that the Rams were getting healthy and coming off their bye week. At this point in the season, the Rams couldn’t be more hurt at key positions, and they don’t have their bye until Week 11.
Still, Sunday’s game against the Raiders is important. If the Rams are going to turn it around, it starts on Sunday. We can talk about playoff scenarios all we want, but none of it matters if the Rams can’t start winning games. The margins are already small and they get narrower with every loss. If they can get to the bye week with some momentum, the season could look very different. At 2-4, however, they can no longer afford to keep waiting for things to turn around.

title: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams could be without wide receiver Puka Nacua on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. Nacua was officially listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report after injuring his calf on Thursday . Also listed as questionable was cornerback Trent McDuffie, who did not practice on Friday. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has officially been ruled out.
Nacua was a surprise addition to the injury report on Thursday after he left practice with an apparent calf injury. He did not practice on Friday and will be a game-time decision. According to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport , Nacua’s calf injury is only minor, but his status is up in the air for Sunday’s game. Rams head coach Sean McVay talked about Nacua’s injury in more detail in his media availability.
“I don't think he knows exactly when it occurred,” said McVay. “You look at it and there's a little minor thing in there. Felt it where he wasn't able to have some of the power and full explosion. Just noticed it, but I don't think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.”
If the Rams are without Nacua, they will rely on depth players such as Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington. The Rams would also likely lean heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Earlier this season without Nacua, Williams had six receptions against the Denver Broncos and became a big part of the passing game.
Landman being ruled out would imply that he didn’t pass through the concussion protocol this week. With Landman unable to go, McVay noted on Friday that the team would bring up linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad, who they signed two weeks ago.
“He's got a veteran presence, real good concept understanding, can play a variety of schemes,” McVay said. “Has had success in a variety of schemes, understands football from a big-picture perspective, has a good vibe about himself.”
McDuffie missing his fourth consecutive practice with a groin injury certainly isn’t a good sign. McVay didn’t provide much of an update on McDuffie, only that he was questionable. McDuffie did work off to the side to an extent during the media portion of practice.
Rams CB Trent McDuffie working with training staff. He is questionable for game against Raiders. pic.twitter.com/993xUzHHPT
The Raiders will be relatively healthy heading into Sunday’s game against the Rams. After being limited on Wednesday with hamstring and calf injuries, tight end Brock Bowers was a full participant on Thursday and Friday and was not given an injury designation. Tonka Hemingway was also cleared.
With that said, the Raiders will be without wide receiver Dont’e Thornton and tight end Carter Runyon. Running back Mike Washington’s status is also up in the air for Sunday. Washington has been used alongside Ashton Jeanty this season and has averaged 4.9 yards per carry. He did not participate in practice the last two days and is listed as questionable.
The Rams were already going to be shorthanded heading into Week 7, but the uncertainty surrounding Nacua and McDuffie only adds to their challenges. With several starters already sidelined, the Rams will need their depth to step up in a significant way if they're going to get back in the win column.

title: Rams vs. Raiders Prediction: Week 7 Preview, Key Matchups, and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 desperately needing a win. After losing to the Arizona Cardinals last week, the Rams are at risk of dropping to 2-5 and are set to take on a Las Vegas Raiders team that is much better than in past years.
It’s fair to call Sunday a must-win game for the Rams. A loss to the Raiders would drop their already slim playoff chances even lower. Given where the Rams are, they can’t afford many more losses. At some point, they need to find some consistency and string together some wins, which won’t be easy with all of their injuries.
The Raiders are 3-3 and have lost three games in a row. With that said, two of their three losses are by three points, including last week’s 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Much like the Cardinals, the Raiders have been feisty this season and quarterback Kirk Cousins has played well. This isn’t a Raiders team that the Rams can afford to overlook.
Through six weeks, the Raiders’ defense ranks 26th in defensive EPA per play, success rate, and points per game allowed. Despite the injury to Davante Adams , the Rams should be able to move the ball. However, the same could’ve been said last week against the Cardinals, and the Rams managed just 16 points. The Raiders are better defending the run than the pass. This season, they are allowing the second-highest average depth of target and 13 passing touchdowns. Matthew Stafford should be able to find success.
With Puka Nacua as the Rams’ only legitimate threat at wide receiver, how the Raiders cover him will be something to watch. That becomes even more important if Nacua is unable to play and the Rams have to rely on Konata Mumpfield.
However, the Rams need to protect Matthew Stafford and keep him clean in the pocket. While McClendon has allowed a 6.8 percent pressure rate this season, Crosby has generated 25 pressures when facing right tackles, the second-most in the NFL. The Raiders also like to drop Crosby into coverage from that spot, which will also be something for the Rams to look out for.
The Raiders and head coach Klint Kubiak will be plenty familiar with Chris Shula and the Rams’ defense. Kubiak comes over from the Seattle Seahawks and was previously with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023. The Raiders have generated the 14th-most yards after the catch, while the Rams have allowed the most. Kubiak is going to dare the Rams’ defensive backs and linebackers to come up and tackle.
The Rams have done well covering tight ends this season. Last week, they held Trey McBride to seven receptions for only 53 yards. It wasn’t his lowest output of the season, but the Rams still managed to keep him in check. Brock Bowers will be another challenge. Bowers adds an explosive element to the Raiders’ offense. If Lake and the Rams can keep Bowers in check, they’ll force the Raiders to win with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor at wide receiver.
Despite the Rams losing to the Cardinals in Week 6, playing on the road, and sitting at 2-4, they are favored to beat the Raiders. Still, it’s hard to have any confidence in that happening on Sunday. Even without Adams, the Rams should be able to move the ball on offense, but they have to be able to finish drives. Given the injuries on defense, the Rams may need to score 30 points to win. This is a winnable game despite the injuries, but the Rams haven’t shown enough consistency. Prediction: Raiders 27, Rams 21
