title: Rams Get Encouraging Puka Nacua Injury Update, But Week 7 Status Remains Uncertain
full_text:
The injuries just continue to pile up for the Los Angeles Rams. During Thursday’s practice, wide receiver Puka Nacua left early and was listed as limited with a calf injury . While details weren’t immediately available, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported on Friday morning that the injury is believed to be minor.
“My understanding is, after tests, it was more minor than anything else. I wouldn’t say precautionary, because it’s not nothing, but at least not a significant injury,” said Rapoport. What that doesn’t tell us is whether or not Puka Nacua would be able to play.”
From @GMFB : #Rams WR Puka Nacua suffered what is believed to be a minor calf injury, while the #Colts will have a decision to make on RB Jonathan Taylor. pic.twitter.com/lF6yuIEo9I
Rapoport mentioned that it’s safe to say that Nacua’s status is up in the air for Sunday. After placing a handful of players such as wide receiver Davante Adams and defensive lineman Kobie Turner on injured reserve this week , the Rams were hoping to go into Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders as healthy as possible.
The Rams took significant hits on defense this week as Turner was placed on injured reserve along with Poona Ford. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie has not practiced at all this week after injuring his groin last Thursday.
Remaining as healthy as they can on the offensive side of the ball as Adams and Terrance Ferguson recover from injuries will be essential to keeping the offense competitive over the next several weeks.
Nacua has already missed two games this season with a groin/hip injury. When Nacua was out, it was Adams who stepped up in his place. With Adams set to miss the next six weeks, the Rams will be relying heavily on Nacua.
If Nacua were to miss Sunday’s game, it would put the Rams’ offense in a very difficult spot. The offense would likely rely on Tutu Atwell, who previously stepped up in place of Nacua in 2024. Players like Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington would be asked to step up as well, and the Rams could look at rookie CJ Daniels. Even with Nacua out, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams bring up Brennan Presley from the practice squad.
The Rams will get information on Nacua later on Friday when the team reports to practice. Nacua will unlikely be a full participant, but head coach Sean McVay should at least be able to provide some more details.
Given the Rams' injury luck over the last few weeks, they can certainly be relieved that Nacua’s calf injury doesn't appear to be serious. However, while the news surrounding Nacua is encouraging, his availability for Sunday remains uncertain. Given the inconsistencies on offense and Adams' absence, the Rams need Nacua available as they look to avoid dropping to 2-5.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Sean McVay Faces His Toughest Test, Myles Garrett Uncertainty, Wide Receiver Trade Targets
full_text:
Throughout the Sean McVay era, there have been some difficult seasons and slow starts for the Los Angeles Rams. Despite all of the adversity in past seasons, what the Rams are going through now may be his toughest challenge yet.
In 2020, the Rams started 4-1 and had the No. 1 defense in the NFL. However, the relationship between McVay and quarterback Jared Goff hit a breaking point. After McVay broke out in a “run it back” chant at the Super Bowl parade, the Rams went 5-12 and the head coach almost walked away. The Rams started 3-6 in a “re-tool” year, and McVay clawed that team back to make the playoffs. When the Rams started 1-4 in 2024, McVay got that team out of its funk and won the NFC West.
There have been a lot of trials, tribulations, and moments of adversity for McVay. However, what the Rams have gone through in 2026 through six weeks has been mentally exhausting. This is a team that entered the season as Super Bowl favorites. They traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie to help get them over the top.
However, with each passing week, the Rams seem to hit a new low. The issues that have plagued this roster over the last two years continue to haunt them. Against the Buffalo Bills, they were a blocked field goal away from their most impressive win of the season. This is a roster that should be 4-2 instead of 2-4. But that’s not where this team is.
Over the last two years, this is a team that continues to find new ways to lose. The heartbreaking losses continued to mount following Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals. After the game, running back Kyren Williams seemed to throw shade at his role when asked why the offense lacked energy, saying, “I can't tell you, bro. Probably because I'm not out there.”
This isn’t to say that McVay is on the verge of losing the locker room or anything to that extreme. With that said, he needs to find a way to bring this locker room together. Williams’ comments, for as much as the Rams may want to brush them aside, are a sign of the team imploding from within. How the Rams have lost in combination with the pressure they faced coming into the season would be mentally draining on any team.
Entering Week 7, the Rams have hit the injury bug hard. They lost wide receiver Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks and defensive lineman Kobie Turner also ended up on injured reserve . Puka Nacua hurt his calf and was limited in Thursday’s practice.
Whatever timeline the Rams entered in which it’s as if they walked under a ladder once a day for an entire year, it’s with certainty that they want out. McVay has proven throughout the last decade that he’s one of the best leaders in the NFL. His leadership will be put to the test if he’s going to reel this team back in for another comeback.
Following the game against the Denver Broncos, the Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. The next week on the Coach McVay show, McVay told J.B. Long that Ferguson would be ready to go after the four weeks. “Bummer for Ferg, man. But he’ll be back, he’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” said McVay at the time.
That four-week period would have placed Ferguson’s return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers. While McVay didn’t specify an exact timeline, It didn’t sound as if Ferguson would be out past the four-week injured reserve period.
For an offense that has lacked speed and explosiveness out of 13 personnel, Ferguson’s return would certainly be welcomed. McVay answered questions on Ferguson on Monday.
“No updates on Terrance, he's just continuing to rehab,” McVay said. “I don't have any sort of imminent return for him quite yet.”
On Tuesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter noted that Ferguson is not expected to be ready next week. According to Schefter, Ferguson’s recovery will take time. That doesn’t sound as if Ferguson's return is imminent. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams’ tight end was out until the bye week in Week 11.
The Myles Garrett injury saga continues to linger . After Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery, he was given a six-week timeline. However, at the time, it was said that Garrett was determined to beat that. Later, it was reported that the Rams were hopeful that Garrett could return last week against the Cardinals, but a return in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders was more realistic. The six-week timeline was a worst-case scenario.
Earlier this week, ESPN’s Dan Graziano slipped in a nugget on Garrett’s potential return in his weekly notebook. While reporting that the Rams would explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver, Graziano also noted that Garrett could likely be out for “another two or three weeks at least.”
If Garrett is out another two or three weeks, that would make the six week timeline a seven or eight week timeline. Much like Ferguson, it would not be surprising if Garrett remained sidelined until after the bye week.
On the final drive against the Cardinals in Week 6, Davante Adams pulled up with a hamstring injury. After the game, it was revealed that Adams had ruptured his hamstring and would be out 6-10 weeks.
According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Adams is set to undergo a procedure to repair his hamstring by Neal ElAttrache in Los Angeles. Fowler reported that the hope is for Adams to return on the front-end of that 6-10 week timeframe and as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible.
Rams WR Davante Adams will undergo a procedure to repair his ruptured hamstring via renowned Dr Neal ElAttrache, per source. Adams hopes to return on the front end of the 6-10 week timeframe, as close to the post-Week-11 bye as possible, the source said. pic.twitter.com/6V6v0xglhS
McVay said on Wednesday that Adams hadn’t had surgery yet and they were still figuring out details.
“I think they’re going to give it a couple of days and figure out exactly when is the best time. It’s more of a cleanup type of procedure,” said McVay. “There is a surgery, but it's a cleanup. I'm not a doctor so I don't want to speak out of turn, but it will be something that'll get cleaned up.”
Rams Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease, according to CBS Sports . Faulk has been dealing with the disease for 18 months. Faulk mentioned in an interview that he’s in a good place.
"The little tremors that I get, you know, they are what they are. I just pay attention to my gait, you know, while I walk, when I'm working out, my ability to balance. It's still where it is,” said Faulk. “I'm functioning. I'm good. You know, I just, I think I caught it early. I'm in a good place."
Faulk is third on the Rams’ all-time rushing list and is tied with Todd Gurley for the most rushing touchdowns in franchise history. The Rams traded for Faulk prior to the 1999 season and he played a key role in the Greatest Show on Turf. Faulk retired with the Rams in 2005 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2011.
While the Rams didn’t lose because of the unnecessary roughness call, it almost guaranteed that they would lose. The Rams had already jumped offsides on the play and the 21-yard completion put the Cardinals just outside of field goal range. The following night, Fred Warner was initially flagged for unnecessary roughness for a more egregious hit and it was picked up.
According to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer , the NFL believes the officials did get the call right on Wallace. However, it also thought that the Warner flag should have stayed. The issue remains the league's lack of consistency in officiating and its use of replay assist.
There’s no doubt that Matthew Stafford hasn’t played well. He played well against the Buffalo Bills, but in the week before against the Philadelphia Eagles and most of the game last week, he did not. It’s true that Stafford gave the Rams the lead at the end of the game against the Cardinals. The offense was also stagnant and didn’t start moving the ball until under three minutes to play in the game.

title: Rams Trading for Wide Receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Would Be a Mistake They Can't Afford
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may be 2-4, but that doesn’t mean that general manager Les Snead is simply going to sit back and wave the white flag. On Wednesday, it was reported by ESPN’s Dan Graziano that the Rams will at least e xplore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver in the wake of Davante Adams being placed on injured reserve.
It shouldn’t be a total surprise that the Rams aren’t just going to call it a season. Back in 2019, with the team at 3-3, the Rams made moves for Austin Corbett and Jalen Ramsey. Both players were key pieces in the team’s Super Bowl run in 2021.
When the Rams were 3-3 in 2022, they were close to trading for Christian McCaffrey and Brian Burns. However, they were outbid for McCaffrey, and the Panthers weren’t ready to part ways with Burns at that time.
Very few would be surprised if the Rams made a move. However, if they do make a trade, it needs to be the right one . A popular name that has surfaced is Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas Jr. would be a perfect replacement for Adams as the team’s “X” receiver and was originally drafted in the first round. He also plays for the Jaguars, whose general manager, James Gladstone, has a relationship with Snead. While an exciting name, trading for Thomas would also only dig the Rams into a deeper hole.
Sometimes, the best moves are the ones that aren’t made. That was likely the case when the Rams didn’t acquire McCaffrey and the Panthers said no on Burns. The Rams went 5-12 in 2022 and the 2023 NFL Draft played a large role in the team’s quick turnaround.
There’s nothing to confirm that the Rams have interest in Thomas. In fact, McVay said on Wednesday that the team isn’t even looking at wide receiver replacements.
“That's not something that we've talked about right now,” said McVay. “We have some depth on our roster. Maybe we talked about the practice squad, but not anything externally.”
Whether McVay was honest in what he told the media can certainly be argued. However, there has been speculation about wide receiver options the Rams could be interested in, with Thomas being near the top of the list.
There’s no doubt that Thomas would fit the type of player the Rams typically target in trades. The moves for Sammy Watkins, Austin Corbett, Dante Fowler Jr., Jalen Ramsey, and Kevin Dotson were all players who had fallen out of favor with their previous teams.
Per Brian Thomas Jr.'s profile via @RecepPerception 🟣 72% success rate on "go" routes 👀 🟡Down on 1st contact on 48% of “in space” attempts 🟡72.7% contested catch rate and 2 dropped passes Would not be shocked if Rams took BTJ at 19 as an Atwell replacement. pic.twitter.com/fLcIbbZb4T
Thomas played just 21.1 percent of the Jaguars’ offensive snaps in Week 6 and doesn’t have a reception on five targets in the last two games. After a promising rookie season in which he had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns on 87 receptions, he has just 57 receptions for 812 yards and three touchdowns since.
Ever since the Jaguars moved on from Doug Pederson and hired Liam Coen, he simply hasn’t been the same player. Given that evidence, it’s worth questioning his fit since Coen and McVay come from the same offensive coaching tree. The schemes are very similar.
Over the last two years, Thomas Jr. has ranked last in adjusted catch percentage via FTN Fantasy. Adjusted catch percentage is the rate of catchable targets converted into a catch. Among players with at least 15 targets this season, his 22.2 percent drop-rate is the highest in the NFL. Last season, he also ranked inside the top-5 in drop-rate at 9.1 percent. Thomas’ targeted success rate of 47.3 percent over the last two years ranks 78th out of 116 qualifying receivers. Much like Konata Mumpfield, Thomas struggles at the catchpoint.
Matt Harmon of Yahoo Sports and founder of Reception Perception, which focuses on charting wide receivers, gave Thomas a pass for 2025 in his offseason profile .
“Brian Thomas Jr.’s second season was a frustrating one. It included both dips in his play across the board in isolation and a role that continued to get scaled back as the season went on until his final profile looked merely that of a low-volume X-receiver,” wrote Harmon. “He’s a good press and man-beater who wins both on the vertical routes and helps clear space for his teammates. If he simply maintains this level of deployment and success as a route runner, while cleaning up his drops and contested-catch rate, he’d be a good and useful starting X.”
However, we’re now one-third of the way into 2026, and it’s been much of the same. It’s possible that Thomas’ rookie year was the exception and what we’ve seen the last 1.5 years is the norm. This isn’t to say that the Rams couldn’t get the most out of Thomas or that a change of scenery couldn’t be beneficial. However, it’s also a massive risk, and arguably too much of a risk that the Rams can’t afford.
After just one 1,000-yard season, the Rams traded for Sammy Watkins in 2017. The Rams traded a second-round pick and EJ Gaines for Watkins and a sixth-round pick. Watkins had 593 yards for the Rams and was not brought back the following year.
Earlier this season, the Houston Texans traded a second and seventh-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick. Harrison Jr. has never had more than 900 receiving yards in a season.
Unlike Watkins and Harrison Jr., Thomas wasn’t taken inside the top five of his draft class. Still, he’s a former first-round pick and has more production than Harrison and Watkins had. His price point likely starts with a second-round pick unless the Jaguars are desperate to get rid of him, which doesn’t appear to be the case.
Looking at the 2027 NFL Draft, the Rams already don’t have a first or third-round pick. If they were to move off of the second-round pick, they wouldn’t draft until the fourth round. Given the state of the roster and pending free agents, the Rams may need their second-round pick to add young, cheap talent to replenish the roster.
While the Baltimore Ravens gave up a 2028 second-round pick for Cam Jurgens, the Rams don’t have a 2028 second-round pick to give up. Considering their current roster situation, they also aren’t in a position to trade away a 2028 first-round pick.
The Rams may believe that adding a wide receiver can help turn their season around. At the same time, it needs to be one that fits their price point. The Rams got Kevin Dotson for a late-round pick swap and Austin Corbett for a fifth-round pick. A fourth-round pick may not get a flashy name like Thomas, but it could still get them what they need.
This is a front office that has already invested significant resources into building this roster, and the results have been disappointing. Doubling down by sacrificing another valuable draft pick for a receiver who has struggled for the better part of two seasons would only compound the problem.

title: Myles Garrett's Uncertain Status Raises Bigger Questions About the Rams' Blockbuster Trade
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams traded for edge rusher Myles Garrett this offseason , it was thought that he would be the missing piece and help lead the team to the Super Bowl. Garrett was coming off a 2025 season in which he won NFL Defensive Player of the Year and broke the single-season sack record.
Over the past few seasons, the Rams have been rebuilding the defense. After moving on from Leonard Floyd, Bobby Wagner, and Jalen Ramsey, along with Aaron Donald's retirement, the Rams essentially tore the kitchen down to the studs and rebuilt it.
They added some pieces that simply allowed them to get by, such as Ahkello Witherspoon and Darious Williams at cornerback, but they also found strong foundational pieces in players like Kobie Turner and Byron Young. Braden Fiske had proven some value on the defensive line as well. While the Rams still cut some corners, going cheap at linebacker, they had their star centerpiece in Jared Verse.
This past offseason, the Rams looked to complete the rebuild project on defense. They traded for cornerback Trent McDuffie and signed Jaylen Watson to finish the kitchen cupboards. Everything seemed complete until they arguably got greedy.
They had a perfectly good working fridge in Verse. It had plenty of space to work with and had an ice maker. While it may not have been perfect, it was still a high-quality fridge.
In June, Les Snead took a walk through the fridge section at Home Depot when a salesperson on the floor, let's call him Andrew Berry, caught his attention. Snead didn’t need a new fridge, but if he traded in his old one, he could get the Myles Garrett model with all the bells and whistles for a great price. It was a high-end model with commercial-grade engineering and precision climate control. You could control everything from your phone. This was the piece that would bring the entire kitchen together.
While everybody was excited for the new fridge, they were also disappointed to see the old one go. Earlier this offseason, Trent McDuffie went on Bussin’ With The Boys and described the vibe in the locker room after the team acquired Garrett.
“Guys weren't even excited excited, knowing you have Myles Garrett coming,” McDuffie said. “I heard the news, I started smiling. I looked around and I was like, ‘Oh, we’re not like, yeah!’ Everyone was like 'Whoa, hold on. J-Verse? You're going to let him go?'”
Back in August, Byron Young was asked about the trade. “That was unfortunate. It's part of business and it's something that definitely did hit me pretty hard,” said Young. “Building that relationship and friendship with him. That was a brother to me. Still a brother.”
Young wasn’t the only player to voice some disappointment. Braden Fiske also said at the time that his initial reaction was disappointment. That hit pretty hard pretty quick,” said Fiske. “My first instinct isn’t, ‘Oh, s---. We got Myles Garrett.’ My first instinct is like, ‘Oh, s---. We lost Jared. That really sucks.’”
Verse was the heart of the defense. He certainly had his deficiencies, but his presence and impact on the defense and locker room as a whole couldn’t be measured. The NFL isn’t a Madden video game or fantasy football where trading big-time players doesn’t reverberate through a team. There are real human relationships and connections to consider.
This isn’t the first time that general manager Les Snead has traded a player. Back in 2021, the Rams traded Jared Goff for Matthew Stafford. With that said, that trade felt different. Most of the team likely understood that they had reached a ceiling with Goff. That doesn’t mean there wasn’t disappointment, but there was at least some understanding that they had hit a ceiling.
That doesn’t appear to have been the same vibe when the Rams moved on from Verse. Trading away Verse accelerated his development timeline to closer match the Rams' championship window . However, where the argument could be made the Goff was holding the offense back in 2020, that couldn't be said about Verse and the defense.
The core of the defense had been through a lot together.In 2024, they experienced the divisional-round loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Last season, they all came up short together in the NFC Championship game. The Rams built that unit through the draft and it was a tight-knit group.
When the Rams first acquired Garrett, everything appeared to be working great. Everyone seemed pleased with the new fridge in the kitchen. Rams reporter Stu Jackson noted that Garrett looked as fast and explosive as advertised.
“When he's out there, you can just feel his aura,” said McDuffie in training camp.“Everybody likes to say this aura that the guy has. He's gigantic. He's a monster.”
As can be the case with many appliances, that’s when the electronics began to malfunction. Back in early August, Garrett missed consecutive practices with what the team described as lower-body soreness that was expanded to swelling in his knee. While the Rams erred on the side of caution, something still wasn’t right. Garrett didn’t practice for much of August and then was estimated as a full participant in the days leading up to Week 1.
The Rams tested their new fridge for a neighborhood get-together in Week 1with the San Francisco 49ers visiting. Garrett didn’t perform well. For the first time since 2018, he was held without recording a single stat.
When Sean McVay was asked after the game whether Garrett was feeling 100 percent , he responded, “To my knowledge, ya.” Minutes later, Garrett walked in and said, “No. This was the worst version of myself.”
The Rams did what they should have done weeks prior and sent their new fridge back to the factory to get fixed, placing Garrett on injured reserve. Garrett would be out at least four weeks.
While Garrett recovered from arthroscopic knee surgery, reports flooded in on his potential return timeline. To be fair, the Rams never put a timeline on Garrett. However, according to NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport on September 27, Garrett was given a six-week timeline . Rapoport reported then that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline.
On October 4, The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones added more information . Jones noted that the six-week timeline would be a worst-case scenario. The team remained hopeful that Garrett could return in Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, but people inside the building believed that Garrett could return against the Las Vegas Raiders.
As we know now, Garrett didn’t play against the Cardinals, and McVay already stated on Monday that he would not return to practice this week ahead of the Raiders. ESPN’s Dan Graziano added in a report on Wednesday that Garrett could be out another two or three weeks at least.
We’ve gone from being hopeful about four weeks and realistic about five, with six weeks being a worst-case scenario and Garrett being determined to beat that timeline, to Garrett potentially missing at least seven or eight games.
The Rams sent their malfunctioning fridge back to the factory, were given a timeline, and that timeline continues to get pushed back. Without Garrett, the Rams have been left with a minifridge that they could have gotten by with for four or five weeks, but half the season has put them in a difficult spot.
Over the last four weeks, Josaiah Stewart has just a 7.8 percent pressure rate. That ranks 72nd out of 81 qualifying edge rushers. That’s not a knock on Stewart. Coming into the season, he was expected to be the minifridge used to keep drinks cold. Now, he’s one of two edge rushers on the Rams with over 100 snaps and a full-time player.
After Garrett’s surgery, McVay was asked how it went. “He's like Wolverine, healing fast,” McVay said. However, Garrett is like Wolverine if Wolverine healed very slowly and nobody knew when he’d be good to go again.
hoping for more progress than this ... for medical people, is this a bad sign? https://t.co/Ih4ftvGmO2 pic.twitter.com/SfZNV1hNye
Garrett was on the field before the game against the Cardinals and…

title: Kevin Dotson’s Disappointing Start Raises Questions About His Future With Rams
full_text:
Looking ahead to the 2027 offseason, the Los Angeles Rams are going to have some difficult decisions to make . While they will have around $78.2 million in cap space, they also have several free agents they will likely try to bring back. Given their salary cap constraints, it’s highly unlikely that the Rams will be able to bring back everybody.
One of those decisions is whether the Rams should bring back Steve Avila or Kevin Dotson. Both players are set to hit free agency and will be top guard options if they become available. According to Spotrac, Avila’s market value is set at $13.5 million while Dotson is at $19.4 million.
Coming into the season, it was still up in the air who the Rams might bring back one of those two players. With that said, given Avila’s injury history and inconsistency, combined with Dotson’s importance to the run game, the veteran may have had the upper hand.
While Avila has been a promising young player, he’s dealt with injuries and had some lapses in pass protection over the past few years. Meanwhile, when Dotson was out last year, the Rams’ run game went from averaging 4.8 yards per carry down to 4.0.
However, through the first six weeks of the season, the outlook may have changed significantly. Dotson has taken a significant step back, and with the Rams at 2-4, that may change how they approach the offseason.
Pro Football Focus certainly isn’t the be-all and end-all, but even on tape, Dotson has struggled. Among the Rams’ starting five offensive linemen, Dotson’s overall grade of 55.5 is the lowest. Additionally, Dotson’s pass-blocking grade of 44.5 is almost 20 points worse than the Rams’ next closest offensive lineman. That ranks 48th out of 55 qualifying guards this season as well.
Being able to protect from the interior is very important at this point in Matthew Stafford’s career. At 38 years old, Stafford isn’t able to escape the pocket as easily as he used to. Dotson has allowed a 4.9 percent pressure rate, which is 1.2 percentage points higher than Avila’s this season.
He’s also taken a step back in the run gameIn 2025, Dotson was PFF’s third-highest-graded run-blocking offensive lineman. Dotson was fourth in 2024. This season, Dotson’s 62.8 run-blocking grade ranks 30th among guards.
Overall, Dotson ranks 41st out of 55 guards this season via PFF. It’s very possible that Dotson isn’t 100 percent. Back in Week 3, he missed three snaps with an injury. He hasn’t missed a game, but that’s not to say that he’s been fully healthy.
LDT slaps Dotsons hand down after getting Dotson off balance with a strong fake to the B gap, but takes the A gap ... pic.twitter.com/eH7xXfAqvy
The play above is just one example, but Dotson has been on the losing end in pass protection a lot more than he has in the past. Pass protection hasn’t ever been his strength with the Rams, but it’s never been a liability.
There’s also the aspect that Dotson isn’t playing next to a veteran right tackle like he has in the past. Over the past few seasons, Dotson and Rob Havenstein were dominant on the right side. While Dotson played alongside Warren McClendon last year, McClendon has also taken a step back. As Avila has continued playing alongside Alaric Jackson, Dotson is playing next to McClendon, who is in his first full season as a starter.
With the Rams at 2-4 and it potentially being a lost season, it’s fair to wonder if that also changes how they approach the offseason. This past offseason, the Rams started to look at what life would be like after Stafford retires. They took Ty Simpson to be Stafford’s replacement, displaying that the Rams were at least beginning to prepare for the future.
If the Rams were in a spot where they were still committed to the aging core and that group came up just short again, bringing back a 30-year-old Dotson would make sense. Avila may be cheaper and he’s still just 27. The Rams may be able to get another three or four years from Avila in his prime. Avila also remains a steady top-20 guard.
There is still plenty of time for Dotson to turn it around and prove that the first six weeks aren’t a sign of what’s to come. He’s arguably been the most important player on the Rams’ offensive line over the last two years. However, the Rams can’t make a decision based solely on past performance.
With Avila younger, playing better, and potentially cheaper, the Rams may need to reconsider which guard they build around. What looked like a decision that favored Dotson entering the season may now be trending in the opposite direction.

title: Rams Week 7 Injury Report: More Bad News as Trent McDuffie, Nate Landman Face Uncertainty
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are preparing to play the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, and the injuries just keep piling up. Earlier this week , the Rams placed wide receiver Davante Adams and nose tackle Poona Ford on injured reserve. Additionally, defensive lineman Kobie Turner has been ruled out for a handful of weeks.
However, the Rams will be monitoring other key starters as well this week. On Wednesday, cornerback Trent McDuffie didn’t practice with a groin injury and remains day-to-day. Additionally, linebacker Nate Landman has been placed in the concussion protocol.
“Trent will be a DNP with his groin. We'll take it a day at a time, like what I told you guys, and evaluate his status as we go,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Then on Monday, found out Landman landed in the concussion protocol so he'll be a DNP.”
McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report last week. While McVay said that he felt good about him going into Sunday, McDuffie was inactive for the game. McDuffie will certainly be one to monitor this week.
While Landman's presence on the injury report isn’t surprising given that he’s been there the last few weeks, his placement in the concussion protocol is certainly a new development. In order to return to play, Landman will be limited in his allowed activity. He’ll then graduate to an aerobic exercise program overseen by the club’s medical staff.
Once he passes that, he’ll be able to perform sport-specific activities.Step four involves returning to non-contact drills. Finally, in the last phase, Landman would have to be a full participant in practice and contact without showing any signs or symptoms of a concussion.
Cornerback Josh Wallace and tight end Colby Parkinson were also on the injury report, but both were full participants.
Lastly, after leaving Kobie Turner off the injured reserve transactions on Tuesday alongside Davante Adams and Poona Ford, the Rams placed him on injured reserve Wednesday. Turner will be out for a minimum of four weeks. In corresponding moves, the Rams signed EDGE Darryl Peterson III to the active roster and signed Jalen Hunt to the practice squad.
While the Rams only have four players on the injury report to start the week, that’s the same number of players they’ve put on injured reserve over the last few days. It’s almost as if you wake up and expect more injury news from the Rams.
“Everybody sees these and they're on their fantasy team or whatever and they're like, 'I have to trade a guy in and out now.' We're like, 'Well, that guy has worked his ass off for the last eight months to get this opportunity and it's unfortunate he doesn't get to do what he loves to do,’” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “I feel more for our guys than I do for anybody else.I know the work that they put into it to be out here doing what they love, so that hurts me for them. But at the same time, I think I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win.”
For the Raiders, defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway was the only non-participant as he remains in the concussion protocol. The Rams will certainly monitor the statuses of tight end Brock Bowers, offensive tackle Kolton Miller, and linebacker Quay Walker. All three were limited on Wednesday.
The Rams will already be shorthanded against the Raiders, and losing McDuffie or Landman would only make matters worse. With several key starters already sidelined, the Rams can’t afford to lose more players as they look to get back in the win column.

title: Why Raiders Catching Rams at Opportunistic Time
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing for a showdown with the Los Angeles Rams, looking to rebound after losing three straight.
The Raiders may be sliding, but the Rams are in a worse spot. Everyone expected them to be a powerhouse that would mow down every team in their way, but they sit at 2-4 and have lost their last two games, including a loss to the Arizona Cardinals.
For a Raiders team that needs to get back on track, the Rams come to town at the right time. Not only are they significantly injured, but they're not playing with much confidence.
The Raiders have lost three straight, but their confidence does not appear to have wavered. They put a scare into the hearts of the Buffalo Bills, who may be the best team in the AFC and possibly the entire NFL.
It would be a major confidence boost to beat a Rams team that has floundered in the last two weeks. Granted, one of those losses was to the Bills, but they had no business losing to the Cardinals in that fashion.
Klint Kubiak is still learning the ropes as a head coach, and facing off against Sean McVay on the other sideline won't be easy. However, McVay has made some poor coaching decisions this season, which have set the Rams up for failure.
Kubiak should go into this game with a simple plan that doesn't need to be overly complicated. If he thinks too much about how to approach this game, McVay will make him pay and leave Allegiant Stadium with a road victory.
There is a laundry list of players who won't appear in this game for the Raiders' opponent.
Among them: Davante Adams , Myles Garrett, Poona Ford, Nate Landman, and Kobie Turner. Oh, and Puka Nacua is questionable for this game.
All the star power the Rams entered the season with has somewhat faltered, so they may not be bringing their A-game to Las Vegas. The Raiders will face a Rams team that is somewhat comparable in terms of talent level.
For a Raiders team that needs a win, this game presents that opportunity. The Rams are struggling, and they may not be able to rebound and dominate the NFL like we all expected.
That said, this would still be a tremendous win for Kubiak's team if they can pull it off. They would move to 4-3, and with the NFL looking as wide open as it is, that would give the team enough reason not to pull the plug on the season just yet.
Carter Landis studied journalism at Michigan State University where I graduated in May of 2022. He currently is a sports reporter for a local television station, and is a writer covering the Las Vegas Raiders

title: Raiders vs. Rams: 5 Key Players To Watch
full_text:
Week 7 is here, and this game could determine the fate of both franchises for the rest of the season. The Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams go toe-to-toe on Sunday afternoon in a game many saw as a gimme for the supposed "superteam" that is the Rams.
Las Vegas has lost three straight games while Los Angeles is battling injuries to key starters and special teams miscues. Both teams are in a must-win situation as their regular-season futures hang in the balance. The Raiders will need some help to secure a big win over the Rams in what could be an exciting game at Allegiant Stadium.
Here are five players on the Raiders roster to watch in this weekend's crucial matchup.
Even if he has just come out of retirement, Aaron Donald is still a handful for opposing offensive linemen. He is consistently doubled and tripled teamed, which is why the production isn't as high as many were expecting. Yet the Raiders could be the team that leaves their guards on an island, and Caleb Rogers must be ready for the challenge.
Making his second start of the season, Rogers had an impressive day against the Buffalo Bills' defensive front last week. He hasn't shown anything that would warrant a move back to the bench anytime soon, but the former Texas Tech standout could earn a lot of trust from head coach Klint Kubiak if he slows down Donald.
I think if there is a game where the Raiders need Quay Walker to look like a star, it's this one. The former Green Bay Packer has been playing his best football as a versatile WILL linebacker who can rush the passer, set the edge, fit the run off the ball, and run the flag pole in the middle of the field.
Against an offense with the third-best run success rate (48.6%), according to Next Gen Stats , Walker has a chance to be a disruptor in the backfield while closing off the middle of the field in coverage against the Rams' heavy usage of 13 personnel (three tight ends).
After missing last week's game with a concussion, Tonka Hemingway returns to the lineup with no injury designation for this weekend. The Raiders are in desperate need of his explosiveness and penetration skills at the line of scrimmage, as he has emerged as arguably their best defensive tackle. Hemingway faces a tough matchup against a great Rams interior offensive line and will be entrusted to be the difference-maker in the middle of the defensive front.
The Rams' special teams have been the Achilles' heel of their season, and nothing seems to be getting any better. They lack discipline on punt and kickoff coverage and have allowed some serious returns. This is an opportunity for the Raiders to have a great day on special teams and utilize the speed and quickness of both Laube and Benson, so look for this duo to create some big plays.

title: One Trade Deadline Move Raiders Must Prioritize ASAP
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders spent the offseason revamping their roster from the top down. Las Vegas' front office did an admirable job of quickly revamping what was the league's worst roster last season. Still, too many holes remained to fill them all in one offseason.
Las Vegas' season and future will largely depend on the moves the front office makes during this year's free agency and the NFL Draft. A productive offseason saw the Raiders eliminate multiple needs, most notably at center and at quarterback.
The start of the regular season allowed the Raiders to better gauge the strengths and weaknesses of their revamped roster. Just as the new additions have shone, so have their remaining deficiencies at times. Thus, perfectly explaining Las Vegas' 3-3 record.
Arguably the biggest issue the Raiders have right now is their offensive line. Although it is not nearly as bad as last season, improving the unit would eliminate most of the issues that are plaguing the offense overall. The unit is still gelling together after several new pieces joined this offseason.
Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko explained how detail-oriented the staff is with the unit and how it tracks the unit's progress over time.
“I think it's really every meeting, every snap, every play that we go every series and just building those things together," Janocko said earlier this week.
"Can we get 1% better with our techniques, our hand placement, how we come off the ball, what's our eyes look like? What's our pad level? What's our finish? All those things that we can quantify. Can we get 1% better than that? And that's how we're going to grow as not just an offensive line, but as an offense and as an organization."
Las Vegas could easily decide not to make any move at all at the deadline. However, if the Raiders should look to make a move, it would be a trade for an offensive guard. If Las Vegas trades away draft picks or a player, it should be for a dependable offensive lineman.
After adding veteran Tyler Linderbaum during the offseason, the Raiders are now figuring out which offensive line positions still need work. After the season's first six games, it is clear the team will need more from that position group for the rest of this season and likely beyond.
The Raiders are 3-3, but their offense has struggled for long stretches. It has been a major reason Las Vegas has lost three straight games. At times, Las Vegas' offense has struggled to move the ball through the air. The unit has also struggled to run the ball for most of this season.
“It’s just something we’re going to look to improve every week. Whether we have a game that we rush for 150, 200 yards, we’re still going to go back and say, 'Okay, how can we get better?' So, I don’t know that we’re looking at it in terms of it’s close. We’re looking for incremental improvement every week in everything we do,” Kubiak said.
Las Vegas' offensive line could use help and more time together. However, on one level or another, the Raiders' line collectively has room for improvement. The Raiders' offensive line, like the team as a whole, has improved significantly from last season, but still needs more.
The trade deadline would be the quickest and most efficient way to add a quality offensive lineman, but after this offseason's moves, Las Vegas may have to work with what it has. Janocko gave insight into the thought process he and the Raiders' coaching staff use to approach situations.
"I think everything you look at, you got to look at the big picture, and it's not the same thing all the time," Janocko said.
"But what is our efficiency on first down? Are we in are we in second and long? And then, do we have specific tendencies? So, we dig into all of that. Whether it be first down, second down, third down. Wherever we're studying, we look at when we have success, what's the why, and then when we don't, what's the why?"
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Announcers, Referees & Jersey Combination for Raiders' Week 7 Matchup
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders hope this Sunday will go better than the previous three, as they host the Los Angeles Rams. Both teams enter Week 7 with issues that will likely impact Sunday's game. The rebuilding Raiders have a chance to get back on track this Sunday.
Las Vegas continues to work through one of the toughest schedules in the league. Despite their record, Sunday's game against the Rams will be another challenging matchup for Klint Kubiak's Raiders.
The Raiders will continue to lean on quarterback Kirk Cousins, who is playing some of the best football of any quarterback in the league entering Week 7. Still, the 15-year veteran knows he has plenty to work on to play at his best each week.
Even after all this time, and the Raiders' early success compared to last season, Cousins knows that learning the game and improving as a player is a constant process.
"Footwork, progressions, decision-making, your leadership, your presence, your communication skills, your toughness. You're always being tested, mentally, physically, emotionally, and every day you're asking yourself, am I meeting the standard to win a championship? And I think when you go back and look at a game like Sunday, and it's happened a couple times, several times this year, 90% is good,” Cousins said when asked what he can get better at.
“And it's not the 90% that I get worried about. It's the 10% where you say that's not up to the standard of what it takes to win a championship. And so, how do we get that 10% to shrink to 3% to 2% And you're always going to do that. You're always going to have plays you want back, but that's what you're trying to trim to make sure that you meet the standard to go win a championship."
Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko spent multiple seasons with Cousins while both were a part of the Minnesota Vikings' organization. Janocko recently shared his thoughts on Cousins' growth from the last time they worked together to now.
"I think, like you said, experience. So, even more experience than he was then. He's seen good things. He's had success in different systems since we've been apart. So, he has a different base of knowledge that we can bounce ideas off of each other. Being around different ideas, different players,” Janocko said earlier this week.
“Much like I've been around different ideas with different coaches, so you see that, and then you just see a guy that you know he just he wants to do what it takes to win and wants to – he's a guy that thrives on accountability."
“So, he wants to be pushed, he wants to be coached, and when other guys see a guy that's been in this league that long, want to be coached, and is the first one to say, ‘I got to do this, I can make this throw, or I got to step up’. And then when it's successful, it's we, it's us, it's together. That's type of stuff that young guys should mimic."
Jonathan Vilma will serve as an analyst, Chris Meyers will serve as the play-by-play, and  Megan Olivi will be the sideline reporter on Sunday. The Raiders will wear their black home jerseys, silver pants, and silver helmets. Ron Torbert is the head referee designated for the Raiders' Week 7 outing.
The Raiders have a tall task on their hands, as they will face a Rams team desperate to stop their own losing streak. Matthew Stafford poses several problems for the Las Vegas' defensive backfield. However, he also has the potential to score points, no matter who his receivers are.
This means Stafford poses issues for the Raiders' defense and Las Vegas' offense, as the unit will again be forced to face an elite coach-and-quarterback duo. Stafford is yet another strong-armed quarterback Las Vegas will face in consecutive weeks.
Las Vegas has the talent to compete with any team they face this season. This is especially true with the Rams, as they enter Week 7 minus several key contributors. To break its three-game losing streak , it must capitalize on opportunities to pull ahead when they present themselves.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: What Raiders Can Realistically Afford at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders roster is nearly set as the trade deadline approaches, but it is still far from complete. A team can only do so much to fix its roster before the trade deadline, but with room for improvement, Las Vegas could be in the market.
John Spytek noted during the offseason that he is "always listening" to trade offers. During his brief time in Las Vegas, Spytek has not been a man of hyperbole. Still, the Raiders front office made sweeping changes this offseason to revamp what was the league's worst roster last season.
So, as much as Spytek is always listening, he and the Raiders' front office have every right to sit on their remaining resources ahead of the deadline if they choose. The Raiders handed out over $300 million in contracts during free agency. Then, added 10 rookies via the draft.
That is significantly more than most front offices do in one offseason. That is more than some front offices do in years. It would be understandable if Las Vegas did not make a move at the deadline. Their 3-3 start confirms they are on the right track. It may be best to leave things as is.
Still, the Raiders have several talented players who could entice other teams to try to strike a deal. Then there are the numbers. The money Las Vegas spent in free agency left little cap space to work with on the back end. This forced multiple contract restructurings.
Las Vegas has around $11 million in available cap space ahead of the trade deadline. That should be enough to make a solid move, as a potential player-for-player trade could improve the Raiders' numbers. That would undoubtedly change if the Raiders traded a player for draft picks.
As the Raiders know all too well, many things must go right for two teams to complete a trade. Beyond making the numbers work, teams must answer other questions before deciding whether a deal is realistic or reasonable, considering how well they have played overall this season.
For Las Vegas to complete a trade, they would likely have to trade one of their best players with a sizeable contract. That would mean trading the likes of Maxx Crosby or Kolton Miller, which would be unthinkable at this point in the season. However, Las Vegas has three games before the deadline.
The Raiders will face the Los Angeles Rams at home this Sunday, the New York Jets on the road next Sunday, and the San Francisco 49ers on the road the following week. If the Raiders lose two of the next three games, they will be 4-5. A trade could seem more plausible then.
Even at 4-5, Las Vegas trading one of their best players for anything less than a top-tier offer, such as two first-round draft picks for Crosby, would not make much sense because of what it would do to what Klint Kubiak and his coaching staff have started to build.
For the Raiders to trade one of their best players and risk hurting the clear progress they've made would have to mean they received an offer they couldn't refuse. They must consider this as the deadline approaches. Las Vegas is not obligated to consider a trade.
The Raiders could also trade picks in return for a player at a position of need, but trading away picks also seems counterproductive. Las Vegas has made significant progress by inserting several rookies and second-year players into significant roles this season.
Las Vegas trading away draft picks now would go against that. Spytek also values having more picks. The Raiders have drafted at least 10 players in both of their drafts under Spytek. Las Vegas has a higher chance of success drafting players under Spytek than a retread from another team.
The Raiders are ahead of schedule. If they were to make a trade, it should be a very low-key move- nothing big; no need to overdo it.
Las Vegas needs to fine-tune its existing operation unless it can strike a trade for a player they believe can elevate it immediately.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders Injury Update: From Concern to Encouragement in 24 Hours
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev.—It is no secret that the Las Vegas Raiders' (3-3) offensive rushing attack needs improvement ahead of their matchup against the preseason Super Bowl favorites, the Los Angeles Rams (2-4), at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday.
The Klint Kubiak offensive scheme is built on running the football, and teams are stacking the box to stop it.
Still, it shouldn't be as bad as it has been, and Kubiak hasn’t run from it. Often, preemptively, before the media can ask, bringing it up.
Promising rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. (MWJ) has worked hard to earn the right to play more, and early in the week, when I asked Kubiak if he would get more reps this Sunday, he definitively said, “Yes.”
After being listed on Wednesday’s injury report as “limited” with a foot/back injury, the concerning news came on Thursday when it was learned that he did not participate in practice.
Kubiak has stressed the importance of participating in practice to play on Sundays.
MWJ’s status on Sunday certainly was in jeopardy after Thursday’s news.
Today, MWJ did not practice, and Klint Kubiak addressed it. “Mike Washington [Jr.] is questionable,” and added, “We’re expecting him to be ready.”
Didn't see Raiders RB Mike Washington Jr at practice today. pic.twitter.com/H3H9bfV1qo
A source in the building added anonymously, “Nothing has been decided (as far as availability) but I would say the mood for him playing is certainly, optimistic.”
Dylan Laube continues to see his role expand on both special teams and offense, but MWJ needs a bigger role.
If MWJ can't go, I also asked Kubiak if UDFA Roman Hemby could be called up for the first time to the 53-man roster for this game.
“That’d be a good option. He’s been practicing pretty well.”
Additionally, more good news on the injury front came out today for the Silver and Black. Sophomore DT Tonka Hemingway, who started the week not practicing due to a concussion, is back and will play. An enormous boost to the Raiders' defensive line. His head coach was thrilled to have him back.
“He brings a lot of confidence. He’s playing really good football, and we’re really excited to have him back. And he means a lot to our defense.”
One last thing came out of talking with Kubiak today.
Dont’e Thornton Jr. will not be activated this week. On a team needing WR help, now healthy, that should concern the Raiders sophomore.
Thornton came out of his rookie season looking great, but ever since the San Francisco 49ers came to town for the joint practices at 2025 training camp, he has all but disappeared.
The Raiders GM John Spytek will need to make a decision next week. The issue is simple. The Raiders don't have to put him on the active roster, and they don't need to release him. During or at the end of the 21-day practice window, the team has three choices: activate him to the 53-man roster, keep him on season-ending injured reserve, or waive/release him.
​If they do not add him to the 53-man roster by the end of the 21 days, he automatically reverts to injured reserve and is ineligible to play for the remainder of the season.
Kubiak said of his healthy, but not activated, wide receiver, “He’s making big progress. He’s done a lot of good things in practice. Still working back into getting his football legs back after missing a lot of time. But I’ve been really pleased with his effort, with his detail. He’s close.”

title: Biggest Areas of Improvement for Raiders' Long-Term Success
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are suddenly in danger of falling below .500 after losing three consecutive games.
It's a fascinating Week 7 matchup between the Raiders and Los Angeles Rams, as both teams are reeling. The last three games have exposed Las Vegas' shortcomings. With that in mind, here are three areas the Raiders need to improve as soon as possible if they want to maintain their position in the AFC playoff picture.
Through six games, the Raiders are averaging 79.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 30th in the NFL. There are several reasons for this development, including Ashton Jeanty operating at less than 100 percent and the offensive line struggling in run blocking. Over the last two games, the 22-year-old running back has 20 carries for 49 yards and one touchdown.
When assessing this situation, there are two fixes to the problem - one much simpler than the other. The simpler solution is to give Mike Washington Jr. more opportunities. Now, the rookie running back didn't practice on Thursday, so we may not see that come to fruition this week. However, assuming that Washington Jr.'s injury doesn't cause a multi-week absence, utilizing both running backs evenly in the coming weeks should be considered.
The two running backs essentially split the workload last week in the loss against the Buffalo Bills. The second solution is much easier said than done, but the offensive line has to be better at opening rushing lanes.
The solution is currently not in the building. As much as Tre Tucker has impressed in flashes, he's not a bona fide WR1. Las Vegas' pass game is highly dependent on tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer. It's proven effective, but the offense's ceiling is limited without a legitimate threat on the outside.
As the trade deadline draws closer, rumors are circulating about players who could be moved ahead of Nov. 10. One name that continues to draw interest from multiple teams is Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. It would require a steep price. However, the Raiders' front office should consider trading for a wide receiver ahead of the trade deadline. Their decision is contingent on the next few weeks. If Las Vegas is still within striking distance of the wild card, it could be buyers.
You can argue that the first three weeks were somewhat of a fluke, as the Raiders' opposition during that span is cumulatively 2-15. In the previous three games, Las Vegas has faced elite quarterbacks - Patrick Mahomes , Josh Allen, and Drake Maye. In that stretch, the Raiders are allowing 284.6 passing yards per game.
While Matthew Stafford has struggled this season, the 38-year-old quarterback is still one of the best players at his position. Las Vegas' pass rush has been stellar this season, but the secondary has been susceptible against above-average quarterbacks.

title: How Raiders Can Stop Coming Close, Finally Break Losing Streak
full_text:
Technically, the reeling Las Vegas Raiders will face the reeling Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. However, only one of the two teams had Super Bowl aspirations entering this season, and it's not Las Vegas. Hence, only one team enters its Week 7 matchup reeling.
The Rams have a talented roster and coaching staff that can adjust to just about anything. Los Angeles also has the league's reigning Most Valuable Player, Matthew Stafford, starting at quarterback. No matter the Rams' overall health, stopping Stafford is a tall task.
Sunday's matchup against Stafford follows outings against Patrick Mahomes, Drake Maye, and Josh Allen. The past few weeks have been busy for Las Vegas' defense, to say the least, and they will have their hands full again this Sunday.
Las Vegas' defense played well against two of those three quarterbacks. In theory, all three should have helped prepare the Raiders' defense for Stafford's passing. Yet Stafford presents a unique set of challenges in his own right, as his accuracy could pose issues for Las Vegas.
Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard offered insight into the differences between playing the likes of mobile quarterbacks such as Mahomes, Maye, and Allen, compared to facing the less-mobile, but just as accurate, Stafford.
“When you have a mobile quarterback, you fill up rushing lanes so the guy can’t buy as much time. Where do you want to allocate your defenders? Can we rush with four and get home? Can we get to the spot with three, four, five? That’s at least the way I think,” Leonard said before practice on Thursday.
“So, when you’re rushing a guy that doesn’t move as much, it’s just the same conversations. Where do you want to allocate your resources? Do we need to double a guy? Is the quarterback priority over our matchups? That’s at least the way I’m always thinking about it. There’s pluses and minuses to how you want to do it.”
For the Raiders to end their three-game losing streak , their defense must stop Stafford and the Rams enough times to help Las Vegas' offense score. Las Vegas' 3-3 start has confirmed the team will go as far as the defense takes them. Their past three games show the unit needs more production.
Their past three weeks have confirmed that, for this Raiders team, the difference between winning and losing will depend on the defense's ability to create turnovers, extra possessions for their offense, and pressure opposing teams' quarterbacks.
Given the Rams' injuries, Las Vegas' defense should be able to pressure Stafford into a mistake or two. Whether it is a sack, a turnover, or an incompletion, when combined with the Raiders' home crowd, Las Vegas' defense is in position to get back to the unit from Week 1 through Week 3.
That is what it will take for a Raiders' offense that plays significantly differently when its defense creates turnovers and helps it start with solid field position. Las Vegas' offense needs its defense to help put it in position to score consistently enough to win, or it will be another long Sunday.
The Raiders are on track. They have come close to upsetting two of the league's best teams in the past three weeks, even though they've barely begun rebuilding their roster. Las Vegas' future is bright, but at 3-3, with two winnable games on the horizon, it may be too early to look to the future.
Las Vegas has a roster that can compete with any team in the league this season. They admittedly have a long way to go to fully rebuild their roster, but a win on Sunday could spark a mid-to-late season run for a Raiders team still gelling after only six games together.
A fourth loss in a row is far from ideal. However, at the start of the season, few would have been surprised by the Raiders' three losses. The same is true about a potential loss to the Rams on Sunday. Winning is the goal, but things must be kept in perspective.
No one knows what will happen on Sunday,  but a win would be huge for Las Vegas.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: Raiders vs. Rams: 4 Key Matchups To Watch
full_text:
Something has to give on Sunday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium. Two teams, the Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Rams, are trying to stop the bleeding in their respective programs as they collide in a pivotal early-season matchup that could shape each team's path for the rest of the season.
Head coach Klint Kubiak went toe-to-toe with Rams coach and play-caller Sean McVay in Seattle last season, and now has a chance to do it again this weekend. If the Raiders are to pull off an "upset" against a reeling and battered superteam, they must succeed in these four key matchups.
It's been an encouraging season for the Raiders' young right tackle, who has slowly developed into a quality starter up front. However, Glaze has racked up three pressures in each of the last three games after allowing one pressure in the first three games combined. The opponents have gotten more difficult, and it won't get any better against the Rams and edge rusher Byron Young.
Young is sixth in the NFL in total pressures with 29, according to Next Gen Stats. With Myles Garrett still on injured reserve, Young is the Rams' best pass rusher and one of the better ones in the entire league thus far. This is a game where Glaze must have his best game of the season against Young and the reeling Rams.
The Raiders have the best tight end duo in the NFL with Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, who are on pace for big seasons. These two are the best pass-catchers on the roster and are utilized in a variety of ways under Kubiak. With how they're deployed, they'll look to give the Rams' defense, which will likely be without All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and linebacker Nate Landman, some challenges.
Los Angeles' linebacker room could be a weak spot for the Raiders' tight ends to attack, but the rest of the secondary remains strong despite McDuffie's potential absence. This could be a challenging matchup, but losing McDuffie could signal another productive day for Bowers and Mayer.
According to Next Gen Stats, Raiders franchise pass rusher Maxx Crosby is fifth in the NFL with 30 pressures, remaining one of the league's disruptive defenders. He faces Rams right tackle Warren McClendon, who has allowed a 6.8% pressure rate, the sixth-lowest amongst all right tackles. This is a good individual matchup to watch on Sunday. Hopefully, we get to see a signature Crosby performance.
The aforementioned EDGE vs. offensive tackle matchup is one of several the Raiders will have to contend with against one of the NFL's best offenses. Points have been an issue for Los Angeles, of course, but production is far from an issue, as reigning MVP Matthew Stafford continues to play good football.
However, the loss of Davante Adams will sting. This is a chance for Las Vegas to showcase its defense against a battered Rams offense, as defensive coordinator Rob Leonard hopes to get things back on track for his unit this weekend. Look for WILL linebacker Quay Walker to be a big factor for Sunday's game, but keep in mind that Walker was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.

title: Key Clues Raiders Depth Chart Leaves Ahead of Week 7

title: Dolphins-Jets Week 7 National Predictions Roundup: Any More Miami Believers?
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins will look for their first victory of the 2026 season when they face the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.
Here's a roundup of national predictions on this game.
The Dolphins have arrived at one of the games circled on the calendar as presenting one of the team's best opportunities to win in this rebuilding season, though the national consensus remains overwhelmingly in favor of a loss.
At least there's some movement forward after three weeks of unanimous predictions of a loss, followed by one single media member predicting a Miami win in its last game against Cincinnati in Week 5.
As we said, the Dolphins still are widely expected to lose, but there is some progress in terms of their predictions, however small.

title: Great Douglas News Highlights Positive Final Week 7 Dolphins Injury Report
full_text:
After some extensive time off in the form of a bye week, the Miami Dolphins won't be completely healthy when they take on the New York Jets, but they're getting there.
But they will get back a big piece of their offense for the Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets, with wide receiver Caleb Douglas off the injury report after being a full participant in practice Friday.
Douglas missed the past three games because of an ankle injury he sustained in the Week 2 loss against the San Francisco 49ers and the Dolphins clearly missed him.
It's not ridiculous to say the outlook of this game changes with the return of Douglas. The Dolphins passing offense was one-dimensional without him, with only Malik Washington and Greg Dulcich being consistent targets for Malik Willis, but even that's pushing it.
Despite missing three games, Douglas STILL has the third-most receiving yards of any target on the Dolphins with 113.
Miami is lacking a wide receiver that has as much upside as Douglas has shown so far, even with limited snaps due to the injury. His ability to separate from defenders is unmatched on the roster right now, combined with his speed and agility to get open in a hurry. His return brings size back to the position, with his 6-4 frame being taller than any other wide receiver.
The Dolphins currently average 153.6 passing yards per game, the second-fewest in the NFL, just 0.1 yards ahead of the Tennessee Titans. The group could use a splash of youth to energize it against a Jets secondary that allows only 185 yards per game, the fourth-fewest in the NFL.
Douglas isn't the only Dolphins rookie who could make his return against the Jets.
Safety Kyle Louis was listed as questionable for Sunday even though he's currently on the IR, but the encouraging sign here is that he was a full participant in practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. This could be a sign he's ready to return in his first week of eligibility after missing the required four games.
Normally, activating someone from the IR would require a corresponding roster move to stay within the 53-player limit, but the Dolphins are currently at 52.
Running back Jaylen Wright, who's been dealing with a nagging foot injury, also was cleared to play. With that said, Wright has struggled to make an impact as Ollie Gordon's backup, but the Jets' defense hasn't had the best success against rushing offenses - 123 yards per game given up. This could be his best chance yet to contribute.
Rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, specifically noted on Thursday that he'll be ready to play Sunday, and he was cleared on Friday. As mentioned earlier with Wright, attacking the ground might be key for Miami's offense, and Kacmarek has impressed as a run blocker for Gordon thus far.
However, there are a few players on defense who might not play this game. That includes edge rusher Rob Beal Jr., who is listed as doubtful. He had to exit the San Francisco game with a hamstring injury. Before that, he recorded a single tackle against Las Vegas in the season opener.
It's also confirmed that cornerback Reese Taylor will not play Sunday because of a quad injury; he was ruled out.
Linebacker Willie Gay Jr. was back at practice Friday after being out one day with an illness, and he was listed as questionable after being a limited participant.
On the other side, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is dealing with a significantly larger number of questions in terms of who's playing in this game. The most significant player on the list is running back Breece Hall, who was listed as questionable. He's been dealing with a quad injury suffered against Detroit in Week 3.
Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that he'd be surprised if Hall didn't play in this game, but the Jets might not want to rush things with Hall, especially because his replacement, Braelon Allen, has done such a great job in his wake with 314 yards and two touchdowns.
A big boost to the Jets' receiver corps will be the return of wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who is expected to play while dealing with a broken finger. It'll be the first time that Mitchell, Garrett Wilson and rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper Jr. will all be ready to go in the same game since their season opener.
Nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat is dealing with a knee injury but is expected to play Sunday. He's been reliable when healthy, with 15 tackles in six games played. It's a solid contribution for a player who was acquired from Tennessee in a trade that sent Jermaine Johnson to the Titans.
There are a few players officially ruled out: linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quad), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle), and offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion).
Left guard Dylan Parham is questionable to play in this game with a knee injury that has sidelined him for three games. His backup, Jordan Meredith, has played well in his absence, but it would mean a lot for the Jets to get one of their top linemen healthy once again.
Kene Nwangwu is also listed as questionable, which is a big blow for the special teams. He's been a decent kick returner with 251 yards on 11 attempts but hasn't had an opportunity to break a long run yet this season. If he can't go, Isaiah Williams will likely have to shoulder returning once again for the Jets. It should be noted that Williams had a 78-yard punt return for a touchdown for the Jets' only score in the Dolphins' 34-10 victory at MetLife Stadium last December.

In the meantime, it's 36-year-old veteran Geno Smith running the offense in his second stint with the team after first arriving as a second-round pick in 2013.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The best place to start here is that the Dolphins have owned the Jets lately, winning 14 of the past 17 matchups, including a season sweep last year. title: Dolphins Opponent Intel: Jets Insider Dishes on Minkah, Mason Taylor, Geno Smith and More
full_text:
The Miami Dolphins’ Week 7 matchup against the New York Jets will feature a matchup of AFC East in rebuilding situations.
While the Dolphins will head into the game with an 0-5 record, the Jets will come with a 2-4 mark that isn’t exciting, but clearly better than last year when New York started off 0-7 on their way to “earning” the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft.
The Dolphins swept the Jets last season, winning a close game at Hard Rock Stadium in the Week 4 Monday night matchup and blowing out the Jets at MetLife Stadium in December.
While it’s clear the Dolphins aren’t as talented as they were last season, the Jets are a bit more of a mystery.
On an episode of the All Dolphins Podcast earlier this week, New York Daily News reporter Antwan Staley helped provide some inside info on the Jets.
Here were some of the highlights of our conversation with Staley:
On an overall outlook for the season:
"What I would say is the good news is they're not 0-7 like they were last year. The Jets still aren't a good team, but I feel like they've gone from a really bad team to now a mediocre team, one that you know it's gonna be in games there, and it's gonna pressure opposing teams and all that stuff. We saw it against the Patriots there. I felt like they had some grit, had some fight. They just did. They’re just not talented enough to be able to overcome the mistakes that they have. Whether you talk about you know clock management or you know drops or penalties and things of that nature. So I think we're just seeing a team that was really young last year, they're the third-youngest team in football. Now they added some veterans there, Minkah Fitzpatrick, Demario Davis, among others, and now they're just trying to get from a mediocre team to a playoff team. And it might be another year before that happens too. But you know, they're a team that's probably going to be in every single game this year for the most part. But lack of talent is still evident in a few spots."
On Geno Smith’s performance this season and how legit is his 101.8 passer rating:
"Yeah, he's held the ball too long at times. Obviously, him being 36 years old now, like he doesn't have the same athleticism that he once had. Doesn't have necessarily the quick release like he once had. So I think he gets in trouble where you know he can hold on to the ball a little bit longer, waiting for his receivers to get open, and thenI think teams now — kind of what you found in the Patriots game — speed him up, like get him processing a little bit faster. That way he can possibly make mistakes. We've seen him fumble the ball a few times. He's only had one interception, but he's had a few fumble losses as well. So it's been up and down. It's been better than what it was last year with Justin Fields, which is a very low bar. But you know, I think Geno has given them opportunities to win games. He just hasn't always played well, so I think the quarterback rating is a bit of a mirage too.”
On whether head coach Aaron Glenn is on his way to solidifying his spot as Jets head coach for the future after a shaky first season, or is that still way up in the air:
"Yeah, that's still to be determined. The positive again is the Jets are fighting; they're in these games. They're showing grit. They're not just laying down and letting teams beat them by 30 points, like you saw sometimes last year. So it looks a lot different. However, they're just not closing games the way that they should be, and it seems like it's the same mistakes that are happening all over again. It seems like it's some kind of boneheaded penalty. It seems like it's some kind of mistake as far as play calling as well. … And I think ultimately the biggest thing, the damning stat on Aaron Glenn is this: opponents have outscored the Jets right before halftime within the last two minutes 90-6 throughout his tenure. And then him being 0-7 in the AFC East. Those are the two damning stats on Aaron Glenn. So until those change, then yeah, it's gonna be up in the air whether he comes back for 2027 or not. It starts there. You have to be able to take care of the division. Forget about New England and Buffalo for a minute, but you cannot get swept by the Dolphins and expect to keep your job this year. So this is a critical game for him. I'm sure it's a critical game for Jeff Hafley and the Dolphins organization too. The loser is going to be in really bad shape, especially if it's the Jets, because people were already calling for Aaron Glenn to be fired even before the season started. If you lose to the Dolphins, then it's hard to kind of overcome that."
On the play so far of two-time Dolphins safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, who they traded to the Jets this offseason for a seventh-round pick:
"I mean, he's been solid. He actually recorded their first interception. They broke the drought, so he'scome in and done the things that they expected him to do: be a quarterback for the defense, be a ball hog. Really helped young safety Dane Belton, who I think has been one of the biggest surprises of the Jets too this year. So I think Minkah is doing a really good job, especially since coming back (from a hamstring injury). He's not the same player that he once was when he was younger, but I think the Jets still benefit from his intelligence and just be able to see just diagnose what the offense is trying to do on a down-to-down basis."
On how Mason Taylor, the son of Dolphins Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, is doing in his second season as a Jets tight end after the team drafted fellow tight end Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of the 2026 draft:
“Well, he had a thumb injury, which kind of kept him out for a little bit, and then since coming back, think he's become more of a safety valve for Geno Smith, especially with Breece Hall being out the lineup too. If you're getting opponents pressuring you and blitzing you regularly, then you need somebody that can kind of get you out of those situations. That's something Mason Taylor can do, kind of find those soft spots in the zone, get some 4- or 5-yard catches and just kind of move the chains down the fiel. He has a different kind of athleticism than Kenyon Sadiq. I think Sadiq is more of a genetic freak, running 4.3, where I think Mason Taylor is more that guy that can move the chains, is just going to be a possession guy, and there's nothing wrong with that. "
On this idea that Malik Willis is very similar to former Jets starter Justin Fields:
“Here's the thing. Like, at least Malik is not afraid to throw the ball down the field. Now, hethere's times where he shouldn't, but he's not afraid to take those chances down the field. I feel like Justin Fields was very scared and hesitant to throw the ball past 10 yards. I don't see the comparison whatsoever. Justin was very cautious, like overly cautious of taking the football, protecting the football. Malik, I don't think it's that at all. He should be sometimes, but I don't think he is. So, no, I don't think that's a good comparison at all.”
