title: Sam Darnold Knows How Seahawks Can Turn Things Around
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are in the biggest slump they've faced in the last two seasons, and they risk going under .500 if they were to lose in Week 7 against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs.
The Seahawks are doing their absolute best to avoid that outcome at all costs, and it has shown in how they prepare in practice this week. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold explained the difference in how the team is approaching this upcoming game compared to the previous ones.
"There's a lot of good things that we're doing on tape. Sometimes it doesn't show it in the scoreboard or sometimes how it feels on the field. We're doing a lot of good things," Darnold said via the team's website.
"We need to create a little more consistency in how we're doing it. That's sustaining drives. Having six, seven, eight plays that we're stringing together and not being able to convert a third down on that eighth play. Sustaining drives and continuing to play one play after the other."
The biggest culprit in the lack of consistency has been Darnold. He has thrown at least one interception in each of the four games he has played since returning from a glute injury that held him out for nearly all of the first two weeks of the season. Darnold played in just one series during the season opener against the New England Patriots and sat out of the team's Week 2 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.
Darnold's turnovers have cost the Seahawks more than once, and it is becoming a glaring issue for a team that leads the league in yards allowed per game on defense.
If Seattle is able to play at an elite level on defense, all they need is Darnold to consistently keep the football in Seattle's hands. If he can do that, there's a good chance points are coming on the board on at least three drives throughout the game, and that might be enough to pull out a win.
The Seahawks don't need to blow every team out, but they need to score more than their opponent. The defense does more than enough to accomplish that goal, but now it's time for the offense to step up. If Darnold can maintain the consistency he's been showing in practice on the field on Sunday, they should be able to get things back on track.

title: Sam Darnold Shares Seahawks Game Plan vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks don't have an easy task on their hands for Week 7 as they take on the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football.
The Chiefs have one of the most complete rosters in the league, and they should be a strong test for the Seahawks, who have lost three of their last four games. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold explained how the team plans to attack the Chiefs.
"Had a few days to look at ourselves, look at the Chiefs… There are some things that we have to get better at and we've addressed those things," Darnold said via the team's website.
"The biggest thing for us is consistency. Consistency day in and day out. With these guys (Chiefs) coming in here, great defense, good players, good scheme. Have to prepare well and do everything that we can to all be on the same page and go out there so we can play decisively."
The Seahawks have fallen by three points or less in each of their losses this season, showing that they haven't played poorly. However, not playing poorly doesn't always equate to wins, especially in the NFL.
Depending on the opponent, good enough might not result in a victory, and the Seahawks have faced some stiff competition this season. Their loss in Week 5 came against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, and they dropped Week 6 against the Denver Broncos on the road.
Based on their Week 7 opponent, the Chiefs, this is a game the Seahawks could absolutely lose as well, based on the patterns that have formed over the course of the season.
This makes the details that much more important. Their couple extra days of preparation after losing on Thursday night football to the Broncos certainly helped.
"We all came in here and put in a lot of hours, just taking the time to look at the film from the first six games and evaluate what we're doing well at every level," offensive coordinator Brian Fleury said about last weekend's preparation.
"Just, in general schematically, and even at the position level, and kind of highlight some things that we can lean into and focus on moving forward, then it'll give us a better chance to succeed."
The Seahawks know that their margin for error against a team like the Chiefs is minimal at best. Therefore, making sure all of the details are on point is what will determine whether they win or lose this game.

title: Kyle Shanahan Isn’t Ready to Give Up on These 2 Struggling 49ers
full_text:
One of the best parts about the San Francisco 49ers this season is seeing a bunch of players step up.
Whether it’s the rookies or players entering their second or third year. They’re getting major contributions from players who aren’t their stars, and it’s played an enormous role in their 6-0 start.
However, as fantastic as the 49ers have played this season, they’ve had a couple of notable weak links. These two players have made the 49ers’ last two wins tougher than they needed to be. Yet Kyle Shanahan isn’t ready to give up on them.
In the last two games, returning punts has been a disaster for wide receiver Jacob Cowing. First, he fumbled a return against the Seattle Seahawks. Rather than wisely fair catching the punt, he decided to field it normally.
As a result, he gifted the Seahawks favorable field position. They’d inevitably score on that possession since they were in striking distance of the end zone. Cowing spotted seven points to the Seahawks thanks to his blunder.
His mistakes would continue against the Washington Commanders , where he fielded two punts inside the 49ers’ own five-yard line. The obvious decision was to let those punts bounce into the end zone.
That’s back-to-back games where Cowing registered negative plays for the 49ers. He’s become a liability as a punt returner and doesn’t help as a wide receiver, but Shanahan still thinks he can bounce back.
“I know Jake's had some mistakes. He's got to be better at it, but I also have confidence he will get better at it too,” Shanahan said.
If he doesn’t improve, the 49ers will need to pivot from him. Otherwise, Cowing will eventually cost them a game.
The only reason the game against Washington was on the line was that kicker Eddy Pineiro missed an extra point earlier in the game. He’s been doing that often this season.
That miss only confirms that he has the yips. He’s a shell of himself from last season and is poised to cost the 49ers their first loss . But similar to Cowing, Shanahan is holding out hope with Pineiro.
“Not much to discuss. I can make stuff up, but he knows he's got to make kicks, and we all do. I'm not going to try to teach him how to do that,” Shanahan said.
He’s more cut and dry when talking about Pineiro, but that’s all that needs to be said. Pineiro has to make his kicks. If he continues to struggle, you can expect the 49ers to look elsewhere.

title: Steve Young Explains Why Winning 'Dogfights' Will Boost 49ers' Super Bowl Hopes
full_text:
On paper, the San Francisco 49ers have had enjoyed perfect start to 2026 as they're 6-0 for the season so far.
However, the game is played on grass, and San Francisco is dealing with a temporarily depleted offense, including injury concerns for key veterans Mike Evans and Nick Bosa .
The Atlanta Falcons arrive for Week 7, then a bye week, but the second half of the season brings tough games against the Minnesota Vikings, the Seattle Seahawks, the Los Angeles Rams, and the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Chargers could be tough games too, but the former has placed quarterback Jalen Hurts on season-ending IR while Justin Herbert has yet to perform to his previous standards. Who knows what will happen for these matchups.
Former 49ers quarterback Steve Young believes that, despite San Francisco boasting the best record possible, certain games will still provide tricky tests. The last thing he wants is to see the team repeat what happened against the Washington Commanders, when they built a 23–3 lead only to nearly surrender it following an inspired late comeback.
“We’re 6-0, but I want to make sure that we lock things down because we’re not we don’t have that. The team in ’23 was by far the best roster in football. That’s the fact," said Young on KNBR’s Sports Leader show .
"And we were just running people out of the state. We’re just running them out. And that’s not what’s going to happen this year. So, we’re going to get in some dogfights, maybe more than we want to. And so, I don’t want to get in dogfights by allowing teams that are down and out ways to live again.
“Like, all the games where we want to just put people away or the games where we’re not in the dogfight, and I think there’s dogfights coming, and I always want to make sure we’re ready for them.
There are games coming up that the 49ers simply cannot afford to lose, particularly against opponents they are expected to beat.
Tougher tests later in the season mean the occasional defeat may be inevitable, but dropping a winnable game could come back to bite them. Defeating both the Rams and the Seahawks gives a buffer, but questions about whether they can do it again could be raised.
San Francisco must be smart with its veteran players, manage injuries carefully and ensure its key contributors are available for the games that will ultimately define its season. Case in point: future Hall of Famer Mike Evans .

title: 5 Biggest Questions Facing 49ers Ahead of Week 7
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for a key Week 7 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, there are plenty of questions surrounding the roster. What do the 49ers need to answer?
The team is banged up. They are 6-0 with a three-game lead on the Seahawks, and they hold the tiebreaker. The 49ers do not want to lose this game, but if there was a game to rest some players, this might be it. They have a bye next week, so anyone banged up would get this week and the following week. It would position San Francisco in a good spot after the bye.
Nick Bosa, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Marques Sigle, and Upton Stout are the names to watch . Do any of them play?
All indications are that the team is going to activate Christian Kirk from the PUP this week. Kirk has practiced the last few weeks, but did not have any offseason work. So, he will likely come in a bit rusty. Still, San Francisco is thin in their wide receiver room. Beyond that, Jacob Cowing has been an issue as a punt returner. Does Kirk take on that role? How many offensive snaps does he play?
The 49ers' run defense has not been tested because they have not faced many strong opponents. However, they are in the bottom third of the NFL in success rate, which means they consistently allow small chunks. Robinson is the type of runner to turn a small gain into a game-breaking run. Is this the week the 49ers' run defense gets exposed?
Stout has a shoulder injury that sidelined him for the end of the 49ers' Week 6 win. He has not practiced this week, and with the bye week looming, he might not play. The team tried to use Ashtyn Davis in his place, but he struggled. So, they used Deommodore Lenoir in the slot with Jack Jones on the outside.
Still, Jones has also struggled. What is the 49ers' best option?
Drake London has 550 yards. Their next three pass catchers have 549 yards combined. In the Falcons' wins, he is averaging 145 yards per game. In the losses, he averages 65 yards per game. If they shut down London, they will win. Do they have the cornerback depth?

title: Mike Evans Among 6 Crucial 49ers Ruled Out for Week 7 vs. Falcons
full_text:
Six crucial players will not be available for the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7 when they take on the Atlanta Falcons.
The headlining player is Mike Evans. He's been expectedly ruled out after he aggravated his Achilles in the Week 6 win against the Washington Commanders.
Holding Evans out of this game is the right call. It's what the 49ers should've done in the last game to avoid this situation. Now they have to rely on Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and newly signed Brandin Cooks.
The 49ers ran Evans out against the Commanders as if their wide receiver depth wasn't already thin . They need to think long-term with Evans moving forward, since it's clear they weren't before.
That's why they're letting him rest and recover now with the Bye Week to follow after this game. They'll have their fingers crossed that two weeks off will make a significant impact.
Nick Bosa will miss his fifth consecutive game with a calf injury. It's a bit of a surprise after he recently indicated that he'll be ready to go against Atlanta.
Kyle Shanahan said that Bosa was overly optimistic. He revealed that Bosa still felt soreness in his calf after he made those comments, so he's still on the mend.
You have to wonder if Bosa will be any better in two weeks. He's been resting and ramping up his calf for weeks. Yet he hasn't made any significant strides.
Whenever he returns, he'll be a constant worry about reinjuring his calf or something else. Bosa's status should further push the 49ers to make a trade for an edge rusher .
They've been doing an excellent job getting to the quarterback in the last two games. The entire defensive front is playing collectively.
The 49ers haven't had that since 2021. As amazing as it is to see, they still need a big-time player to help lead the charge. It will take their defense to greater heights.
Bosa cannot be counted on, and if he does somehow remain healthy for the rest of the year when he returns, then it's even better for the 49ers. There's no such thing as too many pass rushers.
As for the other four players who are out: Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Marques Sigle (ankle), Garrett Wallow (hamstring), and Luke Gifford (groin).

title: The One Quality Kyle Shanahan Believes Has Fueled the 49ers' 6-0 Start
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have started 6-0 twice under their head coach Kyle Shanahan.
In 2019, the 49ers went on an inspired run to reach the Super Bowl . In 2026, it remains to be seen, but it's a stat that shows it's been an impressive start to the year.
Shanahan believes there's one quality behind their unbeaten start to the year, stating during an interview with Bay Area radio station KNBR : "I just like the grit of our team. I wouldn't say we're an offensive team, a defensive team, special teams. I wouldn't say we're dominant in this area and not in another.
"I just feel like, every week, we try to figure out what it takes to win, collectively as coaches, collectively as a team. Our guys really focus on that stuff, and they try to go get it done.
"And not always in these games does it go exactly how we're thinking it's going to go," Shanahan continued. "And I think we assess the situation, players and coaches, and we see the adjustments we've got to make, and our guys are willing to just really put it on the line every single week and do what it takes to get it done.
"I think our guys have a very good understanding of how this league works, and how fast it can change. Each week, it's a one-game season, and I think we look at it every week that way, and I think we've played that way."
"I think maybe a difference with our team [compared to] most other teams is I feel like our guys play every team like it's make-or-break to make the playoffs or not. There is no 'Hey, this is just Week 5' or 'Hey, we've got a good record.' There's none of that.
And he's right. However you look at it, the 49ers' 6–0 record has been built on grit. They've beaten three of the final four teams from last season and dug deep in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders, nearly surrendering a 20-point lead before holding on for the win.
San Francisco have faced different moments of adversity throughout their unbeaten start, but they've consistently found a way to get the job done.
Don't forget the biggest factor that has repeatedly plagued San Francisco in the past: injuries. As was the case last season, the sheer number of players sidelined hasn't derailed their campaign so far.
Instead, the 49ers have continued to find ways to win despite the setbacks. It's a testament to Shanahan and the entire organization that they've managed to look this strong while dealing with so many absences.

title: One 49ers Player Who Could Surprisingly Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are likely to be buyers at the trade deadline. However, one player on their roster that they could trade or use in a package to add a better player is cornerback Jack Jones.
Jones signed a one-year, $1.2M contract with the 49ers this offseason. With that in mind, his contract is very tradeable. He has not started or played well for the 49ers. However, he was a 16-game starter for the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 and a 17-game starter for the Miami Dolphins in 2025.
If a team is looking to add a cheap starter, the draft compensation to pry Jones away from the 49ers will not be too much. Jones has not been a fit, and the team might just want to move on.
The team has tried to play Jones in dime scenarios. When they need an extra defensive back, they will bring Jones on the field. Deommodore Lenoir will shift into the slot, joining Upton Stout. Then Jones and Renardo Green would play the outside.
Jones only played eight snaps in Week 1, but jumped to 10 snaps the following week. He allowed 88 yards. San Francisco had to play him 28 snaps the following week, and he allowed 53 yards. After allowing 18 yards on 15 snaps in Week 4, the 49ers have been trying to limit his snaps.
Jones played just three snaps against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5. Then, he played seven snaps against the Washington Commanders in Week 7. However, they called on him after they tried Ashtyn Davis.
They pulled Upton Stout and put Davis in the slot, keeping Lenoir on the outside. Davis struggled, so Jones got seven snaps on the final drive, when they needed extra defensive backs. Otherwise, the team is trying to phase him out of their defense.
San Francisco has fourth-round rookie Ephesians Prysock, who has not played this year. They could give him a shot on the outside when they want to push Lenoir into the slot. The 49ers also have Nate Hobbs on the IR, and he still has a chance to return this season.
More than that, the 49ers might need more help along the front seven than the secondary. Using Jones to help improve another piece of the roster is a smart move. Either way, we will not see Jones much.

title: 49ers DC Raheem Morris Sounds Off On Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr.
full_text:
One big advantage the San Francisco 49ers will have on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons is Raheem Morris .
He was Atlanta’s head coach for the last two seasons before being relieved of his duties. Morris will have amazing insight on how to game plan for the Falcons, especially quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
Morris was one of, if not the top advocate in the Falcons drafting Penix No. 8 overall in 2024. Naturally, Morris was asked about Penix and the process of drafting him over two years ago.
“Loved the kid, loved everything about him,” said Morris. “The personality, who he was, the thrower. We were in the business of looking for that guy that can take over for the franchise quarterback, had been through some quarterback purgatory and didn't want to go back in that realm.”
Penix missed the first two games of the season. The Falcons looked like they were going to be a dumpster fire all year based off of those two games. However, Penix returned and got the Falcons back on track.
In four games, he’s thrown for 944 yards, six touchdowns, one interception, and has a passer rating of 106.0. This is the best Penix has looked since he was drafted, which isn’t shocking for Morris to see because he’s healthy.
“When he has been healthy, he's had some explosive games, even as a rookie. I can still see him going into the D.C. game and find a way to get us into that game, make us some big-time plays in order for us to go to overtime,” he said.
“And as he started the season last year, had some ups and downs, had some probably more ups than downs, and now you've seen him have a couple really big ups since he's been back and been back in that lineup and changed that team completely. So, it's been pretty cool to watch.”
I’m sure Morris feels very proud of how Penix has looked. The player he believed in to push for the Falcons to draft him No. 8 overall doesn’t go away overnight.
“He's back healthy and he's probably everything that you thought and hoped for as far as being a play-action passer, a guy that can push the ball down the field, can make all the throws, go through the whole process. Just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for.”
But on Sunday, he’ll aim to make it a nightmare for Penix. Morris should know all of Penix’s strengths and weaknesses. That’ll aid him tremendously in curating the perfect defense to help lead the 49ers to victory.

title: NFL Insider Lays Out Perfect Trade for 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' biggest need is quietly a big run-stuffing interior defensive lineman. While a reunion with Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, the smarter move for the 49ers to make at the trade deadline would be to add his teammate, Grover Stewart.
Bill Barnwell of ESPN outlined the trade as one of the 11 best deadline offers. Barnwell believes that the 49ers can trade a sixth-round pick to acquire Stewart and a seventh-round pick.
Barnwell notes that because he is a specialty player with one role in mind and he is in the last year of his contract, the team could get him for such a cheap cost.
“Adding Stewart to the defensive line rotation would go a long way in helping San Francisco plug up those run game woes,” wrote Barnwell. “The 33-year-old is a useful player and in the final year of his deal, but his contract is also expensive; he's owed $8.2 million in cash over the remainder of the season.”
The 49ers currently have over $40M in cap space for this season. They have some contract decisions to make next year, but they can roll over the money from this year to make the cap look much cleaner. Adding Stewart and his expiring deal would not be a major issue.
Stewart is a former fourth-round pick from the 2017 NFL Draft. He is in his ninth season in the NFL, and he has started in at least 13 games in seven seasons of his career after he was a depth piece in the first two seasons.
Stewart has only 13.5 sacks, but he is such a good run defender that the pass rush stats do not matter. His run defense alone has made him $71M in his NFL career.
The Colts are 2-4, and they just fired their GM. Their season is not going anywhere. They could have a run defender on their team to try to stay competitive in games where they are overmatched. He will likely leave in free agency, considering the GM who kept him so long just got fired. So, they will gain nothing by having him this year or in the future.
Or, they can move up a few picks in the draft while clearing some cap space to roll over for next year. It is better than nothing from the Colts' perspective.

title: 49ers TE George Kittle's 2026 NFL Season is Flying Under the Radar
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle's 2026 NFL season is flying completely under the radar.
Firstly, let's rewind to January, when Kittle was carted off the field during the 49ers' Wild Card Round matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. He had suffered a devastating Achilles injury, bringing his season to a devastating end after already missing six regular-season games.
Yet, somehow, Kittle made it back for Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams in Australia. He defied expectations, returning to the field in just eight months despite a typical Achilles recovery taking nine to 12 months. He set out to be ready for the season opener, and that's exactly what he did.
And ESPN reported that in June 2026, Michigan State University published in the Physician and Sportsmedicine Journal said only 27.1% of NFL players return to pre-injury performance levels. That recovery rate is already remarkably low, and the odds are arguably even more daunting given Kittle's age and the stage of his career.
Now in Week 6, the newly turned 33-year-old has made an incredible start to the season, which is remarkable given the serious injury he suffered and spent the whole offseason rehabbing.
Yes, there was some rust in Week 1 , which was understandable, but through six games, Kittle is tied for the team lead in receiving touchdowns with five and has racked up 338 receiving yards - more than half of his total from last season.
All things considered, he's on pace to record the fifth 1,000-yard receiving season of his career for the City by the Bay. Don't forget this year is his tenth representing the franchise.
Kittle has also overtaken Vernon Davis to become the 49ers' all-time leader in touchdown receptions among tight ends. With 57 receiving touchdowns, he is closing in on third place on the franchise's all-time list, currently held by Gene Washington with 59. Terrell Owens ranks second with 81, while Jerry Rice leads the way with 176. Obviously, he won't ever beat Rice's tally, though.
Kittle defied the odds and came out the other side looking like his same explosive self. For whatever reason, he isn't getting the attention he deserves, but this is a storyline the 49ers should be shouting from the rooftops.
In my eyes, no other comeback story comes close to his, and if his performances continue at this pace, he'd have a compelling case for Comeback Player of the Year.

title: What the 49ers Can Realistically Afford at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
In most years, trade proposals are pipe dreams or fan desires. The San Francisco 49ers will likely be active at the trade deadline, but, in addition, similar to Keion White. However, this is a team that added Emmanuel Sanders at the trade deadline before, albeit at a reasonable price. Still, they have swung when the time is right. Looking at the 49ers' cap, draft picks, and roster outlook, it feels like this year is the best year for the team to go all-in.
It does not hurt that the team is off to a 6-0 start while the Seattle Seahawks are 3-3 and the Los Angeles Rams are 2-4. Aside from the Minnesota Vikings, every team in the NFC has at least two losses. The conference is not going to be more wide open entering November.
The team also has Trent Williams, who is 38 years old. George Kittle and Mike Evans are 33 years old. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Fred Warner is 39, and while Nick Bosa is 28, he has some of the biggest injury concerns of the group. They need to win a Super Bowl with this corps, and they are running out of seasons.
The addition of Evans showed they are going for it and not worrying about the future. Now they can make a splash to solidify it.
More than that, the team is well equipped to make a run. They currently have the most salary cap space in the NFL. With $43M in cap space , the team can take on a big salary this year, and they will still have money to roll over for next year.
So, they can rid any team of their bad contract players without much issue. More than that, they have all of their noteworthy draft picks for the foreseeable future. Their first- through third-round picks for the next three seasons are all accounted for.
There are not many teams across past seasons that sit with such a lead in the division with the cap space and pick situation that they have. When adding in the win-now nature of their roster, there are few teams that historically are more primed to make a blockbuster trade deadline move than the 49ers.
While the team could put a few band-aids on the roster with smart and savvy moves, they could also be the team that goes all-in this year.

title: Todd Bowles Makes His Decision Between Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play the Carolina Panthers on Sunday in what could be the most important game of the year. The Bucs are 1-5 as it stands — a victory over the NFC South leaders would gain ground in the division and keep playoff hopes alive, while a loss could be the beginning of the end for Tampa Bay.
In a game like this, the Bucs will naturally want as many of their best players on the field. Perhaps the most important of those players, quarterback Baker Mayfield, has been off the field since Week 3 while he's been recovering from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings.
In Mayfield's stead, undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels has been starting for the Bucs at quarterback. Daniels has played admirably, even winning Tampa Bay's only game in Week 5 against the Dallas Cowboys, and when the week began, head coach Todd Bowles said that they'd begin preparing as if Daniels were set to play in his fourth start as Mayfield worked his way back.
Signs pointed toward Mayfield being ready to go this week, though, and now, Bowles has given us the confirmation we've been waiting for.
Bowles confirmed that Mayfield is ready to go and will start against the Panthers on Sunday, officially marking his return to the field for the first time since Week 3.
Todd Bowles says that Baker Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go”, so he’ll start Sunday. Luke Goedeke is OUT — Emeka Egbuka needs to clear concussion protocol to play so Bowles said the team will see, but he’s currently still in protocol. pic.twitter.com/Znw8PO8QIr
Mayfield threw for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions during his opening three-game stint. He also fumbled the ball three times, losing all of them to the defense.
Now, he's set to come back with some precautions, given the injury to his thumb. He's set to play with a glove that features a plate restricting movement in his injured thumb, which the Bucs' training staff developed with the Tampa Bay Rays. Mayfield told the media Thursday that the plate would not restrict his throwing motion, however.
Mayfield also mentioned that the biggest obstacle was taking impacts to his hand from snaps from center Graham Barton. He feels good about his ability to take those snaps on Sunday.
I think I was more so concerned about the impact of getting the ball from under center with Graham [Barton] sending it back there," Mayfield said. "It feels fine gripping it, throwing it — it's just the impact stuff, that was really what my concern was, and it's felt great so far.”
The Buccaneers play the Panthers — one of Mayfield's former teams — at 1 p.m. on Oct. 25.

title: Could 2 Crucial Buccaneers Starters Miss Week 7 Game vs. Panthers?
full_text:
Every game is a must-win in the NFL, but for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , this Week 7 game really earns the term. The Bucs are playing the NFC South leaders, the Carolina Panthers, in their first NFC South game of the year — a win keeps their meager playoff hopes alive, and a loss could bury them entirely.
Naturally, the team will want everyone healthy to try and pick up the crucial victory, but that's never all that simple in the NFL. Quarterback Baker Mayfield is likely to return for Tampa Bay under center for the first time since Week 3, but he may not have as many offensive players to work with as he'd like.
Based on Thursday's practice, the Buccaneers could go without two important members of their offense.
A few players, like running back Bucky Irving and cornerback Zyon McCollum, were back at practice on Thursday after being absent on Wednesday. But two key Buccaneers did not practice, and that could put them in danger of not playing on Sunday.
Left tackle Luke Goedeke was listed as a non-participant with a calf injury on Wednesday, and he also did not participate on Thursday. Additionally, wideout Emeka Egbuka, listed with a concussion and a foot injury, was working off to the side with a trainer and thus was also not practicing.
With two days off of practice, both players are in danger of missing Tampa Bay's game against Carolina on Sunday.
Goedeke has been a bright spot on Tampa Bay's offensive line along with left tackle Tristan Wirfs. If he cannot go because of his calf injury, one of the team's swing tackles — likely Ben Chukwuma — would step in for him at right tackle.
Egbuka has been healthy this whole year so far, but he'll have to clear concussion protocol to play against the Panthers — and that's assuming that his foot is healthy. If he cannot go, wideouts like Tez Johnson and potentially David Sills, should the latter come off of IR, could help bolster the receiving corps. Rookie wideout Ted Hurst has already been involved in the offense in the absence of receiver Jalen McMillan, who re-injured his knee in Week 3.
The Buccaneers would love to see one or both of Egbuka and Goedeke be able to make it for Sunday. But in the very real possibility that they aren't able to, Tampa Bay's depth will have to step up when the team heads to Charlotte on Oct. 25.

title: Could the Buccaneers Actually Trade Away Vita Vea?
full_text:
As each week passes, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' chances of making the postseason drift further and further away.
That's what happens when you consistently lose football games.
Another thing that happens when you consistently lose football games, as the Bucs have done this year, is that you gradually begin to focus on the future more than the present. If the Buccaneers can't knock off the Carolina Panthers this Sunday in what will be their first divisional matchup of the season, then prioritizing future seasons over this one becomes a necessity rather than just a consideration.
Should Jason Licht and the Buccaneers truly commit to focusing on the future, then they would be well positioned to do so simply because they have plenty of high-quality, established NFL talent at a number of different positions.
That being said, it's not like every player on the roster would all of a sudden become available for a trade. If the Bucs do head down that path, which players might the Bucs be willing to part with in order to improve their roster for the future?
ESPN recently published an article by a collection of NFL insiders exploring the latest intel and buzz traveling around the NFL, and according to Dan Graziano, one player we could see the Bucs look to move on from is veteran defensive tackle Vita Vea.
"The Buccaneers are 1-5. Vea is 31 years old, and he and the team begrudgingly came to a compromise agreement on his contract during training camp," Graziano wrote. "The Bucs didn't act as if he was part of their long-term future, and if teams come looking for a big, run-stuffing defensive tackle, Tampa would be silly not to listen."
Graziano also dug into why a trade for Vea would make sense for plenty of teams in the market for an upgrade along the interior of their defensive line.
"He is on a minimum salary this year and is guaranteed $23 million for 2027, which would rank about 15th in terms of cap numbers for defensive tackles in the league," he wrote. "If you need interior D-line help right now and don't mind paying Vea $23 million next season at age 32, why not call to see what it would take to get him out of Tampa?"
Based on his contract, consistent production and championship experience, the concept of adding a player like Vea would certainly appeal to a variety of teams. The same could be said for Antoine Winfield Jr., Chris Godwin Jr. and other veterans on the roster who still have plenty of gas left in the tank.
What's more of an unknown is, will the Bucs actually commit to that approach?
Whether or not Licht and his staff are seriously considering moving on from homegrown stars to acquire valuable draft capital for the future remains to be seen, but they will need to make that decision soon.
And if the Bucs do lose to the Panthers this week and fall to 1-6? That decision should become that much easier to make.

title: Buccaneers' Chris Godwin Says His Offensive Role Has Been 'Interesting'
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have found it tough sledding on offense to begin the season.
Whether it's questionable play calling, injuries, or lack of production, it just hasn't come together for a team that was thought to have all the pieces to be one of the NFL's top units to begin the season.
One of those players who has kind of disappeared is veteran wide receiver Chris Godwin. Heading into their matchup against the Carolina Panthers, Godwin spoke about his limited role in the offense and why it's been such a slow start.
“It’s definitely been interesting, different than anything I’ve been through in my career … I’m trying to stick to the process and make sure I’m where I need to be," Godwin said of his role within the offense, per FOX Sports' Greg Auman.
It's been the longest stretch of his career under 50 yards (seven straight games), and when asked why he's had such a slow start to the season, Godwin couldn't quite find an answer.
“That’s a great question. I wish I had an answer. It’s a multitude of things … it’s definitely frustrating at times.”
Godwin has seen his targets tick upward with Jalon Daniels under center and has continued to be great at gaining separation from cornerbacks, but the results have not followed no matter who has been at quarterback.
This season, Godwin has compiled just 23 receptions for 216 yards and no touchdowns. That puts him on pace to finish the season with 65 receptions for 612 yards and no touchdowns — a far cry from what we have seen from the former Pro Bowl wideout.
How can the Bucs find a way to get the ball to Godwin? That comes down to offensive coordinator Zac Robinson putting him in spots that the quarterbacks can easily locate and let him work.
Godwin isn't someone who will stretch the field or beat you with blazing speed, but his football IQ and ability to shed tackles should be something this offense leans on rather than away from.
The hope is that with Baker Mayfield returning as the starter, things will start to open up and flow more as Mayfield looks more Godwin's way, but that isn't a given.
Like Godwin, we can't quite pinpoint why things have been the way they are for him. We can narrow it down, but it's ultimately a combination of factors that have led to Godwin's down year.
There is still plenty of season left to play, so hopefully the offense starts to find its gear. And if that is the case, Godwin should figure to play a large part in that.

title: Buccaneers Hit With Multiple Surprise Injuries
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have shown some fight over the past couple of weeks, but ultimately are still struggling as they sit 1-5 on the season.
Despite their struggles, the Bucs can still make up for it, considering they haven't reached division play. That starts this week when they head to Carolina to take on the Panthers.
It will undoubtedly be an uphill battle for them, and things might be a bit tougher than usual as they had numerous players show up on the injury report midweek.
Per the Bucs' official injury report , the Bucs saw multiple key players miss Wednesday's practice, including wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), Bucky Irving (illness), Zyon McCollum (illness), Luke Goedeke (calf) and Christian Rozeboom (finger).
The Bucs are dealing with injuries, but it also appears that some kind of sickness has made its rounds through the locker room. Outside of Irving and McCollum, Riley Dixon Calijah Kancey, and Chase McLaughlin all had illness designations but participated in some sort of fashion.
The hope is that the illness is able to subside as the week progresses towards game time, but the more serious concern is undoubtedly that of Egbuka and Goedeke's respective injuries.
The Tampa Bay offense has already been suspect to begin the season, and losing one of your top wideouts and starting right tackle would be detrimental to them trying to keep pace with the Panthers' offense, which has shown that they can put up points.
On a positive note, however, Baker Mayfield appears ready to return from his dislocated thumb, and the likes of Sean Tucker and Benjamin Morrison have returned from their injuries that kept them out against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Antoine Winfield Jr. also logged a limited practice as he recovers from his rib injury.
It would be hard-pressed to say that Winfield Jr. would make his return even if he logs limited practices the rest of the week. However, I would fully expect to see Tucker and Morrison back in the fold for their respective sides of the ball.
The real question will come down to whether or not the Bucs and Mayfield are on the same page on him returning after logging his first full practice back. If Mayfield is able to continue logging full practices through the rest of the week, one would imagine he would be behind center come Sunday. If not, or if the medical staff doesn't give the full clearance, then we could see Jalon Daniels make his fourth consecutive start.

title: How Baker Mayfield Looked Throwing at Buccaneers Practice Today
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have played backup quarterback Jalon Daniels for the last three weeks. They've been without incumbent starter Baker Mayfield since he dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3, but they likely won't be without him for much longer.
Mayfield returned to practice on Wednesday, marking his first one since Sept. 25. He arrived after the team stretched and started doing drills with the other quarterbacks — but how did he look in his first practice back?
BucsGameday was live at One Buccaneer Place to watch practice. Here's what we saw during our limited window:
Mayfield participated in practice with a white glove on his throwing hand. He did handoff drills first, opting to hand off with his left hand as opposed to his injured right hand, but he quickly started throwing during the latter half of the practice window.
There did not seem to be anything noticeably off about the way Mayfield threw the football. He was working with wideouts and tight ends like Chris Godwin and Bauer Sharp during this throwing period, and he didn't appear to struggle with accuracy or velocity during the practice window.
Baker Mayfield is back at practice today for the Bucs! He was wearing a white glove on his injured hand, but he was practicing and throwing today. #Buccaneers #GoBucs pic.twitter.com/bxSZuAt9SO
Mayfield also participated in ball security drills while holding the ball during practice. Mayfield has already struggled with that so far this season, fumbling the football three times in Week 1, but his injured hand could make it even more difficult to hold the football if he does end up playing on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.
It's unclear if Mayfield will go on Sunday, but if he can, the Bucs will really want him to. Tampa Bay is playing the Panthers, who lead the division at the moment with a 3-2 record. Tampa Bay is 2.5 games back from Carolina — a win keeps the Bucs alive in the division and a playoff berth, while a loss would put them 3.5 games out from Carolina and see them fading fast.
The Bucs have not determined who is starting yet against the Panthers. That should become clearer on Thursday, when either Mayfield or Daniels will speak to the media ahead of Sunday's NFC South matchup.

title: Buccaneers' Wednesday Practice Brings Huge Update for Baker Mayfield
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took a loss last Sunday to the Pittsburgh Steelers, which put the team at 1-5. That loss happened without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, but it looks like the Bucs won't be without Mayfield for long.
The Buccaneers held practice on Wednesday as they prepare to face the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, and Mayfield officially returned to practice. It's his first appearance at Bucs practice since Week 3, but that doesn't necessarily mean he'll play football on Sunday.
Mayfield returned to practice on Wednesday. His participation was likely limited, but he was seen out on the practice field as he continues to figure out how well he can grip the football after dislocating his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. He was wearing a white glove on his throwing hand.
Baker Mayfield is back at practice today for the Bucs! He was wearing a white glove on his injured hand, but he was practicing and throwing today. #Buccaneers #GoBucs pic.twitter.com/bxSZuAt9SO
Quarterback Jalon Daniels has subbed in for Mayfield while Mayfield has been out. Daniels, a rookie UDFA out of Kansas, has played admirably while deputizing Mayfield, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions (one of which was a hail-mary pick at the end of that Vikings game).
That being said, the Bucs signed Mayfield to a three-year extension worth around $55 million this offseason, so he's the quarterback the Bucs expect to lead them into the future. Before getting hurt in Week 3, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions.
Daniels started against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and head coach Todd Bowles told the media on Monday that the team would initially prepare as if Daniels were starting. This is a very likely game for Mayfield to come back for, however, and it will be arguably the team's most important game of the year against an NFC South leader they're currently 2.5 games back on. With that in mind, the Bucs will have to make a decision between a healthy Daniels and a recovering Mayfield.
Mayfield rarely misses football games. The last NFL game he missed to injury before he got hurt against the Vikings was in 2022, when he missed two games with a high-ankle sprain while playing for the Carolina Panthers. If he can get healthy quickly, he may not miss much more time in Tampa Bay.
The Bucs will face the Panthers at 1 p.m. on Oct. 25 in Charlotte in hopes of moving to 2-5 and keeping their already-struggling season alive.

title: Why a Buccaneers Loss Against the Panthers Would End Their Playoff Hopes
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers haven't played very good football this season. They've started 1-5, and although the defense is slowly getting better, the offense hasn't caught up. The Bucs haven't won a game at home and currently hold the worst record in the NFC.
Because of all that, the team has arguably the most important game on its schedule already. The Bucs are set to play the division rival Carolina Panthers, and while all NFC South games are important, this game could be the game that sets Tampa Bay back on the path to contention — or so far down the depths that they cannot climb back up.
Here's why a Tampa Bay loss to Carolina could end their season just eight weeks into the year:
The math isn't in favor for Tampa Bay with a loss against Carolina in multiple respects.
The first? Their record would be 1-6 were they to fall to the Carolina Panthers, and history would bury them. No NFL team has ever made the playoffs after a 1-6 start, with only four teams at 1-5 ever moving on to the postseason. The Buccaneers could be the first, of course, but the chance that they make the playoffs would become nigh impossible.
The NFC South is an easy division, though, so Tampa Bay does have that on its side — unless it loses. The Bucs are playing the Panthers on Sunday, and the Panthers lead the NFC South with a 3-2 record. The Bucs are 2.5 games out of first place, but naturally, a Panthers win puts them 3.5 games out of first place. That wouldn't be absolutely impossible to overcome, but it put Carolina at a massive advantage heading into the rest of the year.
No season is truly over just seven games in. But Tampa Bay has struggled tremendously ever since the season began, and there hasn't been much hope outside of the Dallas Cowboys game the Bucs won that they'll get anything going anytime soon.
The Bucs play the Panthers at 1 p.m. in Charlotte, North Carolina on Oct. 25. A win keeps them in the fight — a loss may see the season slip away for good.

title: Could Baker Mayfield Miss Another Buccaneers Game?
full_text:
The NFL season is a roller coaster.
The Bucs had high expectations coming into the 2026 season. Those expectations quickly went by the wayside when starting quarterback Baker Mayfield — fresh off signing a massive new contract just before the season began — looked as bad as we've ever seen him in Tampa. His turnovers, poor timing and inaccuracy downfield played a big role in the team's disastrous 0-4 start.
Mayfield dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand on the final play of the team's Week 4 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and things appeared to be going from bad to worse.
That was until undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels surprised everyone by taking two quality teams to the wire in two consecutive weeks, highlighted by a standout performance in the Bucs' first win of the season against the Cowboys in Dallas on Thursday Night Football.
But just when some optimism began to creep back into the minds of the Buccaneers' faithful following that elusive victory, Daniels came back down to earth in a big way vs. the Steelers this past Sunday.
Despite a solid first half, he completely fell apart in the second half, going 8-for-20 passing while also throwing two interceptions. That ultimately allowed the Steelers to erase a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to win the game.
So now, as the roller coaster that has been the Buccaneers' season takes yet another turn, it seems as though at this point, most people would prefer to see Mayfield back under center as soon as possible.
But when will that happen?
This weekend, the Buccaneers will face off against the Carolina Panthers, their first NFC South matchup of the year. The fact that the Bucs have six divisional games remaining means that, as unlikely as it may seem, there is still technically a chance that Tampa Bay could turn its season around.
On Monday, Todd Bowles was asked about what he needs to see from Mayfield, who continues to work his way back from his thumb injury, before he declares him ready to resume his role as the Bucs' starting quarterback.
"He's supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said. "We're going to take a good look at him there and then we'll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does."
Bowles was then asked if the team will be preparing as if Daniels will start.
"I think you have to," Bowles said. "Both will be in the meetings…Obviously, both will be in the meetings. We'll see how the week goes before we decide who it is."
Bowles was extremely vague about Mayfield's status heading into this game, so unfortunately, we don't have any clear information to work from. That being said, it wouldn't be advantageous to his football team in any way to disclose whether or not Mayfield will be available so early in the week.
Based on Bowles' comments this week, it does seem as though there is a legitimate chance that Mayfield will not be ready in time for this game against the Panthers, but no one outside of the building really knows. And if Mayfield does end up playing, then it's probably a good thing that his opponent isn't sure yet, either.

title: Buccaneers NFC South Update: How Far Back is Tampa Bay After Week 6?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to 1-5 on Sunday after a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, and with just six games played, they're already right on the edge of a lost season.
Only four teams have ever made the playoffs on a 1-5 start in NFL history. Tampa Bay started the season 0-4, and only one team in NFL history has ever made the playoffs off that — their win against the Dallas Cowboys helped a bit, but another loss could plunge them too far down to make it up.
The Bucs face a weak division in the NFC South, though, which could be keeping their playoff hopes alive. What does the competition look like in the division? Are the Bucs close enough to claw their way back to the top, even at 1-5?
Here's what the NFC South looks like six weeks in:
As it stands, the Buccaneers are the worst team in the NFC — the Washington Commanders also have one win, but they have a tie as well, putting them ahead of Tampa Bay. The Bucs drop to 1-5 on the year after losing to the Steelers and, unbelievably, are one of three NFC South teams that have not won at home. The Bucs are still just two and a half games back from the Panthers, so they have time to string some wins together.
The Carolina Panthers remain at the head of the division after a win over the Philadelphia Eagles. The Panthers are the only team in the NFC South with a winning record, and they've played one less game than everyone else in the division because they've already had their bye week. They're the only NFC South team with a positive point differential and the only NFC South team that has won a game at home this season.
The Falcons were at one point 2-2 on a two-game win streak, but they've since developed a two-game losing streak and just fell to the Chicago Bears. The Falcons remain second in the division because they have an NFC South win over the New Orleans Saints already this year.
The Saints are third in the division behind Tampa Bay. They got a win on Sunday, defeating the New York Giants, so they're back in the win column and moved up in the standings after falling below Tampa Bay last week. The Falcons and Saints have the same record, but New Orleans falls behind because they've lost to the Falcons this year in a divisional matchup.
The Bucs and Panthers play each other next Sunday for Tampa Bay's first divisional matchup. The Falcons play the red-hot San Francisco 49ers, while the Saints will play the Steelers in Paris.

title: Titans Red Zone Report: 1 Main Reason Drives Failed And How to Fix Them in Week 7
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans pulled off a win in Week 6, but that triumph had little to nothing to do with the offensive side of the ball.
Tennessee piled on 26 points, but a closer look at that number doesn't do the offense any favors. A blocked kick touchdown and four field goals complicate the kudos set to be handed out after a win. Once again, QB Cam Ward struggled to make his mark on a contest.
Ward completed only 11 passes in Indianapolis vs. the Colts, notching one touchdown and one interception on his way to an underwhelming outing from every angle. In this week's red zone report, we're taking a look at one of the main reasons Tennessee's drives continued to stall in Week 6.
In addition, I'll try and pose a solution as the Titans prepare to try and win two games in a row. The 4-2 Cleveland Browns are on deck tomorrow in a Week 7 homestand.
Not every issue with the offense can be pinned to Ward. For a look at the share of blame in that unit, check out our analysis of the group's struggles as they extend from Ward and OC Brian Daboll.
However, facing off with the Colts, Ward's passing chart reveals a major problem. Not only did the QB fail to complete a pass of 20 yards or more, but he refused to look over the middle to any impactful degree. Take a look, per Paul Kuharsky.
Cam Ward at Indianapolis. #Titans . pic.twitter.com/vhkCBeYvTy
Sure, Ward still found Carnell Tate in the end zone for a touchdown, and he led enough semi-successful drives in the second half to help eek the Titans to a win. But if the defense doesn't have three takeaways and six sacks, Tennessee doesn't win that game.
The Tiatns need Ward to take more risks. They need him to find guys over the middle and search for chunk plays.
Clearly, playing it safe vs. Indy didn't go far for Ward's numbers. 11/22 for only 102 yards hints at a QB just trying to survive in the pocket. Ward was less than a game manager in Week 6; he was throwing checkdowns and trying to avoid crucial mistakes.
I'd argue that Tennessee would embrace a few more mistakes if it meant Ward threw for more than 200 yards in a game again, which he's done only once through six weeks. The Titans need involvement out of more WRs than Carnell Tate alone. We need to see looks to TE Gunnar Helm, more work for Tyjae Spears in the passing game, and again, far more tries downfield.
Simply put, opposing defenses are no longer scared of Ward's big-play ability. Let's circle back to the aforementioned 20+ yard pass stat. Ward threw 40 of those balls in his rookie season. That was more than Bryce Young, Jaxson Dart, Aaron Rodgers, and Daniel Jones, per FantasyPros.
This season so far, Ward has only 10. That's less than any healthy starter in the league, save for Jacoby Brissett with the Arizona Cardinals. One statistic says it all, although Ward making the less surefire decision now and again may be the basic key to fixing this issue before it's too late.
Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. A longtime sports fanatic and recent baby blue jersey aficionado.

title: Major Storylines to Watch in Titans' Week 7 Matchup vs. Browns: A Huge Test Awaits 1 Position Group
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans host the Cleveland Browns on Sunday in an AFC battle between two teams who entered the season with minimal expectations.
Unfortunately, the Titans have performed as many expected. However, the Browns have genuinely been one of the biggest surprises in football. Cleveland enters the weekend sitting atop arguably the toughest division in football with a 4-2 record. Meanwhile, the Titans are coming off their first win of the season and hope to build on it.
One team is trying to prove they’re not a fluke, while the other is desperately trying to find relevancy once again.
Something’s gotta give in this one, so let’s take a look at three of the biggest storylines heading into the Titans’ Week 7 matchup with the Browns.
You don’t need to tell Titans fans how bad things have been lately. But every now and then, you see something that really puts it into perspective. The Titans haven't won consecutive games since beating the Broncos and Packers in November 2022.
Since then, they‘ve gone 13-51, and are 7-33 since firing Mike Vrabel. In total, that is a 64-game stretch where they’ve failed to win consecutive games — One shy of the 65-game record set by the Browns back in 2014-2018, per Chad Withrow.
Ironically, those two teams will now meet in a game that can send the Titans into the type of record books they don’t want to be a part of.
At this point, there’s no denying that this is one of, if not, the roughest stretch this franchise has experienced since moving to Tennessee. They’ve certainly had bad years, but nothing like the run we’ve seen from late 2022 till now. Tennessee desperately needs to get this win on Sunday solely for the fans who have stuck with them through this brutal stretch over the last few years.
Realistically, a few wins probably isn’t going to lead to a late-season playoff push, but they can be the type of culture-setting wins that HC Robert Saleh needs to get his program where he wants it.
Rookie WR Carnell Tate has been one of the genuine bright spots this season. Going into the draft, there was so much skepticism surrounding his potential to be a true number one, and he’s quickly putting all that to bed with each passing week.
Tate’s 344 receiving yards over his first six games are the most by a rookie receiver in Titans history (since 1999).
Most receiving yards over first 6 career games in Titans team history Carnell Tate            344 Kenny Britt              289 Kendall Wright       285 A.J. Brown               273 Treylon Burks         264 pic.twitter.com/Kz74hQVDp7
That alone would be a remarkable accomplishment. But when you throw in the fact that his quarterback play has been inconsistent at best, along with the fact that he’s the only real threat defenses have to worry about, it makes it that much more impressive.
To put this offense’s struggles into perspective, the Titans’ rookie receiver is coming off a game where he had 70 of the team’s 102 passing yards (68%). That type of production (or lack thereof) isn’t sustainable, so they’ll need more efficient play out of QB Cam Ward going forward in order for Tate to reach his full potential.
But make no mistake about it, at the age of 21, Tate is already the focal point of this entire offense. They go as he goes, and if the Titans are wise, they’ll continue to feed him like the budding star he’s rapidly becoming.
The Browns enter the game with one of the most ferocious pass rushes in the NFL. Cleveland is currently tied for second in sacks with 19 on the year. The lethal DT tandem of Mason Graham and Maliek Collins lead the way with 7.5 sacks between the two of them.
Tennessee’s interior trio of LG Peter Skoronski, C Austin Schlottmann, and RG Atonio Mafi will have their hands full, but one thing I’ve learned about this gritty group is to never count them out.
OL coach Carmen Bricillo has done a fantastic job of getting this group ready to play each Sunday (excluding the Texans game). You could argue no coach has gotten more out of less than he has. This offensive line undoubtedly needs more talent still, but through six games, they’ve proven they can hold their own more often than not.
Another massive test awaits them on Sunday, and how they perform will directly impact this team’s chances. If they’re able to hold up, then this team should have a realistic shot to pull off the upset.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Calvin Ridley is Questionable for Titans in Week 7: How Likely is a Trade?
full_text:
The first sign that something is happening behind the scenes ahead of the trade deadline: Things don't quite add up. Ahead of the Tennessee Titans' Week 7 matchup with the Cleveland Browns, Calvin Ridley's status has pushed him into that category.
Ridley was listed as a non-participant in the Titans' Thursday practice due to a hip injury. Today, not only did Ridley miss practice again, but he's been tagged with a questionable designation for Sunday's game.
Last week vs. the Indianapolis Colts, Ridley caught zero passes on two targets. He's been slowly phasing out of the Titans' offense all season. The veteran simply doesn't fit the evolving vision of this franchise... but he may fit the vision of another.
FOX Sports listed Ridley as the Titans' top trade candidate earlier this week. Our own Shaun Calderon forecasted him to the Los Vegas Rams for a sixth round pick. Seeing his game status be thrown into doubt after six straight weeks of play certainly fuels the fire a little.
While Ridley may not be a fit in Tennessee any longer, a team like the Rams - who have been without Puka Nacua and just lost Davante Adams for an extended period in their WR room - could definitely spare a late-draft pick to bulk up their pass-catching core in the present.
Staying out west, the Los Angeles Chargers are also in dire need of playmakers for QB Justin Herbert. A benefit of the Titans' current lowly position is that other franchises are likely to buy the aging pieces they're selling.
If Ridley really is on the market, it would be no surprise to see Tennessee move him within the next few weeks. It wouldn't even be surprising if they moved him now, making his questionable tag all the more interesting.
Between Ridley and Tony Pollard, it would almost be shocking at this point if the Titans didn't make a move. Ridley's contract restructuring in the offseason suggested at the time that he may ride out the final two years of his contract, but his role simply hasn't looked the same this year.
Just yesterday, Brian Daboll expressed his confidence in Calvin Ridley, and noted that the team have been working on upping his involvement in practice.
A sign of safety for Ridley, or one final smokescreen before the team trades him? We won't have to wait long to find out.

title: The Titans' X Factor vs. Browns is Also Their Most Likely Trade Candidate
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching on November 10, multiple teams' relationships with their players are beginning to take on new layers. The Tennessee Titans, in their need-to-change 1-5 state, are no exception.
We've already outlined three guys that the Titans could part ways with over the next few weeks. As the deadline gets closer, however, Week 7 offers a particularly interesting crossroads for Tennessee. The Cleveland Browns are headed to Nashville on Sunday, and with them comes a compelling bit of recent history.
Last December, when the Titans and Browns clashed in the snow, RB Tony Pollard had a career game in what became a Tennessee win. He rushed for a career-high 161 yards (including a career-high 65-yard rushing score in the first quarter), and two touchdowns.
The veteran, who even then appeared past his prime, dominated the Browns' front line. Cleveland looks different this year - with a new DC and having swapped Myles Garrett for Jared Verse - but they're still allowing 112 rushing yards per contest, per TeamRankings.
Even without the snow (barring a different kind of historical event), Pollard is tracking to take a bulk of Tennessee's backfield touches against the same team. He's also in an offense that has struggled mightily through the air. Not only could he be the Titans' X factor, but Pollard could also make the perfect case for himself on the trade market.
Pollard has gradually moved away from the split snaps he shared with backup RB Tyjae Spears to begin this year. Spears played just 11 snaps to Pollard's 35 last week vs. the Colts. Spears had just one rushing attempt. For the time being, Pollard has full control over the ground game.
You can expect Tennessee to once again hit the ground game heavily against a Browns defense that appears slightly weaker there than downfield. Pollard may not repeat his outrageous showing from last year, but he'll still have the opportunity to define an otherwise struggled Titans offense.
If Pollard shows out and has a great game, his stock may hit exactly the sort of pick that would encourage the Titans to trade him. Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame just listed Pollard in his top 10 players that could be moved by the deadline.
The chips are falling into the right places. Pollard is in the last year of his contract. The Titans drafted backfield depth earlier this year. The Titans are in "sell mode" as the rebuild continues under Robert Saleh.
Pollard going off vs. the Browns for the second straight time would serve as the ultimate sendoff for one of Tennessee's most impactful veterans. A trade makes more sense every week, and Week 7 may very well be the watershed moment.

title: Best — and Worst — Case Scenario for Titans' Week 7 Matchup With Browns
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans are preparing to face off against the 4-2, surprise-story Cleveland Browns this Sunday in Nashville. Both Cleveland and Tennessee are coming off a victory, although it meant a whole lot more to the latter.
Beating the Indianapolis Colts for their first win of the 2026 season gave the Titans some much-needed life. Robert Saleh is still 1-5, but his group has a little more to play for now. We're only six games into the year, after all.
I've already penciled a prediction for this contest, but in the spirit of playing both sides, I'm outlining both best and worst-case scenarios for Tennessee in Week 7. We'll start with the (potentially) good news.
Given the current state of the Titans' offense, it was the defense that won them their first game of the season last Sunday. If Tennessee topples Cleveland, it will likely once again come down to the defense causing problems.
The Titans picked Daniel Jones off twice in Week 6, forcing a fumble and logging six sacks in the process. The Browns' offensive line has allowed a league-high 24 sacks this year already; expect Saleh to send his guys to the house on more than a few occasions in Week 7.
It helps that, after starting the season off hot offensively, the Browns have quieted down in the past two weeks. Cleveland scored 12 points in a road loss to the New York Jets, before beating the Baltimore Ravens on a game-winning field goal that brought them to 13 points.
In the best-case scenario, Saleh's defense continues to build momentum, and Tennessee buries Cleveland by way of great defense and just enough offense.
Oppositely, the Browns' defense has also been keeping them in contests, if not outright winning them. Cleveland has allowed 20 points in just one game this season.
FOX Sports has the Browns' overall defense rated at 13th in the league, and their passing defense all the way up at eighth. The Titans' defense just got hot, but Cleveland's ball-stopping unit has been hot pretty much all year long.
In the worst of cases, it stays that way. We'd see Cam Ward struggle to make plays against the likes of CB Denzel Ward in the secondary, while DT Mason Graham creates pressure on Cleveland's d-line. Ward already has a pick and two forced fumbles this season, and Graham has four sacks.
Defense will likely tell the story either way, and Cleveland's offense is more likely to break free than Tennessee's. However, what the Titans did to the Colts last week would be good enough to disrupt just about any opponent.
We'll see which way the pendulum swings. Titans fans have a right to be a little more excited than usual, with Saleh's team returning home off their first win. Tennessee will try to win their second straight game for the first time in nearly four years against Cleveland.

title: How Tyjae Spears' Frustrating Lack of Growth Could Force Titans to Hit Reset Button in Backfield
full_text:
Even coming into the 2026 season, it was clear that the Tennessee Titans' backfield wasn't quite up to date with the rest of the franchise's rebuild. 29-year old Tony Pollard, entering the final year of his contract, was trotted out as the team's RB1 from the jump.
The springier, more long-term Tyjae Spears was meant to split snaps with Pollard from the beginning. It's long been expected that Spears would replace Pollard if the latter were to be traded or cut. However, even now that he's fully healthy, Spears' production calls that plan into question.
In last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts, Spears logged just 11 snaps (24.4%) to Pollard's 34 (75.6%). This is a far cry from the even split that the two backs shared all the way back in Week 1, and things have been trending this way for weeks now.
Spears has missed a few practices with an ankle issue, but that hasn't kept him off the field. More and more with every passing game, it seems, Spears' own struggles are limiting his opportunities. Spears had one rush for one yard in Week 6, and one reception for seven yards.
When the Titans are forced to make a change with Pollard in the backfield, their succession plan may no longer be as obvious as it initially seemed.
Tennessee isn't without options here. Rookie RB Nick Singleton, who was drafted in the fifth round earlier this year, could click into Spears' role if he were to take Pollard's spot. That may ease the former's transition into a leading role.
Although, not only has Spears been underwhelming this year, but so has Singleton. The first-year playmaker has only proven his need for far more time to develop in the limited chances he's had. Singleton has 12 total yards on seven carries across two appearances.
The young talent is there in basically every other unit for Tennessee. Carnell Tate is heading up an overhaul of the WR room. Anthony Hill Jr. looks like the best LB on this team in his first season. JC Latham and the currently injured rookie Fernando Carmona have been excellent on the offensive line.
Pollard has done a servicable job as the Titans' RB1 this year. But an extension seems almost out of the question for the veteran, and he's even been mentioned as a potential trade candidate. When Pollard inevitably goes, it may take more than a simple substitution to replace him.
Spears should at least have the rest of this year to prove his capability in that role. If he continues to struggle, however (18 carries for 66 yards, with a 3.7/rush average through six games), Tennessee could be in for a big-red-button reset on the ground.

title: Examining the Complex Blame Share for Titans' Offense Between Cam Ward and Brian Daboll
full_text:
On Thursday ahead of the Tennessee Titans' Week 7 matchup with the Cleveland Browns, OC Brian Daboll gave a sort of status update on the offense. Regarding Cam Ward specifically, Daboll said he likes the direction that the second-year QB is headed, but the results aren't satisfying.
Through six games, Ward has four touchdowns to four interceptions. He's thrown 998 yards in total and has a 39.5 QBR, which is good for 29th in the league. In the Titans' first win last week, Ward barely broke 100 yards (he had 102), throwing one touchdown and one interception on 11 completions.
Not only is Ward not there yet, but he's behind the needle of expected growth. He looks worse in almost every facet compared to his rookie campaign. Some of his issues are simply bad decision-making and ugly passes, but Ward can't be pinned for Tennessee's subpar offense alone.
After all, Daboll is the one calling the plays. Daboll may have his own perspective on Ward's progress, but he himself has to answer for what is one of the NFL's least efficient offenses.
It's a complex share of blame that the Titans need to see improvement from on either side. The road goes both ways, and right now, both ways are bumpy.
In a graph from Nutshell Sports that demonstrates QBs' expected points added per play both inside and outside the pocket, Ward is one of the few passers that landed in the "struggles everywhere" category.
An updated look at quarterback EPA per play inside and outside the pocket after Week 6. Justin Herbert and the Chargers have struggled to produce on passes from inside the pocket while still being fairly effective outside the pocket. Inside/outside pocket designation via… pic.twitter.com/7n7gRsbhpu
He's closer to being deemed an "improviser" than a "pocket passer," which doesn't bode well behind a much-improved Tennessee o-line that has allowed just 10 sacks up to this point. Again though, Ward's inability to make strides downfield is due in part to Daboll's milquetoast scheme.
Not only are simple mistakes - like receivers being drawn up to run right toward one another - clouding Ward's options, but looks deep are so far and far between that it's impossible to expect the QB to produce consistent explosive plays.
FantasyPros has Ward tracked with just 10 passes for 20+ yards, and three passes for 30 yards or more this season. He's got just one completion beyond 40 yards. Last season, Ward ended up with 40, 13, and three in each category, respectively.
It's a decline across the board in looks past the sticks. We've seen what Ward is capable of on plays like that, even if he managed those flashes in an offense that we thought couldn't get any worse last season.
Tennessee has promise on offense. Carnell Tate fully looks the part of a budding superstar WR. Again, Carmen Bricillo's offensive line, specifically T JC Latham, has taken leaps and bounds. But Ward is noticably behind, and the offense being built around him isn't helping in the way that it should.

title: Titans Midweek Report: Week 7 is a Must-Win, Trade Candidates Heat up, Alontae Taylor 'Reset'
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans, fresh off their first win of the season, have seen no shortage of headlines this past week. We'll get to Alontae Taylor's unexplained absence, but the big note was the dismissal of DT Jordan Elliott after a firearm-related incident at the Titans' facility.
It's a busy time for a 1-5 football team. A 1-5 football team that, with a win this week, could open the door to a more redemptive season than it seemed they were headed for through the first month of the 2026 NFL season.
Heading into Week 7, here's a midweek report covering all the latest for Tennessee. We'll start with Sunday's matchup.
After the Titans host the Browns in a few days, the team will face the Cincinnati Bengals, the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Dallas Cowboys, and then the Jaguars again. Gone are the days of games against the Jets and Giants in a three-week span.
Cleveland is good this year, but they appear very much beatable. The Jaguars are leading the AFC South at 4-2. Cincinnati, on the heels of their offense, are 3-2 and haven't scored less than 20 points in a single game this year. The 2-4 Cowboys are struggling, but that game is on the road.
When Deshaun Watson marches into Nissan Stadium in Week 7, Robert Saleh needs to run his aggressive d-line showing from last week back in the biggest way. Another six sacks would certainly do, although that may be lofty.
Either way, the 4-2 Browns, in their first year with Todd Monken leading the way, represent a prime opportunity for Tennessee to beat a good team before their schedule ticks up even more. Another leading defensive performance may be the key to making the most of that opportunity.
FOX Sports just listed WR Calvin Ridley at the top trade candidate on the Titans, citing his "career-low 13.5 receiving yards per game" and snap share that barely breaks the 50% mark. "Ridley would be best utilized on a contending team with a receiver need."
Our own Shaun Calderon agrees, suggesting Tennessee move Ridley to the Rams for a sixth-round pick in next year's draft. Anything in that ballpark would appear acceptable for the Titans.
With guys like Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson being brought in to hold down the pass-catching fort, Ridley's role already looked limited heading into this season. It's become clear through six weeks that even second-year WR Elic Ayomanor has more stake in the unit than Ridley.
His offseason paycut isn't a good enough argument to keep Ridley aboard in Nashville. His complimentary role could unsurprisingly give way to a move before November 10 if Tennessee makes a move on the market.
Robert Saleh said Taylor was deactivated vs. the Colts last Sunday to give him a "reset." The Titans' secondary, and really defense as a whole, went on to have their best game of the season without the recently-signed CB.
DC Gus Bradley said today that Tennessee still has confidence in Taylor, and that he'll be playing meaningful snaps for the defense moving forward. Could him being sat have just been a fluke as a result of recent bad performance? Sure, even if that seems a tad extreme for a guy you paid $58 million.
Now, at least, it seems that Tennessee isn't keen on moving on from Taylor. A trade is still possible, but perhaps this whole scenario really comes down to Saleh trying to give the Tennessee native a clean slate moving forward.
Of Saleh approaching Taylor with the decision to bench him, Taylor said "you gotta take it to the chin." At least Taylor is a team player, and right now, appears bought in to the process that Saleh is selling him. If it works and Tennessee wins, it's hard to complain about what we don't know.
